title: Dispatch: Compare the canonical revocation position in the scheduled-successor guard (closure pass F2 bypass)
description:
Bounded follow-up to eshyra-jhpt.rev15 (merged at 8e9d77d). Supervisor probe at 8e9d77d found that the new F2 store guard in revokeCampaignRule compares input.revokedPosition (the caller's RAW anchor) against existing.effectivePosition BEFORE canonicalization. Because the __future__ anchor sorts before any real anchor at the same ordinal, a caller can bypass the guard by supplying the successor's effective ordinal with fabricated session/turn ids.

REPRO at 8e9d77d: A effective 1; ten committed turns; supersede A with B effective 15 (stored future(15)); revokeCampaignRule(B, revokedPosition {s, t15, 15}) -> ACCEPTED, stored revokedPosition = {__future__, __future__, 15} == B.effectivePosition; active sets: 14 = [A], 15 = [], 20 = []; validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules) -> THROWS "successor 'B' of 'A' was revoked before taking effect". So the store produced a history the validator rejects — the exact store/validator mismatch class this closure pass exists to remove. (Revoking at 11 is correctly rejected; only the same-ordinal path leaks.)

WORKTREE / BRANCH: .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev16 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev16, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 8e9d77d. npm ci already run.

FIX: in revokeCampaignRule, validate/format input.revokedPosition and compute the canonical revokedPosition (canonicalizeFuturePosition) FIRST, then run the strict-prospectivity guard and the scheduled-successor guard against the CANONICAL position (compareCampaignPositions(canonical, existing.effectivePosition) <= 0). Keep messages unchanged. Also assert the reverse direction in the same function: after the write, the persisted rule must satisfy the validator's mirror (revokedPosition > effectivePosition whenever a prior names it) — a cheap self-check is acceptable but not required; say which you chose.

EVIDENCE (must FAIL against 8e9d77d): extend campaignRuleLifecycleMatrix.test.ts X2 with the same-ordinal fabricated-anchor case: revocation at {fabricated ids, ordinal == B.effective ordinal} is rejected with the F2 message; rows and active sets unchanged; validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules) still accepts the pre-revocation history. Also add the positive boundary: revocation at ordinal B.effective+1 is accepted, B active exactly at B.effective, and the history validates.

title: Dispatch: Lifecycle-graph closure pass over campaign-rule domain and store (PR #524 review 7, head 4aaf5e8)
description:
LIFECYCLE-GRAPH CLOSURE PASS over eshyra-jhpt.1/.2 at PR #524 head 4aaf5e8, triggered by external review #5119845911 (2026-09-05) and the reviewer's process note: four consecutive single-blocker rounds all sat in the same lifecycle/state-integrity family, so this round must exhaust the family rather than fix one edge. The supervisor enumerated the state machine (statuses active/superseded/revoked; transitions create/supersede/revoke; temporal relations before/equal/after current, predecessor, successor, revocation; chains A->B, A->B->C, later revoke, scheduled successor, cancellation before effect; disputed-turn vs prospective; validator vs store; read/list/active-at-position; checkpoint; rejected-mutation atomicity) and PROBED every suspect cell at 4aaf5e8. Five cells are defective. Fix ALL of them in this one dispatch.

WORKTREE / BRANCH: .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev15 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev15, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 4aaf5e8. npm ci already run.

# =============================================================
F1 (BLOCKING, reviewer) — validateCampaignRules accepts reverse-time supersession.
Probe: validateCampaignRules([A effective P10 superseded-by B, B effective P5]) -> OK. The store rejects the same transition ("successor 'B' cannot take effect before 'A'"). activeRows would end A at B.effective (P5) so A is never active.
FIX: in the relation loop, fail when compareCampaignPositions(successor.effectivePosition, rule.effectivePosition) < 0 with the message `successor '${successor}' cannot take effect before '${rule}'` (same wording as the store). Equal positions remain accepted (the store accepts them; a scheduled prior replaced by a same-position successor is coherent — probe D2 confirmed prior never active, successor active).

# =============================================================
F2 (BLOCKING, supervisor) — cancelling a scheduled successor strands its prior.
Probe at 4aaf5e8: A effective 1 (active); after ten committed turns, supersede A with B effective 15 (scheduled); revoke B at 11 (cancellation, allowed since rev10 E5). Result: active set at 12 = [A], at 15 = [], at 20 = []; revokeCampaignRule(A) -> "campaign rule 'A' is not active"; supersedeCampaignRule(A) -> "campaign rule 'A' is already superseded"; validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules) -> accepts. So A silently dies at 15 although its replacement never took effect, and A can never again be revoked or superseded. Both the store (producer) and the validator (acceptor) are wrong.
FIX (supervisor decision): forbid cancelling a successor before it takes effect. In revokeCampaignRule, after loading `existing`, look up whether any rule in the campaign has supersededBy === existing.ruleIdentity (single query); if so AND the canonical revokedPosition compares <= existing.effectivePosition, reject with `campaign rule '${B}' supersedes '${A}' and cannot be revoked before it takes effect; supersede it instead`. Revoking a successor AT OR AFTER its effective position stays allowed (A ends at B.effective, B active until revoked). Cancellation of a scheduled rule that supersedes nothing stays allowed (rev10 E5). Mirror in validateCampaignRules: for every superseded rule whose successor has revokedPosition !== null and compareCampaignPositions(successor.revokedPosition, successor.effectivePosition) <= 0, fail with `successor '${B}' of '${A}' was revoked before taking effect`. Document in the module comment that "cancelling a scheduled replacement" is expressed as superseding the scheduled successor with a new rule (typically a copy of the prior's prose) effective at the same position, which keeps continuity: prior until P, replacement from P.

# =============================================================
F3 (supervisor) — validateCampaignRules accepts two priors naming the same successor.
Probe: [A1 superseded-by B, A2 superseded-by B, B] -> OK. The store cannot produce this (a successor is written once through supersede and must not already exist), so the validator certifies structurally impossible history. FIX: fail `campaign rule '${B}' is named as successor by more than one rule` when a successor identity is referenced by two or more supersededBy values.

# =============================================================
F4 (supervisor) — validateCampaignRules accepts overlapping active rulings for one ambiguity.
Probe: two ambiguity rulings for 'amb', R1 effective 1 and R2 effective 2, both active -> OK. The store rejects this at write time (assertNoOverlappingAmbiguityRuling) and the context assembler fails closed on conflicting active rulings, so the validator accepts history the runtime treats as unplayable. FIX: add a set-level overlap check mirroring the store's half-open interval algebra: interval start = effectivePosition; end = revokedPosition for revoked rules, successor.effectivePosition (resolved via the same byId map) for superseded rules, open for active rules; intervals with end <= start are empty and never overlap; two rulings with the same provenance.ambiguityId whose intervals overlap fail with `active ambiguity ruling '${x}' overlaps '${y}' for ambiguity '${id}'` (store wording). Factor the interval algebra into ONE exported helper in campaignRules.ts and make the store's intervalsOverlap/existingIntervalEnd use it (behaviour identical; keep the store's pending-successor case).

# =============================================================
F5 (low, supervisor) — hydration symmetry. rowToRule fails closed on status/revoked_position mismatch (rev11) but not on status/superseded_by mismatch; the SQLite CHECK constraint covers the latter today, but a materialized snapshot from a future schema, or any other row source, would hydrate a superseded row without a successor as if coherent. FIX: in rowToRule, fail `superseded campaign rule '${id}' is missing superseded_by` when status is superseded and superseded_by is null, and `only a superseded rule may name supersededBy (campaign rule '${id}')` when non-superseded and non-null. Then existingIntervalEnd's own superseded_by null check becomes unreachable — remove it or keep it as an invariant assertion, your call, but say which.

# =============================================================
VERIFIED COHERENT BY THE SUPERVISOR (do not change): strict prospectivity of ordinary create/supersede/revoke (rev10); disputed-turn bounded exception; equal-position supersession (D2); revocation being terminal (a rule revoked at a future position has status revoked immediately, is still active until that position, and can be neither superseded nor re-revoked — intentional, exposed through revokedPosition); later-revoked successor accepted (rev14); rejected mutations atomic; checkpoint restore + typed reads (rev11-13).

# =============================================================
EVIDENCE — a LIFECYCLE MATRIX test, not one test per finding. Add `packages/core/test/campaignRuleLifecycleMatrix.test.ts` (store-backed, real .2 APIs) that, for each of these graphs, (a) builds it through the live mutations where the store allows it, (b) asserts validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules) accepts it, (c) asserts the active identity set at every boundary position — one before and at each of: each effective position, each revocation position, each successor effective position, plus one far-future ordinal — as literal lists, and (d) round-trips it through serializeCampaign + materializeSnapshot and re-asserts (b) and (c) on the restored DB:
  G1 single active rule; G2 rule revoked later; G3 scheduled rule cancelled (no prior); G4 A->B prospective; G5 A->B then revoke B after effect; G6 A->B->C then revoke C; G7 A scheduled, superseded by B at the same scheduled position; G8 disputed-turn successor at the current turn; G9 disputed-turn successor at the immediately preceding turn across sessions; G10 two rulings for one ambiguity in disjoint intervals (R1 revoked before R2 effective).
And for each REJECTED graph, prove BOTH boundaries reject with their exact messages and that the store leaves rows/active sets unchanged: X1 reverse-time successor (F1, validator) and the store's existing rejection; X2 cancel a scheduled successor before effect (F2, store and validator); X3 two priors -> one successor (F3, validator; store: second supersede naming an existing successor is rejected 'already exists'); X4 overlapping rulings (F4, validator; store rejection message); X5 superseded row without superseded_by / active row with superseded_by (F5, hydration; construct via a test double row or by temporarily dropping the CHECK in a scratch table — say how).
Every negative assertion asserts the distinctive message. NEGATIVE PROOF: run the matrix against 4aaf5e8 before fixing; report exactly which cells fail and with what.

VERIFICATION: npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing; report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution. Do not touch migrations, the position encoding, admission rules other than F2, or context assembly.

Dispatched 2026-09-05: codex gpt-5.6-luna, effort HIGH, YOLO, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev15 (cut from eshyra-jhpt @ 4aaf5e8), pgid 1233131.
Completion report (commit 3a1867b).

Implemented all five lifecycle-graph cells:
- F1: validateCampaignRules now rejects reverse-time successors with successor 'B' cannot take effect before 'A'; equal positions remain valid.
- F2: revokeCampaignRule rejects cancelling a scheduled successor before effect with campaign rule 'B' supersedes 'A' and cannot be revoked before it takes effect; supersede it instead. The validator mirrors this as successor 'B' of 'A' was revoked before taking effect. The module documents cancellation via same-position supersession/copy continuity. Standalone scheduled rules with no prior remain cancellable.
- F3: validator rejects a successor named by multiple priors.
- F4: added the exported internal campaignRuleIntervalsOverlap half-open interval helper; validator and store overlap admission use it, including revoked/superseded endpoints and empty intervals.
- F5: rowToRule now rejects both status/superseded_by asymmetries. The existingIntervalEnd null check remains as an unreachable invariant assertion after fail-closed hydration.

Negative proof against baseline 4aaf5e8: the lifecycle matrix ran with exactly 5 failures (X1-X5) and 10 accepted graphs passing. F1 validator accepted with no message; baseline store emitted successor 'B' cannot take effect before 'A'. F2 store and validator both accepted with no message; the supervisor probe observed active [A] at position 12 and [] at positions 15 and 20, then revoke A emitted campaign rule 'A' is not active and supersede A emitted campaign rule 'A' is already superseded. F3 validator accepted with no message; baseline store emitted campaign rule 'B' already exists. F4 validator accepted with no message; baseline store emitted active ambiguity ruling 'R2' overlaps 'R1' for ambiguity 'amb-matrix'. F5 hydration accepted both superseded-without-successor and active-with-successor rows with no message; the pre-existing domain validator messages were superseded rule must name supersededBy and only a superseded rule may name supersededBy.

title: Dispatch: Accept a later-revoked successor in the campaign-rule set validator (PR #524 review 6, head 671c9a9)
description:
External review #5119130556 (2026-09-05) of PR #524 head 671c9a9: CHANGES REQUIRED, ONE blocking finding. Review-5 revocation-history blocker CONFIRMED FIXED (rev11-13). Supervisor REPRODUCED the new one at 671c9a9.

FINDING (BLOCKING) — the .1 set validator rejects a canonical lifecycle that .2 intentionally creates.
campaignRules.ts::validateCampaignRules resolves rule.supersededBy and unconditionally fails with 'a revoked rule cannot supersede another rule' when successor.status === 'revoked'. But a successor that validly superseded its prior and was LATER revoked is a legitimate history: .5 explicitly allows edit-by-supersession then revocation, and the reviewer-required R5 test creates exactly r5-original -> r5-successor then revokes r5-successor. SUPERVISOR REPRO at 671c9a9: create A (effective 1, current 0); persist turn 1; supersede A with B (effective 2); revoke B at ordinal 3; listCampaignRules returns [A superseded, B revoked]; validateCampaignRules(rules) throws 'CampaignRuleError: a revoked rule cannot supersede another rule'. The transition-time invariant is ALREADY enforced at the right boundary: supersedeCampaignRule rejects a prior whose CURRENT status is not active, and the successor is written through the live create path as active. The set-level check wrongly treats a LATER status as proof about the EARLIER transition. The existing domain test (campaignRules.test.ts ~line 295) builds a revoked successor with revokedPosition null and asserts only .toThrow('revoked'), so the single-record 'revoked rule must carry revokedPosition' guard fires first and the set-level check is never actually exercised — a false green.

REQUIRED FIX (supervisor decision):
1. In validateCampaignRules, REMOVE the `successor.status === 'revoked'` rejection. Keep: successor existence, cross-campaign rejection, cycle detection, per-rule validation, duplicate identity. Do not add any replacement status-based assumption about the successor (a superseded successor is also valid history: A -> B -> C).
2. Keep supersedeCampaignRule's live guards exactly as they are ('campaign rule X is revoked' / 'is already superseded' for a non-active prior).
3. Repair campaignRules.test.ts: the revoked-successor case must build a COHERENT revoked successor (revokedPosition set) and now assert that validateCampaignRules ACCEPTS the graph {A supersededBy B, B revoked with revokedPosition}; also assert a longer chain A->B->C with C revoked is accepted. Remove the broad .toThrow('revoked') false green. Keep a separate test proving the single-record guard 'revoked rule must carry revokedPosition' still rejects an incoherent revoked rule.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE (each must FAIL against 671c9a9):
V1 (store test, real .2 APIs): create A, supersede A with B, revoke B, then validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules(db, { campaignId })) does not throw; the returned pair matches [A superseded/supersededBy B, B revoked with the canonical revokedPosition].
V2 (store test): superseding an already-revoked PRIOR through supersedeCampaignRule is rejected with the exact message "campaign rule 'X' is revoked" and leaves the prior unchanged (may extend the existing 'rejects superseding a revoked rule' test — confirm it asserts the exact message).
V3 (domain test): the coherent graph above is accepted directly by validateCampaignRules.

title: Dispatch: Expose revocation position through the campaign-rule domain and read APIs (PR #524 review 5, head 459887b)
description:
External review #5118796759 (2026-09-04) of PR #524 head 459887b, semantic-system profile: CHANGES REQUIRED, ONE blocking finding. The review-4 equality-boundary fix (rev10) is CONFIRMED FIXED; everything else re-checked stands. Supervisor confirmed the new finding against the code at 459887b.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev11 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev11, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 459887b. npm ci already run.

# =============================================================
FINDING (BLOCKING) — revocation timing is persisted but erased by the .1 domain shape and the .2 read APIs.

eshyra-jhpt.2 requires persistence of the REVOCATION POSITION and read/list APIs; .5 must display supersession/revocation history through the .1/.2 APIs; ADR 0020 requires history to be attributable and replayable through the typed contract. Today:
- campaign_rule.revoked_position is durable; revokeCampaignRule writes the canonical (rev10 __future__-anchored) position; activeRows reads the RAW column; checkpoint round-trips the raw row.
- But CampaignRule (campaignRules.ts:60) has status + supersededBy and NO revokedPosition; CampaignRuleProjection (line 76) has none either; rowToRule (campaignRuleStore.ts ~226) receives row.revoked_position and drops it.
- So getCampaignRule, listCampaignRules and the value returned by revokeCampaignRule expose only status:'revoked', never WHEN. The existing tests prove the gap: they reach for raw `SELECT revoked_position FROM campaign_rule` to check it.
- Worse after rev10: the stored anchor deliberately differs from the caller's input (__future__ replaces fabricated ids), and the caller has no typed way to learn what was persisted. The supersession side is symmetric and fine (supersededBy + successor.effectivePosition); revocation is the asymmetric missing datum. Domain validation also cannot express status/revoked-position consistency because the field does not exist.

# =============================================================
REQUIRED SHAPE (supervisor decision — implement exactly this)
1. Add `readonly revokedPosition: CampaignPosition | null` to CampaignRule, directly mirroring supersededBy (required field, null when not revoked). Add `readonly revokedPosition: string | null` (formatCampaignPosition output) to CampaignRuleProjection and populate it in projectCampaignRule.
2. rowToRule hydrates it from row.revoked_position. A row with status 'revoked' and NULL revoked_position must FAIL hydration with a CampaignRuleError naming the rule (reuse/relocate the message existingIntervalEnd already uses: "revoked campaign rule 'x' is missing revoked_position"); a non-revoked row with a non-null revoked_position must also fail hydration ("only a revoked rule may carry revokedPosition" or similar). Then make activeRows and existingIntervalEnd consume rule.revokedPosition instead of re-reading the raw column, so there is ONE hydration path.

FINDING (BLOCKING) — ordinary lifecycle mutations at the latest persisted position rewrite that turn's canonical history.

Invariant (eshyra-jhpt.1/.2/.5/.8, ADR 0020 state integrity): ordinary campaign rules and lifecycle changes are PROSPECTIVE; retroactivity is reserved for the explicit disputed-turn mode bounded to the current or immediately-preceding turn. assertCurrentPosition defines currentPosition as the latest PERSISTED campaign_turn_position row. That row is created inside the turn savepoint and survives only when the turn commits, so "currentPosition" at a management call is an ALREADY-ADJUDICATED turn. The live boundary rejects `< currentPosition` but accepts `== currentPosition` in all three ordinary mutations:

- create: checkTemporalMode (campaignRules.ts) rejects prospective effectivePosition only when `< currentPosition`. A rule effective at P10 with current P10 is accepted and activeRows(P10) immediately includes it.
- revoke: revokeCampaignRule rejects only `revokedPosition < currentPosition`; combined with assertPersistedPosition (revokedPosition must be a persisted row) the ONLY admissible non-future revocation is P10 itself, and activeRows keeps a revoked rule only while revoked_position > cutoff, so P10 flips to inactive. There is currently NO genuinely prospective revocation path for an active rule at all.
- supersede: the prospective successor is rejected only when `effectivePosition < currentPosition`; successor at P10 rewrites the rule set P10 used.

SUPERVISOR REPRODUCTION at f886c24 (bareDb, rule 'early' effective ordinal 1 created at current ordinal 0, then ten resolveCampaignPosition turns so persisted current = P10; activeRows queried at P10 after each ordinary mutation with currentPosition = P10):

  create after       ["early","late"]        <- 'late' effective P10
  revoke after       ["late"]                <- 'early' revoked at P10
  supersede after    ["late2"]               <- 'late' superseded by 'late2' effective P10
All three succeeded and each changed P10's active set.

REQUIRED SEMANTICS (supervisor decision — implement exactly this; if you find it incoherent with replay, say so in your notes rather than inventing an alternative)

Ordinary (prospective-mode) admission is STRICTLY AFTER the persisted current position:
1. create: prospective effectivePosition.ordinal must be > currentPosition.ordinal. `==` is rejected with a distinctive message, e.g. 'prospective campaign rule cannot take effect at or before the current position' (update the existing '< current' message/guard in checkTemporalMode; keep a single guard). The existing future canonicalization (canonicalizeFutureEffectivePosition -> __future__ anchor) then applies to every admitted prospective rule, so there is no fabricated-anchor path left for prospective creation. Bootstrap (no persisted row, current ordinal 0) is unchanged: effective ordinal >= 1.
2. supersede: same rule for a prospective successor — effective ordinal must be > current ordinal, canonicalized to the __future__ anchor. The prior's interval therefore ends strictly after the current turn: prior still active at P10, successor active from P11. Disputed-turn successors keep today's bounded current/immediately-previous checks unchanged.
3. revoke: revokedPosition.ordinal must be > currentPosition.ordinal (distinctive message, e.g. "campaign rule 'x' cannot be revoked at or before the current position"). Since such a position cannot be persisted yet, DROP assertPersistedPosition for revokedPosition and instead canonicalize it to the __future__ anchor exactly as create does for effective positions (add a shared helper rather than duplicating). Because __future__ sorts BEFORE a real anchor at the same ordinal, a rule revoked at future(11) is active at real P10 and inactive at real P11 — verify this against compareCampaignPositions and activeRows and assert it in tests. Ordinary between-turn revocation is then: revokedPosition = { ordinal: current+1 } (any session/turn ids; they are replaced by the anchor).

Future-rule cancellation (round-5 fix): a rule scheduled at ordinal E > current may still be cancelled; it now happens with revokedPosition.ordinal > current (typically current+1), which may be < E. Decide and DOCUMENT one canonical representation — either store the given future revokedPosition (activeRows already yields "never active" because effective > cutoff for every cutoff < E and revoked <= cutoff for every cutoff >= revoked) or canonicalize revokedPosition up to the effective position. Either way the round-5 guarantee holds: the rule is never active at any position, and the current position's active set is unchanged by the cancellation. Retire the now-unreachable canCancelBeforeEffective / 'cannot be revoked before its effective position' branch only if it is genuinely unreachable under the new admission; if you keep a guard, its test must be able to fail.
5. Disputed-turn mode is UNCHANGED: creation/supersession at the current or immediately-preceding turn (including the cross-session adjacent case) remains accepted, with persisted-anchor validation as today.
6. All rejected mutations remain atomic: no row, chain, or historical active-at-position change on rejection (already inside withTransaction — assert it).

title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 6 findings on PR #524 head 8dfbd25
description:
Supervisor self-review round 6 of PR #524 head 8dfbd25. FIVE findings: one HIGH, two MEDIUM, two LOW. The sweep independently re-verified as correct the half-open interval arithmetic (including the pending-successor case), __future__ sort-before-real semantics, resolveCampaignPosition savepoint nesting and failed-turn chronology, parseCampaignPosition round-trip canonicality, the seenRuleIdentities/includeAllActive interaction, and automatic checkpoint/migration pickup.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev9 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev9, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 8dfbd25. npm ci already run.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (HIGH) — an ambiguity ruling can never be superseded. Introduced by the very first review fix on this PR.
=============================================================
supersedeCampaignRule validates the ALREADY-PERSISTED prior rule against the SUCCESSOR's validation options:
    validateCampaignRule(prior, input.validation);
    validateCampaignRules([{ ...prior, status: 'superseded', ... }, successor], input.validation);
validateCampaignRule on a ruling with ambiguity provenance calls ambiguityFor(ambiguityId, options) and fails with 'unknown ambiguity ...' when it does not resolve. A caller replacing ruling R (ambiguity X) with a house rule, or with a ruling for a DIFFERENT ambiguity Y, naturally supplies validation describing only the successor — so the call throws on the prior, which was already validated at creation and is not being changed semantically.
REPRODUCED at 8dfbd25 (supervisor): create a ruling for ambiguity:x, then supersede it with a plain house rule ->
    CampaignRuleError: unknown ambiguity ambiguity:x
This blocks the ambiguity-ruling lifecycle outright, which eshyra-jhpt.6 and .7 are built on. Existing store tests only supersede rules that share the successor's provenance, so the path is untested.
PROVENANCE OF THE DEFECT: `validateCampaignRule(prior, input.validation)` was added by the first blocking-review fix (eshyra-jhpt.2.4) at the supervisor's instruction, to stop validation being fed a prior whose status had been rewritten. That instruction was right about the status and wrong about the options: the prior must be checked for the invariants supersession actually changes, not re-validated as if it were being created now.
FIX: validate the prior only for what supersession changes — identity, campaign, status/supersededBy transition — and do not re-run provenance/ambiguity validation against the successor's options. If you believe the prior's ambiguity linkage must still be checked, resolve it from the pack via ambiguityLookup rather than from the caller's successor-scoped options, and say why. Keep the round-1 property intact: the prior's REAL stored status must still be what gets checked, never a rewritten copy.
EVIDENCE: supersede an ambiguity ruling with (a) a house rule, (b) a ruling for a different ambiguity, and (c) a ruling for the same ambiguity — all succeed with correct chain state; and the round-1 guards (already-superseded, revoked prior) still reject.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (MEDIUM) — the recoverable category was drawn too wide: packaging defects now degrade silently.
=============================================================
Round 5 asked for a positive category so pack-CONTENT failures degrade by construction. The implementation marks the BASE RulesPackError constructor (rules/types.ts) plus CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError, so every RulesPackError in the codebase is now recoverable. That includes packaging defects: a campaign still bound to the retired 'rules:dnd5e-srd' placeholder, or a shipped build with a corrupt or missing data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/. bundledSrdPack.ts documents exactly that case as "a packaging defect, not a recoverable runtime condition", yet the turn now proceeds with an AMBIGUITY SOURCE UNAVAILABLE line, all ambiguity metadata dropped, and every active ambiguity ruling flattened into the generic rules list — while tools later fail on the same binding with a different error. The operator sees degraded play instead of a clear failure.
This is partly the supervisor's fault: round 5 said "pack content" and the marker was applied to the whole error base class. The category is right; its membership is wrong.
FIX: mark only the errors that represent unusable pack CONTENT encountered while interpreting a resolved pack — CampaignRulesPackAuthoringError and the ambiguity-interpretation failures — not the base RulesPackError and not binding/packaging resolution failures. Keep it a positive category (a future content-error class opts in by marking itself); just narrow the membership. Then confirm the round-3 finding-1 behaviour is preserved for the case it was actually about, and state explicitly which failures now degrade and which are fatal.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 (MEDIUM) — the ambiguity boundary's try wraps far more than the comment claims.
=============================================================
campaignContext.ts ambiguitiesFromStack wraps the WHOLE record loop, not just the optRulesAmbiguities call, and rethrows anything unmarked as CampaignRulesPackAuthoringError. So a genuine programming error — a TypeError from iterating stack.recordsByKey after some future stack-resolution change — becomes a marked recoverable error, is swallowed by finding 2's handler, and surfaces only as a prompt line reading "AMBIGUITY SOURCE UNAVAILABLE: Cannot read properties of undefined". The comment says "unrelated failures retain their original behavior outside this boundary"; the boundary is wider than the comment describes.
FIX: narrow the try to the optRulesAmbiguities call itself, so only pack-content interpretation is reclassified. Test that a non-pack error thrown from the surrounding loop propagates unchanged.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 (LOW) — revokeCampaignRule is the only mutation whose guards and write are not in one transaction.
=============================================================
createCampaignRule and supersedeCampaignRule wrap their writes in withTransaction; revokeCampaignRule runs assertCurrentPosition, getCampaignRule, the position/ordering guards and the UPDATE directly on db. If another writer advances campaign_turn_position between the check and the update, the revocation commits against a position that is no longer current — precisely what those guards exist to prevent.
FIX: wrap it in withTransaction like its siblings. Note also that supersedeCampaignRule performs its guard reads before opening its transaction, a smaller version of the same window; close that too if it is cheap.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 (LOW, performance) — the per-turn path scans the campaign's whole rule history twice.
=============================================================
assembleCampaignRulesContext calls activeRows twice per turn, each call decoding and projecting every revoked and superseded row in the campaign's history.
FIX: compute the active row set once per assembly and share it between the two lists. Behaviour must not change.
Index note: activeRows does every position predicate in JS, so the two position indexes from migration 0025 can never be chosen. That is already tracked as eshyra-jhpt.2.5 — do NOT change indexes or migrations here. If you judge that an `effective_position <= ?` prefilter on the encoded string is a safe superset given the cp1~<12-digit ordinal>~ layout, record the reasoning on eshyra-jhpt.2.5 rather than implementing it in this PR.

GENERAL

  - Preserve every earlier fix, in particular: the prior rule's real stored status is what gets validated (round 1), deterministic future-anchor ordering (round 4), and returning exactly what was persisted (round 5).

description:
STANDALONE HANDOFF for a clean Opus session. Assumes NO conversational memory.
Read this bead in full before touching anything. Created 2026-07-27 by the

1. STATE OF THE THREE INVALIDATED PRs
================================================================================
All three are CLOSED UNMERGED, converted to draft, branches PRESERVED on origin.

  PR #475  eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1  head 68e5253f0a41aae5a4aff95564c38ceff8d08f79

history in notes, and is blocked on F1 so it cannot read as complete. None was
closed as successful.

UNPUSHED SALVAGE: branch eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1.6 holds commit 7f38879
("fail closed on unresolved obligations"), produced by a dispatch that finished
after the stop decision. It was deliberately NOT pushed. It is potentially
useful design input for F1 — it demonstrates the fail-closed correction for
CAPTURED on an unresolved obligation — but must not be pushed to #475.

================================================================================
2. GOVERNING CONCLUSION
================================================================================
DESIGN_INVALIDATED. The three PRs failed differently but share one cause:

  UNSETTLED CONCEPTS WERE GENERALIZED ACROSS THE CORPUS BEFORE THEIR TRUST
  BOUNDARIES WERE PROVEN BY A SMALL NUMBER OF CONCRETE SOURCE-TO-EXECUTION
  EXAMPLES.

Successor work inverts that order. Prove the boundary on five real procedures,
then generalize.

================================================================================
3. CROSS-PR TRUST-BOUNDARY ANALYSIS (the eleven questions)
================================================================================
1. WHO ESTABLISHES THAT A SOURCE OBLIGATION EXISTS?
   UNRESOLVED, and this is the central defect. #475 let the projector carry
   sourceObligations on the same emitted Clause it was judged by; the registry
   that was meant to fix this could not be authoritative because the source
   census underwriting it is deferred (eshyra-s38f). #476 let the pack under
   repair define its own membership. #477 let a hand-written alias table stand
   in. NOTHING in the three PRs independently establishes obligation existence.
   F1 must settle this FIRST.

2. STABLE IDENTITY OF AN OBLIGATION?
   #475 and #477 converged on obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>. #476 never
   participated — it uses MembershipIdentity{recordKey, clauseId?, path?,
   sourceSpan?} with no obligationId. Even where the string shape matched, #477
   minted it for EVIDENCE ITEMS (code-symbol, ownership, primitive-relevance),
   a category error later split into an ev::: namespace. The shape is NOT yet a
   proven identity; treat it as a candidate.

3. WHAT IS AUTHORITATIVE vs MERELY PROJECTED OUTPUT?
   Never cleanly separated. #475's obligations lived beside the projection;
   #476's "derived" rows were generated from the pack being repaired; #477's
   readiness evidence WAS the pack projection. In all three the artifact under
   repair was used as evidence about itself.

4. HOW DOES A PROJECTED ATOM DISCHARGE AN EXACT OBLIGATION?
   UNRESOLVED. #475 evaluated obligations against clause-GLOBAL fields, so one
   save atom could discharge two distinct source saves. The one-obligation-per-
   clause invariant was introduced to dissolve this and is a HYPOTHESIS TO
   RE-TEST in F1, not a settled result.

5. MULTIPLICITY, ALTERNATIVES, OPTION LOCALITY, LIFECYCLE, TIMING, TERMINATION?
   Partially modelled, never proven. Facets existed for duration/recurrence/
   repeatChecks/immunityWindows/termination; alternatives could pass with a
   DISCONNECTED exclusion graph (mutual exclusion is a partition property, and
   one member proves nothing about it). Option locality was asserted, not
   demonstrated. F1 must demonstrate all of these on real procedures.

6. WHAT IDENTITY PERSISTS AFTER A FINDING IS REPAIRED?
   #476 eventually separated a durable obligation+target+invariant from a
   transient violation predicate that may go empty. THAT SEPARATION IS SOUND AND
   SHOULD SURVIVE. What did not survive was the membership behind it.

7. SOURCE-BACKED vs CURRENT-BROKEN-PACK MEMBERSHIP?
   The rule was stated correctly — a row's authority may not be the pack under
   repair — and then not enforced until the final round. An obligation already
   omitted from the pack is invisible to a query over that pack, which is
   exactly the case the registry exists to catch. Ending state: 0 derived,
   68 underived. That zero is the honest measure.

8. EVIDENCE THAT PROVES ONLY PRESENCE / OWNERSHIP / CANDIDACY?
   Exported-symbol existence; bead existence; a record having any engineHooks;
   an alias appearing in a hard-coded universe; a readiness clause existing.
   All four were used as if they proved semantic implementation. They do not.

9. STRONGER EVIDENCE — SEMANTIC IMPLEMENTATION AND PACK-DRIVEN EXECUTION?
   NEVER ACHIEVED in any of the three. This is F4's subject and it must define
   what each category does NOT prove, not only what it does.

10. HOW CAN ABSENCE BE POSITIVELY ESTABLISHED?
    UNRESOLVED and the hardest question. #477 tried invented sentinel markers
    (absence of a made-up token), then anchor-record-only scanning, then closed
    predicates over allowed schemas. The last failed because RulesRecord.data is
    typed unknown and the kind validator does not reject unregistered fields —
    there IS no closed schema to enumerate against. The only sound position
    reached: unclassified structured material must remain UNDERIVED, never
    "absent". Recognising nothing is not evidence of absence.

11. WHICH CONCEPTS MUST STABILIZE FIRST?
    obligation identity + discharge (F1)

ANSWERS TO SECTION 6 (unresolved design questions for F1) -- proposed, pending review:

Q "Is one-obligation-per-clause correct, or does it merely relocate the multiplicity
   problem into clause decomposition?"
A It RELOCATES it. Replaced by ONE OBLIGATION = ONE FACET OCCURRENCE with `ordinal` in
  the identity: obl/<digest8>/p<page>/q<quoteHash8>/<facetSlot>/<ordinal>. The
  decomposition unit is now the thing being counted, so there is nowhere left to hide
  the problem. Proof case: Burnt Othur Fumes (SRD p.204) has TWO Constitution DC 13
  saves with identical facet content -- obl:::<sourceRef>::<locator>::<facet> cannot
  express them as two. The shipped pack collapses them to mechanics.saves[1 entry].

Q "What creates obligations if the source census does not exist yet -- a curated seed
   for five procedures, or a real extractor?"
A A CURATED, QUOTE-ANCHORED LEDGER for five procedures. Curation alone is untrustworthy
  (that is how #477's alias table failed); what makes it FALSIFIABLE is that every row
  carries a verbatim quote plus the number of occurrences on its cited page, and the
  loader re-derives both from a digest-pinned extraction of the frozen PDF. A curator
  cannot invent an obligation over text that is not there. Completeness is handled
  separately and BOUNDED to five pages by a PageCensus with a mandatory-empty residual.
  Reviewer question Q2.

Q "Can option locality be expressed without a scope/closure layer?"
A YES. Locality is JSON-Pointer containment in the projected record. An obligation with
  locality {kind:'option', optionLabel:'Archery'} is discharged only by an atom whose
  pointer lies under the choices[i].options[j] carrying that label. The projector cannot
  assert scope it does not have. Demonstrated by hoisting Fighting Style's six option
  mechanics to the parent: type-valid, and six LOCALITY_VIOLATIONs.

Q "How is a model-adjudicated boundary represented so it neither satisfies nor blocks?"
A A separate `classification` (deterministic | model-adjudicated | source-ambiguous)
  that fails closed IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: an adjudicated obligation requires an explicit
  in-band declaration (ADJUDICATION_MISSING otherwise) AND forbids a deterministic atom
  covering the same span (ADJUDICATION_SILENTLY_DETERMINIZED); a deterministic
  obligation forbids discharge by an adjudication declaration
  (DETERMINISTIC_DISCHARGED_BY_ADJUDICATION). Proof case Wish (SRD p.193): the
  GM-latitude clause is silently ABSENT today, and mechanics.damage[1d10 necrotic] is
  hoisted out of its stress precondition so it reads as unconditional. NOTE a vocabulary
  gap: the pack's existing RulesAmbiguity (3 records) models SOURCE ambiguity resolvable
  by campaign ruling; Wish needs DESIGNED adjudication with owner 'model'. Extending the
  pack vocabulary is handed to eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4; F1 does not design it.

Q "Does provider-neutral execution require the engine capability registry, or can a
   narrow reference harness prove it for five procedures?"
A A NARROW REFERENCE HARNESS, inside F1. This is also what makes the repointed graph
  non-circular: olc5.1 -> olc5.5 -> 19.1.16 -> 19.1.7 -> 19.1.14 serializes all engine
  work behind F1..F5, so F1 cannot depend on the capability registry to satisfy its own
  real-pack execution acceptance criterion. Recorded as finding D4 so it cannot be
  silently reinterpreted. Reviewer question Q4.

title: Foundation 1: prove source-obligation identity and discharge on five real procedures
description:
THE FIRST SUCCESSOR. No other foundation may be designed in implementation detail
until this stabilises.

PREMISE CHANGE (why this exists): PRs #475/#476/#477 reached DESIGN_INVALIDATED
after repeatedly producing NEW defect classes following material contract changes
and fresh full reviews. The shared root cause was not implementation quality: in
all three, unsettled concepts were GENERALIZED ACROSS THE CORPUS before their
trust boundaries had been proven by a small number of concrete
source-to-execution examples. Successor work inverts that order.

GOAL: prove the disputed trust boundary — that an authoritative source obligation
can be created INDEPENDENTLY OF THE PROJECTOR and discharged by exact projected
atoms — on a SMALL VERTICAL SLICE of real SRD procedures. Do NOT design a
universal clause taxonomy. PR #475 is a design spike, not an accepted IR.

REQUIRED PROOF SET (five real, source-backed procedures):
  1. a compound save / damage / duration / repeat / termination procedure;
  2. a mutually exclusive attack or damage-mode procedure;
  3. an option-local feature whose mechanics must NOT be hoisted to its parent;
  4. a lifecycle or resource procedure;
  5. a deliberately model-adjudicated or source-ambiguous boundary.

ACCEPTANCE — each of the five must demonstrate:
  * the obligation is produced INDEPENDENTLY of the projector (the producer of
    an artifact can never define the standard its own output is judged by);
  * exact source identity and locator;
  * the required semantic facets;
  * the exact projected atom or branch identities that discharge it;
  * multiplicity — one atom cannot discharge two distinct obligations;
  * option or branch locality;
  * fail-closed handling of a missing facet;
  * provider-neutral execution against a REAL generated pack record, for the
    cases where the clause is a direct engine input.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS: no universal obligation identity, no contract-composition
framework, no aggregate closure, no registry authority generalisation, no
corpus-wide taxonomy. Those consume this and are blocked on it.

SALVAGE INPUT from PR #475 (design input only, not code to extend): the ADR
reasoning about clause-level completeness; the CAPTURED / PROJECTED / SUPPORTED /
DISCOVERABLE separation; structured failure vocabulary; cardinality and
fail-closed predicates; the adversarial test cases; and the worked examples
showing why projector-authored obligations are unsafe.

DESIGN (decided):
1. Core service packages/core/src/campaign/ambiguityResolution.ts:
   - export function lookupCampaignAmbiguity(db, {campaignId, ambiguityId, position: CampaignPosition, resolveRulesPack?}): {ambiguity: RulesAmbiguity, status: 'unresolved'|'resolved'|'conflicting', ruling?: CampaignRulingProjection, conflictingRulings: CampaignRulingProjection[]}. Unknown id -> throw CampaignRuleError('unknown ambiguity <id>; known ambiguity ids: a, b, c') (sorted). Uses assembleCampaignRulesContext at formatCampaignPosition(position) — NO new store, no pack write.
   - export function recordAmbiguityRuling(db, {campaignId, ambiguityId, interpretationId, prose?, currentPosition, effectiveOrdinal?, sessionId?, resolveRulesPack?}): {created: boolean, rule: CampaignRule}. If an active ruling for that ambiguity exists at the position immediately after current -> return {created:false, rule: existing} WITHOUT writing (idempotent; 'existing active ruling prevents re-prompting'). Else validate interpretationId against ambiguity.interpretations (unknown -> CampaignRuleError listing the known interpretation ids), build the ruling: ruleIdentity 'ruling:<ambiguityId without the "ambiguity:" prefix>:<effective ordinal>', ruleKind 'ruling', origin 'player-approved', provenance {kind:'ambiguity', ambiguityId, selectedInterpretationId}, effectivePosition {...currentPosition, ordinal: effectiveOrdinal ?? currentPosition.ordinal + 1}, temporalMode prospective, scope 'rules-ambiguity', governingRecordKeys = ambiguity.affects (non-empty; if the pack's affects is empty use ['ambiguity:<id>']), prose = provided ?? `${ambiguity.question} Ruling: ${interpretation.summary}`; persist via createCampaignRule with validation {ambiguity}. Return what was persisted.

Tool packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRequestAmbiguityRuling.ts: name 'request_ambiguity_ruling', mutates:false, args {ambiguityId: string}. run: lookupCampaignAmbiguity at the turn's current persisted position (getCurrentCampaignPosition(ctx.db, ctx.campaignId) — the turn's own row exists because runTurn resolves the position first). Returns ok({ambiguityId, question, interpretations:[{id, summary}], status, ruling: {ruleIdentity, selectedInterpretationId, prose} | null}); unknown id -> err('unknown_ambiguity', message, {knownAmbiguityIds}). Description tells the DM: call when an outcome depends on an ambiguity marked UNRESOLVED in Campaign Rules; then narrate the published uncertainty, present the interpretations neutrally, and tell the player they will be asked to choose; never choose yourself; if status is 'resolved', apply the ruling.
3. Prompts: add ONE bullet to buildSystemPrompt tool guidance (protocol.ts) stating the above. Add ONE line to the auditor's campaign-rules paragraph (turnAuditor.ts): a candidate that asserts a definite outcome for an ambiguity listed as UNRESOLVED without an active ruling must be rejected, reason citing the ambiguity id; a candidate that surfaces the uncertainty and defers to the player is acceptable.

CLI play loop: new file packages/cli/src/playRulings.ts exporting async function offerAmbiguityRulings(deps: PlayDeps, db: Db, campaignId: string, toolCalls: readonly ExecutedToolCall[]): Promise<void>. For each executed 'request_ambiguity_ruling' call with result.ok and data.status === 'unresolved' (dedupe by ambiguityId): io.write the question and numbered interpretations, io.prompt('Choose an interpretation number, or press Enter to leave it unresolved: '); Enter/undefined/invalid -> write 'Left unresolved.' and create nothing; a valid number -> recordAmbiguityRuling with currentPosition = getCurrentCampaignPosition(db, campaignId) and write 'Ruling <identity> recorded (<interpretationId>); takes effect from turn <ordinal>.' Errors -> write the message, create nothing. Call it from turnLoop right after deps.io.write(result.narration). (The ruling is prospective, so the NEXT turn's DM and auditor contexts carry it; that is the spec's 'prospectively active'.)
5. CLI rules command additions (packages/cli/src/rules.ts): 'rules ambiguities [campaign-id]' lists every ambiguity id with status (unresolved/resolved:<ruleIdentity>/conflicting) and its interpretation ids; 'rules resolve <ambiguity-id> --interpretation <id> [--prose <text>] [--effective <ordinal>] [campaign-id]' calls recordAmbiguityRuling and prints the same confirmation shape as 'add' (identity, effective ordinal, provenance, takes effect from turn N), or 'already resolved by <identity>' with exit 0 when created:false. Update USAGE.
6. Pack immutability: never write to the pack; tests assert the resolved stack's ambiguity record is unchanged (deep-equal before/after) and that no row other than campaign_rule changed.

title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 5 findings on PR #524 head d3d8781
description:
Supervisor self-review round 5 of PR #524 head d3d8781. SIX findings (4 medium, 2 low). No highs; the sweep independently re-verified as clean the interval-overlap algebra, __future__ anchor ordering, revoked/superseded predicates in activeRows, savepoint placement (failed turns leave no ordinal hole), nested withTransaction, the seenRuleIdentities/includeAllActive interaction, and the sessionDebug section labels.

Findings 2, 3 and 4 are all consequences of round 4's __future__ canonicalization. Fix the CLASS: that canonicalization rewrites a value the caller supplied, and every path that reads, returns, or compares that value must agree about which form it is looking at.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev8 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev8, cut from eshyra-jhpt at d3d8781. npm ci already run there.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (medium) — the per-turn degrade path still does not catch the pack-defect class it exists for.
=============================================================
contextAssembler.ts catches CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError and CampaignRulesPackAuthoringError, but assembleCampaignRulesContext -> ambiguitiesFromStack also calls optRulesAmbiguities, which throws RulesPackError on any malformed mechanics.ambiguities block. resolveRulesStack performs only meta-level assertions, so a pack supplied through deps.resolveRulesPack is never record-validated. A record declaring ambiguity id 'ambiguity:Foo_Bar' (fails the kebab-case regex) makes every runTurn throw out of assembleContext and roll back, instead of degrading to ambiguitySourceUnavailable.
This is the THIRD instance of this class: each round a new error type reaches the per-turn path and the catch list does not include it.
FIX: stop enumerating error types. Decide the rule positively — any failure to interpret PACK CONTENT while assembling per-turn context degrades to ambiguitySourceUnavailable with the error recorded; failures that are not about pack content still propagate. Implement it so a future pack-content error class is covered by construction rather than by remembering to add it. State how you achieved that.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (medium) — createCampaignRule returns a rule that does not match what it stored.
=============================================================
writeRule canonicalizes a future-dated prospective effectivePosition to the reserved __future__ anchor, but createCampaignRule returns the CALLER'S rule object, not what was persisted.
REPRODUCED at d3d8781 (supervisor), current ordinal 3, scheduling for ordinal 9:
    returned effectivePosition: {"sessionId":"s1","turnId":"t9","ordinal":9}
    stored   effectivePosition: {"sessionId":"__future__","turnId":"__future__","ordinal":9}
A caller that round-trips the returned value gets different ordering under compareCampaignPositions (future anchors sort before real anchors at equal ordinal) and a position assertPersistedPosition will reject. The existing test asserts canonicalization only via getCampaignRule, so the divergence is uncovered.
FIX: return what was persisted. Test that the returned value deep-equals getCampaignRule for both the future-dated and the ordinary case.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 (medium) — same divergence in supersedeCampaignRule.
=============================================================
It returns input.successor rather than what writeRule persisted, so a successor scheduled for a future ordinal is reported with anchors that were rewritten before insert. Same fix, same test shape.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 (medium) — a future-scheduled rule can NEVER be revoked before it takes effect.
=============================================================
Three guards compose into an unsatisfiable constraint: assertCurrentPosition forces currentPosition to equal the latest persisted turn; assertPersistedPosition forces revokedPosition to be a persisted turn; and revokedPosition >= currentPosition. Together those pin revokedPosition to the current ordinal — and the effective-position guard then rejects it for any rule effective later.
REPRODUCED at d3d8781 (supervisor): a rule scheduled at ordinal 9, player changes their mind at ordinal 2 ->
    campaign rule 'sched' cannot be revoked before its effective position
Every revoke attempt fails until ordinal 9 arrives, at which point revoking leaves the rule active for zero turns. There is no way to cancel a scheduled rule. supersedeCampaignRule has no equivalent block, so the two mutations disagree about the same lifecycle.
FIX: cancelling a not-yet-effective rule is a legitimate operation and must be possible. Decide the semantics deliberately — most likely revoking a rule that has not taken effect removes it from ever being active (revocation at its own effective position, or an explicit cancel), rather than requiring a revocation position that cannot exist. Make revoke and supersede consistent about not-yet-effective rules, and say in your notes what you chose. Test: schedule at ordinal 9, cancel at ordinal 2, prove the rule is never active at any position including 9 and later.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 (low) — duplicate governingRecordKeys duplicate the rule in the context packet.
=============================================================
The seam's governed loop pushes one entry per governingRecordKeys element with no dedup, and withRule appends to campaignRules/campaignRulings unconditionally (only routes is dedup-guarded by trigger). validateCampaignRule never rejects duplicate or empty governingRecordKeys, and keysColumn.decode returns the array verbatim. A rule persisted with ['spell:fireball','spell:fireball'] attaches twice, emits two identical placedRules trace entries, and duplicates the prose against the packet byte budget.
FIX: reject duplicate and empty governingRecordKeys in validateCampaignRule (write-side), and make the seam's placement idempotent per (ruleIdentity, governingRecordKey) so restored or legacy rows cannot duplicate either. Test both sides.

=============================================================
FINDING 6 (low) — a house-rule carrying ambiguity provenance is silently dropped from every context branch.
=============================================================
Such a rule is excluded from `rules` (provenance.kind !== 'ambiguity'), from unboundRulings (ruleKind === 'ruling'), and from `rulings` (isAmbiguityRuling requires ruleKind === 'ruling'). validateCampaignRule rejects the pairing on the write path, but migration 0025's CHECK constraints do not, and CheckpointStore restore inserts snapshot rows directly with no domain validation. Restoring such a checkpoint yields a rule active in listCampaignRules that never reaches the DM prompt, with no loss or diagnostic.
This is the silent-disappearance class again, and the same restore-bypass route as round 3 finding 7.
FIX: the context must not silently drop an active rule for any reason. Give the assembly a total accounting — every active rule lands in exactly one branch or is explicitly recorded as unrepresentable, with its identity visible. Consider also whether migration 0025 should carry the CHECK constraint that matches the domain invariant; if you think it should, file a bead rather than editing the merged migration.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against d3d8781; report observed counts and quote the asserted guard messages.
  - Every negative assertion must assert the distinctive guard message.
  - Do not weaken existing tests, do not touch merged migrations, the position encoding, eshyra-umyb, or eshyra-jhpt.2.5.
  - Keep every earlier fix intact, especially the deterministic future-anchor ordering from round 4.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.

Pack-content failures carry a shared internal marker and the per-turn assembler catches that positive category, covering RulesPackError and future interpreter failures by construction; the ambiguity interpreter boundary wraps unmarked failures, while unrelated resolver/database failures still propagate.

title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 4 findings on PR #524 head fdce24e
description:
Supervisor self-review round 4 of PR #524 head fdce24e. Severity is dropping — round 3 had a HIGH playability regression; this round's worst is MEDIUM, and the sweep independently verified several previously-suspect areas as clean (savepoint-nested position rollback, the recurring-question reclassification agreeing on both sides of the seam, late-join dedup not dropping a placeable ruling, migration/ledger/snapshot consistency).

FOUR findings. Three are consequences of round 3's own fixes. Finding 2 is round 3's finding 2 NOT actually fixed.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev7 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev7, cut from eshyra-jhpt at fdce24e. Run `npm ci` before verification.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (MEDIUM — the real bug this round) — a rule scheduled for a future turn is live or silently dead depending on a value the caller cannot know.
=============================================================
Round 3 finding 5 routed caller-supplied positions through persisted-chronology validation, but assertPersistedPositionAtOrBeforeCurrent deliberately SKIPS validation when the ordinal is above the current one — so a future-dated prospective rule keeps a fabricated sessionId/turnId. compareCampaignPositions tie-breaks equal ordinals on exactly those anchors. So whether the rule is actually in force on the turn that later receives that ordinal depends on a lexicographic comparison against a turn id that did not exist when the rule was written.
REPRODUCED at fdce24e (supervisor), current turn {s, abc, 1}:
    scheduled with fabricated anchor turnId=zzz; real turn 2 turnId=def
    active at real turn 2: []                      <- rule scheduled for this turn is missing
    same rule, fabricated anchor turnId=aaa -> active at real turn 2: [ 'scheduled' ]
Identical rule, opposite outcome, decided by a coin flip. The sweep also found the rule is then un-revocable at that turn: revokeCampaignRule with the REAL ordinal-2 anchor throws 'cannot be revoked before its effective position'.
FIX: a future position has no persisted anchor, so it must not carry a fabricated one that participates in ordering. Either reject future ordinals outright at the mutation boundary, or store a chronology-only anchor for a not-yet-persisted position — an ordinal plus a sentinel session/turn that sorts deterministically ahead of any real anchor for that ordinal — so ordering depends only on the ordinal, which is the authoritative field. State which you chose and why. Whichever you choose, scheduling for a future turn must either work deterministically or be refused; it must not depend on unknowable input.
EVIDENCE: the two cases above must produce the same outcome (both active, or both rejected). Plus revocation at the real anchor must behave consistently.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (round 3 finding 2, NOT fixed) — the probe closure assertion still cannot fail.
=============================================================
Round 3 added m5.ambiguityCoverage, but the underlying problem stands: measurements.ts's early return makes m5.unqueriedAmbiguityIds unconditionally [] in every production trace. runDiscoveryStages calls the first joinCampaignRules without `conditional`, so `asked` is always true and rulingQueryScope is always 'all-active', so the `|| lateRuleJoin` disjunct is never reached. m5.allActiveRulingsRequested is a constant true and ambiguityCoverage a constant 'all-active' — and the NEW probe assertion added in round 3 asserts a constant too. discoveryProbes.test.ts:219's closure invariant ("every ambiguity that reached the packet was offered to the seam") still cannot fail for any input.
This is the same failure mode as round 3's findings 9/10, in the measurement layer: an assertion that is structurally incapable of failing.
FIX: re-express the invariant against what the seam actually RETURNED, not against a scope flag that is short-circuited to a constant. If the invariant is genuinely subsumed by all-active scope, then delete the dead computation and the vacuous assertion and say so explicitly in a comment — do not leave an assertion that looks like a guarantee and is not one. Whatever you choose, demonstrate the probe can fail: temporarily break the property and show the probe catches it, then restore.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 — round 3's collision rejection can brick a campaign, because round 3's degrade only catches binding errors.
=============================================================
Round 3 finding 8 made ambiguitiesFromStack throw CampaignRuleError on a duplicate ambiguity id across record keys. Round 3 finding 1 made contextAssembler degrade — but only for CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError; everything else rethrows. So a pack-authoring mistake (an add-on restating a base ambiguity under a different record key; optRulesAmbiguities enforces id uniqueness only WITHIN a record, and resolveRulesStack merges by record key) hard-fails assemble_context on every turn. That is precisely the bricked-campaign outcome finding 1 was dispatched to eliminate, arriving through the door finding 8 opened.
FIX: a pack-authoring error must degrade, not brick play — the same treatment as an unavailable pack. Surface the collision in the assembled context (both record keys, as the current message already does) and continue, rather than throwing on the per-turn path. Keep a hard error where pack content is validated, not where a turn is assembled.
EVIDENCE: a stack with a colliding ambiguity id assembles successfully, the collision is visible in the context and the rendered prompt, and both record keys are named.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 — N+1 queries on the per-turn hot path, plus two dead indexes.
=============================================================
activeRows already holds every campaign_rule row for the campaign in memory, but for each superseded row it issues a fresh getCampaignRule query from inside the .filter callback to find a successor that is guaranteed to be in that same set (validateCampaignRules enforces same-campaign supersession). assembleCampaignRulesContext calls activeRows twice per turn, so a long-running campaign pays 2 x N_superseded avoidable point queries every turn.
FIX: build a Map<ruleIdentity, row> once from the rows already fetched. Behaviour must not change; this is purely removing redundant queries.
ALSO NOTE (non-blocking, decide and record): migration 0025's campaign_rule_effective_position and campaign_rule_status_position indexes are unused — every read path is WHERE campaign_id = ? with the position predicates evaluated in JS. Do NOT drop them in this PR (that is a migration change on a merged migration); instead say in your notes whether they should be dropped in a follow-up bead, and file it if so.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against fdce24e; report the counts you actually observed. For finding 2, demonstrating the probe CAN fail is the evidence, not a passing run.
  - Every negative assertion you add or touch must assert the distinctive guard message, per the standard established last round.
  - Do not weaken existing tests, do not touch merged migrations, the position encoding, or eshyra-umyb.

VERIFICATION

title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 3 findings on PR #524 head 4f3dcfb
description:
Supervisor self-review round 3 of PR #524 head 4f3dcfb. Round 2's seven findings are all confirmed fixed (6 of 97 observed failing against 97b2ff0 — see finding 9, the seventh test does not actually exercise its defect).

TEN findings. Finding 1 is a playability REGRESSION and is the priority. Findings 9-10 are a test-integrity class the supervisor found while doing the negative proof, and they explain how earlier rounds' defects survived.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev6 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev6, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 4f3dcfb. Run `npm ci` before verification.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (HIGH — regression, fix first) — an unresolvable rules binding now breaks EVERY turn.
=============================================================
contextAssembler.ts assembleContext now calls resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack(input.db, input.resolveRulesPack) unconditionally on the per-turn path. That function throws CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError for any binding it cannot resolve exactly. Before this branch, assembleContext never touched the binding, so an unresolvable binding degraded lookup_rules and the item/effect tools; now it throws inside the turn savepoint and the campaign is completely unplayable.
REPRODUCED at 4f3dcfb (supervisor), using the documented pre-adoption case — a DB bound to the retired placeholder RETIRED_DND5E_SRD_PLACEHOLDER_PACK_ID ('rules:dnd5e-srd'), which bundledSrdPack.ts says "fails resolution with a clear, actionable error":
    assembleContext -> CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError: campaign rules pack 'dnd5e-srd' / 'rules:dnd5e-srd' @ '5.1' is unavailable
The same applies to any campaign bound to a non-bundled base or add-on pack: packages/cli/src never supplies resolveRulesPack, so the CLI cannot satisfy it at all.
FIX: campaign-rule context must not be able to make a turn impossible. Degrade rather than throw — if the stack cannot be resolved, assemble the campaign-rule slice without pack-side ambiguity metadata and record that the ambiguity source was unavailable, so the DM still receives active campaign rules and the failure is visible rather than fatal. Do NOT silence the error; make it observable in the assembled context. Keep the strict behaviour for the paths that legitimately require an exact stack (lookup_rules, item/effect tools) — this fix is about the per-turn context path only.
EVIDENCE: a test with an unresolvable binding proving assembleContext succeeds, that active campaign rules are still supplied, and that the unavailability is represented in the result. Plus a test that a resolvable binding is unaffected.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 — m5.unqueriedAmbiguityIds is permanently empty, so a probe closure assertion is vacuously true.
=============================================================
measurements.ts's new early return makes m5.unqueriedAmbiguityIds always []. The first joinCampaignRules call is never conditional, so `asked` is always true, so rulingQueryExecuted is always true, so rulingQueryScope is always 'all-active', so the guard's first disjunct is unconditionally satisfied and the body below is unreachable. discoveryProbes.test.ts:220 asserts that array is empty as the closure invariant ("every ambiguity that reached the packet was offered to the seam") — that assertion can now never fail.
FIX: if all-active scope genuinely subsumes the check, say so explicitly and make the measurement state it, rather than leaving a dead computation behind a permanently-true guard and an assertion that proves nothing. Whatever you choose, the probe must once again be capable of failing when the property is violated.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 — the oracle seam ignores the new options argument, so probes assert a guarantee the double never provides.
=============================================================
test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts activeRulingsForAmbiguities ignores the second `options` parameter, while the production seam honours includeAllActive. Under the probes the trace therefore records rulingQueryScope 'all-active' and m5.allActiveRulingsRequested true while the fixture actually filtered by the requested ids. With finding 2 this means the probes record and assert a scope guarantee the double does not implement.
FIX: make the double honour includeAllActive exactly as the production seam does. This is the same class as eshyra-jhpt.2's original contract pinning: the oracle is the executable statement of the seam contract and must not drift from it.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 — the fixture-contract `continue` also skips the ruleIdentity check.
=============================================================
test/diagnostics/fixtureContract.ts:836-840 short-circuits before nonEmptyString(item.ruleIdentity, ...), not merely before the ambiguity-field checks. Every ruling case used to require a non-empty ruleIdentity; now a recurring-question ruling case may omit it, and oracleCampaignRules.ts substitutes item.caseId silently, so the omission is invisible.
FIX: hoist the ruleIdentity check above the continue.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 — revokedPosition and effectivePosition are still unvalidated against persisted chronology; only disputedPosition was fixed.
=============================================================
Round 2 finding 2 routed temporalMode.disputedPosition through assertPersistedPosition. revokeCampaignRule never validates input.revokedPosition that way, and create/supersede never validate effectivePosition that way. The only constraints are the ordering ones (>= effectivePosition, >= currentPosition). So a caller can revoke at a fabricated anchor — ordinal 999999 with invented session/turn ids — and because activeRows compares ordinal-first, the rule stays active for the realistic life of the campaign while the row claims a revocation at a turn that will never exist.
This is the same defect as round 2 finding 2, one field over. Fix the class, not the instance: every caller-supplied CampaignPosition that is persisted or compared against persisted chronology should go through the same validation. Enumerate them in your notes and say which ones you routed and why any were left out.

=============================================================
FINDING 6 — a dispute immediately after a session boundary is rejected.
=============================================================
campaignRules.ts immediatelyBefore requires disputedPosition.sessionId === currentPosition.sessionId. Ordinals are campaign-wide and unique (UNIQUE (campaign_id, ordinal)), so ordinal + 1 already identifies the preceding turn unambiguously. The consequence is that the first turn of a new session cannot dispute the last turn of the previous session — a realistic case, since a player may object to the last thing that happened when play resumes.
FIX: decide this deliberately and document the decision in the module. Default expectation: drop the sessionId requirement from immediatelyBefore, since the ordinal is already unique and authoritative, and keep sameTurn as-is. If you conclude cross-session disputes should stay forbidden, say why in the doc comment and add a test asserting the rejection is intentional rather than incidental.

=============================================================
FINDING 7 — failing closed on conflicting rulings can permanently wedge a campaign.
=============================================================
assembleCampaignRulesContext throws on multiple active rulings for one ambiguity, and it is now on the per-turn path. The single-active-ruling invariant is enforced only in application code; migration 0025 has no SQL constraint. A row arriving by any other route — checkpoint/Dolt restore, a direct write, a future importer — makes every turn throw and roll back, with no way to play or repair through the game.
The supervisor asked for fail-closed in round 1 and still wants the conflict surfaced rather than silently collapsed — but aborting every turn forever is too blunt.
FIX: surface the conflict in the projection so the DM context shows that the ambiguity has contradictory active rulings and that none is authoritative, instead of throwing. Keep a hard rejection at the ADMISSION boundary (assertNoOverlappingAmbiguityRuling), which is where it belongs. Test that a campaign holding a conflicting pair (inserted directly, as a restore would) is still playable and that the conflict is visible in the context.

=============================================================
FINDING 8 — a duplicate ambiguity id across records silently last-wins.
=============================================================
campaignContext.ts ambiguitiesFromStack does found.set(ambiguity.id, ambiguity), so when two different record keys in the resolved stack declare the same ambiguity id, the later silently replaces the earlier. optRulesAmbiguities only enforces id uniqueness WITHIN one record. Iteration is recordsByKey insertion order (base then add-ons), so an add-on overrides a base ambiguity by accident rather than by any stated precedence rule, changing the interpretations the DM is shown with no error and no trace.
FIX: either reject the collision loudly with both record keys in the message, or define and document an explicit precedence. Do not leave it to insertion order. Test the collision.

=============================================================
FINDING 9 (test integrity) — a committed regression test passes for the wrong reason and cannot fail.
=============================================================
test 'rejects a disputed anchor that disagrees with persisted chronology' (campaignRuleStore.test.ts:906) passes sessionId 'aaa-turn'/'zzz-turn' and turnId 'turn-1'/'turn-2' to resolveCampaignPosition — the session ids differ, so checkTemporalMode rejects on the SESSION mismatch and the anchor validation is never reached. The supervisor's negative proof observed 6 failures against 97b2ff0 where the report claimed 7; this is the missing one.
The FIX for that finding is genuinely present and correct — a correctly shaped test (same sessionId, differing turnIds, fabricated anchor) throws 'temporalMode.disputedPosition does not match the persisted campaign turn position' on this head and FAILS on 97b2ff0. Only the test is wrong.
Second confirmed instance: 'rejects direct creation of a revoked rule before its effective position' (campaignRuleStore.test.ts:978) omits currentPosition, so it trips 'currentPosition is required for live campaign rule creation' and has never exercised the guard in its name — it would still pass if that guard were deleted.
FIX: reshape both so they exercise the guard they name, and re-verify each fails against 4f3dcfb for the RIGHT reason.

=============================================================
FINDING 10 (test integrity, systemic — this is why the above was invisible) — negative tests assert only the error class.
=============================================================
All 28 negative assertions in campaignRuleStore.test.ts use bare toThrow(CampaignRuleError) with no message matching. The store now has roughly a dozen guards that fire in a fixed order, and earlier guards preempt later ones, so a test can pass on a guard other than the one it targets — which is exactly findings 9's two instances. Supervisor captured the messages; they are distinct and specific:
    backdated prospective create : prospective campaign rule cannot take effect before the current position
    stale currentPosition        : currentPosition does not match the persisted current campaign position
    duplicate identity           : campaign rule 'base' already exists
    revoke before effective      : campaign rule 'base' cannot be revoked before the current position
    supersede w/ backdated succ  : successor 's' cannot take effect before the current position
    cross-campaign supersede     : supersession cannot cross campaigns
FIX: every negative test in the campaign-rule suites must assert WHICH guard fired — toThrow(/distinctive message/) or an equivalent message assertion — not merely the error class. While doing so, check each test still trips its intended guard; report any further tests that were passing on the wrong one. This is the highest-value item here: it is what makes the rest of the suite mean what it says.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against 4f3dcfb; report the counts you actually observed, and for findings 9-10 confirm each reshaped test fails for the RIGHT reason (quote the message).
  - Do not weaken existing tests or assertions.
  - Do not touch merged migrations, the position encoding, or the rejected relevance-selection finding (eshyra-umyb).
  - Keep every earlier fix intact.
