title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 2 findings on PR #524 head 97b2ff0
description:
Supervisor self-review round 2 of PR #524 head 97b2ff0. Round 1's eight findings are all confirmed fixed (8 of 60 tests fail against 7199f7a; full verification 276 files / 4868 tests). Round-2 probes of the new position-authority surfaces found no holes — the ordinal-0 bootstrap closes once real chronology exists, and stale AND future currentPosition assertions are both rejected.

SEVEN new findings. Four of them (1, 2, 3, 6) are consequences of round 1's own fixes, which is why this loop exists. All are accepted; none was rejected this round.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev5 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev5, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 97b2ff0. Run `npm ci` before verification.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — a disputed turn cannot be corrected by SUPERSESSION, only by adding a competing rule.
=============================================================
campaignRuleStore.ts supersedeCampaignRule rejects any successor whose effectivePosition precedes currentPosition, unconditionally. But checkTemporalMode explicitly PERMITS a disputed-turn position at the immediately preceding turn, and createCampaignRule accepts exactly that. So the one operation a disputed turn most needs — replacing the rule that produced the bad adjudication — is the one that is forbidden.
REPRODUCED at 97b2ff0 (supervisor): r1 prospective at turn 1, advance to turn 2, supersede r1 with a disputed-turn successor anchored at turn 1 ->
    "successor 'r2' cannot take effect before the current position"
Consequence: the correction can only be authored as a NEW rule, the prior rule stays active, and both apply at the disputed turn — which is precisely the contradictory-active-rules state this branch has been closing elsewhere. eshyra-jhpt.8 depends on this path.
FIX: the guard must carry the same temporalMode condition checkTemporalMode uses — only a PROSPECTIVE successor must be at or after the current position; a disputed-turn successor is bounded by the disputed-turn rules instead. Test that a disputed-turn supersession at the immediately preceding turn succeeds, that the prior rule stops being active at the disputed position, and that an OLDER disputed target is still rejected.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking) — the disputed-turn anchor is never validated against persisted chronology.
=============================================================
Round 1 made currentPosition authoritative by checking it against campaign_turn_position (assertCurrentPosition). disputedPosition got no such treatment. checkTemporalMode's immediatelyBefore accepts on sessionId + ordinal + 1 alone, so the turnId is unchecked.
REPRODUCED at 97b2ff0 (supervisor): real turn 1 is 'aaa-turn'; current turn 2 is 'zzz-turn'. A caller reusing the CURRENT turn id with the PREVIOUS ordinal — an easy and realistic mistake — creates { s1, 'zzz-turn', ordinal 1 }, which is ACCEPTED. Then:
    active at the REAL disputed turn: []      <- the correction is not there
The rule exists, is active, and is silently never in force at the turn it was created to correct. Whether it appears at all depends on lexicographic comparison of two turn ids.
FIX: validate disputedPosition against the persisted campaign_turn_position row for that ordinal, the same way assertCurrentPosition validates currentPosition. The store already has getCurrentCampaignPosition and the table; add the lookup it needs rather than trusting the caller. Keep the domain-level checkTemporalMode as-is for pure-domain use, but the STORE must not admit a fabricated anchor.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 (blocking) — the comparator comment I asked for in round 1 asserts something false, and the divergence is reachable.
=============================================================
campaignRules.ts:312 and campaignRuleStore.ts:490 now justify SQL BINARY comparison with "Equal ordinals cannot be persisted for one campaign". That uniqueness constraint exists only on campaign_turn_position. campaign_rule.effective_position and revoked_position are caller-supplied and unconstrained, so equal-ordinal/different-anchor rows ARE reachable — finding 2 is one route to them.
On such a tie, SQL compares the percent-ENCODED sessionId~turnId while compareCampaignPositions compares the DECODED values, and they disagree whenever encodeURIComponent escapes a character ('a b' -> 'a%20b' sorts after 'a!b' encoded, before it decoded). assertNoOverlappingAmbiguityRuling / intervalsOverlap and the active-at-position query can then reach opposite conclusions about the same pair.
FIX: a comment is no longer sufficient — round 1 tried that and the comment is wrong. Make the two orderings genuinely one. Either compare the canonical encoded form on both sides, or stop relying on BINARY SQL ordering where a tie is possible. Then correct or delete the false justification at both sites. Test an equal-ordinal pair whose encoded and decoded orders differ, and assert the SQL predicate and the JS comparator agree.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 — overlap check runs before the duplicate-identity check, so a duplicate reports a nonexistent conflict.
=============================================================
campaignRuleStore.ts writeRule runs assertNoOverlappingAmbiguityRuling before the existence check, so re-creating an existing ambiguity ruling compares the row against ITSELF: "active ambiguity ruling 'r1' overlaps 'r1' for ambiguity 'ambiguity:x'" instead of "campaign rule 'r1' already exists". A caller — or a tool retry path — will hunt a conflicting ruling that does not exist.
FIX: move the existence check above the overlap check. Test that a duplicate create reports the duplicate, not an overlap.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 — a player-approved ruling silently vanishes from DM context if its ambiguity leaves the bound pack.
=============================================================
campaignContext.ts excludes ambiguity rulings from `rules` and re-attaches them only by matching ambiguities present in the currently bound rules stack. If the campaign rebinds to a pack revision where that ambiguity id no longer exists, the still-active, player-approved ruling is fetched by nothing and rendered nowhere — no trace, no loss record — while listCampaignRules still reports it active.
This is the silent-disappearance class the epic exists to prevent; the DM would adjudicate as if the table had never ruled.
FIX: an active ruling whose ambiguity is not in the bound stack must not vanish silently. Surface it (with its provenance, noting the ambiguity is absent from the current pack) or record an explicit loss the caller can see. Decide which and say why. Test it by binding a stack without the ambiguity and asserting the ruling is still accounted for.

=============================================================
FINDING 6 — round 1's finding-7 fix made the trace under-report the query that ran.
=============================================================
campaignRuleSeam.ts passes includeAllActive: options.rulingsOnly !== true, so the first join's ambiguityIds argument is now dead — the seam returns every active ambiguity ruling regardless of what was asked. But the trace still reports requestedAmbiguityIds as the candidate-derived list, directly contradicting the comment twenty lines above it: "Request evidence is derived from the calls that ACTUALLY executed, never from what this stage could have asked."
Concretely, measurements.ts m5.returned can contain ruling identities for ambiguities absent from m5.requestedAmbiguityIds, and m5.unqueriedAmbiguityIds is computed from that under-reported offered set, so the trace no longer describes the query that ran. That trace is transition-measurement evidence (M5), so its truthfulness is load-bearing.
FIX: make the trace describe the call that actually executed. If the first join asks for all active rulings, say so in the request evidence rather than reporting a candidate-derived list it did not use. Keep the comment's rule true.

=============================================================
FINDING 7 — the new prompt section is not registered, so structural debug logging misattributes it.
=============================================================
renderContextMessage now emits a "## Campaign Rules" heading, but debug/sessionDebug.ts KNOWN_PROMPT_SECTION_LABELS was not updated, and its docstring states it is "The fixed set of `## ` headings emitted by ... renderContextMessage". sanitizePromptSectionName therefore collapses this code-owned heading into the "## (content)" placeholder reserved for UNTRUSTED prompt-derived text — so the debug log reports a code-emitted section as unrecognized.
FIX: register "## Campaign Rules". The sweep also found "## Character Chronicle" and "## Adventure Module (DM-only)" already missing for the same reason; fix all three together and note it, since it is one defect with three instances.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against 97b2ff0; report the counts you actually observed.
  - Do not weaken existing tests or assertions.
  - Do not touch the merged migrations, the position encoding format, or the rejected relevance-selection finding (eshyra-umyb).
  - Keep every round-1 fix intact: persisted-chronology currentPosition authority, single validation channel, sameTurn ordinal equality, CampaignRuleError on duplicate, ambiguity payload validation, single ruling placement.

VERIFICATION
`npm ci` first, then `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local @eshyra/core resolution.

title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review findings on PR #524 head 7199f7a
description:
Supervisor's OWN fresh review of head 7199f7a (PR #524), run per the standing instruction to self-review after clearing a reviewer's findings and loop until clean. Review #5097921608's single blocker is CONFIRMED FIXED: currentPosition is a required field on all three mutation APIs, checkTemporalMode rejects a prospective rule effective before the current position, and the bounded disputed-turn exception still works for the current and immediately preceding turn (verified by supervisor; the 6 new regressions fail against 7c8eafe).

TWO NEW BLOCKING DEFECTS, both reproduced by the supervisor at 7199f7a.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev4 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev4, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt at 7199f7a. Run `npm ci` first if node_modules is missing; verify:worktree now enforces worktree-local resolution.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — currentPosition is caller-asserted and never checked against real campaign chronology, so the history rewrite the last review demanded be fixed is still reachable.
Owner: eshyra-jhpt.2 (mutation boundary), with eshyra-jhpt.3 owning the chronology source.
=============================================================
Making currentPosition a required ARGUMENT closed the "omitted authority" hole but not the "false authority" one. The store never consults campaign_turn_position, which is the campaign's real canonical chronology and lives in the same database. A caller that asserts a stale position backdates exactly as before.

REPRODUCED at 7199f7a — the campaign genuinely advanced to ordinal 10 through ten real resolveCampaignPosition calls, then:
    claimed currentPosition: 2  (real: 10)
    historical active-at-position(P5) now reports: [ 'backdated-via-stale-authority' ]   <- history rewritten again
This is the same defect the previous review blocked on, one level down: the parameter is now mandatory but unverified.

FIX: make the campaign's current canonical position authoritative from persisted state rather than from the caller.
  - Add a read-only accessor alongside resolveCampaignPosition (campaign/campaignPosition.ts) that returns the campaign's current canonical position without allocating one — the MAX-ordinal row for that campaign. resolveCampaignPosition must stay as-is; it ASSIGNS, and moving it would break the turn lifecycle and .8's replay reuse.
  - Then either (a) drop the currentPosition parameter from the three mutation APIs and resolve it internally, or (b) keep the parameter and reject it when it disagrees with the persisted current position. (a) is simpler and cannot be bypassed; (b) keeps callers explicit. Choose one, state why, and make the other impossible rather than merely discouraged.
  - Define and test the behaviour for a campaign with NO turn positions yet (a brand-new campaign creating its first rule). Do not let that case silently permit arbitrary backdating.
EVIDENCE: advance real chronology to ordinal 10 via resolveCampaignPosition, then prove a mutation asserting an earlier current position is rejected (or ignored in favour of the persisted value) for create, revoke and supersede, and that historical active-at-position results are unchanged. Must fail against 7199f7a.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking) — two channels carry current-position authority and they contradict each other; supplying both rejects a legitimate supersession.
Owner: eshyra-jhpt.1 / eshyra-jhpt.2.
=============================================================
SupersedeCampaignRuleInput now has BOTH `currentPosition` (required) and `validation.currentPosition` (optional, pre-existing). supersedeCampaignRule deliberately validates the historical prior rule with `input.validation` alone — correct, because the prior is legitimately older than the current position — but a caller that also sets validation.currentPosition causes that same prior to be validated against it and rejected.

REPRODUCED at 7199f7a, stating the same truth through both channels:
    supersede old(P1) -> new(P10), currentPosition: P10, validation: { currentPosition: P10 }
    -> "prospective campaign rule cannot take effect before the current position"
A correct, non-adversarial call fails. The prior rule is historical by definition; validating it against "now" is never right.

FIX: one authority for current position. Preferred: remove currentPosition from CampaignRuleValidationOptions entirely (or stop threading caller-supplied validation into the prior-rule check) so the historical prior can never be evaluated against the current position, and the mutation APIs' own current-position field is the single source. If CampaignRuleValidationOptions.currentPosition must stay for the disputed-turn path, make it structurally impossible for it to reach the prior-rule validation, and document which check owns which rule.
EVIDENCE: a test that supersedes an old prospective rule while supplying current-position authority through every channel the API exposes, and succeeds. Plus the existing disputed-turn coverage must keep passing.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against 7199f7a; report observed counts, do not infer them.
  - Do not weaken existing tests. Updating call sites for a changed signature is expected; relaxing an assertion is not.
  - Do not touch the four fixes from review #5097622281, the position encoding, the seam contract, merged migrations, or the active-at-position predicate.
  - Keep the bounded disputed-turn exception working for the current and immediately preceding turn.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm @eshyra/core resolves into this worktree.

=============================================================
ADDITIONAL FINDINGS from a supplementary /code-review sweep of the branch (supervisor triaged each; these six are accepted, one was rejected).
=============================================================

FINDING 3 (blocking) — checkTemporalMode's `sameTurn` ignores ordinal, so a disputed-turn rule can be backdated arbitrarily far.
campaignRules.ts checkTemporalMode accepts a disputed-turn rule when disputedPosition.sessionId/turnId equal currentPosition's, WITHOUT comparing ordinals — while the sibling `immediatelyBefore` branch does compare them. Ordinal is the documented authoritative chronology field.
Reproduced by the sweep: currentPosition { s1, 't-current', ordinal 100 } with effectivePosition = disputedPosition = { s1, 't-current', ordinal 3 } is ACCEPTED, and listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition at ordinal 50 returns the rule — a house rule silently backdated across 97 resolved positions, exactly what revoke/supersede now refuse.
FIX: require disputedPosition.ordinal === currentPosition.ordinal in the sameTurn branch. Note this interacts with FINDING 1: a legitimately resolved (session, turn) pair has exactly one ordinal because campaign_turn_position is keyed (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id), so this only becomes reachable through a caller-fabricated position — which is precisely what FINDING 1 is about. Fix both; neither alone is sufficient.

FINDING 4 — createCampaignRule leaks a raw SqliteError on duplicate identity.
campaignRuleStore.ts createCampaignRule has no duplicate-identity guard and relies on PRIMARY KEY (campaign_id, rule_identity). Creating the same identity twice throws SqliteError "UNIQUE constraint failed", and `e instanceof CampaignRuleError` is false — while supersedeCampaignRule explicitly guards the analogous case with "campaign rule 'X' already exists". A caller catching CampaignRuleError to turn a bad player request into a message instead gets an unhandled DB error naming SQL columns.
FIX: guard it like supersede does, throwing CampaignRuleError. Test it.

FINDING 5 — unvalidated pack JSON is cast to RulesAmbiguity and dereferenced at render time.
campaignContext.ts ambiguitiesFromStack accepts any object with a string `id` (`value as RulesAmbiguity`) and checks nothing else; contextAssembler.ts renderContextMessage then reads ambiguity.question and calls ambiguity.interpretations.map(...). Supervisor confirmed this is REACHABLE, not merely defensive: pack-load validation of mechanics.ambiguities via optRulesAmbiguities is applied per record KIND, and the kind schemas do not cover all 15 RULES_RECORD_KINDS, while the pack-level assertAmbiguityIdentityAndProvenance only touches `id` and `source`. So an ambiguity with a valid id and source but a missing or non-array `interpretations`, on a kind whose schema omits mechanics validation, passes pack load and then throws TypeError inside prompt rendering — failing EVERY turn for that campaign, far from the cause. A third-party/add-on pack supplied through CampaignRulesPackResolver is the realistic vector.
FIX: validate the ambiguity shape in ambiguitiesFromStack and either drop the entry or fail loudly there, with the record key in the message. Do not fix this at render time.

FINDING 6 — an active ambiguity ruling is rendered twice, with two different framings.
The discovery seam excludes ambiguity rulings from activeRulesAtPosition (!isAmbiguityRuling), but assembleCampaignRulesContext builds `rules` from listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition, which does not. The DM prompt therefore shows the same decision once in the rules list as "- [ruling] <id> (ambiguity:X#int-1; ...): <prose>" and again under its ambiguity as "Active ruling <id> (int-1): <prose>".
FIX: make the two consumers agree. The ambiguity subsection is the meaningful placement (it pairs the ruling with the source material it resolves, which is the point of amendment A1), so prefer excluding ambiguity rulings from the flat rules list. Assert the rendered output contains each ruling exactly once.

FINDING 7 — an ambiguity ruling cannot surface its own governing record, contradicting the seam's documented contract.
Because activeRulesAtPosition excludes ambiguity rulings, the only route to joinCampaignRules is activeRulingsForAmbiguities(ambiguityIds), and those ids are derived solely from ambiguities already present on candidate records. A ruling with governingRecordKeys ['spell:fireball'] resolving an ambiguity that spell:fireball does not itself carry is never returned, never placed, and never surfaces its governing record — while campaignRuleSeam.ts's own comment states "A governing record that resolves in the active stack therefore ENTERS as a candidate here." No unplaced-rule loss is recorded either, because the projection is never returned at all.
FIX: close the gap so an active ambiguity ruling reaches the join regardless of whether its ambiguity was already discovered, without reintroducing double-processing (the seam concatenates [...rules, ...rulings], so the same identity must not arrive twice) and without breaking FINDING 6's single-placement rule. If you conclude the correct answer is that the loss must at least be RECORDED rather than the ruling surfaced, argue it in your notes — but silence is not acceptable either way.

FINDING 8 (hardening, latent) — two different orderings are defined over the same value.
activeRows compares effective_position as SQLite BINARY text; compareCampaignPositions compares the DECODED sessionId/turnId. encodeURIComponent reorders: raw 'a b' < 'a!c' (0x20 < 0x21) but encoded 'a%20b' > 'a!c' (0x25 > 0x21). The zero-padded ordinal prefix masks this for any pair produced by resolveCampaignPosition, and UNIQUE (campaign_id, ordinal) makes equal-ordinal pairs impossible, so it is not reachable today — but these are the SQL predicate and the JS admission check for the same fact.
FIX: pin it. A shared canonical comparison is best; a comment at both sites naming the invariant that keeps them agreeing is the minimum. Do not restructure the encoding.

REJECTED FINDING (do not act on it): the sweep also flagged that every active rule and every stack ambiguity is injected into every turn. That is the deliberate contract of eshyra-jhpt.3 ("correctness takes priority over selective retrieval"; prompt retrieval optimization is an explicit non-goal), and the supervisor measured the per-turn scan at ~0.13 ms over 1812 records. It is recorded as eshyra-umyb for when pack curation or campaign age makes it material. Do not add relevance selection or truncation here.

title: Dispatch: Enforce prospective lifecycle admission against current campaign position (PR #524 review 3)
description:
Dispatch for PR #524 review #5097921608 (exact head 7c8eafe, semantic-system profile). The four defects from the previous review are CONFIRMED FIXED at this head. ONE blocking defect remains, independently reproduced by the supervisor before dispatch.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev3 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev3, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt at 7c8eafe (the reviewed head). npm ci has been run; @eshyra/core resolves into the worktree. verify:worktree now enforces this (PR #525). Work only inside that worktree.

=============================================================
DEFECT — ordinary lifecycle mutations can be backdated and rewrite canonical history
Owner: eshyra-jhpt.1 (temporal invariant) + eshyra-jhpt.2 (mutation boundary). Both are reopened.
=============================================================
eshyra-jhpt.1 permits exactly two temporal modes and excludes arbitrary historical retroactivity; .2 says ordinary rules apply prospectively with the disputed turn as the bounded exception. Neither is enforced against the campaign's CURRENT position.

campaignRules.ts checkTemporalMode returns immediately when mode === 'prospective', so currentPosition is never compared against a prospective rule's effectivePosition. The store then has no current-position authority of its own: revokeCampaignRule takes none at all, and create/supersede only compare a position against the rule's OWN effective position.

REPRODUCED at 7c8eafe (campaign current position P10 throughout):
  A. createCampaignRule effective P1 with validation.currentPosition = P10 -> ACCEPTED;
     historical active-at-position(P5) then reports [ 'backdated' ].
  B. revokeCampaignRule with revokedPosition P5 (no current-position input exists):
     active at P7 before: [ 'live' ]   after: [ ]                 <- history rewritten
  C. supersedeCampaignRule with a successor effective P5 and validation.currentPosition = P10:
     active at P7 before: [ 'old' ]    after: [ 'new' ]           <- historical set rewritten
  D. currentPosition can simply be OMITTED on create; nothing requires it.

TWO FACTS THAT SHAPE THE CORRECT FIX — verify them yourself, then use them:
  1. There are NO production callers of createCampaignRule / revokeCampaignRule / supersedeCampaignRule yet. Grep shows only the re-exports in src/internal.ts; eshyra-jhpt.5 will be the first real consumer. Making current-position authority REQUIRED is therefore a cheap breaking change that costs only test updates. Do it now rather than after .5 exists.
  2. The justification recorded on eshyra-jhpt.2.4 for allowing direct creation of non-active (superseded/revoked) rows was "so checkpoint/restore can rehydrate history". That justification does not hold: checkpoint restore does NOT use these APIs — persistence/checkpoint/store.ts materializes rows with raw `INSERT INTO` from the serialized snapshot. So the live mutation boundary can be made strict without breaking restore. Confirm this before relying on it.

REQUIRED PROPERTIES
  - The live mutation boundary must FAIL CLOSED without current-position authority. A caller must not be able to bypass the invariant by leaving currentPosition undefined. Preferred shape: make the current campaign position a REQUIRED argument of createCampaignRule, revokeCampaignRule and supersedeCampaignRule. An acceptable alternative is for the store to resolve the campaign's current canonical position itself from campaign_turn_position (which cannot be spoofed by a caller) — if you choose that, define and test the behaviour for a campaign with no turns yet. State which you chose and why.
  - Prospective creation must be rejected when effectivePosition precedes the current canonical position. Decide and document whether "at the current position" is permitted or only strictly after it; either is defensible, be explicit and test the boundary case.
  - Revocation must be rejected when revokedPosition precedes the current canonical position (in addition to the existing revokedPosition >= effectivePosition rule).
  - Supersession must be rejected when the successor's effectivePosition precedes the current canonical position (in addition to the existing successor >= prior rule).
  - The disputed-turn mode must KEEP working for the current or immediately preceding turn. Do not fix prospectivity by deleting the bounded retroactive exception — that mode is the whole point of eshyra-jhpt.8.
  - If a historical-row path is still wanted, make it a DISTINCT, explicitly named entry point that a caller cannot reach by accident, and say in your notes who is expected to use it. Given fact 2, consider whether it should exist at all.

REQUIRED PERMANENT EVIDENCE (the review names these; each must establish a LATER current position, which the existing tests never do)
  1. At current position P10, ordinary prospective creation backdated to P9 or earlier is rejected at the live storage boundary, the row set is unchanged, and historical active-at-position results are unchanged. Current/future prospective timing still works.
  2. A revocation backdated before the current canonical position is rejected, and the rule remains active in every historical slice the rejected mutation tried to change.
  3. A prospective supersession backdated before the current canonical position is rejected, preserving the prior rule, the supersession chain, and both historical and current active sets.
  4. The disputed-turn exception remains valid for the current and immediately preceding turn, and still rejects an older turn.
  5. Omitting current-position authority fails closed — prove the API cannot be called without it (a compile-time required argument counts, but add a runtime test for the resolved-from-DB case if you choose that design).
Note the existing tests named "applies supersession and revocation prospectively" and "rejects non-prospective lifecycle changes" only compare a transition against the rule's own effective position. They do not establish a later current position and so do not prove prospectivity in the contract sense. Strengthen them rather than leaving two tests whose names overstate what they check.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF: confirm each new regression fails against 7c8eafe (check the relevant source files out from that commit, observe failures, restore your fix). Report the counts you actually observed; do not infer them.
  - Do not weaken existing tests or assertions to accommodate the change. Updating test call sites for a newly required argument is expected and is not a weakening; silently relaxing an assertion is.
  - Do not change the active-at-position SQL predicate, the position encoding, merged migrations, the seam contract, or the four fixes from the previous review.

title: Dispatch: Fix four PR #524 fresh-review defects (position chronology, seam position authority, recurring-question rulings, ruling multiplicity)
description:
Dispatch for PR #524 fresh-full-review findings (GitHub review #5097622281, exact head 0479116, semantic-system profile). FOUR blocking defects spanning eshyra-jhpt.1, .2 and .3, plus closing eshyra-neus. All four were independently reproduced by the supervisor at 0479116; probe output is quoted so you can write tests that fail today. Fix all four on ONE head — the reviewer requires a fresh full review after any material repair, so batching gives one review cycle instead of four.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev2 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev2, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt at 0479116 (the reviewed head). npm ci has already been run there and @eshyra/core resolves into the worktree; AGENTS.md now REQUIRES this and verify:worktree enforces it. Work only inside that worktree.

=============================================================
DEFECT 1 (owner eshyra-jhpt.3, breaks eshyra-jhpt.8's contract)
Abandoned turns permanently consume campaign chronology.
=============================================================
runTurn calls resolveCampaignPosition BEFORE `SAVEPOINT eshyra_turn`, and resolveCampaignPosition commits its own transaction. A terminal turn failure rolls back only to that savepoint, so the abandoned attempt KEEPS its ordinal. The real CLI producer (packages/cli/src/playTurnLoop.ts) then reports the failure and calls `deps.nextId('turn')` again for the next input, so the next canonical turn gets a LATER ordinal with a dead attempt wedged between two canonical turns.
campaignRules.ts checkTemporalMode defines immediacy as `disputedPosition.ordinal + 1 === currentPosition.ordinal`, so a single provider/model/audit failure makes the genuinely previous adjudication ineligible for disputed-turn timing.

REPRODUCED at 0479116:
    canonical A=1  abandoned=2  next canonical C=3
    disputed-turn rule targeting A while current is C -> "disputed-turn mode may target only the current or immediately preceding turn"

REQUIRED PROPERTIES (the design choice is yours; state your reasoning in your notes):
  - An abandoned/failed attempt must not affect canonical turn adjacency.
  - A deliberate replay of a disputed turn must still reuse that turn's existing position (this is why resolveCampaignPosition sits before the savepoint — do not move it without preserving that).
  - eshyra-jhpt.8 says abandoned adjudication MAY remain diagnostic/provenance history but must not be continuing campaign canon, so deleting the evidence is acceptable only if you can still satisfy that; marking the row non-canonical and computing adjacency over canonical rows only is the more faithful reading.
  - If adjacency must be computed against persisted state rather than raw ordinal arithmetic, changing the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain contract is IN SCOPE here (that bead is reopened for this) — e.g. resolving the previous canonical position and passing it in, instead of comparing ordinals directly. Keep the two temporal modes as they are.
EVIDENCE: an integration regression through the REAL runTurn / turn-id lifecycle — a successful canonical turn, then a forced terminal failure, then the next successful turn — proving canonical adjacency survives, plus proof that an intended replay reuses the existing position rather than allocating a new one. Exercise the persistence table and the actually returned positions, not checkTemporalMode in isolation.

=============================================================
DEFECT 2 (owner eshyra-jhpt.2)
The DB-backed read seam can mix two campaign positions in one run.
=============================================================
createCampaignRuleReadSeam binds canonicalPosition and documents "binds a required campaign position so every query is replay-accurate", but activeRulesAtPosition honours a per-call `query.campaignPosition` override while activeRulingsForAmbiguities always uses the bound one. discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts joinCampaignRules DOES pass options.campaignPosition, so this is reachable, not a theoretical type state.

REPRODUCED at 0479116 (seam bound at P10):
    house rules with no override : [ 'house-early', 'house-late' ]
    same seam, override P5       : [ 'house-early' ]        <- different position
    activeRulingsForAmbiguities always uses the BOUND P10
This is the same temporal-divergence class already fixed once between house rules and rulings in the SQL predicate, now re-entering through the seam.

FIX: make campaign position single-authority across both methods. Either reject a per-call position that differs from the bound one with CampaignRuleError, or resolve one explicit position that both methods use. Do not leave a silent substitution.
EVIDENCE: construct a DB seam at one position, query it with another, and prove the contract either rejects the mismatch or returns the same historical slice from both methods.

=============================================================
DEFECT 3 (closes eshyra-neus; producer contract owned by .1/.2)
Recurring-question rulings fall through the discovery boundary entirely.
=============================================================
eshyra-jhpt.1 defines a ruling as EITHER a source-ambiguity resolution OR a stable recurring interpretation question. At the seam, a recurring-question ruling is returned by NEITHER method: activeRulesAtPosition filters to `ruleKind === 'house-rule'`, and activeRulingsForAmbiguities filters to ambiguity provenance.

REPRODUCED at 0479116 with one active recurring-question ruling:
    activeRulesAtPosition      : []   (house-rules only)
    activeRulingsForAmbiguities: []   (ambiguity-provenance only)
The complementary half is the open eshyra-neus defect: discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts withRule casts EVERY ruleKind==='ruling' projection to CampaignRulingProjection, which is unsound for a recurring-question ruling that legitimately has no ambiguityId/selectedInterpretationId.

FIX both halves in this PR; the reviewer is explicit that a known fix-worthy defect is fixed in the current PR rather than deferred.
  - Producer: a recurring-question ruling must be returned by the seam. It cannot come from activeRulingsForAmbiguities (it has no ambiguity id), so activeRulesAtPosition is the correct carrier — i.e. that method returns active rules that are not ambiguity-linked rulings, rather than house rules only. Note the in-repo oracle fixture packages/core/test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts pins the current house-rules-only shape because its cases only ever contain house rules and ambiguity rulings; update it in step with the real contract and say in your notes how you kept them consistent.
  - Consumer: withRule must classify by PROVENANCE, not by ruleKind alone — only an ambiguity-provenance projection may be treated as a CampaignRulingProjection. Do not fabricate ambiguityId/selectedInterpretationId to satisfy the type (a previous attempt did exactly that and it was rejected), and do not loosen CampaignRulingProjection.
EVIDENCE: persist a real recurring-question ruling, read it through the DB-backed seam, run it through joinCampaignRules, and assert it is retained in a semantically valid shape with no fabricated ambiguity fields. The test must fail against 0479116. Then close eshyra-neus with a reason referencing this work.

=============================================================
DEFECT 4 (owner .1/.2 for the invariant, .3 must fail closed)
Two contradictory active rulings for one ambiguity are accepted, then silently collapsed.
=============================================================
Migration 0025 has no uniqueness constraint, createCampaignRule performs no sibling-active check, and listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition can return several. assembleCampaignRulesContext then does rulingByAmbiguity.set(...) per row, so the last one silently wins the "Active ruling" slot — while `rules` still carries BOTH, so the rendered Campaign Rules section can show two contradictory rulings for the same ambiguity.

REPRODUCED at 0479116 (two active rulings on ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition selecting mixed-within-total and homogeneous-alternative):
    ambiguity section shows exactly one "Active ruling": ruling-two
    but rules[] carries both: [ 'ruling-one', 'ruling-two' ]

FIX: close the multiplicity semantics. At most one ACTIVE ambiguity-provenance ruling per (campaignId, ambiguityId) at any position — enforce it in the store on create (and on any path that can produce an overlapping active interval), with CampaignRuleError. A partial unique index cannot express overlapping intervals on its own, so the admission check is the primary guard; add a DB constraint only if it genuinely helps. Separately, eshyra-jhpt.3 must FAIL CLOSED rather than silently collapsing if conflicting state ever reaches projection — do not let Map.set pick a winner.
If you believe scoped multiplicity is intentionally desirable, do not just allow it: represent it explicitly in the domain and make .3 preserve it, and justify that in your notes. Default expectation is the single-active-ruling invariant.
EVIDENCE: attempt two overlapping active rulings for one ambiguity and prove persistence rejects it; plus a historical supersession case proving the old ruling is still the active one before the successor's effective position and exactly one is active after it.

=============================================================
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
=============================================================
- NEGATIVE PROOF, per defect: confirm each new regression test fails against 0479116 (check out the relevant file(s) from that commit into your worktree, observe the failures, restore your fix). Report the per-defect failure counts in your notes. Do not report a count you did not observe.
- Do not weaken any existing test or assertion to accommodate a fix. If an existing expectation is genuinely wrong under the corrected contract, say so explicitly in your notes with reasoning.
- Do not change the active-at-position SQL predicate, the position encoding, the migrations already merged, or anything outside these four defects.
- Scope note: .1, .2 and .3 are all reopened for this, so the domain model, the store and the context assembler are all editable where a defect requires it. Discovery (campaignRuleSeam.ts, discovery types, the oracle fixture) is editable ONLY for defect 3.

`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Report final pass/skip counts and confirm @eshyra/core resolves into this worktree.

title: Dispatch: Fix campaign-rule lifecycle admission (PR #524 blocking review, attempt 4)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.2 (attempt 4) — blocking review defect on PR #524.

PR #524 (head 2d6b7c7) received a BLOCKING review under the semantic-system profile (GitHub review #5097504606): campaign-rule lifecycle admission can rewrite canonical history. The supervisor independently reproduced all four sub-claims before dispatching this; the probe output is quoted below so you can write tests that fail today.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.4 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.4, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt (2d6b7c7, the exact reviewed head). Work only inside that worktree.
*** Run `npm ci` in this worktree FIRST, before any verification *** — a fresh worktree has no node_modules and packages/cli tests will otherwise resolve @eshyra/core up to the parent checkout on main and report a false green (tracked as eshyra-3dmq). The supervisor has already run npm ci here, but re-run it if anything looks off, and confirm node_modules/@eshyra/core resolves INTO this worktree before trusting a result.

ROOT CAUSE
revokeCampaignRule guards `if (existing.status !== 'active') throw`, but supersedeCampaignRule has no equivalent guard on the prior rule's status. Worse, it then calls validateCampaignRules with `{ ...prior, status: 'superseded', supersededBy: input.successor.ruleIdentity }` — it OVERWRITES the prior's real status before validating, so validation structurally cannot observe that the rule was already superseded or revoked. The create path (writeRule) has matching admission holes.

REPRODUCED (supervisor probe against 2d6b7c7, all four passing i.e. all four defects present):

CLAIM 1 — re-superseding a superseded rule overwrites its original successor and corrupts history:
    old.supersededBy after second supersede: second (was "first")
    active at position 7: [ 'old', 'first' ]   <- old overlaps its own first successor
  This is the severe one. After `old` is superseded by `first` (effective 5) and then again by `second` (effective 9), the historical active-at-position query at 7 returns BOTH `old` and `first` as active, because the stored supersededBy now points at `second` and the "successor.effective_position > cutoff" predicate no longer excludes `old`. eshyra-jhpt.4 auditor parity and eshyra-jhpt.8 replay both read that query.

CLAIM 2 — a revoked rule can be converted to superseded, keeping its revocation position:
    revoked rule status after supersede: superseded | supersededBy: s
  The revocation is silently erased from the rule's status while revoked_position remains set.

CLAIM 3 — createCampaignRule accepts a revoked rule whose revocation precedes its own effective position:
    created revoked-before-effective rule: bad  (effective ordinal 10, revoked at 2)
  revokeCampaignRule enforces this ordering; the direct create path does not.

CLAIM 4 — createCampaignRule accepts a superseded rule with a dangling successor reference:
    created superseded rule pointing at: does-not-exist  (no such rule)
  validateCampaignRule (singular) checks only that supersededBy is non-null for a superseded rule; the referential check lives in validateCampaignRules (plural), which the create path never calls.

REQUIRED FIX
1. supersedeCampaignRule must reject a prior rule that is not `active`, with CampaignRuleError, BEFORE any mutation — mirroring revokeCampaignRule's existing guard. Distinct messages for already-superseded and revoked are preferable.
2. Do not let validation be fed a rewritten status. Validate the prior rule's ACTUAL admission state first; keep the existing validateCampaignRules pair call for the post-transition shape, but it must no longer be the only thing standing between a bad transition and the database.

title: verify:worktree can false-green cross-package tests when the worktree has no node_modules
description:
PROBLEM
A linked worktree created with `git worktree add` has no node_modules of its own. Node/vitest module resolution then walks UP to the parent checkout's node_modules, whose @eshyra/core and @eshyra/cli symlinks point at the PARENT checkout's packages - i.e. whatever branch the parent is on, normally main. Tests that import a sibling workspace package by name therefore exercise MAIN's build, not the worktree's.

Core tests are unaffected: packages/core/test/* import via relative '../src/...'. The exposure is packages/cli/test/*, which import from '@eshyra/core' and '@eshyra/core/internal'.

OBSERVED 2026-09-02 on eshyra-jhpt.3.3
packages/cli/test/play.test.ts passed with `campaignPosition: 'test-position'` at three assembleContext call sites, even though eshyra-jhpt.3 had made campaignPosition required and eshyra-jhpt.3.3 had added parseCampaignPosition validation that rejects exactly that value. `npm run verify:worktree` reported a clean 276 files / 4844 tests.
After `npm ci` inside the worktree (which creates node_modules/@eshyra/{core,cli} -> ../../packages/*) and a rebuild, the same file failed 2 tests with `CampaignRuleError: invalid campaign position "test-position"`.

WHY IT MATTERS
verify:worktree is the repository's pre-commit gate and the supervisor's merge gate. A false green here is not a flaky test - it silently validates the wrong code for every cross-package test, and it is invisible because the run is green.
Typecheck is NOT affected: `tsc --build` compiles from source across the workspace, so CLI/core source incompatibilities are still caught. Only runtime module resolution in vitest is wrong. That is why this can persist while the tree looks healthy.

AGENTS.md already documents `npm ci  # CI or worktree install` under Build & Test, but nothing enforces it and verify:worktree does not check for it, so a dispatched agent that goes straight to `npm run verify:worktree` gets a green run against the wrong code.

SUGGESTED FIX
Have scripts/verify-current-worktree.mjs fail fast (or install) when the active git root lacks node_modules/@eshyra symlinks resolving INTO that same git root. A cheap assertion is enough: resolve @eshyra/core from the worktree root and confirm the resolved realpath is under the worktree, not under the parent checkout. Consider the same check in the sandbox variant. Also consider stating the requirement in the Agent Worktree Workflow section rather than only under Build & Test.

SCOPE NOTE
Found while supervising eshyra-jhpt. It is not caused by that epic and affects any multi-package change verified from a worktree.

title: Dispatch: fix leftmost-open-paren semantics in stripTrailingParenthetical (attempt 3)
description:
Dispatch bead for `eshyra-e1kt` (read that bead for the spec). Attempt 3 —
blocking review finding on PR #523 at head b0ff8ddf. Attempts 1 and 2 stay
merged; this repairs one defect in `stripTrailingParenthetical`.

Branch/worktree: `eshyra-e1kt.3`, cut from branch `eshyra-e1kt` (head b0ff8dd).
Model config: gpt-5.6-luna, reasoning effort medium.

## The defect

`stripTrailingParenthetical` in
`packages/core/src/state/nameNormalization.ts` claims exact equivalence to
`text.replace(/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/, '')`. It is not equivalent. It selects the
opening parenthesis with `text.lastIndexOf('(', end - 1)` — the LATEST `(` —
but the regex is leftmost-match and `[^)]*` admits `(`, so the regex can start
at an EARLIER `(`.

Confirmed counterexamples (regex result vs current helper):

| input | `/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/` | current helper |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"(()"` | `""` | `"("` |
| `"name ((x)"` | `"name"` | `"name ("` |
| `"a ((b)"` | `"a"` | `"a ("` |
| `"x (( )"` | `"x"` | `"x ("` |
| `"  ((a)  "` | `""` | `"  ("` |

The attempt-1 spec asserted a false lemma — "leftmost-match forces the `(` to
be the last `(` in the string" — and the helper's doc comment and the PR body
both repeat it. The existing `'nested (a (b) c)'` fixture does not catch this
because that input has an interior `)` that makes BOTH candidate opens fail, so
the two implementations agree by accident.

## Correct semantics

The closing paren is pinned: `text[end-1]` must be `)` where
`end = text.trimEnd().length`, because `\s*$` cannot span a non-whitespace
character. So the match is `[q, end)` for an opening paren at `q` where
`text[q] === '('` and `(q, end-1)` contains no `)`.

Let `lastClose` be the index of the last `)` strictly before `end-1`. Then
`q` is viable exactly when `q > lastClose`: any `q < lastClose` puts that `)`
inside the span. The regex takes the leftmost viable `q` — and since a smaller
`q` also yields a smaller match start once the leading `\s*` run is absorbed,
leftmost `q` is leftmost match.

So the selection is `indexOf('(', lastClose + 1)`, NOT `lastIndexOf`:

```ts
export function stripTrailingParenthetical(text: string): string {
  const end = text.trimEnd().length;
  if (end === 0 || text[end - 1] !== ')') return text;
  const lastClose = end >= 2 ? text.lastIndexOf(')', end - 2) : -1;
  const open = text.indexOf('(', lastClose + 1);
  if (open === -1 || open >= end - 1) return text;
  return text.slice(0, open).trimEnd();
}
```

This is still linear: two bounded scans plus a slice, no backtracking. Verified
equivalent to the regex across all 22 inputs in the table below.

Rewrite the doc comment so it states the ACTUAL rule — leftmost `(` after the
last interior `)` — and drop the false "last `(` in the string" claim.

## Tests

In `packages/core/test/nameNormalization.test.ts`, extend the shared `fixtures`
list used by the differential test (the one asserting against the inline
original regexes as oracle) with at least:

`'(()'`, `'name ((x)'`, `'a ((b)'`, `'x (( )'`, `'  ((a)  '`, `'()'`, `'('`,
`'))'`, `'(()) '`, `'(('`, `'a)(b)'`

Keep every existing fixture. The differential assertion is the regression —
it must fail against the current implementation and pass against the fix.
Confirm that by running the new tests against the OLD helper once before
applying the fix, and record in your completion notes that you saw them fail.

Do not weaken or delete any existing assertion, and do not touch
`replaceParentheticals` or `trimEdgeChar` — both were checked against this
defect class and are equivalent for their inputs.

## Scope

Nothing else. No semantics change to usage counters or action economy: for
every real SRD/pack ability name — no unmatched interior `(` — the old and new
helpers already agree, so counter keys and display names are unaffected. This
repairs the equivalence claim the bead requires, not observed behavior.

## Verification

From the worktree root: `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing (it
rewrites files). All non-skipped tests must pass; documented skips are the
live-API integration tests and the Dolt-gated checkpoint tests.

Dispatched 2026-09-02: pgid 544068, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-e1kt.3, branch eshyra-e1kt.3 (cut from eshyra-e1kt @ b0ff8dd), model gpt-5.6-luna effort medium, log .worktrees/.dispatch/eshyra-e1kt.3.log
Completed on branch eshyra-e1kt.3 in commit ae98e4e. Repaired stripTrailingParenthetical to choose indexOf('(', lastClose + 1), matching the leftmost viable opening parenthesis after the last interior ')'; updated the doc comment to state the actual rule. Added all requested differential fixtures while preserving existing assertions. Confirmed the new differential test failed against the old helper ('(()' expected '' but returned '('), then passed after the fix. Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed (273 test files passed, 4 skipped; 4827 tests passed, 19 skipped). No discovered follow-ups.
