title: Make finding-registry violation predicates executable defect checks
description:
Decomposed out of eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 (PR #476) 2026-07-26 under the churn stop
rule. Review of f75acb2 found this as a NEW DEFECT CLASS.

DEFECT: the violation queryId merely SELECTS a row, after which every finding
runs the same baseline-existence join. Wrong field values, missing branches,
incorrect resets and lifecycle errors are never evaluated, and
`expectedAfterRepair` is unused entirely. So a "violation query" proves only
that the row's baseline members still exist — which is not a defect check.

CONSEQUENCE: the registry cannot detect recurrence. A repaired defect that
regresses in a different form leaves the baseline intact and the query green.
That defeats the zero-repeat certification at eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4, which is the
registry's whole purpose.

SCOPE: give each finding an executable predicate that evaluates the ACTUAL
defect condition against the committed pack — wrong value, missing branch,
absent alternative, incorrect reset, broken lifecycle, unsupported provenance —
and make `expectedAfterRepair` operative: 'empty' rows must go empty when
repaired and fail if they do not; 'stable' rows must keep their membership.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE: deriving membership for prose-scoped rows (that is
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7) and capability target identity (the sibling bead created
alongside this one).

DEPENDENCY NOTE: clause-level predicates likely need the clause IR from
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1, which is itself under design reopening. Record any row whose
predicate cannot be written yet rather than writing a shape-only stand-in.
acceptance_criteria:
• Every finding row carries a predicate that evaluates its actual defect condition, not a baseline-existence join.
• expectedAfterRepair is operative and tested in both directions.
• A repaired-then-regressed defect in a different form is detected by its predicate.
• Rows whose predicate cannot yet be written are explicitly recorded and block closure rather than carrying a shape-only stand-in.

title: Dispatch: separate obligation/evidence namespaces, ground relevance and absence (attempt 6)
description:
Fresh full review of PR #477 at 71d4eed: three P1, one P2, one P3. The reviewer
states NO new defect class was found — these are incomplete resolutions of
existing contract invariants — so the churn rule does not yet require rescoping
and ONE more correction round is permitted. It is the last one before the stop
rule bites. Sibling PRs #475 and #476 have already triggered it.

ACCEPTED AS FIXED — do not touch: the exact 31-row canonical roster;
owner-to-bead-evidence binding; readiness query ID uniqueness within a row;
replacement of synthetic sentinels with real record/source/page anchors.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== SUPERVISOR DECISION ON P1-A — SEPARATE THE TWO NAMESPACES ===
The identity incompatibility with PR #475 is a CATEGORY ERROR, not a validation
gap, and widening #475's facet vocabulary would be the wrong fix.

'obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>' denotes a SOURCE OBLIGATION. #477
currently mints that shape for things that are not source obligations at all —
facets 'readiness-hook', 'code-symbol', 'ownership' and 'primitive-relevance'
describe EVIDENCE ITEMS. Only 'projection-absence' is arguably a real source
obligation, and only when tied to a genuine source clause.

FIX:
 * Use 'obl:::' ONLY for genuine source obligations, and only with a CANONICAL
   SemanticFacet drawn from the same vocabulary PR #475 validates. Import
   nothing across branches; duplicate the vocabulary locally and add a parity
   test asserting the two lists match, so drift is caught.
 * Mint evidence-item identities in a DISTINCT namespace — e.g.
   'ev:::<kind>:::<row>:::<discriminator>' — which #475 will never be asked to
   join against.
 * Bind each obligation identity's sourceRef and locator to that obligation's
   own authoritative evidence, as #475 does.
 * Reject duplicate identities REGISTRY-WIDE, not per row.
Concrete divergences to fix: the first row's audit identity names indep:001
while its evidence cites sol:CAP-002; shared owners reuse identical bead
obligation IDs across rows; two different primitives reuse the Aboleth
projection-absence identity.

=== P1-B: AUDIT RELEVANCE IS PROSE-SHAPED, NOT EVIDENCE-BACKED ===
The validator proves a sentence quotes the selected subject and has enough
unique wording. It does not prove the finding actually DISCOVERED the primitive.
The reviewer confirmed five unsupported mappings:
  wizard spellbook copying        -> '221 magic items blocked by engine'
  short-rest Hit Dice             -> Natural Recovery
  derived attack/AC/proficiency   -> inconsistent damage field names
  canonical currency mutation     -> Tack/Harness/Drawn Vehicles taxonomy
  downtime procedures             -> '221 magic items blocked by engine'
FIX: a citation is valid only when the finding's own recorded scope covers the
primitive. Where it does not, DROP the citation — a row may stand on
readiness/code/bead evidence alone. Do not rewrite the sentence to sound better;
that is the same prose-shaped failure. Fix all five, then re-audit every
remaining audit-finding citation against the finding's scope in
/mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md.

=== P1-C: KNOWN-MISSING ROWS STILL DO NOT PROVE SEMANTIC ABSENCE ===
The resolver checks a generated pack record exists with some nonempty data, then
searches readiness clauses for one exact proposed hook name. That proves neither
that the source clause exists at the anchor NOR that an equivalent or partial
representation is absent elsewhere. Multi-save incompleteness is anchored to the
generic Saving Throws rule rather than to the entries whose later saves were
dropped. The test only proves an injected hook label is detectable.
FIX, for each of the 12 rows:
 (a) anchor to the SPECIFIC source material whose projection is missing — for
     multi-save, the entries that dropped later saves, not the generic rule;
 (b) prove the source material is present at that anchor;
 (c) prove no equivalent or PARTIAL representation exists elsewhere in the pack,
     searching by semantic shape rather than by one proposed hook name.
If (c) cannot be established for a row, mark it evidence-underived so it FAILS
the closure predicate. An unprovable row must block, never pass.

=== P2-D: PROJECTION QUERY IDS CAN DUPLICATE WITHIN A ROW ===
Same-row uniqueness covers only readiness queries. A repeated
known-missing-source-clause with the same projectionQueryId and a different
obligation ID is still accepted, and the regression test covers only readiness
duplication. FIX: enforce uniqueness across ALL query-bearing evidence kinds
within a row, and extend the test.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Edit only the four
files above. Do not touch package.json, internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,
.github/, or any script/CI file. Do not regenerate the pack or run the importer.
Do not modify any bead but your own; no bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or
merge. Never delete a test to make a finding disappear. The PR body is the
supervisor's to fix.
acceptance_criteria:
• obl::: is used only for genuine source obligations with canonical SemanticFacets; a parity test guards the vocabulary against PR #475 drift.
• Evidence-item identities use a distinct namespace and are never presented as source obligations.
• Obligation identity sourceRef and locator are bound to that obligation own evidence; duplicates are rejected registry-wide; the indep:001/sol:CAP-002, shared-bead and Aboleth divergences are fixed.
• The five unsupported audit citations are dropped or re-cited, and every remaining citation is re-audited against the finding recorded scope.
• Each known-missing row anchors to the specific unprojected source material, proves source presence, and proves absence of equivalent or partial representation; rows that cannot are evidence-underived and block closure.
• Query ID uniqueness within a row covers all query-bearing evidence kinds, with the test extended.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
notes: Completion report (2026-07-26): Re-architected the four owned artifacts around separate registry-wide ev::: evidence identities and canonical obl::: source-obligation identities. Duplicated and parity-tested PR #475's 29 SemanticFacet values; bound sourceRef/locator to each known-missing anchor; rejected non-canonical/duplicate identities, retired obligationKind/overloaded evidence, and all-kind query collisions. Added committed auditFindingPrimitiveRelations and dropped the five unsupported citations (spellbook copying, short-rest Hit Dice, derived attack/AC/proficiency, canonical currency, downtime). Known-missing resolution now verifies real source paths/terms and scans projected clauses for semantic equivalent/partial terms; underived results fail closed. Extended regression tests and documentation. No decision disagreement: I followed the supervisor's binding namespace split, reviewed finding relation, and fail-closed evidence-underived decisions. Unfulfilled obligation: five rows still have partial projected shapes and cannot honestly claim closure-grade absence; follow-up eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1.6.1 filed. title: Dispatch: contract-review corrections - one obligation per clause, base requirements, evidence binding (attempt 4)
description:
Contract-grounded fresh full review of PR #475 at 1b33b18 returned nine P1 and one
P2. Supervisor spot-confirmed the most structural ones. Pre-contract findings
are superseded — do NOT re-litigate real pack-driven execution, SRD enumeration,
importer migration, or engine certification; the contract defers all of those.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/adr/0020-source-clause-semantic-ir-and-completeness-contracts.md
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/obligations.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/index.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrObligations.test.ts

=== SUPERVISOR ARCHITECTURE DECISION — READ BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE ===
Finding 4 offers two routes. TAKE THE SECOND: enforce ONE OBLIGATION PER CLAUSE
as an invariant.

Rationale: the clause IS the unit of one source obligation. A single obligation
may carry MANY FACETS (save + duration + repeat-check + termination from one
source sentence). Where a source sentence carries genuinely separable mechanics,
it decomposes into multiple CLAUSES, each with its own obligation and its own
projection. This dissolves the whole class of defects in findings 4 and 7:
  * two duration obligations can no longer share one duration atom;
  * negative facets become coherent — 'save-without-damage' meaning 'this
    clause's damage is empty' is exactly right when the clause is that single
    obligation;
  * option-local mechanics cannot be hoisted, because hoisting would put two
    obligations on one clause, which now fails validation.
Enforce it in the evaluator and registry, document it in ADR 0020 as the
load-bearing invariant, and add tests that a clause claiming two obligations
fails closed. Retain field-count multiplicity WITHIN a facet (two saves in one
clause).

=== F1 (P1) CANONICAL BASE REQUIREMENTS ARE GONE — contracts.ts:111 ===
The published contract makes identity, sourceSpans, provenance, semanticOwner
and recordOwner UNREMOVABLE canonical requirements. The facet re-architecture
deleted BASE_REQUIREMENTS entirely; FACET_REQUIREMENTS holds only facet rules
and the evaluator never validates identity/provenance/ownership. A generated
clause with empty identity or owner evaluates semantically complete. Affects
every facet and all 15 families.
FIX: reinstate executable canonical base requirements that apply to EVERY
obligation and cannot be removed or overridden, plus an adversarial matrix that
removes or corrupts each base field in turn.

=== F2 (P1) SPECIALIZED FACETS ARE NOT CLOSED UNDER THEIR BASE — contracts.ts:115 ===
'save-with-damage' requires only a damage atom, not a save, so saves:[] plus one
damage certifies. Same for save-without-damage, save-with-alternate-outcomes,
attack-with-one-damage-mode, attack-with-conditional-alternatives,
resource-with-reset, and effect-without-lifecycle.
FIX: define ENFORCED facet implications (specialized implies its base mechanic)
or make each specialized facet self-contained. Add GENERATED removal tests for
every specialized facet — remove the base atom, assert incomplete.

=== F3 (P1) FACET VOCABULARY CANNOT EXPRESS THE CONTRACT'S TIMING — types.ts:80 ===
The contract assigns duration, recurrence, repeatChecks, immunityWindows and
termination to this PR, required exactly when an obligation declares them. There
is no generic recurrence facet and no immunity-window facet, so an authoritative
obligation cannot state them without a caller-side extension. Cross-kind gap for
spells, creature entries, hazards, features, magic items.
FIX: add canonical facets and predicates for recurrence and immunity windows,
with permanent sibling coverage.

=== F5 (P1) ALTERNATIVES PROVE NOTHING — contracts.ts:427 ===
The check only requires each alternative to name SOME existing alternative, so
A<->B plus C->A passes though B and C may overlap, and the committed test
permits every clauseIds list to be empty. Branch predicates count shells without
proving a source-backed outcome or condition.
FIX: validate the exclusion GRAPH (symmetry and partition), bind branches and
alternatives to projected atom identities, and add asymmetric, partially
connected, empty-binding and cross-kind regression cases.

=== F6 (P1) OBLIGATION IDENTITY IS NOT TIED TO ITS EVIDENCE — obligations.ts:104 ===
Validation checks only the obl: shape and that the terminal facet appears in
requiredFacets. It never verifies the ID's sourceRef/locator against the
obligation's source-span or authoritative-input evidence. Tests append synthetic
::index suffixes to the ID locator while keeping a DIFFERENT evidence locator,
and two same-facet obligations at one locator collide.
FIX: define a stable source-derived occurrence/clause locator so repeated
clauses at one anchor are distinguishable, and validate EVERY identity component
against origin-appropriate evidence. Reject synthetic locator divergence.

=== F7 (P1) CLOSURE BYPASSES ITS SCOPE AND CROSSES RECORDS — obligations.ts:263 ===
evaluateObligationClosure accepts any structurally shaped ObligationScope and
never requires createObligationScope, so a selectively omitted membership
returns a false-green empty closure. It also never checks
clause.recordOwner.family/key against the scope, so another record's clause can
satisfy this scope. T1/T7 only cover the constructor path.
FIX: consume an OPAQUE validated scope (brand it so a raw object literal cannot
be passed), validate applicability evidence, enforce exact family+record owner
matching, report unexpected claims, and add bypass / wrong-family / wrong-record
tests.

=== F8 (P1) AUDIT-ONLY EVIDENCE SATISFIES CAPTURED — contracts.ts:516 ===
The ADR says CAPTURED requires source-span or authoritative-input evidence, but
the loop accepts ANY registry evidence kind when the injected resolver returns
resolved. Since audit-finding origin is valid with only audit-finding evidence,
a KNOWN MISSING source clause can become captured and therefore semantically
complete.
FIX: restrict CAPTURED satisfaction to source-span or authoritative-input
evidence tied to that obligation. audit-finding and known-missing-source-clause
evidence IDENTIFY a gap; they must never close one. Add audit-only and
known-missing fail-closed tests.

=== F9 (P1) THE ENGINE-CAPABILITY CONTRACT IS NOT ENCODED — types.ts:375 ===
'export type EngineCapability = string' — any string. The contract requires
qualified engine:F1..engine:F10 owned through the eshyra-olc5 family epics, yet
committed tests use engine:save / eshyra-cap-save and an injected resolver
certifies them. Separately, ClauseReadinessEvidence.supported is never consumed,
so stored evidence can drift from requiredEngineCapabilities.
FIX: encode the closed identity shape and validate it; reconcile the two
capability-evidence surfaces so they cannot diverge; test unqualified,
wrong-owner, stale and mismatched references. This does NOT require real
execution — the contract defers that.

=== F10 (P2) THE VALIDATED REGISTRY IS MUTABLE — obligations.ts:176 ===
Records are shallow-frozen; evidence arrays, requiredFacets and nested evidence
objects are not, and scope applicability/evidence are retained by reference.
FIX: deep-copy and deep-freeze validated artifacts, or encapsulate them behind
immutable accessors. Add mutation-attempt regression tests.

=== ADR 0020 ===
Update it for the one-obligation-per-clause invariant, the base requirements,
facet implications, the recurrence/immunity facets, the identity-to-evidence
binding, opaque scopes, the CAPTURED restriction, and the capability identity.

CROSS-PR HONESTY: the ADR currently claims a shared identity with #476/#477 that
does not mechanically exist — #476 uses MembershipIdentity{recordKey, clauseId?,
path?, sourceSpan?} with no obligationId, and #477 accepts a broad obl:::
string. Do NOT overclaim. State precisely what is shared today, what is not, and
that validated adapters or parity tests are required before this is treated as
an integration boundary. A supervisor correction to #477's identity validation
is already in flight.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Design/type-contract
scope only — no importer, projector, pack regeneration, or engine registry
implementation. Edit only the files above; do not touch package.json,
internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/CI file. Do not
modify any bead but your own; no bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or merge.
Never delete a test to make a finding disappear.
acceptance_criteria:
• One-obligation-per-clause is enforced and documented as the load-bearing invariant; a clause claiming two obligations fails closed.
• Canonical base requirements are executable, unremovable, and covered by an adversarial removal matrix.
• Specialized facets imply their base mechanic, with generated removal tests for every specialized facet.
• Recurrence and immunity-window facets exist with sibling coverage.
• Alternatives validate the exclusion graph and bind to projected atom identities; branches prove source-backed outcomes.
• Obligation identity components are validated against origin-appropriate evidence; repeated clauses at one anchor are distinguishable; synthetic locator divergence is rejected.
• Closure consumes an opaque validated scope and enforces exact family+record ownership; bypass and wrong-record tests exist.
• CAPTURED is satisfiable only by source-span or authoritative-input evidence; audit-only and known-missing fail closed.
• EngineCapability is a validated closed identity; the two capability-evidence surfaces are reconciled.
• Validated registry and scope are deep-frozen with mutation-attempt tests.
• ADR 0020 states the real cross-PR position without overclaiming.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
notes: Completion report: re-architected the owned clause-IR contract boundary. Enforced exactly one source obligation per clause while retaining multi-facet obligations; restored immutable canonical base requirements; added specialized-facet implications; added recurrence and immunity-window facets; validated alternative exclusion partitions, projected-atom bindings, and source-backed branch bindings; bound obligation identity components and repeated occurrence locators to origin-appropriate evidence; made scopes opaque/branded and exact-family/record closure reject unexpected claims; restricted CAPTURED to source-span/authoritative-input evidence; closed EngineCapability to engine:F1..F10 with eshyra-olc5 ownership and reconciled capability evidence; deep-copied/deep-froze registries and scopes; expanded adversarial tests and corrected ADR 0020 cross-PR honesty. Decision disagreement: none. Obligations not satisfiable in this bead: real PR #476/#477 validated adapters/parity, the production capability ledger/engine registry, importer migration, source census, pack regeneration, discovery index, and engine certification remain explicitly deferred; follow-up eshyra-gvzx tracks the cross-PR adapter/parity work. Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed (264 test files, 4734 passed, 19 skipped).

description:

=== READ THIS FIRST — THE PATTERN BEHIND FINDINGS 2 AND 3 ===

   evidence for that row rather than inventing a citation. A row may stand on
   readiness/code/bead evidence alone.

=== F3: KNOWN-MISSING CLAUSES ARE NOT PROVEN ABSENT ===
sourceRef is 'SRD5.1:<primitive>' and locator is
'known-missing/<engine>/<primitive>' — both invented from the row's own name.
The resolver then searches the serialized pack for those invented markers.
Absence of a string you just made up proves nothing about the source procedure
or its projection. The regression test only proves an injected marker is
detectable.
FIX: a known-missing row must name a REAL source anchor (sourceRef plus a
locator that identifies actual SRD 5.1 material) and prove BOTH that the source

If a real anchor cannot be supplied for a primitive right now, mark that row

=== F4: owningBead IS NOT TIED TO BEAD EVIDENCE ===
owningBead is checked only for ID syntax; bead resolution runs on separate
evidence entries and equality is never required. Confirmed: 1 of 31 rows — the
spellbook-copy row naming eshyra-o9bd.19.5.5.3 — has no bead evidence for its
owner.

entry on that row, and that the entry resolves. Test the mismatch case.

queryOwners maps queryId -> primitive, so the same queryId twice within ONE row
passes whenever the obligationIds differ. The test named for duplicate bindings

title: Dispatch: durable exact-membership model for all 68 rows (attempt 4)
description:
Human review of PR #476 at cd2d6ae accepted the previous corrections but found
one remaining P1: the membership model is not exact or durable enough to govern
repair and prove zero recurrence. This is a CONTRACT-LEVEL change affecting all
68 rows. The supervisor has fixed the model below; implement it and migrate
every row.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== THE ROOT DEFECT ===
Today a row carries `membershipQuery` and nothing else that survives repair.
That single field conflates two different things: WHAT MUST HOLD (durable) and
WHAT IS CURRENTLY WRONG (transient). When the defect is repaired the query
returns zero rows and the obligation evaporates — so the registry cannot prove
non-recurrence, which is its entire purpose at eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4.

=== SUPERVISOR ROW MODEL — apply uniformly to all 68 rows ===
One coherent model. Do NOT create weak per-family conventions.

  canonicalId, aliases[], title, status, statusReasoning
  obligation {
    obligationId      shared format above where source-backed
    evidenceKind      the closed union above
    authority         what establishes this obligation INDEPENDENTLY of the
                      current pack — a source locator, an authoritative input,
                      or an audit-finding identity. The pack under repair may
                      never be the sole authority for its own obligations.
  }
  target {            what the obligation is ABOUT; survives repair
    kind              'record'|'clause'|'field'|'path'|'relationship'|'capability'
    selector          STRUCTURED and exact — not a text search
  }
  invariant           stated POSITIVELY, as what must hold. Durable.
  violation {         the CURRENT defect predicate. May legitimately go empty.
    queryId
    expectedAfterRepair  'empty' | 'stable'
  }
  baselineMembership { the audited baseline, reproducible
    capturedAtCommit
    members[]         exact member identities
  }
  currentMembership   GENERATED at evaluation time; never stored as authority
  owningBead
  regression { evidenceKind, locator }

The durable identity is obligation + target + invariant. The violation query is
separate and MAY become empty after repair WITHOUT the row losing meaning. That
separation is the whole fix — do not collapse them back.

=== THE MODEL MUST SUPPORT ALL TEN CASES ===
Each needs at least one real row and a test:
 1 clause missing entirely from the current pack
 2 clause present on the wrong owner

title: Dispatch: clause obligation-boundary architecture (attempt 3)
description:
Human review of PR #475 at b0395e4 found FIVE P1 ARCHITECTURAL defects. Per the
churn stop rule this is a NEW DEFECT CLASS, so this is a re-architecture of the
obligation boundary, NOT five isolated patches. The supervisor has done the
threat model and fixed the architecture below; implement it.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/adr/0020-source-clause-semantic-ir-and-completeness-contracts.md
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/obligations.ts        (new)
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/index.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrObligations.test.ts          (new)

=== SUPERVISOR THREAT MODEL — the evaluator must defeat all eight ===
T1 projector never declares an obligation the source contains -> nothing fails.
T2 projector misclassifies the clause to a narrower/laxer kind.
T3 projector declares the obligation but weakens its requirement list.
T4 caller passes a permissive or empty contract to the evaluator.
T5 caller asserts readiness dimensions true with no evidence.
T6 a kind contract demands semantically invalid things, pressuring projectors
   toward T2 to escape it.
T7 a family is reported covered although its obligations were never enumerated.
T8 unknown or contradictory contract selection silently defaults to something.

Every one of these needs an adversarial test named for the threat it defeats.

=== D1: OBLIGATIONS HAVE AN AUTHORITY INDEPENDENT OF THE PROJECTOR (T1,T2,T3) ===
Today `SourceObligation.requirements` is inline on the Clause, so the producer
of the output also defines the standard its output is judged by. That is the
root defect; the other four are consequences.

Introduce an OBLIGATION REGISTRY, separate from any clause:
  * a `SourceObligationRecord` carries obligationId (shared format above),
    `origin`, evidence, and `requiredFacets`.
  * `origin` is a closed union that CANNOT be 'projector':
    'source-extraction' | 'curated-specification' | 'audit-finding'.
  * a Clause REFERENCES obligations by id only. It must not be able to state
    their requirements.
  * the evaluator resolves each obligation FROM THE REGISTRY. A clause citing an
    obligationId absent from the registry FAILS CLOSED (defeats T2/T3).
  * registry construction validates that each record carries resolvable evidence
    of its declared origin.

=== D2: OMISSION MUST BE VISIBLE — CLOSURE OVER A SCOPE (T1, T7) ===
Add `evaluateObligationClosure(registry, clauses, scope)` returning, per
obligation: satisfied | claimed-incomplete | UNCLAIMED. An obligation in the
registry that no clause claims is the ONLY way T1 becomes visible, and it is the
real answer to finding 5: a record-family array establishes APPLICABILITY, never
closure. Keep these four concepts explicitly distinct in types and in the ADR:
family applicability; source-derived obligation membership; per-obligation
completeness; aggregate family closure.

=== D3: CANONICAL REQUIREMENTS ARE NOT BYPASSABLE (T4, T8) ===
`evaluateClauseCompleteness(clause, contract)` currently accepts ANY contract,
so an empty one certifies anything. Change the signature so the evaluator
derives the canonical contract internally from the resolved obligation's facets.
Extensions may only be ADDITIVE (`additionalRequirements`); there must be no
code path by which an ordinary caller removes a canonical requirement. Unknown
facet, unknown contract id, or contradictory selection FAILS CLOSED — never
defaults to a laxer contract.

=== D4: FACETS REPLACE UNIVERSAL KIND CONTRACTS (T6) ===
The `save` contract currently requires `nonEmpty('damage')`, so a save that
deals no damage — a save against being frightened — cannot be represented as
complete. That is an invalid universal assumption and it actively pressures
projectors toward T2.

Replace kind-level universals with COMPOSABLE SEMANTIC FACETS. Each facet owns
its own requirements; the OBLIGATION names which facets the source demands. The
model must express at least, and each needs a test:
  save with damage                     | save without damage
  save with alternate outcomes         | attack with one damage mode
  attack with conditional or mutually exclusive alternatives
  resource use with reset              | resource use without reset
  duration with concentration          | duration without concentration
  effect with lifecycle state          | effect without lifecycle state

DO NOT solve this by making requirements optional. The obligation must still
state EXACTLY which facets are required for that source clause; what changes is
that the requirement set comes from the source-declared facets rather than from
a blanket kind assumption.

=== D5: READINESS NEEDS EVIDENCE, NOT BOOLEANS (T5) ===
`ClauseReadiness.dimensions` is four caller-set booleans. Self-attestation is
not proof. Replace with per-dimension EVIDENCE:
  captured      resolvable source-span/authoritative-input evidence
  projected     DERIVED from the semantic evaluation — not settable by a caller
  supported     a capability reference naming an engine capability identity AND
                its owning bead; unresolved, unowned or unimplemented => failed
  discoverable  a resolver/index/path reference; unresolved => failed
Evidence must be inspectable and must reject stale or nonexistent references.
A clause must NOT be green when the representation exists but its required
engine capability is unowned.

This PR stays design/type-contract scope: do NOT build the engine capability
registry. Inject resolver interfaces (e.g. a CapabilityResolver and a
DiscoveryResolver) so the evaluator consumes evidence it cannot forge, and
provide test doubles. The requirement is that the TYPES AND EVALUATOR CANNOT
ENCODE SELF-ATTESTATION AS PROOF.

=== SHARED SOURCE-OBLIGATION IDENTITY (supervisor decision, binding across
PRs #475, #476, #477) ===
This identity is fixed by the supervisor so the three branches cannot invent
competing definitions. Implement it here; #476 and #477 will align to it.

  obligationId := "obl:<sourceRef>:<locator>:<facet>"
     sourceRef  stable source document identity, e.g. "srd-5.1"
     locator    source anchor, e.g. "p.104#fireball"
     facet      semantic facet name (see the facet model below)

EVIDENCE KIND is a closed union, shared conceptually across all three PRs. Never
overload one "sourceSpan" field to carry incompatible evidence types:

  'source-span'                 exact span in the licensed source document
  'authoritative-input'         non-PDF authoritative input (curated spec, table)
  'audit-finding'               a 2026-07-24 finding identity
  'code'                        an implementation site in @eshyra/core
  'bead'                        a bead identity
  'known-missing-source-clause' source clause known absent from projection

#475 owns 'source-span' and 'authoritative-input' in depth; the other members
must exist in the type so #476/#477 can align without redefining the union.

DO NOT import code across branches. Align the CONCEPTS; duplicate the small
identity/evidence types locally and note the integration boundary in the ADR.

=== ADR 0020 ===
Rewrite to describe this architecture: the obligation authority boundary, the
facet model, non-bypassable canonical requirements, evidence-backed readiness,
and the applicability/membership/completeness/closure distinction. State the
cross-PR identity and the deferred integration boundary. The ADR is what the
rest of the program cites — it must not describe the superseded design.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it
rewrites files. Machine load matters: if rulesPackAuditCli or dolt-gated suites
time out, rerun that file in isolation before concluding a regression.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files under FILES YOU OWN. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, packages/core/src/internal.ts, AGENTS.md,
  CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/protocol/CI file. Adding review
  infrastructure is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this session.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack, run the SRD importer, or touch
  packages/core/data. Do not absorb importer migration or corpus recompilation —
  this PR stays design/type-contract scope.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, open/comment on a PR, or merge.
* PRESERVE the regression coverage for the three previously-fixed defect classes:
  requirement cardinality, independent readiness dimensions, and non-mutable
  disposition. If a preserved test must change shape, keep an equivalent
  assertion and say so in your notes.
* Where a committed test encodes defective behavior, change it deliberately and
  record why. Never delete a test to make a finding disappear.
acceptance_criteria:
• Obligations live in a registry with a non-projector origin; a clause can reference but never define them; an unknown obligationId fails closed.
• evaluateObligationClosure reports UNCLAIMED obligations, making omission visible; applicability, membership, completeness and closure are distinct in types and ADR.
• No caller-supplied contract can remove a canonical requirement; extensions are additive only; unknown/contradictory selection fails closed.
• Facets replace universal kind requirements; all twelve listed facet combinations are representable and tested, including save-without-damage.
• Readiness dimensions are evidence-backed; projected is derived; supported binds to a capability identity and owner and fails when unowned; resolvers are injected, not implemented here.
• An adversarial test exists for each of threats T1-T8, named for the threat.
• Prior regression coverage for cardinality, independent dimensions, and non-mutable disposition is preserved.
• ADR 0020 describes the new architecture and the shared cross-PR identity.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
notes: Completion report: Re-architected the clause IR around an independently validated source-obligation registry. Clauses now reference obligation IDs only; registry records enforce non-projector origin, shared obl::: identity, closed evidence kinds, facet validation, contradiction rejection, and immutable records. Canonical requirements are derived from composable semantic facets with aggregate atom multiplicity and no caller-replaceable contract; closure now distinguishes applicability, source membership, per-obligation completeness, and UNCLAIMED scope coverage. Readiness now consumes captured evidence plus injected source/capability/discovery resolvers; projected is derived and supported/discoverable fail closed without owned, implemented, resolvable evidence. Rewrote ADR 0020 and added named T1-T8 adversarial tests while preserving cardinality, independent dimensions, and non-mutable disposition regression coverage. No design decision disagreed with; no in-scope obligation could not be satisfied. Deferred production source census/capability/discovery integration to follow-up eshyra-s38f. Verification: npm ci; npm run verify:worktree passed (264 test files passed, 4 skipped; 4726 passed, 19 skipped); isolated importer pipeline rerun passed 44/44 after one initial full-suite timeout under load. Commit 1b33b18.

title: Dispatch: bootstrap ledger review corrections from PR #477 (attempt 3)
description:
HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #477 at head 8fd61cf returned "request changes": three P1,
four P2 and one remaining P3. All are accepted. Read the review on
https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/477 for the reviewer's exact wording.
Both CI workflows pass — these are contract defects CI cannot catch.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== P1-A: THE VALIDATOR CAN NO LONGER REPRESENT proposed-new-bead ===
*** THIS IS THE SUPERVISOR'S REGRESSION, INTRODUCED IN COMMIT 8fd61cf. ***
The schema requires every row to have an owningBead. The new invariant then
UNCONDITIONALLY rejects 'eshyra-olc5' as owningBead — including when
ownershipStatus is 'proposed-new-bead'. The failure message advises using
ownershipStatus=proposed-new-bead, which does not bypass the rejection. There is
now no honest value for owningBead when no bead and no exact family owner
exists: a caller must invent a nonexistent bead ID or falsely assign a family
epic. That contradicts the documented workflow, which says future unowned
primitives are recorded as proposed in the same manner.

Fix: make owningBead optional/null for proposed rows, OR permit the engine epic
root ONLY when ownershipStatus === 'proposed-new-bead'. Then add a POSITIVE test
that constructs a proposed row and validates it successfully — the existing
proposed-row loop is vacuous because the checked-in ledger now contains none.
Keep the real invariant intact: an 'owned' row may never name the engine epic
root.

=== P1-B: THE RECONCILIATION STILL REACHES THE WRONG CONCLUSION ===
See the CORRECTION note on the parent bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 — read it first;
it is authoritative over the parent description's four-category list.

The document concludes zero premature closures and classifies eshyra-2n1t itself
as only a taxonomy mismatch. But the PR that closed it was titled "Complete SRD
audit and engine gaps", claimed source-grounded executable mechanics for ALL 240
magic items, reported zero deep-audit findings, and named eshyra-2n1t and
eshyra-o9bd.18 as its beads.

Narrow child beads may still be correctly closed — their primitives landed. The
umbrella completeness claim is a different object. Distinguish explicitly:
  * narrow child acceptance genuinely completed;
  * broader integration not completed;
  * umbrella epic closed on a global claim later proven false.
Classify eshyra-2n1t as premature / overstated umbrella closure, or add an
equivalent explicit category and define it. Rewrite the "Why no category is
PREMATURE CLOSURE" section accordingly — do not leave a heading that contradicts
the table.

Also reconsider eshyra-o9bd.18.7: source clauses omitted or silently partially
projected are IMPORTER/COMPILER completeness defects, not merely downstream
engine work. Its current DIFFERENT SCOPE OR TAXONOMY classification rests on
that mischaracterization.

Still do not reopen, close, or modify any bead. Record recommendations as data.

=== P1-C: packEvidence IS PROSE, NOT AN EXECUTABLE QUERY ===
This is the deepest finding. The docs say membership is represented by generated
queries and tell consumers to execute them. In reality packEvidence is a
free-form string; validation only checks non-emptiness and the test only greps
for the substrings 'record.key' and 'data.executionReadiness'. There is no query
identifier, evaluator, predicate, generated record-key membership, or
source-comparison function.

Consequences: membership cannot be regenerated; two ledger versions cannot be
mechanically diffed; invalid or copy-pasted query prose stays green; and
eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 cannot reliably reconcile the authoritative ledger against
this bootstrap one — which is that bead's entire purpose.

Fix: give rows STABLE QUERY IDS backed by executable functions, or a structured
query representation with a tested evaluator. Execute against the committed pack
at packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json. Rows whose
evidence is a negative or source-comparison claim need a REPRODUCIBLE SECOND
INPUT, not prose saying to compare against "the audit" — if the second input
cannot yet be expressed, say so explicitly on the row with a defined follow-up
rather than leaving prose that reads as executable.

Note the sibling work: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 (PR #476) is concurrently adding
stable membership identities {recordKey, clauseId/path, sourceSpan} to the
finding registry. Use a compatible identity shape so 19.5.12 can join them
later. Do not edit that file — it is on another branch.

=== P2-D: THE engine:F1 ROW QUERIES engine:F2 ===
Row capabilityId engine:F1, primitive 'seeded-selection-and-roll-replacement',
but its packEvidence selects hooks qualified as engine:F2 with activation /
action-economy semantics. That is unrelated evidence copied from the F2 family.
It should query F1 selection, table/pool/percentage, or roll-replacement hooks.
The executable query contract from P1-C must also ENFORCE that a row cannot
silently target another family.

=== P2-E: THE SEVEN-ROW NON-PACK PROOF IS NOT ASSERTED ===
The PR body claimed 7 of 31 rows are non-pack discoveries with a test asserting
it. The test only requires more than two rows plus the presence of the legendary
and point-origin primitives; the validator requires only three. The docs also
list retained-asset creation as a non-pack discovery, but that row includes
'readiness-artifacts' in discoveredBy, so by the ledger's own definition it is
not in the non-pack set.

Fix: pin the exact non-pack primitive IDs explicitly and assert that set. This
set is the evidence that the five-source method escaped the pack's blind spots,
so it must be exact and the prose must match the data.

=== P2-F: CORRECTIVE OWNERSHIP OMITS TWO OF FOUR OVERLAPS ===
The corrective section routes only eshyra-2n1t.7 and .12 to the new beads, but
the table itself establishes two more:
  * .6 includes spell copying among its missing engine:F4 procedures ->
    eshyra-o9bd.19.5.5.3
  * .9 includes planar-return clocks among its missing engine:F7 procedures ->
    eshyra-o9bd.19.5.8.3
Route .6, .7, .9 and .12.

=== P2-G: STORED-COUNT REJECTION IS NOT MEANINGFULLY TESTED ===
The validator rejects only four exact top-level keys: count, counts,
recordCount, clauseCount. Nested counts and names like total, storedCount or
hookTotal pass. Worse, the test mutates capabilityId AND count together, and
capability validation runs first — so the test can pass without ever exercising
count rejection.

Fix: split into separate tests, and either use a strict schema or recursively
reject count/total-shaped fields at any depth.

=== P3-H: THE VALIDATOR DOES NOT ENFORCE THE ADVERTISED SHAPE ===
The PR claims 31 rows and 2-4 per family; the validator enforces only >=2 per
family. It does not enforce a total, an upper bound per family, unique
primitives, or unique family/primitive pairs. Primitive uniqueness is checked
only against the current static file, not by the exported validator.
Enforce uniqueness of primitives and of family/primitive pairs in the validator.
Use judgement on hard totals — a fixed row count is itself a hand-copied number
and should NOT be asserted; an upper bound per family is also arbitrary. Prefer
enforcing the structural invariants and correcting the prose instead.

=== COUNT HYGIENE, CLARIFIED ===
A GENERATED, regenerable snapshot of member identities is NOT a hand-copied
count and is exactly the right instrument here. What is forbidden is a human
transcribing a total (391, 399, 77, 79, 794) into an assertion. Do not let the
count-hygiene rule block P1-C or P2-E.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it
rewrites files.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed above. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, or packages/core/src/internal.ts.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a PR, do NOT merge.
* Where a committed test encodes defective behavior, change it deliberately and
  record why. Do not delete a test to make a finding disappear.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack and do NOT run the SRD importer.

• A proposed-new-bead row is representable and validates, proven by a positive test; an owned row still may not name the engine epic root.
• eshyra-2n1t is classified as premature/overstated umbrella closure or an equivalent defined category, with narrow-child acceptance distinguished from the umbrella claim; the contradicting section heading is rewritten.
• eshyra-o9bd.18.7 reconsidered on importer/compiler completeness grounds.
• Every row carries a stable query ID backed by an executable function or a structured query with a tested evaluator; negative/source-comparison rows have a reproducible second input or an explicit stated gap.
• A row cannot silently target another capability family, enforced by the query contract; the engine:F1 row queries F1 hooks.

Reconciliation now distinguishes narrow child acceptance from premature/overstated eshyra-2n1t umbrella closure, classifies eshyra-o9bd.18.7 as premature importer/compiler projection closure, and routes .6/.7/.9/.12 to .19.5.5.3/.6.3/.8.3/.11.3. The committed tests that asserted only more than two non-pack rows and combined capability/count mutation were deliberately changed because they encoded the defective behavior identified by review. I disagree with none of the accepted findings. Focused ledger tests: 8 passed. Final npm run verify:worktree: 263 test files passed, 4 skipped; 4717 tests passed, 19 skipped. title: Dispatch: clause IR review corrections from PR #475 (attempt 2)
description:
HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #475 returned "changes required": three P1 findings and one
P2. All four are accepted. Read the inline comments on
https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/475 for the reviewer's exact wording,
then fix the underlying design — not just the cited line.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/adr/0020-source-clause-semantic-ir-and-completeness-contracts.md
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/index.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts

=== P1-A: COMPLETENESS IS NOT SOURCE-SPECIFIC (contracts.ts:48) ===
Today the only authority is the projector-selected ClauseKind plus a generic
field list. Nothing binds an exact source clause to the semantic obligations
actually present in its source text.

The reviewer's worked example, which your tests must cover: a source clause
containing a save, a duration, a repeated save, and a termination condition can
be emitted as `kind: 'save'`. The save contract never requires duration,
repeatChecks or termination — so the evaluator CERTIFIES the partial projection.
That is the audit's root failure reproduced inside the very mechanism built to
prevent it.

Fix: completeness must be driven by SOURCE-BACKED PER-CLAUSE OBLIGATIONS, not by
the selected kind. Concretely, the clause must declare the obligations detected
in its source span, and the evaluator must require each declared obligation to
be discharged by a satisfied contract. Support composed contracts and/or child
clauses so one source clause can carry several obligations. A projector that
selects a narrower kind than its source text supports must fail closed rather
than silently narrowing.

You choose the exact representation, but the invariant is: the SOURCE decides
what must be present; the kind only decides HOW it is shaped.

=== P1-B: REQUIRED COLLECTIONS PASS WHEN EMPTY (contracts.ts:298) ===
Only `sourceSpans` has a cardinality check. Every other required array —
`saves`, `attacks`, `damage`, `alternatives`, `ledgerChanges`,
`stateTransitions`, `regressionEvidence` — passes when `[]`. A save clause
with `saves: []` and `damage: []`, populated branches and all dimensions true
returns `complete`. That directly violates the fail-closed invariant.

Fix: the contract vocabulary needs requirement PREDICATES with cardinality, not
boolean field presence. Include cross-field alternatives where the source
genuinely allows them (an attack roll XOR a saving throw, for example) so the
fix does not force absurd requirements. Add a test for the exact empty-array
case above.

=== P1-C: THE EVALUATOR COLLAPSES THE FOUR DIMENSIONS (contracts.ts:91) ===
ADR 0020 says CAPTURED, PROJECTED, SUPPORTED and DISCOVERABLE must fail
INDEPENDENTLY and no gate may collapse them. Requiring all four in every
ClauseCompletenessContract means a fully captured and projected clause that is
merely awaiting an engine or lookup path is labelled generically "incomplete".

*** THIS ONE IS MY FAULT, NOT YOURS. *** The attempt-1 dispatch spec explicitly
instructed that a CAPTURED+PROJECTED-but-not-SUPPORTED clause must not evaluate
complete, and the test at clauseIrContracts.test.ts:180-213 faithfully locks that
in. That instruction was wrong. You are expected to CHANGE that test.

The distinction to encode:
  * SEMANTIC COMPLETENESS — is the projection of this source clause complete?
    Determined by CAPTURED and PROJECTED and the source obligations from P1-A.
  * READINESS — can it execute end to end? SUPPORTED and DISCOVERABLE, reported
    per dimension.
A clause can be semantically complete and unsupported; that is the exact
distinction the audit needed and the pack lacked. Return independently gated
per-dimension results, or separate the two evaluations. Do not emit a single
all-or-nothing status that hides which dimension failed.

The nine-point green definition on eshyra-o9bd.19 still governs the FREEZE gate
and still requires an engine implementation — but that is a freeze gate, not a
clause-completeness verdict, and must not be smuggled into this evaluator.

=== P2-D: DISPOSITION CAN CONTRADICT THE CLAUSE (types.ts:277) ===
`disposition`, the dimension booleans and the free-text `note` can contradict
one another, and `evaluateClauseCompleteness` ignores `disposition` entirely.
So `disposition: 'complete'` with `projected: false` is legal, and
`disposition: 'incomplete'` with everything satisfied evaluates complete. The
clause also carries no structured failed-contract reasons, although the ADR
requires an emitted INCOMPLETE clause to NAME each failed requirement.

Fix: make the status derived/canonical, or validate consistency and fail closed
on contradiction; and carry structured contract failures on the emitted clause —
or make the evaluation result the sole authoritative readiness artifact and stop
storing a disposition that can drift.

=== ADR 0020 ===
Update it to match. It is the document the rest of the program will cite, so the
source-obligation rule, the cardinality rule, and the independence of the four
dimensions must be stated there, not only in code.

=== UNCHANGED ===
Design and type contracts only — no importer changes, no projector changes, no
pack regeneration. Small hand-built fixtures; do not load the 7.4 MB pack. No
hand-copied counts. Qualified engine:F* / fable:F* / opus:F-* / sol:CAP-* /
indep:* prefixes only, never a bare "F5".

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
This worktree already contains the previous attempts' committed work; you are
correcting it, not starting over. Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===

  in parallel on a disjoint file set. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, or packages/core/src/internal.ts.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a PR, do NOT merge.
* Do NOT weaken, skip, or delete an existing test to make a finding go away. If
  an existing test encodes the defective behavior, CHANGE it deliberately and
  say so in your completion notes with the reason.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack and do NOT run the SRD importer.

• Completeness is driven by source-backed per-clause obligations; the reviewer's save+duration+repeat+termination example fails closed and is covered by a test.

• Semantic completeness and readiness are separated; the four dimensions report independently and no single verdict hides which failed.
• The attempt-1 test that locked in dimension collapse is deliberately changed, with the reason recorded.

title: Certify the deterministic reference engine for SRD re-freeze
description:
The gate that permits the SRD pack to be re-frozen. Depends on all ten family
certification tasks and on the authoritative capability ledger
(eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12). Blocks eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1, and therefore the whole
closure chain down to eshyra-o9bd.14.

WHY THIS GATES THE FREEZE: where structured pack data is a direct input to
deterministic execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are one
co-designed system. Implementation pressure exposes missing distinctions,
invalid abstractions, and fields that look complete but cannot actually drive
execution. A pack frozen before its reference implementation would preserve a
separation that does not exist in practice. Precedent: the unfinished
house-rules section was previously frozen ahead of its consumer, and that is the
pattern being corrected here.

Certify:

  * Authoritative-ledger count of unowned capabilities: ZERO.
  * Deterministic engine-pending clauses: ZERO.
  * Stale or falsely green clauses: ZERO.
  * Every implemented capability is reached by at least one REAL pack-driven
    test, not a fixture.
  * All eshyra-2n1t discrepancies resolved per the four-way classification.
  * The only remaining non-executable clauses are the four approved categories,
    each represented in-band with its alternatives / campaign-ruling requirement
    and failing CLOSED.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: the house-rule and source-ambiguity boundary is different in
kind and is NOT expected to be executed by the base deterministic engine. It
must be explicitly represented and fail closed, not implemented.

*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.

    'derived' and never applies the executable-generator and snapshot
    validations directly below it, and the suite explicitly constructs an
    invalid all-derived registry and expects true.

*** CROSS-ARTIFACT PATTERN 2026-07-27: FAIL-OPEN 'READY' PREDICATES ***
PR #476's findingRegistryClosureReady() and PR #477's ledger closure check were
built in separate rounds by separate dispatches, and BOTH shipped fail-open: each
reports readiness from a status field without applying the validations sitting
directly beneath it, and each has a test that constructs the invalid case and
expects true.

Treat fail-open as the DEFAULT failure mode of any 'ready'/'complete' helper in
this program. A closure predicate must prove the negative: name the exact blocker
set, assert blocker IDENTITIES rather than a count, and be tested in both
directions — not-ready on real data with real blockers, ready only on a fixture
where every blocker is resolved. A test pinning a COUNT of blockers passes
identically for a different set of the same size, which is how both of these
survived review.

Applies to the #476 rescope's retained fail-open gate and to eshyra-o9bd.19.1.8.
*** SUPERVISOR REVIEW MISSES 2026-07-27 ***
Two findings at 6a1b275 passed my own review and should not have. Recording the
mechanism, not just the fact.

1. CLOSURE SUBSET FIXTURE. I read the test that builds
   validFixture = registry.rows.filter(derived) and asserts ready===true, and
   called it 'a genuinely valid fixture'. Deleting the 64 unresolved obligations
   is the cheapest possible way to fake closure, and I blessed it. The lesson:
   when reviewing a gate, ask what the CHEAPEST way to make it green is, and
   check that path is blocked. A fixture that removes the failing inputs is
   always that path.

2. WEAK REGRESSION TEST OF MY OWN. I added 'rejects reasons that share a template
   across rows' using two rows whose text is byte-identical apart from an
   interpolated title. The guard already caught that. The data's actual pattern
   is a shared skeleton with PARAPHRASED subjects, which survives normalization.
   So my test passed against a case that was never at risk and created false
   confidence that the guard was protected. The lesson: a regression test must
   fail against the pattern PRESENT IN THE DATA, not against an idealized
   version of the defect. Before adding one, confirm it fails on the current
   implementation for the real reason.

Both are instances of the same reviewer error: verifying that a mechanism exists
rather than that it binds.

title: Reopen deterministic engine completeness under the clause-capability contract
description:
Provider-neutral deterministic engine/tool capability work, reopened under the clause-capability contract established by the 2026-07-24 SRD audit repair program (eshyra-o9bd.19).

SEPARATION OF CONCERNS — the reason this epic exists outside eshyra-o9bd.19:
  * The PACK question (eshyra-o9bd.19) is whether the data completely and
    accurately expresses the rules.
  * The ENGINE question (this epic) is whether Eshyra can execute the rules the
    pack expresses.
These interact but must never again become indistinguishable. An engine-pending
clause is NOT automatically a pack defect. Conversely, no engine gap may remain
invisible: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 (bootstrap ledger) and eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12
(authoritative ledger) own the inventory and the ownership gate that guarantee
every requirement here has a real owner.

Capabilities implemented here are PROVIDER-NEUTRAL engine primitives. They are
not SRD-specific runtime branches, and must not be implemented as such: the SRD
5.1 pack is the first consumer that exercises them, not their definition.

Children are the engine:F1..engine:F10 capability families. Exact membership is
owned by the ledger beads; do not hand-copy counts into acceptance criteria.

*** engine:F* IS A QUALIFIED PREFIX — see eshyra-o9bd.19.5 for the full
taxonomy-collision warning. engine:F1..F10 (pack executionReadiness engineHooks)
are NOT the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t's F1-F10, and NOT the fable:F1..F8 audit
findings.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every engine:F* family is implemented as a provider-neutral capability with executable conformance scenarios driven from pack clause data.
- Unsupported clauses fail CLOSED at runtime; no silent degradation.
- Every capability required by the authoritative ledger (eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12) is green or carries an approved explicit house-rule/design dependency.
- No capability is closed by asserting the pack is data-complete.
- The release/re-freeze gate can depend on this epic and eshyra-o9bd.19 jointly for end-to-end playability.
notes:
Supersedes the scope ambition of the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t, which used a DIFFERENT F1-F10 taxonomy. Do not treat eshyra-2n1t's closure as evidence of engine completeness; eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 owns the four-way reconciliation of that contradiction.
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.
*** DECOMPOSITION IS MACHINE-GATED (2026-07-25) ***
bd forbids epic->task dependencies, so this epic cannot itself depend on the
bootstrap ledger. Instead:

  eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 bootstrap ledger
    -> "Authorize Engine F1-F10 decomposition ..." (shared, under this epic)
    -> ten per-family "Decompose Engine F<n> ..." tasks
    -> implementation children (created only by those decomposition tasks)
    -> ten per-family "Certify Engine F<n> ..." tasks
    -> "Certify the deterministic reference engine for SRD re-freeze"
    -> eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 -> ... -> eshyra-o9bd.14 formal re-freeze

The ten Engine F epics still appear in bd ready. That is a bd display
limitation, not permission to start: every executable task beneath them is
blocked by the authorization gate. Do not dispatch implementation agents to an
Engine F epic; the first legitimate work in each is its decomposition task.

*** IDS ARE HISTORICAL, NOT PATHS (2026-07-25) ***
The ten family epics keep their eshyra-o9bd.19.5.* IDs on purpose. Bead IDs are
durable historical identifiers; recreating them for cosmetically matching
eshyra-olc5.* IDs would invalidate references already placed in bead
descriptions and the finding registry, create confusing duplicates, and
complicate audit archaeology. Judge parentage by the tree, and query the family
set by the "engine-capability" label rather than by ID prefix.
*** ADR 0020 NARROWING (2026-07-31) — SUPERSEDES THE ZERO-ENGINE-PENDING BAR ***
Authority: ADR 0020, and the integrated transition design
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md
sections 5.4, 5.5, 5.9 — the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8
(PR #485, reviewed head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). Recorded here as accepted authority;
NOT implemented in code by this bead update.

1. engine:F1..engine:F10 IS THE GENERATED MAGIC-ITEM CAPABILITY BACKLOG, not a
   corpus-wide engine inventory. Verified extent: 240 records carrying
   executionReadiness — all of kind magic-item — 1,016 clauses, of which 794 are
   engine-pending, 218 green, 3 adjudicated-by-design, 1 design-blocked; 795
   clauses carry non-empty engineHooks. No other record kind carries
   executionReadiness. The 794 and 795 counts are two different predicates over
   the same data: magic-item:candle-of-invocation/c1-burn-time is GREEN while
   still declaring an F5 hook, so "green" is not interchangeable with
   "hook-free", and neither count may be reported as a capability inventory.
   The ten family epics are REASSESSED against that bounded scope, not deleted:
   221 of 240 items still carry at least one engine-pending or design-blocked
   clause, and those obligations remain real.

2. "AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES" IS NO
   LONGER THE RE-FREEZE BAR. It requires a global negative the corpus cannot
   support: RulesRecord.data is typed unknown (rules/types.ts:135), kind
   validators accept unregistered data fields, and key closure over mechanics
   exists for magic-item only. The replacement is the nine-condition truthfulness
   bar in section 5.9 of the transition design, recorded on eshyra-o9bd.14 and
   eshyra-2zyy. Nothing in the new bar requires global deterministic closure,
   universal discovery completeness, zero engine-pending clauses, or a
   corpus-wide negative claim of any kind. The nine-point GREEN definition above
   stands as a per-clause quality definition for clauses that ARE positively
   selected for deterministic execution; it is no longer a corpus-wide gate.

3. CAPABILITY WORK IS A SET OF POSITIVE, BOUNDED COMMITMENTS (ADR 0020 section
   3). A capability declares what operation it performs, its required inputs, its
   exclusions, its revision or identity, and what interpretation remains with the
   DM — and fails closed on unrecognized input.

4. eshyra-olc5.6 (transition W13) OWNS CAPABILITY-CONTRACT NORMALIZATION: putting
   every capability in force into that five-field shape and proving fail-closed
   behavior. It depends on eshyra-uiax (the unrecognized-scope fail-open on the
   pilot contract assertMagicItemOperationReady) and on the
   ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE split owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.14 (transition W14).
   It creates no corpus-wide capability inventory and does not widen
   engine:F1..F10 beyond the generated magic-item backlog.

5. ABSENCE OF A CAPABILITY BINDING PROVES ONLY THAT NO CAPABILITY WAS POSITIVELY
   SELECTED. It is a statement about Eshyra, not about the rules. It never means
   the record has no mechanics, the rule is irrelevant or unsupported, the rule
   can be ignored, or the pack is mechanically complete. "Unbound",
   "unclassified", and "not recognized" are not safety properties; any gate,
   report, or predicate that reads an unbound or unrecognized item as satisfied
   is a defect, not a green. Symmetrically, a deterministic operation does not
   imply a complete record: magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3 carries one green,
   positively owned clause (c1-use) and one engine-pending clause
   (c2-static-ammunition-rarity-attack-damage, F8) simultaneously.

clause is green ONLY when all eight hold:

  5. The engine implementation exists.
  6. An executable conformance scenario proves the intended outcome.
  7. Runtime lookup can find the canonical clause.
  8. Unsupported portions fail closed.

green. The Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but explicitly
did NOT prove the semantic appropriateness of every free-form effect.

*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.

Protocol: eshyra-clause-review-v1

Migration baseline recorded 2026-07-26 during the final pre-protocol review
cycle. Derived from the corrected design at commit dee8d0a.

### Source obligation

  implementation primitive rather than a family label.
- Membership derivation: the five bootstrap sources, each with its OWN
  executable resolver — readiness artifacts, @eshyra/core code, open and closed
  beads, accepted 2026-07-24 findings, and source clauses known missing from
  projection. A ledger derived from the pack alone inherits the pack's blind
  spots.
- Source spans or authoritative inputs: evidence is a discriminated union keyed
  by kind — 'readiness-artifact', 'code', 'bead', 'audit-finding',
  'known-missing-source-clause'. sourceSpan is NOT overloaded to carry
  incompatible evidence types.
- Complete obligations covered: bootstrap scope only. This ledger is explicitly
  NON-AUTHORITATIVE; eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 regenerates the authoritative ledger
  from the clause-complete corpus and diffs against this one.

### Pack or artifact representation
- Required semantic distinctions: primitive identity, never family membership.
  Family grouping may organise rows but can never substitute for primitive
  identity or exact affected membership.
- Branches and alternatives: hook selection uses exact structured hook identity.
  Unconstrained substring matching is rejected, with negative tests for
  near-matches, prefixes, suffixes and unrelated strings sharing a token.
- Timing, lifecycle, and termination: carried by the individual primitives —
  planar-return and declared-window clocks, item-instance persistence,
  hit-point and death lifecycle.
- Provenance and ownership requirements: every row names an owning bead. An
  'owned' row may never name the engine epic root eshyra-olc5; a
  'proposed-new-bead' row may, and carries a proposed title and parent.

### Cross-kind and cross-surface checks
- Related kinds or subsystems: engine:F1..F10 plus the four cross-family
  primitive beads eshyra-o9bd.19.5.5.3, .19.5.6.3, .19.5.8.3 and .19.5.11.3.
- Corpus-wide predicates or reconciliation: 2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md
  classifies eshyra-2n1t and all thirteen children plus eshyra-b69j.13,
  eshyra-o9bd.18.7 and .18.7.8. The epic itself is PREMATURE / OVERSTATED
  UMBRELLA CLOSURE; eight children are INCOMPLETE INTEGRATION. Corrective
  ownership routes .6, .7, .9 and .12 to the four new beads.

### Engine capability
- Required capabilities: all ten engine:F* families, at primitive granularity,
  several rows per family.
- Existing owner beads: the ten family epics under eshyra-olc5 own rows that fit
  a family; the four cross-family beads own the rest.
- Known missing capability handling: 'known-missing-source-clause' evidence must
  POSITIVELY PROVE absence from the pack. An empty query result is never
  accepted as proof.

### Reference execution or executable proof
- Real artifact or pack-driven scenarios: readiness-artifact evidence executes
  against the committed pack; code evidence proves the named symbol exists in
  @eshyra/core; bead evidence resolves through bd.
- Negative and fail-closed scenarios: unknown, duplicate, ambiguous, untraceable
  or missing query bindings are rejected; near-match hook identities are
  rejected; recursive stored-count/total fields are rejected at any depth;
  unexpectedly empty results fail per evidence kind.
- Replay, rollback, or determinism requirements: bd resolution SKIPS GRACEFULLY
  when the binary is absent, so the suite never depends on bd being installed.

### Approved residuals
- Source ambiguities: none owned here.
- Deliberately model-adjudicated boundaries: none owned here.
- Explicitly unsupported scope: implementing any engine capability. This bead
  inventories and reconciles; implementation belongs to the decomposition and
  certification tasks under eshyra-olc5.

### Closure evidence
- Generated membership query: per-row query identities resolved through the
  per-source evidence resolvers.
- Permanent regression evidence:
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts — exact structured hook
  identity, proof-of-absence, query-binding rejection, the pinned seven non-pack
  primitives, proposed-row representability, and rejection of the old overloaded
  pack evidence.
- Finding-registry aliases: sol:CAP-007, sol:CAP-014.

1. Evidence became a per-source discriminated union with per-kind resolvers and
   per-kind expected-result semantics. Reason: the sole evaluator read
   data.executionReadiness, which exists on MAGIC-ITEM RECORDS ONLY, so every
   row across all ten families was proved by an evaluator that could not see its
   subject matter.
2. Exact structured hook identity replaced substring matching. Reason:
   text.includes() assigns hooks to the wrong primitive on near-matches.
3. Empty results must be positively justified per evidence kind. Reason: absence
   of evidence was passing as evidence of absence.
4. Rows bind to named query identities; positional or family association is
   rejected. Reason: results could not be traced back to their row.
5. eshyra-2n1t reclassified as premature/overstated umbrella closure. Reason:
   the closing PR claimed executable mechanics for all 240 magic items and zero
   deep-audit findings; narrow child acceptance does not validate a global
   claim later proven false.

Prior review approval does NOT survive these changes. A fresh full review is
required.

- **CANONICAL PRIMITIVE ROSTER.** A committed, versioned roster of
  (capabilityId, primitive); the validator asserts exact set equality. Missing
  and unexpected rows both fail, tested both directions. Adding a primitive now
  requires deliberately editing the roster.
- **AUDIT-FINDING EVIDENCE MUST BE RELEVANT, NOT MERELY RESOLVABLE.** A committed
  alias-to-subject table grounds each citation, and every audit-finding evidence
  item carries a per-row relevance statement that may not be constant or
  derivable from the primitive name. The prior head cited indep:001..012
  round-robin (histogram 3,3,3,3,3,3,3,2,2,2,2,2); citations that no finding
  supports are now dropped rather than invented.
- **KNOWN-MISSING CLAUSES PROVE REAL ABSENCE.** A known-missing row names a REAL
  source anchor and proves both that the source material exists there and that
  no pack record or clause projects it. Synthetic `SRD5.1:<primitive>` markers
  are gone. Rows without a real anchor carry evidence-underived status that
  fails the closure predicate.

  resolving bead-evidence entry on that row; syntax alone is insufficient.
- **QUERY BINDING IS UNIQUE WITHIN A ROW** as well as across rows.
