  `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>` with four non-empty segments. The
  prior head emitted `obl:::` with empty sourceRef and locator, which silently
  broke the cross-PR join.

GREEN DEFINITION — shared verbatim by 19.1.4, 19.1.5, 19.4.5 and 19.5.12. A
clause is green ONLY when all eight hold:
  1. The complete source clause has been identified.
  2. Every deterministic branch is projected.
  3. All source and derived fields are provenanced.
  4. Every required capability is identified.
  5. The engine implementation exists.
  6. An executable conformance scenario proves the intended outcome.
  7. Runtime lookup can find the canonical clause.
  8. Unsupported portions fail closed.
A representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green. The Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but explicitly
did NOT prove the semantic appropriateness of every free-form effect.

The residual semantic check — proving each free-form effect is semantically
APPROPRIATE, not merely reference-resolvable — belongs here and in 19.6.1.

generated ledger/predicate is authoritative. No acceptance test may require a
hand-copied number (e.g. 391, 399, 77, 79).
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.

GREEN DEFINITION — shared verbatim by 19.1.4, 19.1.5, 19.4.5 and 19.5.12. A
clause is green ONLY when all eight hold:
  1. The complete source clause has been identified.
  2. Every deterministic branch is projected.
  3. All source and derived fields are provenanced.
  4. Every required capability is identified.
  5. The engine implementation exists.
  6. An executable conformance scenario proves the intended outcome.
  7. Runtime lookup can find the canonical clause.
  8. Unsupported portions fail closed.
A representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green. The Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but explicitly
did NOT prove the semantic appropriateness of every free-form effect.
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.

title: Add bidirectional source support, field provenance, and resolved ownership
description:
Implement source-to-output AND output-to-source validation at clause and field
level.

Root cause: coverage gates are source->output only. Nothing proves that an
emitted value is supported by the source it cites, so fabricated or
editorially-repaired content passes through a plausible locator. That is exactly
how table:starting-wealth-by-class — hardcoded PHB content emitted by the
importer's emit.ts startingWealthTable() — acquired "SRD 5.1 p. 38" provenance
and the CC-BY-4.0 SRD attribution block despite no starting-wealth text existing
anywhere in SRD 5.1.

Every output value must be exactly one of: directly sourced from a pinned source
span; deterministically derived from pinned source spans with derivation
metadata; supplemental content with a distinct source/license identity; or an
explicit unresolved source defect / campaign ruling. No hand-authored value may
inherit the SRD license/provenance block by default.

Closes findings: SOL-008, SOL-009, CAP-009, CAP-010, F-19, Fable F1, Fable F4,
Fable F5, Fable F7.
design:
Pack evidence on main @4384f25:
- table:starting-wealth-by-class carries source "SRD 5.1 p. 38" + full CC-BY SRD
  attribution; content is not in SRD 5.1. Consumed by srdStartingWealth.ts and
  finalizeCharacter.ts, so removal is a coordinated change (see B1).
- 7 container records cite p. 69 while capacity prints on p. 70.
- table:scrying carries invented "Basis"/"Circumstance" headers.
- acolyte choices[].sourceText labels are synthesized, not verbatim.

Coordinate span identity with A1 clause identity.

- Every emitted source-backed value cites every contributing page/span, not just the first.
- Derived and compiler-authored values identify their derivation and are never presented as verbatim source.
- Supplemental content carries a separate source and license identity from SRD-sourced content.
- Ambiguous and unresolved ownership cannot satisfy the clean-coverage gate.
- Continuations, inherited text, spell-list memberships, class prerequisite data, and flattened records are fully provenanced at field level.
- A fabricated record with a plausible locator fails the gate (negative test using the starting-wealth case).

title: Implement shared cross-kind mechanic primitives and parser normalization
description:
Replace duplicated spell / creature / hazard / feature / magic-item parsing of
recurring mechanics with shared normalized primitives implemented against the A1
IR.

Root cause: separate projectors drift. The half-damage-on-success bug reproduced
independently in creatures, hazards, spells, features, and ancestries is direct
proof — the same printed phrase ("half as much damage on a successful one")
projects differently depending on which projector saw it.

Shared primitives required for at least: attacks and alternate attack modes;
checks, contests, and ability alternatives; saves, multiple saves,
failure/success outcomes, and repeat saves; damage/healing, riders, recurrence,
pools, reductions, and alternatives; action, bonus action, reaction,
legendary-action, and controlled-entity budgets; resources, usage limits,
recharge, reset, and scaling; geometry, range, targets, cover, movement, and
forced movement; conditions, active effects, duration, immunity, termination,
and concentration; options, variants, prerequisites, selection ownership, and
conditional grants; entity creation, summoning, transformation, ownership, and
destruction; currency, inventory, XP, downtime, and persistent ledgers.

Normalization required BEFORE semantic parsing: Unicode minus / en-dash / hyphen
variants, punctuation, range notation, multiplication symbols, parenthetical
alternatives, and wrapped headings.

Closes findings: F-25, F-27, F-28, F-29, F-31, F-32, F-34, F-01, F-08, SOL-005,
SOL-006, SOL-007, CAP-003, CAP-004, Fable F2, Fable F3.

prose mentions half damage but carry no typed success branch —
creature 77, hazard 9, spell 9, plus ancestry:dragonborn,
feature:hunter:superior-hunters-defense, feature:monk:evasion and 5 more
(8 "other"). Typed success fields that DO exist in the pack today:
damageOnSuccess, onSuccessfulSave, successfulSaveDamage, noDamageInsteadOfHalf,
successReductionDice, onSuccess, onSuccessOrFailure.

NOTE: the plan states "79 creature + 8 hazard". A coarse whole-record regex over
main gives 77 creature / 9 hazard. The exact membership MUST be re-derived by a
committed clause-level predicate, not copied from the plan or from this note.
Spell and ancestry/feature members are additional to the plan's stated counts and
must not be dropped.
acceptance_criteria:
- Save branches, attacks, damage, range, geometry, usage, duration, and alternatives share one cross-kind projection path.
- The same source phrase cannot project differently by record kind without an explicit, reviewed override.
- Corpus-wide mismatch predicates exist for every recurring mechanical pattern, not per-example assertions.
- Regression coverage includes every brittle parser shape from Opus F-25 through F-35.
- Unicode-minus, alternate range notation, and parenthetical alternate bonuses cannot silently drop a value.

title: Define the source-clause semantic IR and completeness contracts
description:

that every mechanics-bearing clause must satisfy.

Root cause: no semantic unit smaller than the record exists, so partial
projection is indistinguishable from complete projection.

Every clause must carry: stable clause identity; exact source span or spans;
semantic owner and record owner; clause kind; trigger and eligibility predicates;
activation / action-economy cost; targets and geometry; checks, attacks, saves,

### Scope of this PR
This PR delivers the per-clause completeness contract ONLY.

Removed 2026-07-27 under the second churn stop, user-approved:

  and record authority, the evidence taxonomy including

its authority, because the source census is deferred. `obligations.ts` is now a

stub remains that could read as authoritative while proving nothing.

### Source obligation
- The clause references an obligation by `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>`.
- ONE OBLIGATION PER CLAUSE is the load-bearing invariant. A clause discharges
  exactly one source obligation; that obligation may carry many facets. Source
  material with separable mechanics decomposes into multiple clauses.
- An obligation reference that does not RESOLVE must fail closed on every
  dimension it feeds. A missing or unknown obligation ID may never yield a
  satisfied dimension.

### Per-clause representation
- Composable facets, never universal clause-kind assumptions. A specialized
  facet transitively implies its base mechanic, so `save-with-damage` cannot
  certify `saves: []`.
- `duration`, `recurrence`, `repeatChecks`, `immunityWindows` and `termination`
  are canonical facets, required exactly when an obligation declares them.
- Canonical base requirements — `identity`, `sourceSpans`, `provenance`,
  `semanticOwner`, `recordOwner` — apply to every obligation, cannot be removed
  or overridden, and extensions are additive only. No caller-supplied contract
  can weaken them.
- ALTERNATIVES MUST FORM A COMPLETE PARTITION. For `choice` and `variant`, at
  least one alternative is insufficient: the exclusion graph must be symmetric
  and fully connected across the alternative set. A disconnected graph is not a
  set of mutually exclusive alternatives.
- EVIDENCE EQUALITY MUST BE ORDER-INDEPENDENT. Structural comparison, not
  serialized-string comparison; two evidence values differing only by property
  insertion order are the same evidence.

### Readiness dimensions
- CAPTURED, PROJECTED, SUPPORTED and DISCOVERABLE report INDEPENDENTLY. A clause
  may be semantically complete and unsupported; that distinction is the point.
- CAPTURED is satisfiable only by `source-span` or `authoritative-input`
  evidence tied to the obligation. `audit-finding` and
  `known-missing-source-clause` evidence identify a gap and can never close one.
- Capability resolution failures report against SUPPORTED, never PROJECTED.
- `EngineCapability` is the closed union `engine:F1`..`engine:F10`. Owning beads
  are the family epics under `eshyra-olc5`, which retain historical
  `eshyra-o9bd.19.5.*` IDs, so ownership is judged by actual bead identity and
  never by ID prefix.
- Resolvers (`CapabilityResolver`, `SourceEvidenceResolver`, `DiscoveryResolver`)
  are injected interfaces with test doubles, so the evaluator consumes evidence
  it cannot forge. Real implementations are out of scope.

predicates, a ledger closure predicate, a prose guard, and CAPTURED satisfying

list when a lookup does not resolve, so "no failures" reads as "satisfied".

The first dispatch spec for this bead told the implementer that "a clause that is

### Invariant classes added 2026-07-26 (contract-grounded review at 1b33b18)

These are now normative and are what the next fresh full review must test.

- **ONE OBLIGATION PER CLAUSE.** The load-bearing invariant. A clause discharges
  exactly one source obligation; an obligation may carry many facets. Where a
  source sentence holds separable mechanics it decomposes into multiple CLAUSES.
  Enforced in the evaluator (`missing-obligation-reference`,
  `multiple-obligation-references`). This is what makes per-obligation
  evaluation sound: obligations can no longer share a clause-global atom, and
  hoisting option-local mechanics now fails validation.
- **CANONICAL BASE REQUIREMENTS ARE EXECUTABLE.** identity, sourceSpans,
  provenance, semanticOwner and recordOwner are validated for every obligation
  and cannot be removed or overridden, with an adversarial matrix that corrupts
  each in turn. They had been lost when facets replaced kind contracts.
- **FACET IMPLICATION CLOSURE.** A specialized facet implies its base mechanic
  transitively (`FACET_IMPLICATIONS`), so save-with-damage cannot certify
  `saves: []`. Generated removal tests cover every specialized facet.

  canonical facets, not caller-side extensions.
- **ALTERNATIVES PROVE EXCLUSION.** The exclusion graph is validated for symmetry
  and partition; branches and alternatives bind to projected atom identities.

  validated against origin-appropriate evidence; synthetic locator divergence is
  rejected; repeated clauses at one anchor carry a stable occurrence locator.

  family + record ownership; a raw scope literal cannot be passed, and a clause
  from another record cannot satisfy this scope.
- **CAPTURED REQUIRES SOURCE EVIDENCE.** Only source-span or authoritative-input
  evidence satisfies CAPTURED. audit-finding and known-missing-source-clause
  evidence identify a gap and can never close one.
- **ENGINE CAPABILITY IS A CLOSED IDENTITY.** `EngineCapability` is the union
  engine:F1..engine:F10, validated, with the two capability-evidence surfaces
  reconciled so stored evidence cannot drift from requiredEngineCapabilities.

- **VALIDATED ARTIFACTS ARE IMMUTABLE.** Registry records, evidence arrays,

  symptoms of that, not independent defects.
- This PR now delivers the clause completeness CONTRACT only. obligations.ts is
  a 13-line non-authoritative ObligationSource lookup interface; no validating
  stub remains that could read as authoritative.

### Source obligation
- Source membership: obligations held in an `ObligationRegistry`, keyed
  `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>`, for the scope under evaluation.
  Never the set a projector happened to emit.
- Membership derivation: `ObligationOrigin` is the closed union
  `source-extraction | curated-specification | audit-finding`. It cannot be
  `projector`, so a producer can never be the authority for which obligations
  existed. Every identity component is validated against origin-appropriate
  evidence; synthetic locator divergence is rejected.
- Source spans or authoritative inputs: `ObligationEvidence` of kind
  `source-span` or `authoritative-input`. Repeated clauses at one anchor carry a
  stable occurrence locator so they remain distinguishable.
- Complete obligations covered: this bead defines the obligation BOUNDARY, the
  facet vocabulary, and closure evaluation. Enumerating the SRD corpus's
  obligations is `eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1`.

### Pack or artifact representation
- ONE OBLIGATION PER CLAUSE is the load-bearing invariant. A clause discharges
  exactly one source obligation; that obligation may carry many facets. Source
  material with separable mechanics decomposes into multiple clauses. Enforced
  by `missing-obligation-reference` and `multiple-obligation-references`.
- Required semantic distinctions: composable facets, never universal clause-kind
  assumptions. A specialized facet transitively implies its base mechanic
  (`FACET_IMPLICATIONS`), so `save-with-damage` cannot certify `saves: []`.
- Branches and alternatives: the exclusion graph is validated for symmetry and
  partition; branches and alternatives bind to projected atom identities and may
  target scalar mechanics as well as shells.
- Timing, lifecycle, and termination: `duration`, `recurrence`, `repeatChecks`,
  `immunityWindows` and `termination` are canonical facets, required exactly
  when an obligation declares them.
- Provenance and ownership: `identity`, `sourceSpans`, `provenance`,
  `semanticOwner` and `recordOwner` are canonical base requirements applied to
  every obligation. They cannot be removed or overridden; extensions are
  additive only, and no caller-supplied contract can weaken them.

### Cross-kind and cross-surface checks
- Related kinds or subsystems: all fifteen mechanics-bearing record families
  carry applicability contracts; facets are shared across kinds so one mechanic
  cannot be modelled twice with divergent semantics.
- Corpus-wide predicates: `evaluateObligationClosure` consumes an OPAQUE
  validated scope — a raw object literal cannot be passed — enforces exact
  family and record ownership, reports unexpected claims, and reports UNCLAIMED
  obligations. Family applicability, obligation membership, per-obligation
  completeness and aggregate family closure are four distinct concepts.

### Engine capability
- Required capabilities: `EngineCapability` is the closed union
  `engine:F1`..`engine:F10`, validated.
- Existing owner beads: the ten family epics under `eshyra-olc5`. They retain
  historical `eshyra-o9bd.19.5.*` IDs, so ownership is judged by actual bead
  identity and never by ID prefix.
- Known missing capability handling: capability resolution failures report
  against SUPPORTED, never PROJECTED. A clause may be semantically complete and
  unsupported; that distinction is the point. Stored capability evidence cannot
  drift from `requiredEngineCapabilities`.

### Reference execution or executable proof
- Real artifact or pack-driven scenarios: deliberately out of scope. This bead
  is design and type contract only; `CapabilityResolver`, `SourceEvidenceResolver`
  and `DiscoveryResolver` are injected interfaces with test doubles, so the
  evaluator consumes evidence it cannot forge.
- Negative and fail-closed scenarios: adversarial tests T1-T8, each named for the
  threat it defeats; an unremovable base-requirement removal matrix; generated
  removal tests for every specialized facet; audit-only and known-missing
  CAPTURED rejection; mutation attempts against deep-frozen artifacts.
- CAPTURED is satisfiable only by `source-span` or `authoritative-input`
  evidence. `audit-finding` and `known-missing-source-clause` evidence identify
  a gap and can never close one.
- Replay, rollback, determinism: not in scope; they belong to engine
  certification under `eshyra-olc5.2`.

### Approved residuals
- Source ambiguities: the three deliberate ambiguities remain under
  `eshyra-jhpt.6` / `.7`.
- Deliberately model-adjudicated boundaries: the `model-adjudication` facet.
- Explicitly unsupported scope, each owned by a named bead and NOT a defect in
  this PR:
  - exact source VALUES and relationships — `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.10`. The authority
    here states semantic shapes; encoding values (save ability and DC, damage
    amount, target count, duration unit, reset timing, transition payload)
    requires a source-value model and its extraction.
  - producer and readiness-gate integration — `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1.2.1`.
  - production census and real resolver implementations — `eshyra-s38f`.
  - cross-PR identity adapters or parity tests — `eshyra-gvzx`.
  - importer migration, corpus recompilation, engine registry implementation.

### Closure evidence
- Generated membership query: `evaluateObligationClosure` over a validated scope.
- Permanent regression evidence: `packages/core/test/clauseIrObligations.test.ts`
  and `packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts`.
- Finding-registry aliases: `indep:001`, `opus:F-06`, `opus:F-27`, `sol:CAP-001`.

### Cross-PR integration boundary — actual state
`obligationId` is `obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>`. PR #477 emits and
validates the same shape for genuine source obligations and keeps evidence items
in a separate `ev:::` namespace, so #475 and #477 are mechanically joinable.
PR #476 does not participate: it uses
`MembershipIdentity{recordKey, clauseId?, path?, sourceSpan?}` with no
`obligationId`. Bridging it is `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7`. ADR 0020 states this and
does not claim alignment that does not exist.
*** DESIGN_INVALIDATED — PR #475 STOPPED 2026-07-27 ***
Invalidated PR: #475      Final head: 68e5253f0a41aae5a4aff95564c38ceff8d08f79
This bead is NOT successfully completed. It is superseded and retained for
history and salvage.

NEW DEFECT CLASSES DISCOVERED, in order:
  r1  projector graded its own completeness; obligations not projection-local
  r2  callers could bypass every canonical completeness requirement
  r3  universal clause-kind contracts imposed invalid semantics (damage-less
      save unrepresentable)
  r4  readiness dimensions self-asserted rather than evidenced
  r5  record-family arrays mistaken for family closure
  r6  canonical base requirements silently lost in the facet re-architecture
  r7  specialized facets not closed under their base mechanic
  r8  obligation identity not bound to authoritative evidence
  r9  aggregate closure bypassed its scope and crossed record boundaries
  r10 audit-only evidence could satisfy CAPTURED
  r11 exact source semantics remained caller-supplied, not registry-authoritative
  r12 CAPTURED satisfied on a MISSING or UNKNOWN obligation id (fail-open)
  r13 choice/variant alternatives passed with a disconnected exclusion graph
  r14 evidence equality depended on JSON property insertion order

ASSUMPTIONS DISPROVEN:
  * that an obligation registry can be authoritative while the source census
    that would underwrite it is deferred;
  * that a universal clause IR can be specified before the obligation/projection
    trust boundary is demonstrated on real procedures;
  * that shape facets can stand in for exact source values and relationships;
  * that "the mechanism exists" implies "the mechanism binds".

POTENTIALLY SALVAGEABLE (design input, not code to extend): ADR reasoning on
clause-level completeness; the CAPTURED/PROJECTED/SUPPORTED/DISCOVERABLE
separation; the structured failure vocabulary; cardinality and fail-closed
predicates; the T1-T8 adversarial cases; the worked examples showing why
projector-authored obligations are unsafe; and the one-obligation-per-clause
invariant as a hypothesis to re-test.

DO NOT PRESUME SURVIVES: the universal obligation identity, the contract
composition model, or the evaluator architecture.

WHY LOCAL PATCHING STOPPED: each round produced a NEW defect class after a
material contract change and a fresh full review. The shared root cause was not
implementation quality — unsettled concepts were GENERALIZED ACROSS THE CORPUS
before their trust boundaries were proven by a small number of concrete
source-to-execution examples. Successor work inverts that order: prove the
boundary on five real procedures first (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14), generalize after.

SUCCESSOR STRUCTURE
  F1 eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14  source-obligation identity and discharge proof
  F2 eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15  truthful audit-fact registry, no membership claims
  F3 eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7 + eshyra-o9bd.19.1.8  exact finding membership (reused)
  F4 eshyra-o9bd.19.1.16  capability evidence semantics
  F5 eshyra-olc5.5        bootstrap capability inventory rebuild

THE BRANCH IS RETAINED as historical and salvage evidence. It must not be merged
and must not be treated as an accepted contract by any downstream bead.

title: Build a clause-complete semantic compiler and truthful readiness gates
description:
Path A of the plan's Phase 1. Replace atom-presence readiness with a
source-clause semantic IR, shared cross-kind mechanic primitives, bidirectional
provenance, in-band execution readiness, and audits rebuilt on the clause model.

Root cause this epic addresses: the pipeline is strongest at extracting records
and preserving prose, but treats a record containing ANY mechanics atom (a save,
a damage expression, a condition mention, a reset, a table link) as modeled. A
feature, spell, creature entry, or hazard therefore appears covered while its
procedure is mostly prose.

Execution order within the epic: A1 and A3 may run in parallel once stable clause
and source identities are agreed; A2 implements against A1; A4 stabilizes with
E0; A5 lands last.
acceptance_criteria:
- No record family can report complete from mechanics-atom presence.
- Captured / projected / engine-supported / discoverable are separately represented in pack data and in reports.
- Recurring mechanics are parsed once by shared primitives, not re-parsed per record kind.
- Coverage is proven in both directions (source->output and output->source) at field level.
- The bundle emits a coverage-depth matrix proving semantic — not sampled — review for every mechanics-bearing family.
notes:
Bead-writing contract (plan §VI) — this bead must state: exact scope membership
(explicit records/clauses or a deterministic query that enumerates them), root
cause, required invariant, source evidence, pack evidence, engine boundary,
regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias
list, and completion proof. "Fix the examples above" is not acceptable scope;
close the whole semantic class and reconcile exact membership.

title: Close the 2026-07-24 SRD audit and establish clause-complete pack execution
description:
Umbrella for the repair program answering the 2026-07-24 multi-model SRD audit
(independent Sol review, Opus 5 review + creature/magic-item amendment,
GPT-5.6-Sol agent review, Fable 5 review). Source plan:
/mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md.

The program satisfies two independent requirements:

1. Holistic correction — repair the construction model, compiler boundaries,
   validation approach, and engine-capability accounting that let whole classes
   of defect survive. The semantic unit becomes a source-backed clause, not a
   record; records become materialized views grouping clauses.
2. Finding closure — every numbered finding from all four reviews maps to at
   least one bead with regression evidence that prevents recurrence.

Four meanings currently collapsed into "modeled" must be separated and reported
independently per clause: CAPTURED (source clause present), PROJECTED (complete
deterministic meaning represented), SUPPORTED (engine implements every required
primitive), DISCOVERABLE (DM/tools can find the canonical rule and its
execution/adjudication boundary). A clause is not playable because it is
captured or partially projected.

Blocks re-freeze: eshyra-2zyy (restore SRD thaw-note gating) and eshyra-o9bd.14
(regenerate + re-freeze) must not proceed until this epic closes.

Verified against main @4384f25 on 2026-07-24 (packages/core/data/rules-packs/
rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, 1,813 records).
design:
Parent selection: plan offered eshyra-o9bd or eshyra-ajpc. eshyra-ajpc is CLOSED
(all 6 children merged via PR #377), so it is no longer the designated
audit-finding parent — this epic hangs under eshyra-o9bd, whose re-freeze bar
this work gates.

Existing beads must be LINKED, not duplicated. Reconciled at creation time:
- eshyra-ajpc      CLOSED — do not use as parent.
- eshyra-2n1t      CLOSED epic "engine F1-F10" — see the E epic's taxonomy warning.
- eshyra-2n1t.1/.2 CLOSED design decisions (D1 multiclass scope -> ADR 0018; D2 creation-variant policy).
- eshyra-b69j.13   CLOSED (PR #311, level-1 equipment/proficiency choice flow).
- eshyra-o9bd.18.* CLOSED.
- eshyra-o9bd.14   OPEN — regenerate + re-freeze; must depend on this program.
- eshyra-o9bd.16   OPEN — FINAL max-effort re-audit; is the natural home of V3.
- eshyra-jhpt.6/.7 OPEN — the deliberate campaign-ruling/ambiguity implementation
  that the three explicit SRD ambiguities remain under. Do NOT reclassify those
  three as engine defects.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every finding in the plan's §IV coverage matrix maps to a completed bead and a committed regression test.
- Every source clause and every structured output field is bidirectionally reconciled.
- No unresolved or ambiguous source ownership is counted as complete coverage.
- Every deterministic clause is completely projected, or carries a precise in-band non-engine disposition.
- Every required engine capability is green or covered by an approved explicit house-rule/design dependency.
- No pending capability lacks a real, open bead.
- A fresh audit bundle receives zero repeat findings from independent max-level reviews.
- No semantically sampled record family remains in the coverage-depth matrix.
notes:
Standing caution (bd memory o9bd-reverify-pack-before-implementing-children):
re-verify the committed pack before implementing ANY child. Successive audit
rounds have repeatedly named deficiencies that a later snapshot already fixed.
Records use the "key" field, not "id".

Bead-writing contract (plan §VI) — this bead must state: exact scope membership
(explicit records/clauses or a deterministic query that enumerates them), root
cause, required invariant, source evidence, pack evidence, engine boundary,
regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias
list, and completion proof. "Fix the examples above" is not acceptable scope;
close the whole semantic class and reconcile exact membership.
*** STRUCTURAL REVISION (post-review) ***
1. PACK vs ENGINE split. engine:F1..F10 implementation moved OUT to the new
   top-level epic eshyra-olc5 ("Reopen deterministic engine completeness under the
   clause-capability contract"). This epic keeps clause-complete pack data,
   source authority, truthful readiness, and PROOF THAT EVERY ENGINE REQUIREMENT
   HAS AN OWNER (19.5.1 bootstrap ledger, 19.5.12 authoritative ledger). An
   engine-pending clause is not automatically a pack defect. The engine beads
   retain their eshyra-o9bd.19.5.* IDs for history — judge parentage by the tree,
   not the ID prefix. The release/re-freeze gate depends on BOTH epics.
2. Ledger lifecycle made honest: 19.5.1 is a BOOTSTRAP ledger built from
   artifacts + code + beads + findings + known-missing clauses (a ledger derived
   from the pack alone would inherit the pack's blind spots); 19.5.12 is the
   AUTHORITATIVE ledger regenerated from the clause-complete corpus and diffed
   against the bootstrap.
3. engine:F1..F10 converted to epics. Children are NOT pre-created — the
   bootstrap ledger produces membership first, and children are organized by
   reusable engine primitive and executable scenario, never by hook count.
4. Finding registry created EARLY (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6), before C/D implementation, not near
   closure.
5. Closure chain corrected and serialized:
   19.6.1 -> 19.6.2 -> 19.6.3 (automated gates) -> eshyra-o9bd.16 (independent
   re-audit) -> 19.6.4 (certify) -> eshyra-o9bd.14 (re-freeze) -> eshyra-2zyy.
6. Starting Wealth DECIDED: remove from the SRD pack; do not re-home by label.

CANONICAL ALIAS PREFIXES — never a bare "F1" or "CAP-001":
  engine:F1 .. engine:F10     pack executionReadiness engineHooks[].engine families
  fable:F1 .. fable:F8        Fable 5 audit findings
  opus:F-01 .. opus:F-35      Opus 5 original + amended audit findings
  sol:CAP-001 .. sol:CAP-014  GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit findings
  indep:001 .. indep:012      independent review (formerly "SOL-001..012"; renamed
                              so it stops colliding with the sol: model-name prefix)

COUNT HYGIENE: every number in this bead is a SNAPSHOT at commit 4384f25. The
generated ledger/predicate is authoritative. No acceptance test may require a
hand-copied number (e.g. 391, 399, 77, 79).
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.
*** ENGINE CERTIFICATION NOW GATES RE-FREEZE (2026-07-25) ***
Earlier framing allowed the pack to be re-frozen with engine work still open,
on the theory that this is a pack-data audit rather than an engine-completion
audit. That is superseded for every deterministic clause that is a DIRECT INPUT
to engine execution.

eshyra-olc5's reference-engine certification now blocks eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1, and
therefore the entire closure chain down to eshyra-o9bd.14. See the revised
nine-point green definition above.

The pack/engine SEPARATION still holds as a modeling discipline — an
engine-pending clause is not automatically a pack defect, and the two questions
stay distinguishable. What changed is the freeze gate, not the taxonomy.
*** ADR 0020 NARROWING (2026-07-31) — THIS EPIC'S RE-FREEZE BAR IS REPLACED ***
Authority: ADR 0020 ("Prior assumptions" item 4) and the integrated transition
design docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/
2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md section 5.9 — the accepted deliverable
of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). Recorded as accepted authority; no
code was changed by this bead update.

The line above in these notes — "AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING
DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES" — is WITHDRAWN. It requires a global negative the corpus
cannot support. Its replacement is the nine-condition truthfulness bar recorded
in full on eshyra-o9bd.14 and referenced by eshyra-2zyy: source fidelity;
truthful provenance; deterministic reproducibility; truthful in-band scope for
every audit and readiness artifact; durable disposition of known findings;
correctness of positively selected capabilities; no known source invention; no
unowned live runtime safety contract; and explicit statement of unresolved
discovery and adjudication limits. Explicitly not required: global deterministic
closure, universal discovery completeness, zero engine-pending clauses, or any
corpus-wide negative claim. The nine-point GREEN definition survives as a
per-clause quality definition for clauses positively selected for deterministic
execution; it is no longer a corpus-wide gate. eshyra-olc5 carries the matching
engine-side narrowing and the bounded meaning of engine:F1-F10.

THIS EPIC NOW ALSO HOSTS THE ADR 0020 RULE-AWARENESS TRANSITION (design section
4, "Discovery ... this transition program under eshyra-o9bd.19"), as siblings of
the .19.7 handoff and the .19.8 design:

  eshyra-o9bd.19.9  W7  diagnostic fixture corpus (design sections 10-11)
  eshyra-o9bd.19.10 W8  offline discovery stage harness (Phase 1)
  eshyra-o9bd.19.11 W9  runtime shadow trace integration (Phase 2)
  eshyra-o9bd.19.12 W10 context-packet intervention (Phase 3)
  eshyra-o9bd.19.13 W11 eshyra-jhpt read-interface consumption (design section 8)
  eshyra-o9bd.19.14 W14 artifact dispositions (design sections 5.1-5.6)
  eshyra-o9bd.19.15 W15 held-out and live-play evaluation (Phase 4)

with W13 (capability-contract normalization) at eshyra-olc5.6, and W12
(campaign rules and rulings) unchanged under eshyra-jhpt.1-.9 plus amendments
A1-A4. Campaign-rule persistence and ruling lifecycle do not move out of
eshyra-jhpt under any of these items.

title: Dispatch: ambiguity preflight before RNG; dedupe RulesAmbiguity type (attempt 6)
description:
Third review-response dispatch for eshyra-jw56 (PR #470). Two required findings.
Read `bd show eshyra-jw56` for the design history. Branch from the current tip of
`eshyra-jw56` (d37e7bd).

Worktree: `.worktrees/<this-bead-id>`, branch `<this-bead-id>`. Work only there.

## Fix 1 — an ambiguity failure must consume zero RNG

### The defect (confirmed by the supervisor, do not re-derive)

In `useItem` (`packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`):

- line ~1884 `readItemState`
- line ~1886 `createInitialItemState(packRef, hit.record, { variantId, rng: input.rng, resolveTable })`
  — **consumes `input.rng`** for dice-derived economy maxima, spell-store
  `initialLevels`, and other initialization rolls
- line ~1908 `selectStateTransition(...)` — where `ItemStateAmbiguityError` throws

So a gated operation on a stateful item with no `item_state` row rolls dice
*before* it fails. The DB transaction rolls back; a seeded `Rng` does not. The
stream advances and replay diverges. Cube of Force does not expose this (its
gated transition is not reachable from `inactive`), but the contract now allows
a gate from any state including the initial one.

### Established facts (verified, build on these)

- `createInitialItemState` sets
  `machineState: String(obj(mechanics.stateMachine, ...).initial)`, so the
  machine's **declared `initial`** is exactly the state the later real selection
  will see. A preflight against `initial` cannot diverge from execution.
- Lazy init only happens under `if (stateful && state === undefined)`. When an
  `item_state` row exists, nothing between `readItemState` and
  `selectStateTransition` consumes RNG (`validateItemStateForRecord` takes only
  `{ resolveTable }`). **The RNG-before-gate window is exactly the lazy-init
  branch.**
- Operation-id resolution is at line ~1793 and the execution-readiness check at
  ~1840-1874 — both already before lazy init.

### Required implementation

Insert the ambiguity preflight **immediately before** the
`createInitialItemState` call, running only when that branch is about to be
taken. Use the machine's declared `initial` as the preflight source state.

Do **not** duplicate transition-matching logic. Extract the matching half of
`selectStateTransition` into a pure helper (e.g. `matchStateTransition`)
returning the selected raw transition/destination/outcome, and have both
`selectStateTransition` and the preflight call it. A second copy of the matching
rules that can drift is explicitly rejected by the reviewer.

The preflight must throw **only** `ItemStateAmbiguityError`. If the shared
matcher raises anything else (malformed machine, invalid destination, no
transition from that state, missing machineState), swallow it in the preflight
and let the normal path raise it in its existing position — that is what keeps
error precedence unchanged. The error keeps `ambiguityId`, `question`, all
declared `interpretationIds`, `owner: 'campaign-ruling'`, and pack ref +
operation id in the message.

**Do not** implement this by catching `ItemStateAmbiguityError` after
initialization. The RNG must never be invoked.

This placement preserves every precedence the reviewer listed — confirm each:
invalid operation ids (~1793) and readiness failures (~1840) still precede it;
persisted-state validation and `inert`/`nonmagical` lifecycle checks only apply
when a row exists, in which case the preflight does not run at all; non-stateful
items never lazily initialize; a machine-less stateful item makes the matcher
return undefined and the preflight a no-op.

### Required regression test

A schema-valid stateful magic item with **no** persisted `item_state` row, a
dice-defined economy maximum (so initialization would roll), and an
ambiguity-gated `via` self-transition **from the declared initial state**, plus
the ambiguity declaration with both interpretations. Drive it with an `Rng`
whose `nextInt` both counts calls and throws. Assert:

1. `ItemStateAmbiguityError` is thrown;
2. `ambiguityId`, `question`, `interpretationIds`, `owner` are all present;
3. **the RNG was called zero times**;
4. no `item_state` row exists afterward (query it directly);
5. inventory quantity, economies, and timers are unchanged.

Keep the existing already-initialized regression as-is. Add a positive companion
asserting an *unambiguous* operation on the same fixture still initializes lazily
and consumes RNG as expected — this is what stops the defect being "fixed" by
disabling initialization.

## Fix 2 — one canonical `RulesAmbiguity`

`packages/core/src/rules/rulesAmbiguities.ts` line 5 defines its own
`RulesAmbiguity`, duplicating the established contract at
`packages/core/src/rules/types.ts` line 97 (plus `RulesAmbiguitySource` and
`RulesAmbiguityInterpretation`). They are structurally identical today and can
drift. The drift is already live in the tree: the spell importer
(`s1SummoningSpecs.ts` line 1) imports the type from `types.js` while
`magicItemMechanics.ts` line 3 imports it from `rulesAmbiguities.js`.

Required:

- delete the duplicate interface from `rulesAmbiguities.ts` and
  `import type { RulesAmbiguity } from './types.js'` there (that module already
  imports `RulesPackError` from `./types.js`, so this adds no cycle);
- point `magicItemMechanics.ts` at the canonical `./types.js` type — it also
  already imports from `./types.js`;
- keep `types.ts` as the single definition site (it is the established public
  contract, re-exported from `internal.ts` lines 1048-1050); re-export from
  `rulesAmbiguities.ts` only if it genuinely helps, never redefine;

title: Dispatch: fail closed on unresolved ambiguity gate; tighten citation marker (attempt 5)
description:
Second review-response dispatch for eshyra-jw56, correcting attempt 4
(eshyra-us0u). The reviewer accepted attempt 4's schema and validator work and
**overruled its runtime behaviour**. Read `bd show eshyra-jw56` and
`bd show eshyra-us0u` for context.

Worktree: `.worktrees/<this-bead-id>`, branch `<this-bead-id>`, cut from the
current tip of `eshyra-jw56` (which carries attempt 4). Work only there.

## P1 — an ambiguity gate must fail closed, not default

Attempt 4 made an ambiguity-gated `resetsDuration` fall back to preserving the
deadline and reported the ambiguity id on a **successful** transition result.
That is still a resolution. By the time the id surfaces, the runtime has already
chosen an interpretation, spent charges, committed a timer deadline, and written
all of it into replayable campaign history. A later campaign ruling that
same-face presses do reset would make that committed state wrong and not
recoverable without rewriting history.

The contract treats an ambiguity as a **gate**, not a default: no canonical
resolution, campaign-ruling ownership, resolvable only by campaign-owned prose
outside the pack.

### Required behaviour

Selecting a transition whose `resetsDuration` carries an unresolved
`source-ambiguity` marker must **throw before any mutation** — before charges
are spent, before timers are resolved, and before any item state is written.
Throw from `selectStateTransition` in `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`,
which already runs before the cost loop and every write, rather than relying on
transaction rollback.

The failure must be structured, not a bare message. Add an
`ItemStateAmbiguityError` (extending `ItemStateError`, exported the same way)
carrying:

- `ambiguityId`
- `question` (from the mechanics ambiguity block)
- `interpretationIds` (all declared interpretation ids)
- `owner: 'campaign-ruling'`
- plus pack ref and operation id in the message

`selectStateTransition` already receives `mechanics`, so the ambiguity block is
in scope. Remove `unresolvedAmbiguityIds` from the successful
`UseItemResult['transition']` shape — the ambiguity is surfaced in the failure,
never in a success.

Scope of the block is exact: only an operation selecting a transition that
carries an unresolved gate fails. Different-face presses, `spell-contact-loss`,
`press-face-6`, timer expiry, and every other Cube behaviour stay executable.

### Tests

- Selecting the gated transition throws `ItemStateAmbiguityError` with all four
  fields populated.
- **No mutation on throw**: read the row back after the throw and assert the
  charge economy, `machineState`, and `pendingTimers` are byte-identical to the
  pre-call state. This is the assertion that matters most.
- Literal `resetsDuration: true` still re-anchors (unchanged).
- The unaffected Cube operations still execute.

### Docs

`docs/item-reset-executor.md` must say the gate fails closed pending
campaign-ruling support (epic eshyra-jhpt), replacing whatever attempt 4 wrote
about a provisional preserve default. State that once campaign rulings exist,
runtime will require a recorded choice of one of the declared interpretation ids
and execute accordingly.

## P2 — the citation walker must recognize the exact marker shape

Attempt 4 widened the walker to the whole mechanics subtree (correct) but it

title: Dispatch: ambiguity-gate cube same-face reset; tighten resetsDuration and timer identity (attempt 4)
description:
Review-response dispatch for eshyra-jw56 (PR #470 got "request changes" with one
semantic blocker and two contract defects). Read `bd show eshyra-jw56` for the
original design. Branch from the CURRENT tip of `eshyra-jw56` (it now carries a
merge of origin/main).

Worktree: `.worktrees/<this-bead-id>`, branch `<this-bead-id>`, cut from
`eshyra-jw56`. Work only inside that worktree.

## P1 (blocker) — the same-face ruling canonizes an unresolved source ambiguity

SRD 5.1 says a face press makes a barrier that "lasts for 1 minute", and
separately that pressing a **different** face and expending charges resets the
duration. It never says what happens when the **already-active** face is
pressed. Both readings are defensible; there is no errata or Sage Advice
resolving it. The current PR picks "same-face resets" and hard-codes it as
canonical SRD semantics, and its own artifacts contradict each other: the PR
body and the importer test comment both say only a different face resets, while
the expectation and the generated pack mark the five same-face transitions
`resetsDuration: true`.

Per this repo's ambiguity contract, an authoritative-source ambiguity must be
recorded with multiple interpretations, `canonicalResolution: null`, and
campaign-owned runtime disposition — and the affected mechanic must cite it.
**Do not resolve the ambiguity in either direction.** Note that simply deleting
`resetsDuration` from those transitions is also wrong: it would canonize the
narrow reading silently.

### The contract already exists — for spells only

- `packages/core/src/rules/kindSchemas.ts`: `optRulesAmbiguities` (~line 934)
  validates the ambiguity block; `validateAmbiguityReferences` (~line 1046)
  rejects a declared-but-uncited ambiguity and an unknown `ambiguityId`.
- `packages/core/src/rules/validate.ts` `assertAmbiguityIdentityAndProvenance`
  (~line 274) enforces global id uniqueness and that every `source.locator`
  starts with the owning record's provenance locator. It iterates **all**
  records, so magic items get it for free once they can declare ambiguities.
- Working examples: `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/s1SummoningSpecs.ts`
  ~1653 (the ambiguity block) and ~1524 (the citation, shaped
  `{ kind: 'source-ambiguity', ambiguityId: 'ambiguity:...' }`).
- **Magic-item mechanics cannot declare ambiguities today**:
  `packages/core/src/rules/magicItemMechanics.ts` ~2198 has a closed `only()`
  key list with no `ambiguities`.

### Work

1. Extract `optRulesAmbiguities` and `validateAmbiguityReferences` from
   `kindSchemas.ts` into a new shared `packages/core/src/rules/rulesAmbiguities.ts`
   and import it from both `kindSchemas.ts` and `magicItemMechanics.ts`.
   **Direction matters:** `kindSchemas.ts` imports `magicItemMechanics.ts`, so
   `magicItemMechanics.ts` must not import `kindSchemas.ts` — the shared module
   is what avoids the cycle. Spell validation behaviour must not change.
2. Generalize the citation walker to walk the whole mechanics subtree instead of
   only `effects`, so a `stateMachine.transitions[].resetsDuration` citation
   counts as a reference. For spells this is a strict superset (it can only turn
   "uncited" into "cited"); confirm the two existing spell ambiguities still
   validate.
3. Add `'ambiguities'` to the magic-item mechanics `only()` allowlist, validate
   it with the shared validator, and run the citation check over magic-item
   mechanics.
4. Widen `resetsDuration` to accept **either** `true` **or**
   `{ kind: 'source-ambiguity', ambiguityId: 'ambiguity:<kebab>' }`. Both forms
   keep the existing `from === to` rule and gain the `via` rule from P2 below.
   An ambiguity reference must resolve to an ambiguity declared on the same
   mechanics (the shared citation validator enforces this).
5. Curate the Cube of Force spec in
   `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemComplexStateMachines.ts`:
   the five `face-N --press-face-N--> face-N` transitions carry the
   source-ambiguity form instead of `true`, and the machine's item gains:

   - `id`: `ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset`
   - `question`: whether pressing the already-active face restates the barrier's
     one-minute duration
   - `source`: two entries. Locators **must start with the record's provenance
     locator, which is `p. 215`** (e.g. `'p. 215, barrier duration'` and
     `'p. 215, different-face reset'`); `clauseId` values are plain kebab-case
     (`barrier-duration`, `different-face-reset`)
   - `affects`: five entries, one per same-face transition
   - `interpretations`: at least `same-face-resets` and
     `different-face-only-resets`, each with a `summary`
   - `canonicalResolution: null`
   - `runtimeDisposition: { status: 'engine-pending', owner: 'campaign-ruling' }`

6. Runtime (`packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`): an ambiguity-gated
   `resetsDuration` is **not** a reset — the engine keeps the conservative
   default and preserves the existing deadline, because no campaign-ruling
   facility exists yet (that is epic eshyra-jhpt). Make this non-silent: surface
   the unresolved ambiguity id(s) on `UseItemResult['transition']` (e.g.
   `unresolvedAmbiguityIds`) so a DM/campaign layer can see the gate was hit.
   Only literal `true` re-anchors.
7. Fix the contradictory comment in
   `packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemComplexStateMachines.test.ts`
   and update its expectation to assert the gated form. The three preserve
   rulings (cube `spell-contact-loss`, Bead of Force `move-force-sphere`, Ring
   of Shooting Stars `move-ball-lightning`) are unambiguous and stay as they are.
8. Update `docs/item-reset-executor.md`: describe the gate and state plainly
   that preserving is a provisional engine default pending campaign-ruling
   ownership, not a canonical reading of the source.

## P2 — `resetsDuration` is valid where the runtime never reads it

The validator allows the marker on any self-transition, including `timer`- and
`condition`-triggered ones, but it is only consumed while selecting an
operation-backed `via` transition; timer-fired transitions in
`itemResetExecutor.applyDueTimer` always re-anchor from the expiry deadline and
never look at it. That is a schema-valid, semantically dead declaration.

**Fix:** require `via` whenever `resetsDuration` is present (either form). Add
rejection tests for a timer-triggered and a condition-triggered declaration.

## P2 — preserved-timer identity is under-specified

`resolveItemStateTimers` matches a preserved timer with
`.find(c => c.from === from && c.to === to)`. The state-machine schema does not
forbid two timer transitions sharing a `from`/`to` pair, so in a schema-valid
machine both declarations would reuse the first preserved timer and silently
drop the second's amount, roll, and deadline.

**Fix:** enforce in `magicItemMechanics.ts` that a state machine declares at
most one `timer`-bearing transition per `from`/`to` pair, with a `RulesPackError`
naming the pair. I verified this holds across all 50 machines in the committed
pack, so it is non-breaking. Add a schema test with two same-pair timer
declarations pinning the rejection, and note in `itemTimers.ts` that the
uniqueness rule is what makes the `.find()` match unambiguous.

## Constraints

- `docs/importer-fix-protocol.md` governs the regeneration: regenerate with
  `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1`,
  then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`. The generated diff should touch only
  `magic-item:cube-of-force` (five transitions change form, one ambiguities
  block appears). Anything else is a stop-and-report.
- Do NOT touch `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json`.
- Do not resolve the ambiguity, and do not add a campaign-ruling runtime — only
  the gate and the documented provisional default.
- `npm ci` first. `npm run verify:worktree` **before** committing. Commit on
  your branch. Do not push, do not open or comment on a PR, do not merge. Never
  modify eshyra-jw56.

title: eshyra-c7sx PR #462 review fixes (per-period termination, sibling timers, chronological ordering)
description:
Fix the three P1 findings from the PR #462 review of the item reset/timer executor (parent bead eshyra-c7sx; the executor lives in packages/core/src/state/itemResetExecutor.ts, integrated on branch eshyra-c7sx). All three were verified against head commit 9222f5d. Read the PR's inline comments if helpful: `gh api repos/jbongaarts/eshyra/pulls/462/comments`.

## Finding 1 — per-period resets never stop at maximum (itemResetExecutor.ts ~650, resetAnchoredItem per-period branch)

The while-loop unconditionally installs the next `availableAt` anchor, so a fully restored per-period economy (winged-boots) keeps firing `applyReset` at every later period crossing forever: `restored: 0` evidence entries, pointless state writes, and unbounded evidence growth on large advances. Fix: chain periods only while `remaining < maximum`; when the economy reaches (or already has) its maximum, clear `availableAt` and stop. A subsequent spend re-anchors it (useItem already overwrites availableAt on every spend). Regression: fill the economy, advance another period, assert no new evidence and `availableAt === undefined`; then spend again and assert the anchor is re-established.

## Finding 2 — sibling timers survive leaving their source state (itemResetExecutor.ts ~747, resolveTimers)

`remainingTimers = pending.filter(c => c !== timer)` removes only the fired timer. With two outgoing timer transitions from the same state, the sibling survives after `machineState` changes; when it comes due the executor throws (`timer.from !== state.machineState`) — and because this runs inside advanceWorldTime's transaction, ALL campaign time advancement is permanently blocked for that item's campaign. It also contradicts reconcileItemStateTimers's documented contract ("timers from the state being left are cancelled"). Fix: drop every pending timer whose `from === timer.from` before adding the entered state's newly scheduled timers. Regression: a state with two outgoing timers (1 min and 5 min); advance 1 minute — earlier wins, sibling cancelled; advance 5 more minutes — no throw, no stale transition.

## Finding 3 — clock events execute out of chronological order (itemResetExecutor.ts ~893, resolveDueItemClockEvents)

Current sequence per item: all dawn crossings, then all dusks, then anchored resets, then timers. Consequences: an item whose timer destroys it at minute 1 still receives a dawn recharge at minute 360 first (consuming RNG, emitting evidence for an item that should already be gone); multi-day dawn/dusk crossings are applied out of order; an anchored deadline earlier than an already-applied dawn can move `lastReset` backward. Fix: per item, apply due events in a unified chronological order — repeatedly select the earliest due event among (next unapplied dawn crossing, next dusk crossing, each economy's next anchored/per-period due, earliest pending timer deadline), apply it, and continue until nothing is due at or before `elapsedMinutes`; timer-driven destruction terminates that item's processing. Pick a deterministic tie-breaker for equal minutes (recommend: timers before resets, then a stable secondary key like economy id) and document it in docs/item-reset-executor.md. Keep evidence arrays in applied order. Regressions: destruction-at-minute-1 + dawn-charges item advanced past dawn (no reset evidence, inventory gone); a two-day advance asserting dawn/dusk evidence strictly ordered by boundary minute.

## Constraints

- Preserve all existing behavior otherwise: fail-closed rules, evidence shapes, lastReset/availableAt semantics, and the 16 existing tests (adjust only where an assertion encodes the buggy ordering).
- All state writes stay on the validateItemStateForRecord/writeItemState path.
- Update docs/item-reset-executor.md where semantics change (per-period termination, chronological ordering, tie-breaker).
- `npm run verify:worktree` fully green before commit; commit on this worktree's branch.
- Record your completion report with `bd update <this-bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this-bead>`. Never close or modify eshyra-c7sx; never touch files outside this worktree.
notes: Fixed all three PR #462 P1 findings plus two fixes lost to the branch reset, in commit b00e4d5 on eshyra-c7sx (pushed as a fast-forward, no history rewrite). (1) per-period economies re-anchor only while below maximum; (2) firing a timer cancels every timer owned by the state being left; (3) resolveItemTimeline applies dawn/dusk, anchored, and timer events in chronological order per item, ties running timers first. Restored: anchored resets record their due minute; pendingTerminal completes only when the entered state has no outgoing transition. Also rejects a timer that would expire no later than the transition entering its state (previously an infinite loop inside the advance transaction). Five new regressions all verified to fail against the pre-fix executor. Full verify:worktree green: 4687 passed / 19 skipped.

title: Dispatch: reset executor review fixes — rest evidence, AC test matrix, boundary interleave (attempt 1)
description:
Follow-up fixes from the supervisor review of the item reset/timer executor (landed on branch eshyra-c7sx via eshyra-pukl, commits 0dc1454/7f481c3/f9f9565). Read `bd show eshyra-c7sx` for the parent spec and acceptance criteria, and `bd show eshyra-pukl` for the implementation report. ## Fix 1 — rest benefits drop clock-derived item reset evidence (BUG)

In `rest.ts` `complete()`, the benefits object is built with `itemResets: []` and only rest-event resets are pushed into it, while `time.itemResets` from the rest's internal `advanceWorldTime` call is discarded (note `itemTimerResolutions` IS carried over from `time`). An overnight long rest crossing dawn applies dawn regains to item state but the evidence never reaches the returned benefits or the persisted benefits_json. Fix: seed `benefits.itemResets` with `time.itemResets` (clock-derived first, then rest-event entries). Add an end-to-end regression test: a long rest whose window crosses dawn must surface the dawn reset evidence in the returned benefits AND apply the rest-event resets.

## Fix 2 — close the acceptance-criteria test gaps

The parent bead requires every reset shape in the committed pack to be exercised. Missing today (add to itemResetExecutor.test.ts or a rest-level test where end-to-end wiring is the point):

- dusk boundary (charges/dusk/dice-expr — robe-of-stars shape): crossing minute 1080 fires; crossing dawn only does not.
- days-anchored cooldown (cooldown/days:7/all — horn-of-valhalla shape): spend to zero sets availableAt = spend + 7*1440; advancing 7 days restores to max and clears availableAt; advancing less does not.
- charges/days/all with onDepleted becomes:'inert' (figurine shape): depletion sets inert + availableAt; after 7 days the economy refills AND the inert lifecycle clears (end-to-end through useItem depletion, not hand-written state).
- budget/days/all (manual/tome shape, days:36500): same anchored path at century scale (use a smaller days value only if safe-integer limits force it — they do not).
- budget/long-rest/all (boots-of-speed shape) and per-day/long-rest/all (ring-of-x-ray-vision shape) through `completeLongRest` end-to-end: participant-held item regains; a NON-participant's item does not.
- multi-boundary crossing: one advance spanning 3 dawns rolls the dice regain 3 times (3 evidence entries, distinct boundaryElapsedMinutes, clamped total) — the parent AC names this case.
- timer resolution via rest completion (a short rest whose 60 minutes pass a pending timer deadline resolves it and surfaces it in benefits.itemTimerResolutions).

Prefer synthetic fixtures shaped exactly like the named pack items (existing fixture() helper); where a test is cheap to run against the real bundled record (e.g. frost-brand), that is even better evidence.

## Fix 3 — chronological boundary interleaving (hardening)

`resolveDueItemClockEvents` processes ALL dawn crossings for an item, then ALL dusk crossings. For an economy declaring both dawn and dusk resets, a multi-day advance applies dawn@day2 before dusk@day1; the lastReset guard then skips dusk@day1 entirely (out-of-order boundary). No committed pack item declares both, but the schema allows it. Fix: merge the dawn and dusk boundary streams per item and process chronologically (tag each boundary with its event). Add a unit test with a both-dawn-and-dusk fixture advancing two days asserting all four boundaries apply in order.

## Constraints

- Do not change the executor's documented semantics (docs/item-reset-executor.md) except to clarify; do not touch pack data or importer code.
- All state writes stay on the authoritative validateItemStateForRecord + writeItemState path.
- `npm run verify:worktree` fully green before commit. Work only in this worktree; commit on this branch; do not push or open a PR.

- dusk dice-expr charges regain (robe-of-stars shape): crossing minute-of-day 1080 fires; a dawn-only advance does not.
- days:N cooldown 'all' (horn-of-valhalla shape, cooldown.duration {7,day} + reset {at:'days',days:7,amount:'all'}): spend-to-zero anchors availableAt; advancing 7 days restores; advancing 6 days does not.
- charges days:N + onDepleted becomes inert (figurine shape): depletion sets inert; after 7 days the reset restores charges AND clears inert.
- budget days 'all' (manual/tome century shape, days:36500 with loseProperty+inert): same mechanism at large scale — verify no overflow and restore-at-boundary.
- budget long-rest 'all' (boots-of-speed shape) via completeLongRest: participant's item restored, evidence in benefits.itemResets; a short rest does NOT restore it.
- per-day long-rest 'all' (ring-of-x-ray-vision shape) via completeLongRest.
- long-rest gate: item held by a NON-participant character is not reset by the rest.

## 2. Rest benefits drop clock-derived item evidence (code fix)

In rest.ts complete(), benefits.itemResets is initialized to [] and only rest-event resets are pushed; time.itemResets (dawn/dusk crossings during the rest's own advanceWorldTime — a long rest routinely crosses dawn) are applied to state but silently missing from the persisted benefits_json evidence. Initialize benefits.itemResets from time.itemResets (mirroring itemTimerResolutions) and add a test: a long rest that crosses dawn records both the dawn reset and the rest-event reset in benefits.

## 3. Anchored-reset evidence boundary (code fix, minor)

In itemResetExecutor.ts resetAnchoredItem, the hour/days branch passes elapsedMinutes as boundaryElapsedMinutes to applyReset, recording the application time instead of the true due time. Pass availableAt as the boundary (lastReset then records the due minute, matching the per-period branch which correctly uses its anchor).

## 4. pendingTerminal destruction rule (comment or guard, minor)

resolveTimers destroys the item when ANY timer fires while lifecycle.pendingTerminal === 'destroyed'. For the only real case (bead-of-force sphere->destroyed) the fired timer is itself terminal, so behavior is correct today, but a hypothetical multi-step machine with pendingTerminal would be destroyed prematurely at its first intermediate timer. Either tighten the condition (destroy when timer.to === 'destroyed', or when pendingTerminal is set AND the entered state has no outgoing transitions) or document the current assumption with a comment explaining why it is safe for the shipped pack. Your judgment; keep it fail-safe.

## Completion protocol

Run `npm run verify:worktree` (use writable ESHYRA_HOME as before if sandbox requires), commit on branch eshyra-pukl, append a completion report with `bd update <this-bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this-bead>`. Never close or modify eshyra-c7sx.

Fixed complete() benefits to persist time.itemResets, fixed hour/days anchored evidence to use availableAt as the due boundary, and tightened pendingTerminal destruction so intermediate timer states with outgoing transitions are not destroyed prematurely; terminal state or explicit destroyed destination remains fail-safe. No additional follow-up beads required.
