- When activateCampaignCustody detects the registry head differs from the local campaign sheet, the CLI does not only fail with an error.
- CLI presents a choice: cancel; update this campaign to latest character revision; fork/advanced options if available.
- Catch-up mode: replaces the campaign-local character_sheet with the registry head; stamps globalCharacterId, sourceRevision, and importedAt; re-projects the live character row; acquires custody; does NOT create a new registry revision merely for the catch-up.
- Tests for scene-boundary catch-up and stale-copy refusal/cancel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Define character resume conflict policies
description: Record the product semantics for resume conflicts before more code lands. Design-only: capture the policy in ADR 0012 (or a small follow-up design doc), no implementation. Parent: eshyra-lupf.14.4.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define what happens when a campaign resumes with a registry-linked character whose registry head is ahead of the campaign copy.
- Distinguish at least: fail closed; catch-up-to-head; explicit alternate-timeline fork; future-detour/out-of-order continuity.
- State that automatic mechanical merge/rejoin is NOT supported.
- Define who narrates catch-up continuity: player, DM, or selectable.
- Define special handling/warnings for mid-scene and combat resumes.
- Update ADR 0012 or add a small follow-up design doc.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix landing page stylesheet cache busting
description: The redesigned landing page can be served with a browser-cached pre-redesign /styles.css because the stylesheet URL did not change and the prior header allowed caching. Add cache busting for the stylesheet and reduce CSS caching so deployed HTML and CSS stay in sync.
close_reason: Not needed: deployed site was correct; issue was stale browser-cached CSS resolved by hard refresh.

title: Wire guided character creation into play flow
description:
Problem:
The b69j guided character creation flow is complete as `eshyra create-character`, but `eshyra play` still invokes the legacy `promptCharacterDraft` flow in `packages/cli/src/playCharacter.ts`. Playtest users therefore see the brittle manual-HP creator instead of the new rules-pack-backed wizard/finalized-character flow.

Required behavior:
- When no canonical PC exists, `play` must not use `promptCharacterDraft` for D&D 5e SRD.
- For D&D 5e SRD, `play` should either offer to run the new guided wizard inline and import the finalized character into the campaign DB, or offer to select/import an existing finalized character from `<dataRoot>/characters`.
- `/addpc` should use the same guided/import path.
- Retain the old `completeCharacterCreation` path only for Pathfinder or explicitly legacy/test paths until replaced.
- Preserve current `/defer` behavior if desired.

Implementation notes:
- Add a projection/import function from `FinalizedCharacter` into campaign character DB mutations.
- Reuse existing finalized record fields instead of asking for manual HP.
- Prefer sharing the import/projection path between session-zero startup and `/addpc`.
acceptance_criteria:
- D&D 5e SRD `eshyra play` session-zero flow no longer prompts with `Level-1 max HP:` when no canonical PC exists.
- `/addpc` uses the same finalized-character wizard/import path as initial play/session-zero.
- A finalized character can be imported into a campaign and becomes the active `pc-1`.
- Imported `pc-1` has name, class, ancestry, HP, and ability scores populated from the finalized character record.
- Legacy `completeCharacterCreation` remains available only for Pathfinder or explicit legacy/test paths.
- Tests cover the no-manual-HP D&D 5e SRD play/session-zero transcript and finalized-character import into campaign DB.
close_reason: Implemented guided/finalized character setup for D&D play and /addpc; added finalized-character campaign import and tests.

title: Make POSIX release launcher portable and smoke-test macOS installer
description:
Make the generated POSIX release launcher portable across macOS and Linux, and add macOS installer smoke coverage.

Problem:
Release artifacts target macOS and Linux, but the generated POSIX launcher uses GNU-style command forms such as readlink -- / dirname -- that are risky on macOS's BSD userland. Existing installer smoke coverage is strongest on Ubuntu and may miss macOS launcher failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- Replace GNU-specific POSIX launcher logic with a portable implementation tested on macOS and Linux.
- Preserve symlink resolution behavior expected by installer-created commands.
- Add or extend release workflow smoke coverage so macOS executes the installed launcher path users will actually run.
- Keep existing Ubuntu installer smoke coverage.
- Include focused tests or fixture verification for generated launcher content if practical.
close_reason: Portable POSIX launcher (no GNU dirname --/readlink --), refactored into exported render builders, added macOS to installer-smoke matrix, added releaseLauncher.test.ts (static + functional 2-hop symlink). Local release:smoke-installer passes. PR #320.

title: Eliminate production CLI imports from @eshyra/core/internal
description:
Eliminate production CLI imports from @eshyra/core/internal.

Problem:
Project guidance says production callers should depend only on @eshyra/core's stable root export, while @eshyra/core/internal is unstable. Production CLI code currently imports from @eshyra/core/internal, which weakens the package boundary and risks making internal APIs de facto public.

Acceptance criteria:
- Audit production files under packages/cli/src for imports from @eshyra/core/internal.
- Promote CLI-needed APIs/types to the stable @eshyra/core root export, or create a deliberate supported subpath such as @eshyra/core/cli if that is the chosen design.
- Keep test/evaluation-only internal imports allowed where appropriate.
- Add a boundary test or static guard that fails if packages/cli/src/**/*.ts imports @eshyra/core/internal.
- Do not weaken AGENTS.md or public/internal documentation to make the violation disappear.
close_reason: Promoted CLI-needed APIs to @eshyra/core root export, repointed all 13 production CLI files off /internal, added packages/cli/test/internalBoundary.test.ts static guard. PR #319.

title: Add migration parity, idempotency, and checksum tests
description:
Add tests and CI guards for migration-first schema management.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fresh empty DB applies all migrations successfully.
- Calling initSchema twice leaves the DB unchanged and applies no duplicate migrations.
- A DB with a pending migration applies only the pending migration.
- Editing an already-applied migration file causes checksum verification to fail closed.
- Legacy adoption/reset path is tested.
- A migrated DB and a fresh DB are compared for schema parity where applicable.
- If a generated schema snapshot is added, CI verifies it matches the schema produced by applying migrations.
close_reason: Parity/idempotency/checksum/legacy tests + generated schema.snapshot.sql with drift guard. Landed in PR #318 (merged).

title: Remove latest-schema repair DDL from initSchema
description:
Remove the hand-maintained latest-schema DDL authority from initSchema after migration-first initialization is in place.

Problem:
The existing init path can run latest CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS logic after migration compatibility checks, which can mask incomplete migrations.

Acceptance criteria:
- initSchema delegates schema mutation to the migration runner.
- initSchema no longer contains or executes hand-maintained latest-schema CREATE TABLE/CREATE INDEX repair DDL.
- Safe invariant/bootstrap row insertion remains only where appropriate and is documented.
- Repeated init is idempotent without relying on broad CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS repair behavior.
close_reason: initSchema delegates to migration runner; latest-schema repair DDL + legacy TS chain removed. Landed in PR #318 (merged).

title: Add legacy schema adoption or reset path
description:
Handle databases created before the migration-first schema system.

Preferred behavior:
- If a DB already has the new schema_migrations ledger, use it.
- If a DB has the old meta.schema_version system, either:
  - migrate through the old TypeScript migration chain to the final legacy version, verify parity with the new baseline, then mark 0001_initial.sql as applied; or
  - fail closed with a clear pre-1.0 reset/recreate message if preserving old local DBs is not worth the complexity.
- If a DB is empty, apply all SQL migrations from zero.
- If a DB is neither empty nor recognized, fail closed.

Acceptance criteria:
- The chosen behavior is consistent with the migration policy document.
- Legacy behavior is covered by tests.
- Failure messages are actionable and do not silently modify unrecognized databases.
close_reason: Legacy adoption/reset path landed in PR #317 (merged). prepareDatabaseForMigrations + migrateDatabase + SchemaResetRequiredError, fingerprint-gated adoption at baseline 15, fail-closed otherwise.

title: Baseline current SQLite schema as 0001_initial.sql
description:
Convert the current intended SQLite schema into the new baseline migration.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add 0001_initial.sql containing the current intended schema.
- Preserve all tables, indexes, constraints, and default/bootstrap assumptions from the current schema.
- Empty DB initialization through the new runner produces a working DB equivalent to the current fresh initialization behavior.
- Do not reconstruct historical schema versions unless needed for the chosen legacy adoption path.
close_reason: 0001_initial.sql baseline landed in PR #316 (merged). Encodes current v15 schema + seed rows; proven structurally equivalent to initSchema for fresh init.

title: Add SQLite SQL migration runner and ledger
description:
Implement the migration runner and schema_migrations ledger for migration-first SQLite schema management.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a schema_migrations table with version, name, checksum, and applied_at.
- Discover migration files in deterministic version order.
- Validate contiguous version numbers and unique names.
- Apply pending migrations transactionally.
- Refuse to start if an already-applied migration's checksum no longer matches.
- Refuse ambiguous, duplicate, missing, or out-of-order migrations with clear errors.
- Keep the runner small and deterministic; do not introduce an ORM/migration framework unless separately justified.
close_reason: Migration runner + schema_migrations ledger landed in PR #316 (merged). Discovery/validation, checksum drift detection, per-migration transactional apply.

title: Record migration-first SQLite schema policy
description:
Write the design note or ADR for Eshyra's migration-first SQLite schema policy before implementation.

The decision should settle:
- SQL migration files are the canonical executable schema source.
- Whether schema.snapshot.sql exists and whether it is generated-only.
- How schema_migrations records version, name, checksum, and applied_at.
- Transaction policy for migrations.
- How bootstrap/default rows are handled without becoming hidden schema repair.
- How old meta.schema_version databases are adopted or rejected.
- What developers must do when changing schema after this lands.

Acceptance criteria:
- A committed design note or ADR describes the migration-first policy.
- The note explicitly rejects hand-maintained latest-schema DDL as executable authority.
- The note describes the chosen legacy DB behavior.
- The note includes enough workflow detail for future agent/coding sessions to add migrations correctly.
close_reason: ADR 0015 (migration-first SQLite schema policy) written and delivered in PR #315. Settles all decision points: SQL files as sole schema authority, schema_migrations ledger, SHA-256 checksum drift policy, per-migration transactions, seed-as-migration, legacy adoption-at-15-vs-reset, generated-only snapshot, and the future-migration authoring workflow. Implementation is .1.3-.1.7.

title: Replace latest-schema DDL with migration-first SQLite schema management
description:
Replace the current hand-maintained latest-schema DDL plus TypeScript migration-chain model with migration-first SQLite schema management.

Problem:
Eshyra currently has a latest-schema bootstrap block and a migration chain that both affect schema shape. That creates duplicate schema authority and allows bootstrap DDL such as CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS to mask incomplete migrations. Since Eshyra is still pre-1.0, this is the best time to move to a durable model.

Target design:
- Versioned SQL migration files are the only executable source of truth for schema changes.
- Empty DB creation applies all migrations from zero.
- Existing DB startup applies only pending migrations.
- A migration ledger records applied version, name, checksum, and timestamp.
- A generated schema snapshot may exist for review, but it is generated from migrations and verified, not hand-maintained authority.
- Legacy meta.schema_version databases are either adopted safely or rejected with a clear pre-1.0 reset message.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a migration-first design note or ADR covering source of truth, migration ordering, checksum policy, legacy adoption/reset policy, and bootstrap-row handling.
- Add versioned SQL migrations under packages/core/src/persistence/migrations or an equivalent clear location.
- Encode the current intended schema as 0001_initial.sql.
- Add schema_migrations ledger with version, name, checksum, and applied_at.
- Empty DB initialization applies ordered migrations transactionally.
- Existing DB initialization verifies already-applied migration checksums and applies only pending migrations.
- Remove hand-maintained latest-schema CREATE TABLE/CREATE INDEX authority from initSchema.
- Add tests for fresh init, repeated init, pending migrations, checksum drift, and legacy adoption/reset behavior.
- Add a migrated-vs-fresh schema parity guard where meaningful.
- Document the authoring workflow for future schema changes.
close_reason: All 7 children merged to main (PRs #313-#318 across the migration-first series; runner/baseline/adoption/initSchema-rewrite/tests in #316-#318). Migration-first SQLite schema management complete per ADR 0015: versioned SQL migrations are the sole executable authority, schema_migrations ledger replaces meta.schema_version, latest-schema repair DDL and the legacy TS chain are removed, legacy DBs adopt-at-baseline-or-reset, and parity/idempotency/checksum/snapshot are test-guarded.

title: Address holistic repo review recommendations
description:
Holistic repo-health follow-up after the major Eshyra base has stabilized pre-1.0.

This epic collects architectural, release, persistence, and tooling hygiene recommendations from the repo-wide review. The goal is to address durable design risks now, while the project is still pre-1.0 and before these seams become expensive compatibility commitments.

Scope:
- Move SQLite schema management to a migration-first design.
- Enforce the public/internal package boundary between CLI and core.
- Harden release launcher portability.
- Add focused reliability guards around telemetry and tool registration.
- Strengthen schema-validator coverage for bundled tools.
- Clean stale documentation/comments after runtime and distribution changes.

Non-goals:
- Generic lint cleanup.
- Broad refactors unrelated to the reviewed risks.
- ORM adoption unless a child bead explicitly determines it is necessary.
close_reason: All child beads are complete and verified in this branch.

title: Reduce expensive primary-DM retry churn from audit rejections
description:
The latest playtest suggests the main usage/cost issue is not the cheap auditor call itself, but the extra primary DM call required after an audit rejection. Optimize for fewer expensive DM retries and fewer full regeneration loops, especially in combat. A stronger auditor may or may not reduce total cost if it prevents false rejects that trigger primary-DM retries; this bead should measure and reduce retry churn rather than assuming shorter auditor prompts are the main lever.

Acceptance criteria:

- Add or improve metrics that distinguish auditor call count, primary DM call count, primary DM retry count, retry cause, whether retry succeeded, tools rerun during retry, and usage estimates by primary DM vs auditor where available.
- Identify common audit failures that can be prevented before generating a full primary DM response.
- Add deterministic preflight or postflight checks where appropriate for common combat failures, such as player-affecting roll exists but is not surfaced, HP changed without a valid state mutation, combatant target is invalid, and death/unconscious condition is narrated without state support.
- Avoid full primary-DM regeneration for presentation-only failures when all tool calls and state mutations are already valid. If this is not safe yet, document why and create a follow-up.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior for true state/tool errors.
- Regression tests cover: accepted first-pass combat turn requires one primary DM candidate plus one auditor pass, not a retry; hidden roll-ledger presentation failure is detected; invalid combatant HP target still requires real state repair; retry diagnostics identify whether the expensive retry was caused by missing state, missing world evidence, missing roll visibility, invalid target, or auditor over-rejection.
notes: PR #307 updated after review: persisted audit retry diagnostics in ModelUsageStore with turn_audit table, turn_outcome retry aggregate migrations, timeline reconstruction/rendering, and CLI store/usage tests. npm run verify:worktree now passes after installing local workspace links in the worktree; package-lock unchanged.
close_reason: Merged PR #307 with audit retry diagnostics, persisted ModelUsageStore audit/outcome metrics, tests, and docs.

title: Add first-class encounter combatant state for monsters and NPCs
description:
The first combat playtest exposed that enemies are not addressable durable combatants. Bob's HP was updated correctly, but the near goblin could not be targeted by `adjust_hp`; the model tried several labels such as "near goblin", "goblin", "goblin-1", and "goblin-ambush", all failed, and the goblin's death was handled narratively / as lore instead of combat state. Combat needs a deterministic combatant model for monsters and NPCs.

Acceptance criteria:

- Starting an encounter can instantiate combatants from module encounter creatures.
- Each combatant has a stable id, display label, rulesRef, side/faction, HP, max HP, AC if available, conditions, alive/dead/unconscious status, and location/zone or encounter placement.
- Combatants can represent multiple creatures of the same type, e.g. `goblin-1`, `goblin-2`.
- A state mutation tool can update combatant HP and conditions. This may extend `adjust_hp` or introduce a combat-specific tool, but the target model must be unambiguous.
- Active combatants appear in the DM context with their ids and current status.
- The auditor can verify creature damage/death against combatant state instead of requiring improvised lore.
- Regression tests cover: two goblins ambush Bob; Bob damages `goblin-1`; Bob kills `goblin-1`; `goblin-2` remains active; invalid target labels fail clearly and suggest valid combatant ids; no goblin death is represented only as overlay lore when combatant state should exist.
close_reason: Implemented live encounter combatant state, start/update combatant tools, context/audit prompt support, schema migration, and goblin regression coverage. Verified with npm run verify:worktree.

title: Surface player-visible roll results for player-affecting mechanics
description:
The Claude combat playtest showed initiative and the death save to the player, but hid most other player-affecting rolls. Debug evidence showed attack rolls, damage rolls, ambush/perception-style checks, enemy attacks, and enemy damage were being rolled, but the visible transcript only narrated outcomes. This makes combat feel opaque and makes it hard for a player to trust the mechanics.

Acceptance criteria:

- Define a player-visible roll ledger policy.
- Always surface player attack rolls, player damage rolls, saving throws, death saves, ability checks when the player is aware they are attempting something uncertain, initiative, enemy attack rolls against a PC, and enemy damage rolls against a PC.
- Permit hidden or summarized handling for secret checks where showing the roll would reveal hidden information, monster-vs-monster mechanics not directly affecting the player, and hidden enemy stealth/perception when revealing it would spoil the encounter.
- Update DM prompt guidance so the primary DM knows to include the roll ledger in final narration.
- Update audit guidance so a candidate can be rejected when it narrates a player-affecting hit, miss, damage, save, death save, or ability-check result without surfacing the relevant player-visible roll summary.
- Regression tests cover: Bob attacks a goblin and misses and the attack roll is visible; Bob attacks a goblin, hits, and deals damage and attack and damage are visible; a goblin attacks Bob and misses and the enemy attack roll is visible; a goblin critically hits Bob and drops him to 0 HP in a deterministic roll fixture and enemy attack and damage are visible; a death save remains visible; a hidden ambush/stealth check does not leak hidden information unnecessarily.
close_reason: Implemented player-visible roll ledger policy, DM/audit prompt guidance, and regression coverage for visible vs hidden roll handling.

title: Harden combat runtime and model-tier evaluation after first combat playtest
description:
Follow-up from the first Claude combat playtest after `eshyra-l3b3`. Combat now executes far enough to reveal the next runtime layer: player-facing roll visibility, first-class monster combatant state, and expensive primary-DM retry churn from audit rejections. This epic should not reopen `l3b3`; it should build on it. It should also replace the informal Claude-vs-Codex comparison with a practical model-tier evaluation harness for primary DM and auditor roles.

Acceptance criteria:

- Child beads exist for player-visible roll display, encounter combatant state, primary-DM retry churn, deterministic combat regression, and model-tier evaluation.
- Beads distinguish runtime findings from model-style findings.
- Beads preserve the post-`l3b3` continuity/audit improvements.
- Model comparison work evaluates model tiers within each provider and role, not just Claude-vs-Codex.
close_reason: Completed post-combat-playtest hardening epic: roll visibility, combatant state, retry diagnostics, deterministic combat fixture, and model-tier evaluation all merged.

title: Add continuity dressing for stable descriptive details
description:
Problem

The p4vd canon hierarchy correctly avoids making every descriptive flourish into consequential canon, but the current "decorative color stays in prose" guidance is too blunt.

Some non-consequential details are still important for player experience because they are stable, visible, and memorable. If the DM describes an ornate tapestry in a room, then later describes the same room as having bare walls or different decoration, the player may be pulled out of the fiction or infer false significance from the change.

This is not a clue/hook problem; it is a continuity problem.

Design direction

Add a continuity-dressing tier or equivalent field to campaign overlay lore.

Distinguish:
- Ephemeral atmosphere: transient sensory/mood details that can be safely forgotten.
- Continuity dressing: stable physical details attached to a recurring location/NPC/object that should remain consistent.
- Consequential lore: hooks, clues, NPC knowledge, motives, threats, evidence, consequences, and player-affecting facts.

Examples of continuity dressing:
- ornate tapestry on the west wall
- cracked blue-glass windows
- a statue missing one hand
- three long banquet tables
- dry fountain in the square
- soot-streaked houses around Emberfall Square

Examples of ephemeral atmosphere:
- smell of cold ash
- wind moving through the room
- torchlight flickering
- dust motes in morning light
- a villager shifting uneasily

Acceptance criteria

- Update the canon-tier design to include stable continuity dressing or an equivalent kind/significance/weight field.
- The model can record stable visible details without implying they are clues or plot hooks.
- world_query(location) returns continuity dressing for revisited locations.
- Audit treats continuity dressing as support for descriptive consistency, not as proof of plot significance.
- DM guidance says:
  - do not record every adjective or transient mood detail
  - do record stable physical details when forgetting or contradicting them would confuse play
  - do not imply significance merely because a continuity detail was recorded
- Add or adapt overlay lore fields to support this distinction, such as:
  - kind: location_dressing / npc_dressing / object_dressing
  - or significance/weight: atmosphere / continuity / clue / hook / consequence
- Regression:
  1. DM describes an ornate tapestry in a room.
  2. The detail is recorded as continuity dressing.
  3. Player leaves and later returns.
  4. DM recalls the tapestry or at minimum avoids contradicting it.
  5. The system does not imply the tapestry is a clue unless later promoted separately.
- Regression:
  - transient atmosphere such as "torchlight flickers" is not automatically persisted.
close_reason: Added overlay lore significance for continuity dressing, returned continuity evidence in world queries, updated DM/audit guidance, and covered stable vs transient detail regressions.

title: Sanitize invalid auditor disallowed-tool classifications
description:
Problem

In the post-p4vd playtest, the auditor classified set_plot_flag as a disallowed tool in a case where the real issue was that the DM used insufficient/wrong support for a consequential world fact that should have been recorded as overlay lore.

That is semantically wrong. set_plot_flag may be the wrong or insufficient tool for a given assertion, but it should not be labeled as disallowed unless it is actually part of the configured explicit-action-only/disallowed mutation set.

Goal

Sanitize or constrain auditor output so disallowedToolCalls is reserved for genuinely disallowed tools, while wrong-tool or insufficient-evidence cases are reported as missing required tools or unsupported assertions.

Acceptance criteria

- Auditor cannot mark set_plot_flag as disallowed unless it is explicitly configured as disallowed.
- Non-explicit-action-only tools may still be rejected as insufficient evidence or wrong support.
- If set_plot_flag is used where record_world_fact is needed, the rejection says missing record_world_fact or insufficient lore evidence, not disallowed set_plot_flag.
- Add deterministic post-processing or schema validation that filters invalid disallowedToolCalls.
- Debug output preserves the auditor's useful reasoning while correcting invalid disallowed-tool classification.
- Regression:
  - DM calls set_plot_flag for "Bob learned Sela lost two scouts"
  - Response asserts missing scouts as a consequential world fact
  - Audit rejects due to missing record_world_fact, not due to disallowed set_plot_flag
- Regression:
  - Truly explicit-action-only violations still appear in disallowedToolCalls.
close_reason: Sanitized auditor disallowedToolCalls to explicit-action-only tools and remapped invalid set_plot_flag lore classifications to record_world_fact repair guidance.

title: Harden audit retry convergence for multi-evidence turns
description:
Problem

The retry/repair loop is currently whack-a-mole. A rejected attempt may identify one missing requirement, the retry fixes it, then a second attempt is rejected for a different missing requirement. This produced player-visible hard failures in ordinary dialogue.

Observed pattern:
- Attempt 1 needs record_world_fact for missing scouts and/or movement near the tower.
- Attempt 2 records the facts but is rejected for missing world_query of Warden Sela or another module-canon support.
- Player sees a hard failure even though the repair path is obvious.

Goal

Improve retry convergence for turns that need multiple kinds of support: world_query, record_world_fact, scene-local evidence, and audit-safe wording.

Acceptance criteria

- Retry prompt carries cumulative missing requirements from earlier rejected attempts.
- The system distinguishes:
  - missing world_query
  - missing record_world_fact
  - rumor used as confirmed fact
  - failed tool call incorrectly relied upon
  - unsupported exact detail
  - wrong tool chosen for a consequential fact
- If a later retry fixes earlier requirements but exposes a new missing-tool/evidence class, the system can make one additional repair attempt within a bounded limit.
- Rejected mutating calls remain rolled back; no rejected record_world_fact, set_plot_flag, inventory, clock, HP, or condition changes leak into accepted state.
- Repair guidance should encourage:
  - query module canon first when resolving existing NPCs/locations/lore
  - record consequential new lore before asserting it
  - use scene-local evidence for immediate continuity where available
  - avoid unsupported exact numbers unless sourced or recorded
- Regression covers a turn requiring both:
  - world_query for Warden Sela
  - record_world_fact for missing scouts / new consequential report
- Regression covers a failed first retry followed by a successful second retry without player-visible hard failure.
- Debug logs show the cumulative repair requirements clearly.
close_reason: Added cumulative audit repair requirements and bounded extra repair attempt when a retry exposes a new missing evidence class.

title: Add scene-local evidence for immediate audit continuity
description:
Problem

The playtest showed that the auditor relies heavily on tool evidence and does not sufficiently use recent accepted scene history. This makes immediate conversational follow-up brittle.

Example:
- Warden Sela says in an accepted response that she sent two scouts north and they did not return.
- The player immediately asks what to expect if investigating.
- A response referencing those scouts may still be rejected unless the model records or re-queries the fact.

Eshyra needs scene-local evidence that is weaker than durable campaign overlay lore but strong enough to support immediate local continuity.

Design direction

Introduce compact recent-scene evidence for audit/prompt context:
- accepted NPC statements
- recently established visible facts
- recently stated player-visible reports
- exact details that were accepted into narration, such as "three houses burned"

This should not replace record_world_fact for durable campaign memory. It should support immediate follow-up and prevent contradictions within the same scene.

Acceptance criteria

- Audit prompt receives a compact recent-scene evidence section derived only from accepted turns.
- Recent accepted NPC statements can support immediate follow-up dialogue.
- Recent accepted exact details remain available as scene-local evidence until the scene ends or ages out.
- Scene-local evidence is marked as weaker than module canon, campaign state, and campaign overlay lore.
- Durable consequential facts still require record_world_fact for long-term recall.
- Scene-local evidence does not allow failed tool calls or rejected candidate prose to become support.
- Regression:
  - Sela says two scouts did not return in an accepted turn.
  - Player immediately asks what to expect.
  - DM can reference the missing scouts without hard failure.
- Regression:
  - Accepted narration says three houses burned.
  - A same-scene follow-up can refer to three houses without a contradictory audit result.
- Regression:
  - After scene boundary/aging, durable recall requires overlay lore or module canon rather than stale scene-local context.
close_reason: Added recent accepted scene-log evidence to context assembly and audit prompts for immediate same-scene continuity.

title: Make world_query discovery return module canon records
description:
Problem

The post-p4vd playtest showed that world_query discovery is too brittle for module canon. The model repeatedly tried queries such as:

  {"type":"npc","query":"Warden Sela"}

and received not_found. Exact-id lookup such as:

  {"type":"npc","id":"warden-sela"}

can work, but the DM cannot reliably know exact module IDs during play. Search-style queries also tended to surface overlay lore more reliably than module NPCs, locations, or lore.

This causes ordinary follow-up dialogue to fail mechanics/world audit even when the target is authored module canon.

Acceptance criteria

- world_query search for "Warden Sela" returns the module NPC.
- world_query search for "authority figure Emberfall" returns Warden Sela or enough metadata to query her exact ID.
- search for "watchtower", "north road", "hollow", "Emberfall incident", and similar terms returns relevant module locations/lore plus overlay lore where applicable.
- Module canon search results include enough metadata for safe follow-up:
  - canon tier/source
  - entity type
  - entity id
  - summary/name
  - visibility where applicable
- Overlay lore and module canon both participate in discovery; one does not crowd out the other.
- Type-specific query misuse is handled gracefully:
  - either {"type":"npc","query":"Warden Sela"} performs a constrained NPC search
  - or it fails with actionable guidance telling the DM to use type:"search" or an exact id
- Add regression tests from the Emberfall playtest pattern:
  - find Warden Sela by name
  - find Warden Sela by "authority figure"
  - find the watchtower/hollow by natural subject terms

title: Harden play-loop canon, audit, and continuity after p4vd
description:
Problem

The first playtest after campaign overlay canon landed shows real p4vd progress: consequential lore can be recorded with record_world_fact, retrieved later through world_query, and exposed to audit with canon-tier and visibility metadata.

However, normal play is still too brittle. The DM/audit/tool loop now fails at the integration boundary between module canon, campaign overlay lore, recent scene continuity, and descriptive consistency.

Observed playtest pattern

Session: session-mqskv6co-pdsj5x
Campaign: The Hollow Beneath Emberfall
Scope note: ignore the character creation section; b69j is still in progress.

Key observations:
- The system successfully recorded and retrieved the Emberfall incident as overlay lore after retry.
- Warden Sela / Emberfall module-canon discovery was brittle unless exact IDs were used.
- The auditor did not consistently treat recent accepted dialogue as scene-local evidence.
- Retry repair sometimes fixed one missing tool/evidence issue but exposed another, causing player-visible hard failure.
- The auditor classified set_plot_flag as a disallowed tool in a case where the real problem was insufficient evidence / wrong tool choice.
- The current canon hierarchy risks dropping stable descriptive details as "just color", creating continuity contradictions on later revisits.

Goal

Harden the play loop so Eshyra can combine:
- module canon
- campaign overlay lore
- recent scene facts
- stable continuity dressing
- audit evidence
- repair/retry behavior

without hard-failing ordinary follow-up conversation or creating immersion-breaking descriptive contradictions.

Non-goal

Do not address character creation issues here. Those remain under b69j.

title: Add campaign overlay canon for consequential improvised lore
description:
Problem

The playtest surfaced an important adventure-module design seam: the DM must be able to improvise enough to handle unexpected player choices and flesh out scenes, but that improvisation cannot become untracked, unauditable lore that later causes continuity drift or mechanics-audit failures.

Adventure modules should provide the authoritative story spine, but long-running play needs a campaign overlay where consequential facts introduced during play become queryable, inspectable campaign state. At the same time, ordinary descriptive color should not be promoted into permanent canon.

This bead defines and implements the model for improvised lore promotion.

Context from playtest

In the Hearthmere / waystation sequence, the DM improvised useful adventure-driving facts:
- Old Renn exists.
- Old Renn's charcoal cart is missing.
- His mule returned alone.
- Fresh axe-cuts were found on the north palisade.
- Drag marks led toward the pines.
- Villagers may pay someone to investigate.

Those are good DM improvisations. They create hooks, NPC knowledge, evidence, and decision points. But once introduced, they need to become campaign overlay lore so later turns can query and rely on them. They should not remain only in prose.

Non-goal

Do not address the stale-campaign/baseSystemId mismatch from the same playtest. That was caused by resuming an old campaign after an intentional backwards-incompatible rules/module change. It does not need compatibility work under this bead.

Design direction

Use layered canon:
- Module canon: read-only adventure-module facts and prepared content.
- Campaign state: deterministic state mutations, flags, inventory, quest state, clocks.
- Campaign overlay lore: consequential improvised facts recorded during play.
- Scene facts: short-lived current-scene continuity.
- Decorative color: prose-only description that should not be persisted.
- Rumor/belief: persistent attribution that records what an NPC/group believes or reports without asserting it is true.

The system should support truth status:
- true / confirmed
- false / disproven
- unknown
- rumored
- reported
- observed
- believed
- lie
- exaggeration

Acceptance criteria

- Defines canon tiers and their audit semantics.
- Defines truth-status semantics, especially the difference between a fact being true and a rumor/belief being recorded.
- Adds a constrained way for the DM to promote consequential improvised lore into campaign overlay state.
- Updates world querying so campaign overlay lore is retrievable alongside module canon.
- Updates audit behavior so current-turn lore-recording can support assertions, while failed tool calls cannot.
- Adds prompt/runtime guidance distinguishing consequential lore from decorative scene color.
- Adds regression coverage based on the Hearthmere / Old Renn playtest pattern.

Design intent
Ability-first should support the Eshyra user profile that enjoys 80s-era RPG discovery: see what the scores suggest, then choose a class and ancestry that fit. It should not be hostile or random-only; users may enter or assign scores depending on supported methods.

Acceptance criteria
- User can choose the exact ability-first mode label.
- Ability scores can be collected before class.
- The flow offers deterministic class-fit suggestions from score data and recipe metadata.
- The user can still choose a poor fit if desired after a warning or neutral explanation.
- Later class/ancestry selection reuses the same resolver and validation engine as concept-first.
- Transcript-style tests cover a representative ability-first path.

title: Adopt the generated SRD rules pack at runtime and retire the in-code placeholder
description:
Gameplay currently resolves rules against the 3-record in-code placeholder DND5E_SRD_RULES_PACK (packages/core/src/rules/dnd5eSrd.ts, built from the hand-literal SRD_CATALOG in rules/srd/data.ts: 1 creature 'monster:goblin', 1 spell, 1 class, NO magic-items). Make the runtime SRD pack the generated pack and retire the placeholder. Concrete blockers found while probing:
1. resolveRulesStack (rules/stack.ts) enforces unique record NAMES per kind; the full SRD has legitimate duplicates (e.g. 'Ability Score Improvement' as a feature on every class), so resolving the generated pack THROWS today. The name-uniqueness model must handle real-SRD duplicates (key-addressed primary, name as best-effort/non-unique, or kind+owner scoping).
2. Bundling/perf: loading 1811 records at startup vs lazy; ensure all shipped editions still resolve the data dir.
3. ~7 test files assert against the stub's tiny contents and will need updating.

Decision recorded in ADR 0013. This unblocks eshyra-8bit (adventure rulesRef resolution) by giving the runtime real records incl. magic-items; the rulesRef<->key addressing-convention fix stays in 8bit (or rides along).

title: Fix mechanics audit evidence for inventory quantities and rollback retries
description:
Discovered during the eshyra-eh54 adventure-module/equipment playtest (ESHYRA_DEBUG_SESSION=full ... play).

A player authorized inventory mutation: 'Give bob a sensible starting kit for a 1st level fighter'. The DM correctly attempted give_item calls, but the turn was rejected:

  turn rejected by mechanics audit after retry: missing required tool(s) [give_item (target: Bob's starting kit quantities (10 torches, 10 days of rations, 20 crossbow bolts))] ... The response asserted exact item quantities that were not established by the executed tool calls.

This is NOT an adventure-module bug and NOT a 'DM refused to act' bug. There are two confirmed root causes in the orchestrator/audit layer:

ROOT CAUSE A — audit evidence lacks quantity-bearing detail.
- give_item returns only { applied: true, id, name } (packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolGiveItem.ts ~line 88). It does NOT echo the applied quantity, location, or target character, even though those args were passed and applied.
- The auditor's per-call summary (summarizeExecutedCall in packages/core/src/orchestrator/turnAuditor.ts ~line 188) includes only { tool, source, ok, data(truncated) } and NEVER the original sanitized tool-call arguments.
- Result: the auditor sees that give_item was applied for 'torch', 'rations', 'crossbow-bolt' but has zero evidence of quantities, so it cannot verify a response that says '10 torches, 10 days of rations, 20 crossbow bolts' and rejects it.

ROOT CAUSE B — unsafe retry after rollback.
- Rejected candidates are rolled back via the per-attempt SQLite SAVEPOINT (eshyra_turn_attempt) in packages/core/src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts (ROLLBACK TO / RELEASE around lines 535-544).
- The corrective/retry note (formatCorrectiveNote in orchestrator.ts) only tells the model to fix the missing quantities. It does NOT tell the model that the prior rejected tool calls were rolled back and no longer apply. The retry must replay the ENTIRE intended accepted state change from scratch, otherwise it builds on state that no longer exists.
design:
Two coordinated changes:

1. Enrich audit evidence (turnAuditor.ts summarizeExecutedCall + the ExecutedToolCall plumbing): include the original SANITIZED tool-call arguments alongside the result, and/or have mutating tools echo applied state. At minimum give_item / remove_item evidence must carry item id, name, quantity, location, and target character when present. Prefer enriching results (toolGiveItem.ts / toolRemoveItem.ts return objects) AND/OR including sanitized args, so the auditor can verify quantity-sensitive assertions. Keep the bounded/sanitized property of audit evidence — do not dump unbounded payloads.

2. Retry corrective text (formatCorrectiveNote in orchestrator.ts): explicitly state that rejected candidate tool calls were rolled back and cannot be relied on, and that the model must recreate the full intended accepted outcome from scratch (all required tool calls, with quantities/targets), not just patch the previously-claimed-but-rejected difference.

remove_item already returns removed/previousQuantity/newQuantity (toolRemoveItem.ts ~204) — align give_item to echo comparable applied detail.
acceptance_criteria:
- A response claiming "10 torches" is accepted ONLY when executed give_item evidence includes quantity 10 for torch.
- A response that calls give_item without quantity, or with quantity 1, and claims "10 torches" is REJECTED.
- Retry after a rejected candidate does not assume any prior tool calls applied; corrective text explicitly says the previous candidate was rejected, all candidate tool calls were rolled back and did not apply, and the full intended outcome must be recreated from scratch with all required quantities and targets.
- Audit evidence for give_item/remove_item includes item id, name, quantity, location, and target character when present, while remaining bounded and sanitized.
- Cover quantity-bearing audit evidence, unsupported-quantity rejection, supported-quantity acceptance, and rollback-aware corrective retry text with unit/fixture tests only; no generated SRD runtime pack is required.
- The full real-SRD sensible fighter starting-kit playtest regression is explicitly out of scope here and moved to eshyra-12c3 because it depends on generated SRD runtime adoption and equipment lookup normalization.

Likely files: packages/core/src/orchestrator/turnAuditor.ts (summarizeExecutedCall, buildAuditUserMessage, ExecutedToolCall shape), packages/core/src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts (retry loop, SAVEPOINT rollback ~431-550, formatCorrectiveNote, formatAuditFailure), packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolGiveItem.ts (~line 88 result), packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRemoveItem.ts (RemoveItemResult ~204). title: Stage gameplay tool mutations until audited turn acceptance
description:
Problem
The native Agent SDK MCP path can execute state-mutating tools during a candidate turn before the turn auditor accepts the model response. In session-mqkis411-rlsh20, the player asked a read-style question ("What am I equipped with?"), the model executed inventory mutation tools, the auditor rejected the candidate, and the retry then failed due to provider session limit. The user-facing message said the input was not applied, but some tool calls had already returned applied=true.

This creates a dangerous state-integrity gap:
- candidate model response executes mutating tools
- auditor rejects the response or retry fails
- user is told the turn was not applied
- state mutations from the rejected candidate may still persist

Goal
Make gameplay tool side effects transactional with respect to audited turn acceptance. A player turn should not permanently mutate campaign/session/character state until the accepted candidate response is known.

Acceptance Criteria
- State-mutating gameplay tool effects from a candidate response are staged or wrapped in a rollbackable transaction until the turn auditor accepts that candidate.
- If the auditor rejects the candidate, all tool side effects from that rejected candidate are discarded before retry.
- If retry fails due to provider rate limit, provider error, auditor failure, invalid JSON, or retry-budget exhaustion, all candidate tool side effects from that player input are discarded.
- User-visible messages like "your last input was not applied" are true with respect to persisted gameplay state.
- Read-only tools may execute normally, but the system must have an explicit way to classify read-only vs mutating tools.
- Add regression tests covering:
  1. mutating tool executes, auditor rejects, retry succeeds: only accepted retry mutations persist
  2. mutating tool executes, auditor rejects, retry fails: no candidate mutations persist
  3. read-only tool execution does not require staged mutation handling
- Debug/session traces should make it clear whether a tool call was staged, committed, or rolled back.
- Do not solve this by disabling native MCP tools or by trusting model self-reporting.

Implementation Notes
Likely approaches include:
- transaction/savepoint around candidate tool execution and audit acceptance
- staged mutation journal applied only after audit acceptance
- tool-executor wrapper that records and rolls back mutating operations

Prefer the smallest safe implementation that fits the current orchestrator/tool execution architecture.
close_reason: Already completed by eshyra-dwkm in commit 4d7154a (#244): per-attempt and per-turn SQLite SAVEPOINT rollback, explicit mutating/read-only classification, MCP bridge transaction tests, and committed/rolled-back debug dispositions. Focused tests pass on 2026-06-21.

notes:
Investigation finding: the per-turn SAVEPOINT (TURN_SAVEPOINT) + per-attempt SAVEPOINT (ATTEMPT_SAVEPOINT) added in #241 (eshyra-oobh) ALREADY make candidate tool mutations transactional for ALL transports including the Agent SDK MCP path — a real-bridge probe confirmed reject+retry-success keeps only the accepted mutation, and reject+retry-fail (provider session limit) persists nothing. The 'applied=true' the operator saw is the tool RESULT, not proof of persistence; the SAVEPOINT discards it. The real gaps this bug exposed were (1) no explicit read-only vs mutating tool classification, (2) no staged/committed/rolled-back observability so an operator could not confirm the discard, and (3) the only MCP test fabricated tool results and never exercised the executeTool bridge, so the rollback guarantee was unproven for the path that actually runs MCP mutations.

Delivered: required Tool.mutates classification + ToolRegistry.isMutating (unknown=>mutating fail-safe); ExecutedToolCall.mutates threaded through all 3 transports + into the turn trace; TurnCandidateDispositionEvent (committed/rolled_back with reason accepted|audit_rejected|turn_error) emitted at every release/rollback point and persisted by the CLI file sink; regression tests via a faithful BridgeMcpModel covering reject+retry-success, reject+retry-fail (no persistence, no scene log, no trace), read-only-needs-no-staging, and disposition tracing. CLI 'your last input was not applied' fires only on result.ok===false (outer rollback) so it is true wrt persisted state.
close_reason: Merged via PR #244 (squash 4d7154a). Added required Tool.mutates classification + isMutating, ExecutedToolCall.mutates across all transports + turn trace, TurnCandidateDispositionEvent committed/rolled_back observability persisted by CLI sink, and real-bridge MCP regression tests proving reject+retry-success / reject+retry-fail rollback. SAVEPOINT transactional guarantee confirmed pre-existing and now proven for the MCP path.

title: Add The Hollow Beneath Emberfall module smoke path
description:
Add a smoke path proving that Eshyra can create a campaign from a campaign template (the Emberfall setting), attach the starter module (The Hollow Beneath Emberfall) via a campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, run or simulate initial module progress, persist state, and resume with correct module progress.

This should be the adventure-module equivalent of a hello-world gameplay path.
design:
This does not need a full live model integration test if that would be brittle. A deterministic or semi-deterministic runtime/context-builder smoke path is enough for the first pass.

The important proof is that immutable module source content, campaign instance state (the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding and its progress), runtime context, and persistence all connect cleanly - and that progress updates never mutate the module source.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test, fixture, or scripted smoke path creates a campaign using the Emberfall campaign template and attaches The Hollow Beneath Emberfall starter module via a campaign-owned adventure run / module binding.
- The smoke path starts the module and records initial progress.
- The smoke path advances at least one location or scene.
- The smoke path reveals or preserves at least one secret correctly.
- The smoke path records an objective or encounter state change.
- The smoke path saves and reloads the campaign.
- After reload, the active adventure run / module binding and module progress are intact.
- The authored source module remains unchanged after progress updates.

title: Outline The Hollow Beneath Emberfall starter module
description:
Design the small first-party starter module - The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - at outline level before authoring the full fixture.

The outline should identify the adventure premise, starting hook, key locations, NPC roles, likely scenes, objectives, secrets, encounter concepts, reward, and possible endings.
design:
Keep this intentionally small. Avoid turning the starter module into a campaign arc.

Naming (ADR 0012): the setting is Emberfall (campaign template); the module is The Hollow Beneath Emberfall (scenario). "Ember Hollow" is informal shorthand only, not a separate place. EMBERFALL_HOLLOW is the legacy conflated sample.

Possible placeholder concept:
A local disturbance near Emberfall reveals an old sealed place below a mundane landmark. The module should demonstrate how authored secrets, keyed locations, NPC motives, and player divergence are handled by the engine.
acceptance_criteria:
- The module has a title (The Hollow Beneath Emberfall), premise, intended level range, intended party assumptions, and short summary.
- The outline identifies 3 to 5 keyed locations.
- The outline identifies at least one social encounter, one exploration obstacle, and one combat-capable encounter.
- The outline identifies secrets/clues and which scenes or locations can reveal them.
- The outline identifies objectives and ending states.
- The outline explicitly ties the module to the Emberfall setting without expanding Emberfall into a full adventure script.

title: Build The Hollow Beneath Emberfall hello-world adventure module
description:
Create a small first-party starter adventure module - The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - that serves as Eshyra's gameplay hello-world module.

The Emberfall setting itself should remain setting-scale campaign template content. This work adds a separate scenario-scale module located within or near Emberfall. The module should be intentionally small and useful for testing real play: opening hook, locations, scenes, at least one social beat, exploration, encounter resolution, reward, ending states, persistence, and resume.

Naming glossary (ADR 0012):
- Emberfall - the setting-scale village/region; campaign template. Preserve as setting content.
- The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - this starter adventure module (scenario-scale).
- Ember Hollow - informal shorthand only; not a separate canonical entity. (The ember-hollow label is a project tag, not a third concept.)
- EMBERFALL_HOLLOW - the existing legacy sample that conflates setting and scenario, to be split by this work.
design:
Target size:
- 3 to 5 keyed locations
- 1 to 2 combat-capable encounters
- 1 social encounter
- 1 exploration obstacle
- 3 to 6 secrets or clues
- 1 meaningful choice
- 1 reward
- 2 to 3 possible ending states

The purpose is engine coverage and product shape, not a large polished adventure. The module is immutable authored scenario source; play progress is recorded in the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding (eshyra-eh54.4), not in the module.
acceptance_criteria:
- A small first-party starter adventure module (The Hollow Beneath Emberfall) exists.
- The module is scenario-scale, not a replacement for the Emberfall campaign template/setting.
- The module exercises the adventure module schema, loader, campaign-owned adventure run / module binding and progress, runtime context, and progress persistence.
- The module supports a short playable path suitable for smoke testing.
- The module has enough structure to test hidden secrets, objectives, encounters, rewards, and alternate outcomes.
close_reason: All children complete (.1 outline #268, .2 fixture #269, .3 smoke #270). The Hollow Beneath Emberfall starter module exists as immutable source, loads via the loader, binds to a campaign, feeds the DM runtime context, and round-trips through persistence.

title: Feed adventure module context into DM runtime
description:
Feed bounded adventure module context into the DM runtime.

The DM runtime should receive the relevant module slice for the current situation, not the entire module. The context is derived from BOTH the immutable adventure module source AND the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding (eshyra-eh54.4). The context should help the model run the authored scenario while respecting campaign instance state, hidden-information boundaries, and player-driven divergence. When campaign truth conflicts with module source assumptions, campaign truth wins.
design:
The bounded context is composed from the immutable module source plus the campaign-owned progress object. Suggested bounded context fields:

- current module id/title
- current scene/location candidate
- nearby locations and exits
- relevant NPCs
- active objectives (authored definition + campaign progress)
- encounter/threat options (with campaign outcomes applied)
- unrevealed secrets that may become relevant (filtered by campaign reveal state)
- completed/bypassed module elements (from campaign progress)
- module deviations (from campaign state)

The module should guide the DM, not railroad play. The runtime must prefer campaign truth over source-module assumptions when they conflict.
acceptance_criteria:
- The runtime context builder can include adventure module context when a campaign has an active adventure run / module binding.
- The context slice is composed from both immutable module source and campaign-owned progress, and is bounded and situation-relevant.
- The context includes current or likely scene/location, nearby exits or transitions, relevant NPCs, active objectives, pending encounters/threats, and relevant unrevealed secrets when appropriate for DM-only context.
- The context reflects campaign progress and known deviations, and campaign truth overrides conflicting module assumptions.
- The full module is not dumped into every turn by default.
- Tests or golden fixtures verify the context slice for at least one active-module campaign state.
- Existing campaigns without active modules continue to work.
close_reason: Implemented bounded adventure module context slice (buildAdventureContextSlice + renderAdventureContextSlice), wired into context assembler via optional resolver and threaded through RunTurnDeps. Composes immutable module source + campaign run progress; campaign truth overrides module assumptions. Tests added. PR #265.

title: Add campaign binding and module progress state
description:
Add the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding and mutable module progress to campaign instance state.

A campaign should be able to say which module or modules are active without copying or mutating the authored module source. This is done with a campaign-owned structured object - acceptable names include AdventureRun, CampaignModuleBinding, ActiveAdventureModule, or ModuleProgressState - that references the immutable module by id and records module-specific progress. This object is part of campaign instance state (the fourth layer in ADR 0012); it is NOT a fifth content/state layer and must not be modeled as a separate top-level "adventure instance" peer.

The campaign should persist progress such as visited locations, completed or bypassed scenes, revealed secrets, completed/failed objectives, encounter outcomes, claimed treasure, active clocks/threats, started/completed session ids, status, and explicit deviations from authored assumptions.
design:
The implementation may introduce a structured campaign-owned object (AdventureRun / CampaignModuleBinding / ActiveAdventureModule / ModuleProgressState). It must live inside campaign instance state and reference the immutable module; it must never be written back to the adventure module source pack. It is part of the existing campaign-instance layer, not a new fifth layer.

Suggested shape (campaign-owned, one per active module):
- activeModuleId (reference to the immutable module)
- status
- startedAtSessionId
- completedAtSessionId
- visitedLocations
- completedOrBypassedScenes
- revealedSecrets
- completedOrFailedObjectives
- encounterOutcomes
- claimedTreasure
- activeClocksOrThreats
- moduleDeviations
- notes

A campaign may hold more than one such adventure run / module binding.

Do not require a strictly linear module state machine. A module should support nonlinear exploration, skipped scenes, alternate routes, and emergent deviations. Progress is the only mutable side; the referenced module source remains immutable and re-forkable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Campaign instance state can record one or more campaign-owned adventure runs / module bindings.
- The campaign-owned object references the immutable module id and holds the mutable progress for that campaign; the module source is never mutated.
- The object is explicitly part of campaign instance state, not a separate top-level content/state layer (no "adventure instance" peer layer).
- Module progress can represent active module id, status, started/completed session ids, visited locations, completed or bypassed scenes, revealed secrets, completed/failed objectives, defeated/bypassed encounter outcomes, claimed treasure, active clocks/threats, and module-specific notes.
- Module deviations can be recorded explicitly when play invalidates or alters authored assumptions, as campaign facts rather than edits to the module source.
- Campaign save/resume preserves active adventure runs / module bindings and their progress.
- Tests cover starting a module, updating progress, saving, loading, and verifying the source module remains unchanged.
notes:
Campaign-owned adventure run / module binding + progress implemented: campaign/adventureRun.ts (start/get/list/recordProgress), new adventure_run table (SCHEMA_VERSION 12 + v11_to_v12 migration), exported via internal.ts; 11 tests in test/adventureRun.test.ts + v11->v12 migration test. Save/resume verified via file reopen; module-source-unchanged guard included. PR #264 open: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/264 . Branch feat/eh54.4-adventure-run-state, worktree .worktrees/eh54.4. Left in_progress so dependents eshyra-eh54.5 and eshyra-eh54.6 stay blocked until merge. Close on merge.
Review fix (commit 56be370): added nested progress-delta validation at the write boundary (empty ids, encounter outcome enum + non-empty encounterId, non-negative integer clock fills, non-empty deviation id/description, non-empty optional session ids). Validation runs before the transaction so rejected deltas write nothing. +3 tests (now 16). Full suite 2239 pass / 0 fail.
close_reason: Campaign-owned adventure run / module binding + progress merged to main via PR #264 (squash, incl. nested progress-delta write-boundary validation review fix). Unblocks eshyra-eh54.5 and eshyra-eh54.6.

title: Add adventure module pack loading and validation
description:
Add loading and validation support for immutable adventure module source packs.

Adventure modules should be loadable as authored content alongside rules packs and campaign templates, but they should not be merged into the SRD rules pack or treated as mutable campaign instance state. This bead validates authored module source structure and references only; it does not load, validate, or model campaign progress (that is campaign instance state - eshyra-eh54.4).
design:
Keep the four layers logically separate (ADR 0012):

- rules pack: mechanical reference material (immutable)
- campaign template pack: setting/world reference material (immutable)
- adventure module pack: authored scenario source material (immutable)
- campaign instance: mutable actual-play state, including the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding that records progress (eshyra-eh54.4)

Loading and validation here applies only to the immutable module source pack. If the existing loader architecture already has a generic content-pack path, extend it in the smallest clean way. If it is rules-pack-specific, avoid forcing module content through SRD importer concepts.
acceptance_criteria:
- The content loading path can load an adventure module source pack or fixture.
- Module-pack validation fails closed on broken references.
- Validation catches at least: missing scene/location ids, missing scene exits, missing referenced NPCs, missing referenced objectives, missing encounter creature refs, missing treasure item refs, and incompatible or unknown setting/template refs where applicable.
- Module records can resolve references to existing rules-pack records without duplicating those records.
- Validation covers authored module structure and references only; it does not validate or require campaign progress state.
- Module loading is covered by focused tests and at least one small fixture.
- Existing rules-pack importer behavior remains unchanged.
notes:
Loader + cross-pack reference validation implemented: adventure/loadModule.ts, adventure/references.ts, exported via internal.ts; 15 tests in test/adventureModuleLoad.test.ts. Establishes the rulesRef '<kind>:<key>' resolution convention. PR #263 open: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/263 . Branch feat/eh54.3-adventure-module-loader, worktree .worktrees/eh54.3. Left in_progress so dependents eshyra-eh54.4 and eshyra-eh54.7.2 stay blocked until merge. Close on merge.
Review fix (commit 1d03cfa): enforce rulesRequirements.baseVersions against base meta.version; check requiredAddonPackIds against rules.addons only (base pack id no longer satisfies an add-on requirement). +4 tests (now 19), both bug tests verified to fail pre-fix. Full suite 2225 pass / 0 fail.
close_reason: Loader + cross-pack reference validation merged to main via PR #263 (squash, incl. baseVersions + add-on-only requiredAddonPackIds review fixes). Unblocks eshyra-eh54.4 and eshyra-eh54.7.2.

title: Add adventure module schema and typed records
description:
Add an initial adventure module schema and typed record model for immutable authored scenario content.

The schema represents adventure module source only - the authored scenario as written. It must not contain campaign-specific progress fields. Authored elements such as objectives, secrets, scenes, and clocks/threats are modeled as definitions of what is possible in the scenario; whether any of them has been completed, revealed, or advanced is campaign instance state recorded by the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding (eshyra-eh54.4), not by the module record.

The schema should support a small dungeon/adventure module without assuming every module is a linear script. It should support keyed locations, scenes, hooks, NPC roles, encounters, secrets, objectives, treasure, clocks or threats, exits/transitions, and endings.

The first version should be intentionally conservative. The goal is to create a stable destination for starter module content and runtime integration, not to model every possible published adventure format.
design:
Suggested initial concepts (authored source only):

AdventureModule
- id
- title
- summary
- intendedLevels
- intendedPartySize
- rulesetRefs
- settingCompatibility
- startingSituation
- hooks
- locations
- scenes
- npcs
- encounters
- treasure
- secrets
- objectives
- clocksOrThreats
- randomTables
- milestones
- endingStates
- provenance
- license

Important modeling constraint (ADR 0012):

Authored module truth and runtime campaign truth must remain separate. The module record is immutable authored scenario source. For example, the module may define that a sealed shrine lies under the old mill. Whether the players found it, destroyed the mill, bypassed the shrine, or changed the situation is recorded in campaign instance state (the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding), never on the module record. Objectives/secrets/clocks here are definitions of possibilities, not progress flags.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed adventure module root record exists, representing immutable authored scenario source.
- Module records include stable ids, title/name fields, summary/description fields, tags or categorization where useful, and provenance/license metadata.
- Initial child concepts are represented for hooks, locations, scenes, NPCs, encounters, secrets, objectives, treasure/rewards, clocks/threats, random tables if already supported by existing table concepts, and ending states - all as authored definitions, not progress.
- The schema contains no campaign-specific progress/status fields (no "visited", "revealed", or "completed" flags); progress lives in campaign instance state (eshyra-eh54.4).
- Module records can reference rules-pack content such as creatures, equipment, magic items, rules, actions, and tables without copying mechanical truth into the module.

title: Define adventure module domain boundaries
description:
Define and record the domain distinction between campaign templates/settings, adventure modules, rules packs, and mutable campaign state.

This should prevent Ember Hollow and other future setting templates from becoming overloaded with adventure-module responsibilities. It should also document how authored module content differs from player-discovered campaign truth and player-created deviations.
design:
Likely file location: docs/adr or the nearest existing architecture-decision location.

Capture examples:

- Rules pack: D&D SRD 5.1.
- Campaign template: Ember Hollow, Karameikos-like regional setting, Forgotten Realms-like broad setting.
- Adventure module: a haunted mine under Ember Hollow, Castle Amber-like keyed scenario, Lost Mine-like starter adventure.
- Campaign instance: the user's actual campaign with its chosen rules, setting, active modules, runtime state, and history.

This is primarily design/documentation, but it should be precise enough to guide schema and runtime work.
acceptance_criteria:
- An ADR or equivalent design note exists describing the four-way distinction: rules pack, campaign template, adventure module, campaign instance.
- The note explicitly states that campaign templates are setting-scale and adventure modules are scenario-scale.
- The note uses Ember Hollow as the example campaign template and a separate Ember Hollow starter adventure as the example module.
- The note states that module source content is immutable and module progress belongs in campaign state.
- The note states that player-driven divergence from the module should be recorded as campaign facts or module deviations, not applied as edits to the source module.
- The note gives examples of setting-scale content and module-scale content.

title: Add first-class adventure module support
description:
Problem

Eshyra currently has campaign state persistence and static rules-pack content, but it does not have a first-class representation for pre-written adventure or dungeon module content. That leaves no clear place for starter adventure content to go and forces setting-scale material such as the Emberfall setting to carry responsibilities that belong to a scenario-scale module.

A campaign template should represent a broad reusable world or setting, in the same general scope category as The Grand Duchy of Karameikos, Dragonlance, or Forgotten Realms. A dungeon or adventure module should represent an authored playable scenario, in the same general scope category as Castle Amber or The Lost Mine of Phandelver.

Goal

Introduce adventure modules as first-class immutable authored content, distinct from rules packs, campaign templates, and mutable campaign instance state. A campaign instance should be able to bind to one or more active modules via a campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, expose bounded module context to the DM runtime, persist module progress, and record player-driven deviations without mutating the source module.
design:
Architectural rule - four layers, defined in ADR 0012 (eshyra-eh54.1):

1. Rules packs define mechanical truth (immutable authored/imported source).
2. Campaign templates define reusable worlds/settings (immutable setting-scale source).
3. Adventure modules define authored playable scenarios (immutable scenario-scale source).
4. Campaign instances define actual play history and mutable state.

Adventure modules are immutable authored scenario content. A campaign may contain one or more campaign-owned adventure runs or module bindings that reference modules and record module-specific progress. These adventure runs are part of campaign instance state, not a fifth content/state layer. Do not introduce an "adventure instance" as a peer top-level layer.

Runtime adaptation belongs in campaign instance state as discovered facts, altered facts, completed objectives, revealed secrets, encounter outcomes, and explicit deviations from module assumptions - never written back to the module source.

This epic should avoid third-party adventure conversion until the module schema and runtime destination exist. The frozen starter-content bead can remain blocked until this epic creates somewhere for that content to go.

Naming glossary (see ADR 0012 and eshyra-eh54.7):
- Emberfall - the setting-scale village/region; campaign-template concept.
- The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - the first-party starter adventure module title (scenario-scale).
- Ember Hollow - informal project shorthand only; not a separate canonical entity.
- EMBERFALL_HOLLOW - the existing legacy sample that conflates setting and scenario, to be split by later eh54 work.
acceptance_criteria:
- Eshyra has a documented architecture distinction between the four layers: rules packs, campaign templates/settings, adventure modules, and campaign instances (ADR 0012).
- Adventure module content is represented as immutable authored source material.
- Module progress is represented as mutable campaign instance state via a campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, not as a fifth peer layer.
- A campaign instance can bind to one or more active adventure modules without mutating module source.
- The DM runtime has a path to receive bounded module context without dumping an entire module each turn.
- The Emberfall setting is preserved as setting-scale campaign template content, not forced to become the starter module itself.
- Follow-up work exists for a small first-party starter module (The Hollow Beneath Emberfall) that serves as the gameplay hello-world scenario.

title: Add opt-in session debug logging for prompt and turn diagnostics
description: Add an opt-in session debug logging mode to make live gameplay failures diagnosable without exposing secrets by default. The v0.1.1 native Windows smoke proved the packaged CLI can call the model, but the first turn produced a meta response claiming DM tools such as roll/world_query/mark_scene were unavailable. Debug logging should capture enough sanitized information to diagnose prompt/tool-protocol mismatches, context growth, character-creation state, and session recap behavior. Include per-session debug artifacts under the data root when enabled by an explicit flag/env var, such as ESHYRA_DEBUG_SESSION=1 or a CLI option. Log model call purpose, selected model/profile, prompt section names and approximate sizes, transcript/message counts, tool-protocol mode, available tool names or fenced-tool instructions, campaign/session ids, turn ids, checkpoint ids, and sanitized error/diagnostic events. Prefer redacted/structural logs by default; full prompt capture must be separately gated and clearly marked as sensitive if implemented. Add commands or documentation for locating and packaging debug logs for a bug report. Acceptance: a developer can reproduce a live turn issue and inspect what prompt/tool context was supplied, how large the session context was, and which model calls happened, without leaking API keys or OAuth tokens. Add tests for debug logging enabled/disabled, redaction, and log creation on both successful and failed turns.
close_reason: Implemented opt-in session debug logging (ESHYRA_DEBUG_SESSION). Adapter emits structural per-model-call records (ids, model/profile/auth label, tool protocol, provided-vs-forwarded tools, prompt section sizes, message structure, outcome) on success+failure; full mode adds sanitized content. File sink under <data-root>/debug. Docs + tests added. PR #240.

title: Add model usage tracking for gameplay and maintenance calls
description: Add structured model usage tracking so Eshyra can measure the real cost and context footprint of gameplay. The v0.1.1 native Windows smoke used about 3% of a Claude session for a short deferred-character run with one visible model turn and session close/recap, but it is unclear how much came from turn generation, session recap, prompt/context size, cache misses, or other maintenance calls. Track each model call with purpose, model/profile, provider/auth mode label, input token count, output token count, cache read/write token counts if exposed by the SDK/provider, elapsed time, success/failure, and a safe request/correlation id. Purposes should distinguish at least gameplay turn, session recap, campaign bible extraction, arc rollup, live test, and other maintenance calls. Persist usage in a local diagnostics/telemetry store under the data root and expose a CLI command to summarize usage by campaign/session/model/purpose. Do not log prompts, secrets, raw credentials, or player-private text by default. Acceptance: after a play session, the user can see how many model calls occurred, which purposes consumed tokens, and whether cache usage was observed. Add tests with fake model usage metadata and ensure failures are recorded without leaking secrets.
close_reason: Model usage tracking with best-effort sink complete. PR #243 open for review.

API:
export type CoverageStatus = { kind: 'record'; key: string } | { kind: 'child-of'; key: string } | { kind: 'ignored'; reason: string } | { kind: 'known-gap'; beadId: string } | { kind: 'unaccounted' }
