title: Repair SRD magic-item boundaries and embedded content
description:
Problem

Magic-item coverage improved substantially, but the latest audit found boundary and embedded-content failures.

Known high-confidence failures

- Figurine of Wondrous Power is present in the SRD but missing as magic-item:figurine-of-wondrous-power.
- magic-item:feather-token swallows the Figurine of Wondrous Power heading, rarity line, figurine variants, and Giant Fly stat block.
- Several magic-item tables are likely flattened into descriptions rather than emitted or structured.
- Magic items may contain embedded stat blocks, option tables, dice-result tables, command words, variants, and child entities that need explicit accounting.

Task

Repair magic-item boundary parsing and structured child content.

Implementation guidance

- Build on the bounded source span bead.
- Build on the document-wide table and stat-block inventory beads where available.
- Every magic item heading in the source should map to exactly one magic-item record unless intentionally ignored with reason.
- Magic-item descriptions should not swallow following magic-item headings.
- Embedded tables should be emitted as table records or structured child data.
- Embedded stat blocks should be linked to the stat-block representation chosen by the stat-block bead.
- Preserve source text and provenance for variants and subentries.

Regression cases

Add tests for:

- magic-item:feather-token does not include Figurine of Wondrous Power.
- magic-item:figurine-of-wondrous-power exists and has correct source span.
- Giant Fly is accounted for structurally.
- At least one magic-item option table is accounted for.
- At least one magic-item dice-result table is accounted for.
- Deck of Many Things accounts for Avatar of Death according to the stat-block modeling decision.

Acceptance criteria

- All source magic item headings are accounted for.
- Known boundary bleed is fixed.
- Magic-item tables and embedded stat blocks are not silently flattened without coverage mappings.
- Existing valid magic-item ids remain stable where possible.
notes: Implemented in worktree branch agent/eshyra-4a7.8-magic-item-boundaries. Added Figurine of Wondrous Power with 9 structured variants and Giant Fly link; bounded Feather Token; captured Avatar of Death traits/actions; emitted all 27 remaining Magic Items table structures with reviewed deterministic reconstruction. Source coverage known-gap eshyra-4a7.8: 27 -> 0. Generated semantic diff: 28 records added, 0 removed, only existing record changed is stat-block:avatar-of-death. Verification: npm run format/check/typecheck/test (1587 passed, 19 documented skips) and npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack pass.
close_reason: Magic-item boundaries, embedded stat blocks, variants, and all source table structures are now deterministically emitted and verified.

title: Complete SRD creature and NPC stat-block records
description:
Problem

Creature records are currently too skeletal for actual SRD-backed play. The audit found that creature records generally capture basic header stats but omit major stat-block content.

Example

creature:aboleth captures AC, HP, speed, ability scores, and CR, but the SRD stat block also contains saving throws, skills, senses, languages, Amphibious, Mucous Cloud, Probing Telepathy, Multiattack, Tentacle, Tail, Enslave, and Legendary Actions.

Task

Complete creature and NPC stat-block parsing so creature-like records preserve all structured source sections needed for play.

Expected fields or equivalent schema

- armor class,
- hit points,
- speed,
- ability scores,
- saving throws,
- skills,
- damage vulnerabilities,
- damage resistances,
- damage immunities,
- condition immunities,
- senses,
- languages,
- challenge rating,
- traits,
- actions,
- reactions,
- legendary actions,
- lair actions where present,
- regional effects where present,
- spellcasting blocks where present,
- variant notes where present.

Implementation guidance

- Use source-backed tests before changing parser logic.
- Preserve text where full semantic decomposition is not yet practical, but place it in the correct structured section.
- Do not discard action names, recharge text, attack bonuses, damage expressions, save DCs, or usage limitations.
- NPCs should follow the same stat-block completeness rules unless there is a documented reason for a separate schema.

Regression cases

Include tests for varied stat blocks:

- Aboleth: traits, actions, legendary actions.
- Dragon or similar complex creature: legendary/lair/regional content if present in SRD.
- Spellcasting creature/NPC.
- Creature with immunities/resistances.
- Embedded stat block from the document-wide stat-block bead.

Acceptance criteria

- Creature-like records contain all stat-block sections present in source.
- No major stat-block section remains only in flattened prose.
- Pack verification and importer tests cover representative complex stat blocks.
close_reason: All child slices complete and merged: keyed defensive/sense fields (eshyra-ez6v, #200), trait/action/reaction/legendary sections (eshyra-yevt, #202), and variant sidebars (eshyra-70xr, #203). Creature records now carry every stat-block section the SRD prints (header stats, saves/skills/damage/condition/senses/languages, traits/actions/reactions/legendary actions, variant notes); no major stat-block section remains only in flattened prose. SRD 5.1 has no per-creature lair actions/regional effects. verify:dnd5e-srd-pack green; source-coverage unaccounted=0 for the creature region.

title: Extract and account for SRD stat blocks document-wide
description:
Problem

The importer appears to find monster appendix creatures but misses stat-block-shaped content elsewhere in the SRD. The latest audit identified at least:

- Avatar of Death, embedded in Deck of Many Things on p. 218.
- Giant Fly, embedded in Figurine of Wondrous Power on p. 222.

These are source stat blocks and should not be silently flattened into magic-item descriptions without structured representation.

Task

Make stat-block extraction document-wide and account for embedded stat blocks.

Implementation guidance

- Detect stat-block-shaped content across the full SRD, not only the monster/NPC appendix.
- Decide and document whether embedded stat blocks are emitted as normal creature records, emitted as a distinct embedded-stat-block kind, or stored as structured child data on the containing record.
- Whatever model is chosen, the coverage gate must account for the source stat block.
- Preserve source provenance linking embedded stat blocks to both their own source span and containing source item when applicable.
- Do not duplicate content in uncontrolled prose and structured records without clear ownership.

Regression cases

Add tests proving that the source inventory detects and accounts for:

- Avatar of Death,
- Giant Fly,
- at least one ordinary monster appendix creature,
- at least one NPC stat block if NPCs remain a separate kind.

Acceptance criteria

- Stat-block detection runs over the whole SRD.
- Embedded stat blocks are represented or intentionally accounted for.
- Avatar of Death and Giant Fly no longer disappear as unstructured magic-item prose.
- Existing creature and NPC record ids remain stable unless a documented schema decision requires otherwise.

Wrapped values (Avatar Condition Immunities/Senses) recovered from containing item's reflowed description via cleanTextByName; Giant Fly via single-line raw. Traits/actions (Avatar Reaping Scythe) still in prose — 4a7.8 must not strip inline prose until those are structured.

New stat-block kind emits Avatar of Death + Giant Fly with full keyed fields, container statBlockRefs, and inline-source provenance; source-coverage flips to record:stat-block:*. title: Extract and account for every SRD table document-wide
description:
Problem

The latest audit found that table coverage is still incomplete. The pack has more table records than before, but many SRD tables are still missing or flattened into prose.

High-confidence missing or insufficiently represented examples

- Dragonborn Draconic Ancestry table, p. 5.
- The 12 class progression tables.
- Druid Circle Spells tables.
- Oath of Devotion Spells table.
- Sorcerer Creating Spell Slots table.
- Draconic Bloodline Draconic Ancestry table.
- Apparatus of the Crab Levers table.
- Bag of Beans tables.
- Bag of Tricks table.
- Carpet of Flying table.
- Feather Token table.
- Horn of Valhalla table.
- Iron Flask table.
- Robe of Useful Items table.
- Wand of Wonder table.
- Sentient magic item property tables.
- Other magic-item option tables with dice rows or named choices.

Task

Make table extraction document-wide and require every source table to be accounted for.

Implementation guidance

- Use PDF text and coordinate artifacts where needed.
- Detect table captions, heading-adjacent tables, repeated column-header patterns, and dice-result tables.
- Do not limit table extraction to one chapter or to previously known tables.
- Preserve source row order, typography, and page provenance.
- For nested/grouped tables, use the representation already chosen for the importer, or document and test the chosen representation if not yet formalized.
- Some tables may ultimately become structured child data rather than top-level table records. That is acceptable if the coverage gate records the mapping.

Tests

Add regression tests for at least:

- Dragonborn Draconic Ancestry.
- One class progression table.
- One subclass spell table.
- Sorcerer Creating Spell Slots.
- One magic-item dice-result table.
- One magic-item option/property table.

Acceptance criteria

- Document-wide source table inventory exists.
- Every detected table is emitted, mapped to structured child data, or explicitly ignored.
- Known missing tables from the audit no longer disappear into prose without accounting.
- Table parsing fails closed when expected row counts or headers change.
notes: PR #195 review fix pushed (a68115c): coverage evaluator now resolves explicit record-type rules BEFORE the name auto-match, fixing the duplicate-caption bug where both 'Draconic Ancestry' captions (p5 Races, p44 Sorcerer) were claimed by table:draconic-ancestry. p44 now maps to table:draconic-bloodline-draconic-ancestry via an explicit per-chapter record rule; sentinels + evaluator unit tests pin both mappings. Close this bead when the PR merges.

title: Refactor SRD parsers to consume bounded source spans
description:
Problem

Multiple audit findings point to parser boundary failures:

- Every subclass record description appears to swallow its subclass feature headings and feature bodies.
- magic-item:feather-token swallows the following Figurine of Wondrous Power entry.
- Flattened descriptions are masking places where structured records or child objects should exist.

These are not isolated content mistakes; they indicate that parsers are consuming source spans with brittle stop conditions.

Depends on

This should build on the source inventory/coverage gate bead if possible. The coverage gate should expose the incorrect spans and provide regression cases.

Task

Refactor SRD importer parsing so major record parsers consume explicitly bounded source spans derived from the source structure inventory or equivalent deterministic heading map.

Parser spans should be explicit for at least:

- classes,
- subclasses,
- class features,
- subclass features,
- magic items,
- rules sections,
- tables,
- stat blocks.

Implementation guidance

- Avoid parser logic that reads until a loose text pattern happens to match.
- Prefer start/end offsets, page ranges, or source item boundaries that are deterministic.
- A subclass record description should contain only the subclass overview text, not the subclass feature records.
- A magic-item record should stop before the next magic-item heading.
- Feature records should own feature text once, not duplicate it through parent descriptions.
- Preserve existing record ids unless a source item was genuinely missing.

Regression cases

Add tests for:

- subclass:champion does not include Improved Critical or later Champion feature bodies in its subclass description.
- subclass:circle-of-the-land does not include Natural Recovery or later Circle of the Land feature bodies in its subclass description.
- magic-item:feather-token does not include the Figurine of Wondrous Power heading or figurine variants.
- Figurine of Wondrous Power has its own bounded source span, even if actual record emission is completed in the magic-item bead.

Acceptance criteria

- Major record parsers operate on explicit source spans.
- Known subclass and magic-item boundary bleed cases are fixed or fail visibly in tests.
- No existing valid records lose source-backed content.
- Pack generation remains deterministic.
notes: Fixed via PR #194 (branch work/eshyra-4a7.2). parseSubclasses + parseMagicItems now bound bodies at deterministic font-tier heading boundaries (gated on multi-tier slice). Eliminated all 12 swallowed-feature-heading audit findings; Feather Token no longer swallows Figurine of Wondrous Power / Giant Fly. 13 generated records changed (12 subclass descriptions + feather-token), 0 added/removed. verify:dnd5e-srd-pack matches; source-coverage artifacts unchanged (Figurine stays known-gap for 4a7.8). Awaiting review.
close_reason: Merged in PR #194 (sqaush 9f0fbf6)

title: Add SRD source inventory and coverage gate
description:
Problem

The importer can currently pass tests while the source PDF still contains untracked structured content. The latest audit found missing or flattened source structures even though there are no open importer issues.

Examples from the latest audit

- Figurine of Wondrous Power appears in the SRD but is not emitted as magic-item:figurine-of-wondrous-power.
- Avatar of Death and Giant Fly stat blocks appear outside the monster appendix but are not emitted as creature-like records.
- Many named tables are missing as table records or structured child data.
- Class progression tables are not represented.
- Dragonborn Draconic Ancestry table is not represented.
- Subclass descriptions swallow subclass feature text while separate feature records also exist.

Task

Create a deterministic SRD source inventory and coverage gate.

The inventory should scan the vendored SRD PDF text/coordinate artifacts and identify source structures that require accounting:

- major section headings,
- ancestry headings,
- class headings,
- subclass headings,
- feature headings,
- spell headings,
- magic item headings,
- creature/NPC/stat-block headings,
- table captions or table-shaped structures,
- condition headings,
- action headings,
- feat headings,
- trap, disease, poison, and hazard headings,
- embedded stat blocks outside the monster appendix.

For every inventoried source item, the coverage gate should require exactly one of:

1. emitted as a top-level record,
2. emitted as structured child data on a top-level record,
3. intentionally ignored with a stable reason.

Implementation guidance

- Prefer a machine-readable inventory artifact, for example JSON, committed only if it is deterministic and useful for review.
- Include source page, source heading text, inferred kind, and matching record id or ignore reason.
- The coverage check should fail closed when a new source item appears without a mapping.
- Do not rely on fuzzy prose containment as sufficient coverage for structured tables/stat blocks/options.
- It is acceptable to start with conservative heuristics and an explicit allowlist, as long as unaccounted source items fail the check.
- The output should be reviewer-friendly enough to explain why a source item was or was not expected to become a record.

Tests

Add focused tests proving that the inventory detects at least:

- Figurine of Wondrous Power,
- Avatar of Death,
- Giant Fly,
- Dragonborn Draconic Ancestry table,
- at least one class progression table,
- at least one subclass feature heading,
- at least one magic-item option table.

Acceptance criteria

- A new check exists that compares source inventory to generated records.
- The check fails for unaccounted source structures.
- Existing pack verification still passes.
- The current known gaps are visible in the new inventory/coverage output rather than hidden in passing tests.
- No manual content is inserted into records to satisfy the check.
design:
ARCHITECTURE (from 2026-06-11 empirical font-height probe of SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf via extractPdfText):

Font-height tier map (PageText.lineHeights, already exposed by extract.ts):
- h=25.9 chapter titles (25 lines)
- h=18.0 section titles (105)
- h=13.9 subsection headings incl. subclass names (307)
- h=12.0 RECORD-LEAF headings (1398): spell names (e.g. Acid Arrow p114), magic items (Feather Token p221, Figurine of Wondrous Power p221, Bag of Beans p209, Wand of Wonder p249), creatures (Aboleth p261), EMBEDDED STAT BLOCKS (Avatar of Death p218, Giant Fly p222), TABLE CAPTIONS (Draconic Ancestry p5+p44, The Barbarian p8), subclass features (Improved Critical p25)
- h=10.8 sidebar/callout headings (376; e.g. Sacred Plants and Wood p22, Equipment Packs p70) — parseClassCallouts territory
- h=10.0 page-1/2 legal front matter only (11)
- h=9.8 body prose
- h=8.9 TABLE CELLS/HEADERS (2489; e.g. 'd10 Damage Type Gem' rows in Ring of Resistance p237, progression rows p8)

Detectors:
1. Inventory item = line with h>=10.5 (~2211 items). Tier from height. Merge adjacent same-tier wrapped heading lines (extractor only merges h>=14).
2. Caption-less embedded table = maximal run of h~8.9 lines; attach to nearest preceding leaf heading.
3. Structural classification: heading followed by /^(Tiny|Small|Medium|Large|Huge|Gargantuan) .+,/ body line => stat-block; heading followed by 8.9-run => table-caption; else plain heading.
4. inferredKind from containing chapter via existing sections.ts anchors.

Coverage statuses per item: record:<key> | child-of:<key> | ignored:<reasonCode> | known-gap:<beadId>. Anything unmatched => UNACCOUNTED => gate throws (fail closed). Matching: (a) normalized-name auto-match against emitted records, (b) rule-based ignore predicates with stable reason codes (NOT giant per-item lists; e.g. spell-list headers, legal headings, TOC), (c) known-gap rules referencing epic children (4a7.3 tables, 4a7.4 stat blocks, 4a7.6 progression, 4a7.7 ancestry, 4a7.8 figurine).

FILE MAP:
- Create packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceInventory.ts — pure PageText[] -> SourceInventoryItem[]
- Create packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceInventoryCoverage.ts — (inventory, records) -> coverage report + SourceInventoryCoverageError
- Modify index.ts runImporter — build inventory + coverage post-parse, throw on UNACCOUNTED, write source-inventory.json + source-coverage.json artifacts
- Modify verify-dnd5e-srd-pack/cli.ts — regenerate-and-diff the new artifacts
- Modify create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts — include artifacts in bundle reports
- Artifact location: pack dir alongside manifest.json IF pack loader tolerates extra files, else packages/core/data/srd-source-inventory/ (decide at impl; check loadRulesPack strictness)
- Tests: packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceInventory.test.ts + sourceInventoryCoverage.test.ts (fixture PageText), packages/core/test/srdSourceInventoryArtifact.test.ts (committed-artifact sentinels)

Sentinel assertions (committed artifact): Figurine of Wondrous Power => known-gap:eshyra-4a7.8; Avatar of Death + Giant Fly => known-gap:eshyra-4a7.4 (stat-block classified); Draconic Ancestry p5 => table-caption, known-gap:eshyra-4a7.7; The Barbarian p8 => table-caption, known-gap:eshyra-4a7.6; Improved Critical => record:feature:improved-critical; Ring of Resistance embedded d10 table => known-gap:eshyra-4a7.3.

INTEGRATION: reports may flow through srdAudit finding category (new 'unaccounted-source-structure') for bundle visibility, but the HARD gate lives in runImporter. sourceCoverage.ts name-list layer stays (regression net) — this is the structural superset.
notes: IMPORTANT integration constraint (added by Claude review 2026-06-11): this is NOT greenfield. The repo already has a two-layer audit mechanism: packages/core/src/rules/srdAudit.ts implements the audit finding categories (swallowed-feature-heading, class-proficiency-bleed, missing-coverage) and packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceCoverage.ts is the curated SOURCE-truth layer (name lists independent of what the importer emits; see its header comment for the lifecycle/design rationale). The new PDF-derived structural inventory must EXTEND or REPLACE this machinery deliberately — do not build a parallel third coverage system. Natural shape: the inventory becomes a generated source-truth artifact that supersedes/feeds the hand-curated gap lists in sourceCoverage.ts, and the coverage gate reports through the existing srdAudit finding pipeline (new finding category is fine). The current 13 structure-audit findings (12 subclass swallowed-feature + 1 druid proficiency-bleed) are existing srdAudit output, not new discoveries — keep them reproducible. Follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md including its hard-stop wording.

title: Make SRD importer self-auditing against source PDF
description:
Problem

The SRD importer has no open tracked issues, but the latest manual audit shows the pack is not yet complete or accurately bounded against the source PDF. The importer has made real progress, but remaining failures are now systemic rather than isolated row omissions.

Observed audit facts

- The current generated pack has about 1,650 records.
- verify:dnd5e-srd-pack, check, typecheck, and tests pass.
- The audit bundle metadata still reported srdStructureAudit.hasFindings: true.
- The pack captures broad SRD content, but much of it is flattened into descriptions rather than represented as usable structured records.
- Some source boundaries are still wrong: subclass records swallow feature text, and Feather Token swallows Figurine of Wondrous Power.
- Some document-scoped structures are missed: embedded stat blocks such as Avatar of Death and Giant Fly are not emitted as creature-like records.
- Creature records are skeletal compared with SRD stat blocks.
- Class records omit class skill choices, tool proficiencies, starting equipment options, spellcasting progression, and class progression tables.
- Many source tables are missing as table records or structured child data.

Goal

Make the SRD importer self-auditing against the source PDF so future audits do not rely on manual archaeology. Every source heading, table, stat block, and structured rules object in the SRD should be accounted for as one of:

1. an emitted top-level record,
2. structured child data on an emitted record,
3. an intentionally ignored source item with an explicit reason.

Non-goals

- Do not hand-author canonical SRD pack content.
- Do not weaken current pack verification or regression tests.
- Do not claim source coverage based only on flattened prose when the source content is structured and needed for play.
- Do not opportunistically rewrite unrelated importer code without failing tests or audit findings motivating the change.

Agent instructions

title: Fail closed when SRD ancestry extraction under-extracts races
description:
## Problem

The D&D SRD 5.1 importer slices the Races section and then calls parseAncestries. The section anchor failure path is fail-closed, but parseAncestries itself can still return an empty or partial result if the expected race/subrace boundaries are not found inside an otherwise valid slice.

This undermines the deterministic importer goal: a PDF extraction/layout drift could produce a valid-looking rules pack with missing ancestry records.

## Relevant files

- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts
- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.ts
- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.test.ts or equivalent importer tests

## Requirements

- Add explicit ancestry coverage validation for the SRD 5.1 corpus.
- Fail closed when the parsed ancestry set is empty or missing expected parent/subrace records.
- Include useful diagnostics listing missing expected names.
- Keep section-anchor failures distinct from parser-coverage failures.
- Ensure the failure happens before writing manifest.json / records.json.

## Expected SRD 5.1 coverage

Parent races:
- Dragonborn
- Dwarf
- Elf
- Gnome
- Half-Elf
- Half-Orc
- Halfling
- Human
- Tiefling

Subraces:
- Hill Dwarf
- Mountain Dwarf
- High Elf
- Wood Elf
- Dark Elf (Drow)
- Lightfoot
- Stout
- Forest Gnome
- Rock Gnome

## Acceptance criteria

- A test fixture with a valid races slice but no recognized race headings causes runImporter or the ancestry parsing path to throw.
- A fixture missing one expected ancestry name throws and names the missing record.
- The happy-path SRD import still emits the expected ancestry count.
- Error messages are deterministic and suitable for CI logs.
close_reason: Implemented exact SRD 5.1 ancestry coverage validation before pack writes, with deterministic missing-name diagnostics and no/partial Races fixture coverage; verification passed: npm run typecheck, touched-file Biome CI, npm run test.

title: Fix demo rerun session id collision after PR rebase
description: During rebase of PR 25 onto origin/main, npm run test failed in packages/cli/test/play.test.ts: runDemo > reuses an existing demo campaign on a later run. Symptom: SessionError session 'session-2' already exists in campaign 'campaign-1'. Investigate whether the rebase integration introduced or exposed a demo rerun id-generation bug, then fix with verification. Parent context: loreweaver-d4r.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause is recorded; an automated test covers demo rerun without duplicate session ids; npm run typecheck and npm run test pass after the fix.
notes:
Evidence: after rebasing PR 25 onto origin/main, npm run test fails reproducibly in packages/cli/test/play.test.ts runDemo > reuses an existing demo campaign on a later run. Stack points to packages/cli/src/play.ts:149 createDemoCampaign, then core startSession rejects duplicate session 'session-2' in campaign 'campaign-1'. Recent change on main added runDemo and a test using baseDeps() twice; baseDeps resets deterministic IDs for each call, so a second demo run can generate IDs already used by the first run.
Pattern analysis: runPlay/runDemo expect PlayDeps.nextId to produce unique ids within the target DB. Production buildPlayDeps uses timestamp plus randomness, but packages/cli/test/play.test.ts baseDeps starts ids at 0 for each call. The failing demo rerun test uses a new baseDeps against the same in-memory DB, so the second run can reuse closed-session ids from the first run. Working pattern is to keep one ID source for multiple invocations against the same DB, or otherwise seed a unique offset.
Hypothesis: the implementation path is valid; the failing test fixture violates the nextId uniqueness contract by resetting the deterministic ID generator between demo runs against the same DB. Minimal test: reuse the same PlayDeps/id source for both runDemo calls while swapping the IO object for the second run. Expected result: second run takes the existing-campaign branch and starts a unique later session.
Result: changed packages/cli/test/play.test.ts demo rerun test to reuse the same PlayDeps/id source while swapping only IO for the second run. Targeted verification npm run test -- packages/cli/test/play.test.ts passed with 12 tests. Full verification npm run typecheck passed; npm run test passed with 35 files passed / 1 skipped and 223 tests passed / 1 skipped.
close_reason: Root cause was a test fixture resetting deterministic IDs across two demo runs against one DB; fixed the fixture to reuse the same ID source. Verification: npm run typecheck and npm run test passed.

title: E8 Dolt checkpoint/history/branching subsystem
description:
Goal: the Dolt-backed checkpoint / history / branching subsystem. SQLite stays the
authoritative live operational store; this subsystem makes Dolt the authoritative
checkpoint/history/branching store, OFF the per-turn hot path.

MVP must include (all in scope, none deferred):
- Deterministic SQLite -> Dolt checkpoint export (same SQLite state => identical bytes).
- A Dolt commit per meaningful checkpoint (session close; arc roll-up).
- List checkpoints.
- Restore a checkpoint into a NEW SQLite working copy.
- Fork a campaign from a checkpoint into a NEW Dolt branch (+ materialized SQLite copy).
- Explicit, verified separation from the beads Dolt storage / remotes / ref-namespace.

Hard constraints: Dolt is NEVER invoked in the per-turn write path; SQLite is the
single live truth (Dolt trails to last checkpoint, like a git working tree vs last
commit); there are NOT two independent live truths.

User-visible outcome: a player can checkpoint a campaign, list past checkpoints,
restore an old checkpoint into a fresh working copy, and fork a campaign timeline.
design:
## Architecture

Dolt is invoked via the `dolt` CLI ONLY at checkpoint time (no long-running
`dolt sql-server`, no per-turn calls) — this is what keeps it off the hot path and
avoids server-lifecycle complexity. Each campaign has its own Dolt repo directory,
created/located independently of the beads Dolt repo.

A `CheckpointStore` in core composes three lower units:
1. `serialize` — pure SQLite -> canonical snapshot (deterministic, no Dolt, offline-testable).
2. `doltRepo` — thin wrapper over the `dolt` CLI for one repo dir (the ONLY file that shells to `dolt`).
3. `separation` — guard proving the Loreweaver Dolt location/remote/ref-namespace is disjoint from beads.

## Determinism contract

`serialize(db)` reads every user table (excludes sqlite internal + any
`sqlite_%`), and emits a single canonical `snapshot.sql` string:
- tables ordered by name (ASCII);
- columns in `PRAGMA table_info` ordinal order;
- rows ordered by full-row tuple (stable total order);
- fixed value formatting (NULL as `NULL`, integers bare, text single-quoted with
  `''` escaping, blobs as `X'..'`).
Same SQLite content => byte-identical string (acceptance #8). This artifact is what
gets loaded into Dolt and committed, so `dolt_diff`/`AS OF` are meaningful.

## File map

- `packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/separation.ts` — `assertSeparateFromBeads(doltDir, beadsDir)`.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts` — `serializeCampaign(db): string`.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/doltRepo.ts` — `DoltRepo` (init, applySnapshot, commit, log, branch, checkoutInto).
- `packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/store.ts` — `CheckpointStore` (checkpoint, list, restoreToNewWorkingCopy, forkFromCheckpoint).
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` — barrel exports.
- `packages/core/test/checkpoint.*.test.ts` — one suite per unit.

## Hot-path / separation constraints

- `CheckpointStore` is invoked only by E6 session-close and E4 arc roll-up — never
  from `mutate_state` / the turn loop. This is a design rule enforced by where the
  call sites are (not by code in this epic).
- SQLite remains single live truth; restore/fork always materialize a NEW `.db`
  working copy and never mutate the live campaign DB in place.
- `separation` rejects any Dolt dir that is inside, equal to, or shares a remote
  URL / `refs/dolt/*` namespace with the beads Dolt repo.

## Test gating

`serialize` and `separation` are pure and run offline (no Dolt). `doltRepo` and
`CheckpointStore` suites use `describe.skipIf(!doltAvailable)` (probe `dolt version`)
so CI without the `dolt` binary stays green while the capability is proven where
`dolt` exists.

## Tradeoffs

The serializer is the deterministic export-mapping component Dolt-only would avoid;
accepted because it keeps the per-turn path embedded/zero-ops and yields a
diffable, byte-stable history at session granularity (the campaign's natural
versioning unit).
acceptance_criteria: 1. serializeCampaign is deterministic (same SQLite => byte-identical snapshot), proven offline. 2. A checkpoint creates a dolt commit; list returns it. 3. Restore materializes a NEW SQLite working copy round-trip-identical to the source. 4. Fork creates a NEW dolt branch + isolated SQLite copy; changes in fork do not affect origin. 5. Separation guard rejects any Dolt dir nested in/equal to/sharing remote or refs with the beads Dolt repo. 6. No checkpoint code path is reachable from the per-turn loop. All E8 child tasks closed.
notes: SYNTHESIS UPDATE 2026-05-17: Checkpoint/restore/fork remains a core text-first product differentiator and future demo surface. Keep Dolt checkpointing separate from both the per-turn path and beads storage; this supports restore/fork/history without early VTT/native-mobile scope.

title: E0 Foundation: TS scaffold, core/CLI boundary, SQLite, Agent SDK
description: Foundational scaffold every other sub-epic builds on. TypeScript project, UI-agnostic core library vs thin CLI boundary, SQLite persistence layer (one DB file per campaign), Claude Agent SDK wiring, configuration.
design:
## Architecture

npm-workspaces monorepo. `@loreweaver/core` is the UI-agnostic library; `@loreweaver/cli`
is a thin consumer that depends on core (never the reverse). The workspace package
boundary is the enforced core/CLI seam (acceptance #1). TypeScript strict, ESM
(`"type": "module"`, `NodeNext`). Tests: vitest. SQLite: `better-sqlite3` (synchronous,
real transactions with automatic rollback on throw). Model access is isolated behind a
local `ModelClient` interface; an `AgentSdkModelClient` adapts the Claude Agent SDK so
the rest of the codebase never imports the SDK directly.

## Tech stack

- Node 24, TypeScript ^5.6, ESM/NodeNext, `tsc --build` project references.
- vitest ^2 for tests (`vitest run`).
- better-sqlite3 ^11 (+ @types/better-sqlite3).
- @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk (Claude Agent SDK, TypeScript) — installed via npm,
  wrapped behind `ModelClient`; exact SDK surface confined to one adapter file.

## File map

- `package.json` — root: workspaces, scripts (build/test/typecheck), shared devDeps.
- `tsconfig.base.json` — shared strict compiler options.
- `tsconfig.json` — root solution file (project references to both packages).
- `vitest.config.ts` — test discovery (`packages/**/test/**/*.test.ts`).
- `.env.example` — documents LOREWEAVER_DB_PATH, LOREWEAVER_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
- `packages/core/package.json` — core package + deps.
- `packages/core/tsconfig.json` — composite build config.
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` — public barrel: re-exports config, persistence, model, seams, `CORE_VERSION`.
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — `LoreweaverConfig`, `ConfigError`, `loadConfig(env)`.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/db.ts` — `openDatabase(path)`, `withTransaction(db, fn)`.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/schema.ts` — `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `initSchema(db)` (meta table).
- `packages/core/src/model/client.ts` — `ModelClient`, `ModelMessage` interfaces.
- `packages/core/src/model/agentSdkClient.ts` — `AgentSdkModelClient` adapter (only file importing the SDK).
- `packages/core/src/seams.ts` — empty interface stubs: Orchestrator, ContextAssembler, ToolLayer, MemorySubsystem, WorldSubsystem, Persistence (filled by E1–E7).
- `packages/core/test/*.test.ts` — unit tests per module.
- `packages/cli/package.json` — cli package, depends on `@loreweaver/core`.
- `packages/cli/tsconfig.json` — composite, references core.
- `packages/cli/src/index.ts` — thin entry: `buildBanner`, `main` (prints version + resolved config).
- `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts` — tests pure `buildBanner`.

## Boundaries / tradeoffs

- Core has zero dependency on cli (asserted by core building standalone).
- SDK API surface is uncertain at plan time; confined to `agentSdkClient.ts` and verified
  against installed types during T5. Unit tests use a fake `ModelClient`; the real
  round-trip is a single integration test gated on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- Seam interfaces are intentionally empty now; "typecheck" == `tsc --build` succeeds.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Core package builds with zero UI deps; CLI consumes core. 2. SQLite layer creates a campaign DB and passes a transactional write/rollback test. 3. Agent SDK wrapper makes a successful round-trip model call behind the interface. 4. Component interface stubs exist and typecheck.
notes: SYNTHESIS UPDATE 2026-05-17: E0 must keep Claude Agent SDK as an adapter only. The core model seam should grow toward provider adapters and model profiles (premium_dm, state_extractor, summarizer, rules_adjudicator, memory_reconciler, embedding_provider, economy_or_experimental). Initial config may still expose Anthropic/Claude settings, but naming and interfaces should avoid implying Claude is the only provider.

title: Loreweaver: Agentic DM (solo persistent campaign MVP)
description:
Goal: a text-based agentic Dungeon Master that runs a single-player, persistent D&D campaign across many sessions, where the world changes over time and continuity is preserved within a bounded model-context budget.

User-visible outcome: from a local CLI, the player creates a character, starts/resumes/auto-closes play sessions, and converses with a DM agent that narrates, voices NPCs, adjudicates rulings, and advances an authored adventure while remembering the campaign across sessions.

Scope: MVP = solo persistent campaign on D&D 5e SRD content via the Claude Agent SDK (Pro plan), TypeScript. Non-goals (deferred): prose-rules RAG, semantic/RAG memory retrieval, general module importer, model-generated modules, web/multiplayer/long-running service, party/turn-taking, external character import.

This is an overarching epic decomposed into sub-epics E0-E7 (see Design).
design:
LOCKED DECISIONS:
- Rules: refined Hybrid. Model-trusted for narrative rulings; ALL math/dice/state via deterministic tools; structured SRD stat-block lookup (not fuzzy RAG); prose-rules RAG deferred.
- Memory: hierarchical pyramid (scene->session->arc->campaign_bible) as CORE; bounded always-on context independent of campaign length; anchored by exact provenance-annotated structured state re-asserted every turn; raw scene_log persisted from day one; semantic RAG deferred as future drill-down accelerator; never RAG-only.
- World: immutable authored module template (schema files) + per-campaign overlay-fact diff (latest-wins, git-like, provenance built in); module schema is the real deliverable; MVP seeds via ONE-TIME model-assisted conversion of ONE openly-licensed adventure; general importer deferred.
- Architecture: UI-agnostic TypeScript CORE library (Orchestrator, Context Assembler, Tool layer, Memory subsystem, World subsystem, Persistence) + THIN CLI front-end. Future web/multiplayer = new front-end on same core, deferred.
- Lifecycle: Campaign (long-lived) > Session (explicit start; AUTO-CLOSE on graceful exit runs recap + scene->session roll-up + state reconciliation + arc roll-up if milestone) > Scene (roll-up granularity, summaries written incrementally). Crash/hard-kill leaves session open; relaunch offers Resume vs Close&recap; canon crash-safe via transactional mutate_state + incremental scene summaries; close pipeline idempotent.
- Storage: HYBRID persistence (DECIDED, NOT deferred). SQLite is the AUTHORITATIVE LIVE operational store for active gameplay (embedded, per-turn ACID writes, one .db working copy per active campaign). Dolt is the AUTHORITATIVE checkpoint/history/branching store. At meaningful checkpoints (session close; arc roll-up) a DETERMINISTIC SQLite->Dolt export serializes all campaign tables and dolt-commits. Capabilities required in MVP: list checkpoints; restore a checkpoint into a NEW SQLite working copy; fork a campaign from a checkpoint into a NEW Dolt branch (+ materialized SQLite working copy). HARD CONSTRAINTS: Dolt is NEVER in the per-turn hot path; there are NOT two independent live truths (SQLite is the single live truth, Dolt trails to last checkpoint like a git working-tree vs last commit); Loreweaver Dolt storage/remotes/ref-namespace are EXPLICITLY separated from the beads Dolt repo (own dir, no piggybacking on refs/dolt/data). Authored module content remains version-controlled schema files imported at campaign creation.
- Language: TypeScript + official Claude Agent SDK (SDK is Python/TS only; TS chosen for schema typing, review legibility vs C#/Kotlin, shared types with future web front-end).

DECOMPOSITION (sub-epics, build order E0 -> E8 ; E1 || E3 ; -> E7 -> E4 -> E2 -> E5 -> E6):
- E0 Foundation: TS scaffold, core/CLI boundary, SQLite LIVE persistence, Agent SDK wiring, config. (Unchanged by Hybrid: SQLite remains the live store; persistence seam swappable.)
- E8 Dolt checkpoint/history/branching subsystem: deterministic SQLite->Dolt export, checkpoint commit, list checkpoints, restore-into-new-SQLite-working-copy, fork-from-checkpoint-into-new-branch, explicit beads-Dolt separation guard. NOT in per-turn path. (NEW, MVP, depends on E0.)
- E1 SRD reference store: structured monsters + spells + character-build options (races/classes/subclasses/backgrounds/feats/equipment/spell lists per SRD) + lookup_srd tool.
- E2 World subsystem: module schema, one-time model-assisted conversion of one open-licensed adventure, template + overlay-fact resolution, world_query tool. Conversion step gated on the legal-source blocker task; schema work not gated.
- E3 Game-state subsystem: canonical structured state tables (character/inventory/plot_flags/clock) with provenance, mutate_state tool as SOLE canon+overlay writer, transactional crash-safe writes.
- E4 Memory pyramid: scene_log (append-only), incremental scene_summary, session_recap + arc_summary roll-up steps, campaign_bible reconciliation, structural memory_drilldown tool.
- E5 Orchestrator + tools: turn loop, Context Assembler (bounded prompt = bible + arc + last recap + state snapshot + live scene transcript), roll, mark_scene, DM system prompt encoding the Hybrid rules contract.
- E6 Session lifecycle + CLI: campaign create/fork, start/resume/auto-close, idempotent close pipeline, thin CLI front-end. Session-close and arc roll-up INVOKE the E8 checkpoint export.
- E7 Character creation & import: MVP agent-guided conversational SRD-compliant creation with deterministic validation tools, output = canonical character record via mutate_state. Import (D&D Beyond/OCR/VTT) DEFERRED; all importers are mappers onto the single canonical character schema (E3-owned).

Data model summary in sub-epic E0/E2/E3/E4 designs; checkpoint serialization format in E8 design. Tradeoffs: hierarchy may smooth small details (mitigated by structured-state anchor + structural drill-down + persisted raw log); one-time conversion not reusable (accepted, importer deferred); Hybrid adds a deterministic export-mapping component (accepted in exchange for embedded zero-ops per-turn path + session-grain version graph; Dolt-only rejected because per-turn version resolution is undesirable so it would commit at session boundaries anyway, paying hot-path/server cost for no extra versioning benefit).
acceptance_criteria:
MVP is complete when, from the local CLI on D&D 5e SRD/open-licensed content:
1. Player can create an SRD-legal character via guided flow; sheet persists as canonical state.
2. Player can start a campaign forked from an authored module template; the converted open-licensed adventure loads.
3. Player can play multiple sessions; DM narrates, voices NPCs, adjudicates, runs creatures using looked-up stat blocks; all dice/math/state changes go through tools.
4. World changes (killed NPC, flipped plot flag, spent gold) persist as overlay/state and are reflected on later turns and sessions.
5. Graceful exit auto-closes the session (recap + roll-up); crash leaves session resumable with zero canon loss.
6. After many sessions, the DM demonstrates campaign continuity while assembled prompt size stays bounded and roughly constant with campaign length.
7. memory_drilldown retrieves a specific older session/scene on demand without it being permanently in context.
8. Session close and arc roll-up produce deterministic Dolt checkpoint commits; Dolt is never written in a per-turn path.
9. Player can list checkpoints, restore a checkpoint into a new SQLite working copy, and fork a campaign from a checkpoint into a new Dolt branch with an isolated working copy.
10. Loreweaver Dolt storage/remote/ref-namespace is verifiably disjoint from the beads Dolt repo.
11. Core model integration exposes provider-neutral adapters and model profiles; Claude/Anthropic remains an initial adapter, not a core assumption.
12. The primary DM path is configured for a premium_dm quality floor; economy models are not the default public demo or canonical DM unless explicitly marked experimental/validated.
13. Rules/mechanics, campaign content, live state, user-private packs, and generated memory remain separated with provenance.
14. Pack metadata can enforce license, attribution, hosted-use, sharing, redistribution, and monetization policy.
15. The demo path is premium-model, bounded-turn, and preloaded rather than economy-model-first.
16. Remaining deferred items are recorded explicitly: native VTT, native mobile, hosted billing/credits, general importers, and custom/local primary DM replacement.
All sub-epics E0-E8 closed; deferred items explicitly recorded, not silently dropped.
notes:
DB ARCHITECTURE DECIDED (user + second-model concurrence): HYBRID, not deferred. SQLite = authoritative live operational store (per-turn ACID, never replaced). Dolt = authoritative checkpoint/history/branching store. MVP must include: deterministic SQLite->Dolt checkpoint export; dolt commit per checkpoint; list checkpoints; restore checkpoint into NEW SQLite working copy; fork campaign from checkpoint into NEW Dolt branch; explicit separation from beads Dolt storage/remotes. Prohibitions: Dolt NOT in per-turn hot path; Dolt NOT deferred; NOT two independent live truths. New sub-epic E8 created for the Dolt checkpoint subsystem. E0 SQLite tasks UNCHANGED (SQLite stays the live store).
STRATEGY SYNTHESIS 2026-05-17: Product direction is text-first long-campaign AI DM for tabletop-seeking solo players and living text-world nostalgists. MVP/medium-term remains text-first; native VTT and native mobile are non-goals. CLI/local remains the near-term development and power-user surface; hosted mobile-friendly web/PWA is the likely medium-term public surface. Model strategy is provider adapters + model profiles, not Claude-only. premium_dm targets Opus 4.6+ / GPT-5.5-class or future equivalent; economy models are auxiliary/experimental unless validated. Billing starts BYOK-first; hosted credits are future optional. Public demo should be premium-model, short, bounded, and preloaded rather than economy-model-first. Content strategy separates rules, campaign content, live state, user-private content, and generated memory; public/bundled packs must be open, public-domain, original, or licensed; no fair-use-dependent public pack strategy or ownership-gated closed-IP derived packs. See docs/architecture-report.md and ADR 0001.
close_reason: MVP complete. All 9 sub-epics E0-E8 closed; 16 acceptance criteria verified via manual end-to-end CLI runs (campaign create/fork, session start/resume/close, graceful auto-close, Dolt checkpoint/restore/fork, provider-neutral model adapter). Sole defect found in verification (loreweaver-l0l: EOF graceful-close gap) fixed and merged in PR #14. Deferred items recorded in ADR 0001/0002. Gates green: typecheck + 195 tests pass.

title: Amendment A2: make active ambiguity rulings available to bounded capability preflight (with eshyra-olc5 readiness owner)
description: ADR 0020 transition amendment A2 (integrated transition design 8.3 R5), carved out of eshyra-jhpt.6 on 2026-09-05 so the .4/.5/.6 PR could land without it. Define how an ACTIVE ambiguity ruling (campaign_rule with ambiguity provenance, read through the .2 APIs / assembleCampaignRulesContext) is made available to bounded deterministic capability preflight where execution depends on it — the verified case is magic-item:cube-of-force press-face-1 resetsDuration { kind:'source-ambiguity', ambiguityId:'ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset' } where state/itemState.ts matchStateTransition throws ItemStateAmbiguityError. Constraints from the .6 spec: assertMagicItemOperationReady runs before the first matchStateTransition, so readiness throws first today; A2 must be designed WITH the eshyra-olc5 readiness owner (eshyra-olc5.6, transition W13): a ruling does not make an engine-pending clause ready, and a capability may never consult a ruling that did not come through this runtime. Discovery consumer eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (W11) depends on this output and may not substitute a discovery-local store. Probe P7 expects: no active ruling -> packet carries the ambiguity, both interpretations, explicit unresolved; active ruling -> packet carries the ruling beside the ambiguity and preflight still reports blocked. Ownership stays under eshyra-jhpt.6.

title: Design and evaluate persistent DM seat reconstruction across model sessions
description:
AUTHORITY / REFERENCES

- Repository workflow and review authority: AGENTS.md.
- Accepted architecture: ADR 0001 (provider-neutral model profiles and separation of rules/content/state/user-private data/generated memory); ADR 0010 (API-native versus agent-harness seam and Eshyra-owned behavior across provider sessions); both ADR 0012 records (character continuity/custody and the four content/state layers); ADR 0014 (campaign overlay canon and truth status); ADR 0017 section 8 (audit-architecture restraint); ADR 0020 (rule awareness, model adjudication, and deterministic state-integrity boundaries).
- Current Eshyra producers/consumers to map exactly: packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts (buildSystemPrompt and Hybrid Contract); packages/core/src/model/client.ts; packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts and orchestrator.ts; packages/core/src/memory/recapBuilder.ts, arcSummary.ts, campaignBibleExtractor.ts, campaignArc.ts, and summary.ts; packages/cli/src/playClose.ts, playSession.ts, and playTypes.ts; packages/core/src/session/launch.ts; campaign-bible extraction/rollup; campaign overlay, campaign-ruling, character-chronicle, session resume, trace/usage, debug, and adapter implementations and tests.
- Comparative implementation evidence, not repository authority or a design to copy: gastownhall/gascity engdocs/architecture/nine-concepts.md; examples/gastown/city.toml and Gas Town config recipes; cmd/gc/cmd_prime.go and prompt rendering; cmd/gc/prime_auto_handoff_inject.go; the older Gas Town crew prompt; and session-reset behavior. These show a useful decomposition in which standing agent reconstruction and durable work/state survive a fresh model context, while handoff mail is injected separately as episodic context.
- Existing ownership that must remain separate: eshyra-wsv, eshyra-32m, eshyra-06b/.1, eshyra-x63, eshyra-d4d.6, eshyra-lupf.16, eshyra-ws9.1, eshyra-ckrg, and eshyra-f0hj. Rule discovery belongs to eshyra-o9bd.19.11/.12/.13/.15; campaign rulings, house rules, ambiguity/precedent lifecycle, and disputed-turn replay belong to eshyra-jhpt and children; future campaign-rule context scaling belongs to eshyra-umyb.

PROBLEM / PRIMARY QUESTION

Eshyra invokes frontier models transiently but presents a long-lived campaign Dungeon Master role. Current continuity is reconstructed from a generic DM system prompt, the Hybrid Contract, authoritative campaign/module/rules state, campaign rulings, bounded session/scene memory, campaign bible, arc summaries, character continuity, and other rendered context. Session recaps are deterministic compositions of accepted narration and state deltas; bible and arc maintenance are fresh model calls over persisted inputs. There is no accepted architecture yet for a campaign/table-specific standing DM charter or an explicit outgoing-DM handoff.

The primary question is:

What must Eshyra reconstruct around a fresh frontier-model invocation so that it meaningfully occupies the same long-lived campaign-DM role as its predecessor, independent of provider, model, or provider-session continuity?

Same DM means the same persistent institutional/gameplay role, not identity as a person or continuity of consciousness. The investigation must distinguish standing role reconstruction from durable campaign state, episodic handoff, and the transient model invocation. It must not presuppose that either a new entity or any new production capability is needed.

The implementation default is precise: do not introduce a new storage/entity abstraction unless a real producer/consumer requires one; first determine whether the persistent DM seat is adequately composed from existing and/or narrowly extended prompt, campaign, memory, preference, and handoff primitives.

REQUIRED CONCEPTUAL DECOMPOSITION

1. Standing DM role charter

Map buildSystemPrompt, the Hybrid Contract, live tool roster/protocol instructions, canon guidance, narration/adjudication responsibilities, and related runtime instructions. Determine which instructions are generic to every Eshyra DM and which, if any, legitimately vary by campaign or table. This is the stable role definition reconstructed for each fresh invocation, not campaign world knowledge.

2. Campaign/table-specific DM identity or charter

Evaluate whether a long-running campaign benefits from bounded, stable table-facing commitments that are neither world canon nor one-session handoff notes. Candidate evidence categories include established table style, pacing preferences, descriptive density, player-agency conventions, difficulty/lethality conventions, tone boundaries, recurring adjudication or narrative conventions, stable player-specific interaction preferences, and campaign-specific DM voice/style. These are hypotheses, not requirements.

Map every candidate against existing user-private data, campaign state, campaign bible, generated memory, character chronicle, campaign rulings, model profiles, prompts, and configuration before proposing a new producer or consumer. Do not categorically exclude table-facing style/personality continuity when it has demonstrated product value, but reject unbounded persona preservation and provider-specific behavioral quirks. Do not anthropomorphize the role.

3. Durable campaign/institutional state

Map what Eshyra already reconstructs for a fresh DM: canonical campaign state; module/adventure source and progress; campaign overlay/canon; campaign rulings; rules/source evidence and bounded capabilities; session/scene memory; campaign bible; arc summaries; character custody/chronicle/party continuity; model profiles; and every other currently rendered context section. Keep this state distinct from DM identity even when it helps a model behave continuously.

4. Episodic outgoing-DM handoff

Retain and evaluate the outgoing-handoff hypothesis as a separate path. A bounded explicit note authored for the successor may preserve immediate salience or intent that normal memory loses: subtle NPC characterization trajectory, unresolved dramatic tension, player-specific salience, deliberate setup/payoff intent, tactical/narrative setup, intentionally planted but not-yet-canonical future hooks, or the intended opening beat for the next session.

A handoff is non-authoritative generated continuity memory. It cannot directly mutate state or outrank canonical campaign/state facts, source/module/rules authority, active campaign rulings, or newer evidence. It must never capture hidden chain-of-thought or private reasoning; only concise, explicit intent/salience deliberately authored for the successor is eligible. Provenance, staleness, supersession, retention, and context budgets must be explicit if evidence supports the concept.

5. Transient model/provider session

Treat each Claude, OpenAI, or other invocation/session as an occupant of the DM role, not the durable identity itself. Preserve ADR 0010 provider neutrality: changing provider, model family, adapter family, harness session, or API conversation must not inherently create a new campaign DM. Useful continuity must come from Eshyra-owned reconstruction, never assumed hidden provider memory or same-model affinity.

INFORMATION-FLOW ANALYSIS

Map the current path source-to-consumer:

current DM standing prompt + rendered campaign context -> model invocation -> accepted narration and deterministic state effects -> scene/session memory producers -> campaign bible / arc / character continuity -> next-session context assembly -> fresh model invocation.

Then evaluate two distinct candidate paths:

- standing campaign/table DM charter -> every fresh primary-DM invocation;
- outgoing DM immediate context -> explicit bounded handoff -> next primary-DM invocation.

For each path, identify information it can faithfully preserve that the other paths cannot. Keep these categories explicit and non-convertible without an authorized producer: world facts; game rulings; table facts/preferences; long-lived DM behavioral commitments; immediate DM narrative intent/salience; generated continuity memory; and transient provider/model/session metadata.

SCOPE / EVALUATION

1. Produce the complete current information-flow and producer/consumer map with exact source references, including the primary-DM system prompt, context renderer, resume paths, memory pyramid, campaign rulings, character continuity, traces, and adapter behavior.
2. Identify legitimate candidate campaign/table charter data, its authority/privacy/lifetime, and whether an existing producer and consumer already owns it. Separate generic Eshyra DM instructions from campaign-specific behavior and from campaign facts.
3. Identify legitimate episodic handoff content that is not already faithfully present in authoritative state or generated memory. Distinguish added continuity from simple restatement.
4. Design and, where practical without committing production architecture, run a four-arm ablation over representative multi-session cases:
   A. current baseline: generic DM system prompt plus current campaign/context/memory reconstruction;
   B. standing-seat treatment: baseline plus a bounded campaign/table-specific standing DM charter, if legitimate candidate data is identified;
   C. handoff treatment: baseline plus an outgoing-DM handoff only;
   D. combined treatment: baseline plus both the standing charter and outgoing handoff.
5. Make the experiment capable of independently concluding: neither adds value; standing reconstruction only adds value; handoff only adds value; or both add independent/complementary value. Do not design scoring or fixtures so either concept must win.
6. Cover NPC characterization, unresolved dramatic tension, player-specific salience, tactical/narrative setup, intentional future hooks, table-style/pacing/agency conventions, and an intended next-session opening beat where applicable.
7. Include normal session boundaries and a deliberately hard fresh-context boundary. Include cases where provider/model and, where supported, adapter family changes. Confirm any continuity comes from Eshyra-owned reconstruction rather than retained provider context.
8. Include adversarial cases where standing-charter or handoff text contradicts canonical state, source/module/rules authority, or an active campaign ruling; inject stale/superseded material as well. Demonstrate that it cannot become authority, mutate state, or override newer evidence.
9. Evaluate the runtime auditor separately. Determine whether it needs any standing role reconstruction beyond its current constrained jurisdiction and exact rules/state evidence. Do not assume primary-DM style, narrative intent, or rich seat semantics belong in auditor context.
10. End with one evidence-backed disposition and create no implementation successor until that disposition is accepted.

EXCLUSIONS / NON-GOALS

- No change to ADR 0020 discovery, adjudication, deterministic-capability, or state-integrity boundaries; no general runtime rule-discovery work.
- Do not replace or duplicate campaign bible, session recap, arc summary, character chronicle, campaign overlay, user-private data, campaign rulings, model profiles, trace metadata, or existing prompt/context ownership.
- No new canon/campaign-rule store and no production persistence subsystem, schema, migration, DmSeat table/class/entity, persistent persona, generic agent-identity framework, or broad memory redesign in this bead.
- No hidden chain-of-thought or private model reasoning; no metaphysical/personhood claim; no unbounded personality preservation; no provider-session affinity; no requirement to keep the same provider/model between sessions.
- No gameplay-state mutation from a charter or handoff. A style/preference/intent statement is never authority for a world fact or game rule.
- No generic ADR/process/governance cleanup, review-contract/checkpoint ceremony, agent-swarm/Thunderdome/merge-queue/Wheelhouse infrastructure, Gas City port, or speculative implementation children.

DEPENDENCIES / BLOCKERS

No active dependency or parent is required. Existing memory, adapter, prompt, trace, evaluation, user-private, and campaign-ruling surfaces are evidence inputs rather than blockers. If evaluation needs campaign rulings, consume the current eshyra-jhpt read interface without redesigning its ownership. Coordinate with active model-context work only to avoid fixture or seam conflicts.

MATERIAL-CHANGE STATUS

This semantic-system investigation is non-material while it changes only design/evaluation artifacts. Any accepted production change to prompt reconstruction, campaign/table preferences, durable memory, context assembly, handoff lifecycle, model-role identity, schema, precedence, retention, or auditor inputs is material and requires a fresh implementation bead under the accepted design. Do not implement production architecture here.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE / DISPOSITION

Permanent repository evidence must record exactly one evidence outcome:

- REJECTED: current reconstruction is sufficient; no successor.
- HANDOFF ONLY: handoff has demonstrated value, but no additional standing campaign-DM identity is justified.
- STANDING SEAT ONLY: campaign/table-specific role reconstruction has value, but outgoing handoff does not.
- COMPOSED SEAT + HANDOFF: both provide demonstrated independent/complementary value and can be composed from bounded primitives.
- FIRST-CLASS SEAT FOLLOW-UP: evidence identifies a concrete producer, consumer, and lifecycle that genuinely require a new first-class durable abstraction.

These labels describe evidence outcomes, not architecture chosen in advance. Any non-rejected disposition must specify the exact bounded production successor(s), if any; do not pre-create them before the investigation disposition.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Permanent repository evidence maps, with exact source references, what standing prompt/context currently reconstructs an Eshyra DM on every fresh model call or session, including buildSystemPrompt, the Hybrid Contract, tool/runtime instructions, assembled context, resume paths, and adapter rendering.
2. The evidence classifies every relevant input as generic DM role charter, campaign/table-specific behavior, authoritative campaign/module/rules/state, campaign ruling, generated campaign/character memory, episodic handoff candidate, user-private preference/data, or transient provider/model/session metadata. No category silently becomes another.
3. The analysis states what, if anything, makes the primary DM of one campaign meaningfully distinct from a generic Eshyra DM beyond knowing campaign facts, without anthropomorphism or continuity-of-consciousness claims.
4. Every candidate standing-seat datum and handoff datum is mapped to its authority, privacy, lifetime, provenance, staleness behavior, current or proposed producer, and current or proposed consumer. The evidence identifies which already have authoritative producers/consumers and which would require a new or extended one.
5. A bounded, inspectable four-arm ablation evaluates A current baseline, B standing campaign/table charter, C outgoing handoff, and D both. Fixtures and scoring/decision rules can fail and can independently conclude neither, standing only, handoff only, or complementary value.
6. The ablation measures whether a bounded standing campaign/table DM charter improves continuity over baseline without merely restating campaign facts or duplicating existing memory, rulings, profiles, user-private data, or configuration.
7. The ablation independently measures whether an outgoing-DM handoff improves continuity over baseline by preserving explicit immediate salience/intent not already faithfully carried by current memory, and measures whether it merely restates existing context.
8. The combined arm measures interaction as well as aggregate score, so evidence can show independent, redundant, conflicting, or complementary value from standing reconstruction and handoff.
9. Evaluation includes both normal session boundaries and a deliberately hard fresh-context boundary, plus provider/model changes and representative supported adapter-family variation where practical. Useful continuity must survive without provider-owned conversation state, hidden memory, same-model affinity, or provider-session affinity.
10. Representative cases cover NPC characterization trajectory, unresolved tension, player-specific salience, tactical/narrative setup, intentional future hooks, table style/pacing/agency conventions, and an intended next-session opening beat where applicable. Permanent results report context-budget and retention costs as well as continuity quality.
11. Adversarial regression cases inject false and stale standing-charter/handoff material that conflicts with canonical state, source/module/rules authority, active campaign rulings, and newer evidence. Tests/evaluation assertions prove it cannot outrank those sources, directly mutate state, launder a preference into a world fact/rule, or silently survive supersession.
12. The evidence determines whether the persistent primary-DM seat is best represented as composition of existing primitives, a narrowly extended prompt/preference/generated-memory concept, or a genuinely new first-class durable abstraction. Any first-class recommendation names the concrete producer, consumer, lifecycle, and why composition is insufficient.
13. The runtime auditor is evaluated separately. The evidence states what standing context it needs, if anything, and proves that table style or narrative intent does not expand its constrained rules/state jurisdiction or create false authority.
14. Permanent evidence answers all twelve investigation questions in the owning bead: current standing reconstruction; category boundaries; campaign-specific DM distinction; producer/consumer ownership; standing-charter value; handoff value; combined value; fresh-context/provider-change robustness; conflict precedence; representation choice; auditor implications; and exact justified successors.
15. The final evidence records exactly one disposition: REJECTED; HANDOFF ONLY; STANDING SEAT ONLY; COMPOSED SEAT + HANDOFF; or FIRST-CLASS SEAT FOLLOW-UP. The selected outcome names exact, narrowly scoped production successor bead(s) only where evidence justifies them; no speculative child exists before disposition.

title: Campaign-rule and ambiguity context grows monotonically with campaign age
description:
DEFERRED BY DESIGN, recorded so it is not lost.

assembleCampaignRulesContext supplies every active campaign rule and every ambiguity in the resolved rules stack on every DM turn, and renderContextMessage emits all of them. Raised by a /code-review sweep of PR #524 (finding 4) as monotonic prompt growth.

This is NOT a defect today and was NOT changed, because it is the deliberate contract: eshyra-jhpt.3 says "at initial scale, supply all active campaign-rule prose on every applicable DM turn; correctness takes priority over selective retrieval", and "prompt retrieval optimization" is an explicit non-goal on that bead. The supervisor measured the per-turn full-stack ambiguity scan at ~0.13 ms over 1812 records, so cost is not currently a concern either.

It becomes real when either side grows: the rules-pack compiler's stated direction is to add more ambiguity metadata (only 3 exist in the shipped SRD pack today), and campaign_rule accumulates for the life of a campaign with no upper bound. At that point the context needs relevance selection or a budget, which is a design decision requiring its own bead and probably an ADR note, not an incidental change.

Revisit when either the ambiguity count in a shipped pack or the active-rule count in a long-running campaign makes the per-turn slice materially large. Do not fix by silently truncating; that would reintroduce the "silent canonical certainty" failure eshyra-jhpt.3 exists to prevent.

title: Dispatch: Supply active campaign rules and source ambiguities to DM context (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.3 (attempt 1). Spec and acceptance criteria live on eshyra-jhpt.3 and the epic eshyra-jhpt; read both, including ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A1 on the bead. This bead carries the supervisor's pre-planning only.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.3.1 on branch eshyra-jhpt.3.1, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt (merge 4a9620e), which already contains the completed eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model and eshyra-jhpt.2 storage/seam. Work only inside that worktree.

SCOPE
DM-side context assembly, plus the campaign-position assignment this bead needs (see part 1). NO auditor parity work (.4 — but build the projection so .4 can reuse it verbatim), NO ambiguity dialogue or player prompting (.6), NO precedent inference (.7), NO replay (.8), NO CLI (.5).

PART 1 — YOU MUST FIRST ESTABLISH CAMPAIGN POSITION ASSIGNMENT. THIS IS THE CENTRAL DESIGN TASK.
eshyra-jhpt.2 made campaignPosition REQUIRED on every active-at-position query (listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition, listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition, createCampaignRuleReadSeam). Nothing in the repo can currently produce one at turn time:
  - CampaignPosition is { sessionId, turnId, ordinal } (campaign/campaignRules.ts) and its ordinal is the authoritative chronology key.
  - turnId is generated in packages/cli/src/index.ts makeId() as `turn-<base36 timestamp>-<random>` — opaque and NOT ordered.
  - turn_trace is keyed (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id) with no ordinal; only scene_log.seq and campaign_arc.sequence_no are ordinals, and neither is a campaign-wide turn counter.
So this bead owns assigning and persisting the ordinal.
REQUIRED PROPERTY, because eshyra-jhpt.8 depends on it: the SAME turn must always resolve to the SAME position. A disputed turn is rolled back and replayed, and a rule effective "at the start of the disputed turn" only keeps meaning if the replayed turn occupies the identical position. Do not derive the ordinal from COUNT(*) of turn_trace or any other row count — a rollback changes the count and silently shifts every later position.
DESIGN: add migration 0026 with a small table mapping (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id) -> ordinal, monotonically assigned per campaign on first request and IDEMPOTENT thereafter, plus a resolver (suggested `resolveCampaignPosition(db, { campaignId, sessionId, turnId })`) returning a CampaignPosition. Assign at turn start. Test that re-resolving the same turnId returns the identical ordinal, that a rolled-back-and-replayed turn keeps its position, and that ordinals increase across turns and across a session boundary. Highest existing migration after eshyra-jhpt.2 is 0025_campaign_rules.sql, so yours is 0026_*.sql. Never edit an existing migration — migrationRunner.ts checksums applied ones — and update packages/core/test/migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts ledger expectations, which is mandatory and not a test weakening.

PART 2 — SUPPLY ACTIVE CAMPAIGN RULES TO DM CONTEXT.
packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts is the DM context builder: ContextAssemblyInput -> assembleContext() -> AssembledContext -> renderContextMessage(). It currently carries no rules slice at all.
- Add a campaign-rules slice to AssembledContext and render it in renderContextMessage.
- At initial scale supply ALL active campaign-rule prose at the current position on every applicable DM turn. Correctness beats selective retrieval; do not add retrieval scoring or a budget heuristic.
- Include stable rule identity, kind, effective provenance, and linked ambiguity/interpretation provenance. Do not ask the model to execute deterministic state logic.
- USE THE eshyra-jhpt.2 QUERIES DIRECTLY. Do not write a second active-rule resolver, do not cache rules in campaign state, and do not copy pack data into campaign state. The exact same projection must be reusable by eshyra-jhpt.4 for the auditor — factor the projection so .4 calls the identical function rather than rebuilding it. This is the whole point of amendment A1 and of transition W11's prohibition on a discovery-local store.
- AMENDMENT A1: the active-rule projection must expose, per rule, the linked ambiguity ID and, where one exists, the governing pack record key, so a consumer can pair a rule with its governing source material without re-deriving the association. CampaignRuleProjection already carries `ambiguityId` and `governingRecordKeys`; confirm both survive into whatever you hand the DM, and test it.

PART 3 — SURFACE UNRESOLVED SOURCE AMBIGUITY WITHOUT INVENTING CERTAINTY.
The shipped pack contains exactly THREE ambiguities (verified by grep over packages/core/data/rules-packs/): ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition, ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp, ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset. Relevance selection is therefore not a scaling problem at initial scale — surface every unresolved one from the active rules stack and skip retrieval optimization entirely, consistent with the bead's "correctness takes priority over selective retrieval".
- RulesAmbiguity (rules/types.ts) is { id, question, source[], affects[], interpretations[{id, summary}], canonicalResolution: null, runtimeDisposition: { status: 'engine-pending', owner: 'campaign-ruling' } }. canonicalResolution is permanently null and the owner is 'campaign-ruling' — that is the source telling you it has no answer.
- For each ambiguity with NO active ruling at the current position, the rendered context must carry the question, the enumerated interpretation ids and summaries, and an explicit statement that this is unresolved and the DM must not assert a canonical answer or silently pick one. For each ambiguity WITH an active ruling, carry the ruling's prose beside the ambiguity rather than replacing or hiding the source material.
- Use listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition from eshyra-jhpt.2 for the resolved/unresolved determination. Never write a winner or default back into the pack; assert pack immutability in a test.

TESTS
Prospective and effective-turn filtering (a rule effective later is absent now, present at/after its position); superseded and revoked rules absent at positions after the change and present before; deterministic ordering; A1 association data present; all three ambiguities surfaced unresolved with interpretations and no preferred winner; an ambiguity with an active ruling carries both ruling and source; pack bytes unchanged; position idempotency per part 1.

activeRows resolves an omitted cutoff to `MAX(effective_position) FROM campaign_rule`. The latest rule therefore always defines the cutoff to its own position and always includes itself. Supervisor probe, one house rule effective at ordinal 999, still failing on attempt 2:
    at position 1 : []
    no position   : [ 'future' ]      <- future rule still leaks
