Your schema change must be migration 0021; update migrationLegacyAdoption ledger/applied pins and regenerate schema.snapshot.sql (npx tsx packages/core/scripts/generate-schema-snapshot.ts). Keep wear state separate from held storage (inventory.location free text), world placement (world_location_id), attunement, and character curse state; blocksDoff gating currently fails closed for every held item — narrow it to don/doff semantics without synonym inference. Sources of truth for curse onset/persistence: the magic-item records' curse/attunement fields (Demon Armor, Berserker Axe, Armor of Vulnerability, Shield of Missile Attraction, Robe of the Archmagi, Orb of Dragonkind).
Completion report (2026-07-19): Added migration 0021_inventory_wear_state and regenerated schema.snapshot.sql. Added authoritative inventoryWear donItem/doffItem/getInventoryWearState owner with exact model-facing don_item/doff_item tools; legacy rows without wear state fail closed for don/doff. New give/claim/reacquire/adoption rows initialize not_worn; relinquishment removes holder wear state; transfer moves state to recipient as not_worn. Narrowed blocksDoff custody gating to explicitly worn items, preserving held-not-worn transfer/removal semantics. Don attaches source-defined don-onset curse state to character conditions so it survives doff/placement. Tests added/updated for lifecycle, migration, registry, and conservative custody behavior. Verification: npm run build passed; focused suites passed (138 tests); full npm test had 4620 passed, with remaining failures caused by sandbox EPERM for child-process/loopback operations (git/node/npm spawn and 127.0.0.1 listen). npm run verify:worktree reached format then failed at check:hidden-unicode for the same sandbox spawnSync git EPERM. No follow-up product issues discovered.
Supervisor review round 1 (2026-07-19) — two blocking findings; fix in the same worktree (attempt 2), tree is uncommitted:
F1 (major, fail-open): assertInventoryCurseCustodyReady now treats a MISSING inventory_wear_state row as not-worn, so an unreviewed legacy held blocksDoff item (e.g. pre-migration Demon Armor, worn in fiction) can be dropped/sold/transferred where the previous code failed closed. Required: for a held item whose record declares curse.blocksDoff, a missing wear row is AMBIGUOUS and must fail closed (same message family as before), while an authoritative not_worn row permits custody. Missing-row ambiguity is resolved only by the adoption/repair boundary that seeds authoritative rows.
F2 (major, crash): removeItem partial-quantity relinquish inserts an inventory_wear_state row for the NEW unheld relinquished row, bound to the FORMER holder — violating the 'wear row exists iff held' invariant — and claimItem/reacquireItem then do a plain INSERT into inventory_wear_state for that id, which hits the PRIMARY KEY and throws a raw SqliteError: any claim/reacquire of a partially-dropped/sold stack is permanently broken. Required: do not create wear rows for unheld rows (drop the partial-path INSERT); keep full-relinquish DELETE; make claim/reacquire seeding collision-safe (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(inventory_id) DO UPDATE SET character_id, wear_state='not_worn', ...) so surviving rows are rebound not fatal.
Also add regression tests: claim after partial drop; reacquire after partial sell; legacy blocksDoff held item with no wear row fails closed for dropped/sold/lost/transfer/doff; invariant sweep that every inventory_wear_state row joins to a held inventory row with matching character_id (assert in relevant lifecycle tests).
Completion report (attempt 2, 2026-07-19): Fixed supervisor F1 by making held blocksDoff custody fail closed when inventory_wear_state is missing or bound to a different holder; authoritative not_worn remains allowed. Fixed F2 by removing the partial-relinquishment wear-row insert and making claim/reacquire wear seeding collision-safe upserts that rebind to the new holder and reset to not_worn. Made transfer wear maintenance the same upsert so the invariant is preserved for legacy held rows too. Added regressions for missing-row dropped/sold/lost/doff/transfer custody, claim after partial drop, reacquire after partial sell, and invariant sweeps ensuring every wear row joins a held inventory row with matching character_id. title: Prove campaign rules and ambiguity resolution end to end
description:
Objective
Add end-to-end tests that prove campaign-rule behavior across persistence, model context, audit, ambiguity resolution, accepted-turn commits, and immediate disputed-turn replay.

Required scenarios
1. Create Undead explicit ambiguity question prompts without invented certainty and persists an approved interpretation.
2. Create Undead mixed ghast/wight action establishes visible mixed-within-total precedent only after DM/auditor acceptance.
3. Find Familiar permanent-dismissal-after-0-HP ambiguity prompts and remains unresolved when no choice is approved.
4. Explicit "no material components" house rule is durable prose.
5. Immediate material-components objection applies from disputed-turn start, restores pre-turn state, replays, and makes replay canonical.
6. Ordinary house-rule creation applies prospectively.
7. Supersession and revocation change active sets without mutating history.
8. DM and auditor receive equivalent active rule sets at every tested position.
9. Ordinary contextual adjudication (cover/visibility/terrain suitability) creates no campaign rule.
10. A clear canonical-rule violation never becomes an implicit house rule.

Architecture and references
Exercise the public/runtime path built by eshyra-jhpt.1-.8 and PR #419 RulesAmbiguity metadata from eshyra-o9bd.18.7.9. Assert immutable pack bytes remain unchanged and campaign prose remains in canonical campaign history.

Non-goals
No live-provider tests as the sole proof; no duplicated full ambiguity registry; no arbitrary retrospective history editing; no selective-retrieval optimization benchmark; no deterministic interpretation of arbitrary house-rule prose.
acceptance_criteria:
All ten scenarios pass through realistic campaign turn/context/audit/storage boundaries; tests prove exact DM/auditor rule-set parity, checkpoint/replay timing, accepted-vs-abandoned canon, pack immutability, and no rule creation for contextual judgments or clear canonical violations; full repository verification passes.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT (integrated transition design section 8.3, A3 and
A4; accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). Three of the ten scenarios must be
provable end to end as an explicit triple, because they are the three cases the
transition's campaign-rule probes consume:

1. UNRESOLVED AMBIGUITY - a discovered RulesAmbiguity with no active ruling keeps
   its published uncertainty, surfaces the known interpretations, and never
   acquires silent canonical certainty (existing scenarios 1 and 3).
2. RESOLVED RULING - an approved interpretation becomes a durable prose ruling
   carrying ambiguity ID, interpretation ID, kind, status, provenance, effective
   position, and supersession status, and is supplied on subsequent turns
   (existing scenarios 1 and 2).
3. NON-AMBIGUITY HOUSE RULE - the "no material components" house rule, an
   intentional override of clear canonical behavior with no underlying source
   ambiguity, is durable prose that coexists with the source material it
   overrides rather than replacing or hiding it (existing scenarios 4 and 5).

Scenario 9 (ordinary contextual adjudication creates no campaign rule) is not
weakened by any of this and remains a required negative.

Additionally, the accepted-turn trace evidence required by amendment A3 on
eshyra-jhpt.4 - which active rules and rulings were supplied for the turn, and
under which identities - must be proven end to end here, from the persisted
trace, without a second campaign-rule store or a parallel audit database.

These three cases are what eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (transition W11) consumes for probes
P7 (cube-of-force ambiguity, both the unresolved and the resolved case) and P10
(the material-components house rule). W11 depends on these outputs and may not
substitute a discovery-local rule or ruling store; campaign-rule persistence and
ruling lifecycle remain owned by eshyra-jhpt.

title: Replay an immediately disputed turn under a new campaign rule
description:
Objective
Handle a player objection to the current/immediately preceding adjudication by establishing an approved ruling or house rule effective from the start of that disputed turn, restoring pre-turn state, and replaying once under the new rule.

Required behavior
Recognize an explicit objection to the immediate adjudication, obtain player-approved prose/kind, persist canonical rule identity with effective position at disputed-turn start, restore the checkpoint/state immediately before that turn, replay the same player turn with the rule active in both DM and auditor contexts, and commit the accepted replay as campaign canon. Required canonical-conflict scenario: after a material-component rejection, "we don't use spell components" creates a house rule, rolls back the disputed turn, replays under it, and commits the replay. Abandoned adjudication may remain diagnostic/provenance history but not continuing campaign canon.

Architecture and references
Use eshyra-jhpt.1-.4 for domain/storage/context parity, audited-turn staging eshyra-67qo, turn rollback proof eshyra-c07.8, and checkpoint restore foundation eshyra-7wc.5. Preserve canonical campaign history and auditor evidence across the replay boundary.

Non-goals
No arbitrary historical retroactivity or replay of older turns; no automatic objection inference; no rule without player approval; no prose-to-mechanics compiler; no automatic house rule from an unaccepted canonical violation; no changes to immutable pack semantics.
acceptance_criteria: An immediate material-components objection creates approved house-rule prose effective at disputed-turn start, restores exact pre-turn state, replays once with identical DM/auditor active rules, and makes accepted replay canonical; ordinary new rules remain prospective; failed replay preserves a recoverable canonical pre-turn state; older-turn retroactivity is rejected; diagnostic history distinguishes abandoned and canonical attempts.

title: Persist accepted implicit ambiguity precedents
description:
Objective
Allow an accepted player action to establish a durable campaign ruling when it unambiguously selects a known interpretation of explicit rules-pack ambiguity metadata.

Required behavior
Only operate when the pack marks the mechanic ambiguous, no active linked ruling exists, the action clearly selects exactly one known interpretation, and the DM accepts the action. Persist player-approved/accepted-adjudication prose with ambiguity and interpretation provenance, and make the precedent visible in natural language. Required scenario: "Bob summons a ghast and a wight" may establish mixed-within-total for ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition after acceptance. Couple persistence to audited-turn acceptance so rejected/retried candidates cannot leak a precedent.

Architecture and references
Build on explicit ambiguity resolution eshyra-jhpt.6, audited-turn mutation staging eshyra-67qo, mechanics auditor eshyra-oobh, and shared DM/auditor rule context. The model may interpret whether the action clearly selects an enumerated interpretation; deterministic code validates the ambiguity/interpretation IDs and commits only with accepted turn state.

Non-goals
Do not infer house rules from actions contrary to clear canonical rules. Do not create rules for ordinary fictional judgments. Do not infer when an action fits multiple/no known interpretations. Do not silently establish a precedent without visible acknowledgement. Do not alter the rules pack.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted mixed ghast/wight action establishes one visible durable mixed-within-total ruling; rejected/retried/ambiguous actions establish none; an existing ruling prevents duplicate precedent; canonical-rule violations never infer a house rule; persistence is atomic with audited turn acceptance; DM and auditor receive the new prose on subsequent turns.

title: Resolve known rules-pack ambiguities as campaign rulings
description:
Objective
Implement pre-adjudication resolution for unresolved RulesAmbiguity metadata when no campaign ruling exists.

Required behavior
Look up ambiguity metadata from the active rules stack by stable ID, check campaign storage for an active linked ruling, and when unresolved surface the published uncertainty instead of inventing certainty. Ask the player to choose among known interpretation IDs; persist the player-approved result as prose ruling with ambiguity/interpretation provenance; make it prospectively active and available to both model contexts. Required scenario: "Can I mix a ghast and a wight?" surfaces ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition and can persist either homogeneous-alternative or mixed-within-total. Also cover ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp.

Architecture and references
Consume PR #419 RulesAmbiguity output from eshyra-o9bd.18.7.9. Store only campaign prose/provenance via eshyra-jhpt.2; never write a winner/default back to the immutable pack. Use shared context from eshyra-jhpt.3-.4.

Non-goals
No model-selected canonical winner; no campaign ruling without player approval; no house-rule creation for clear canonical conflicts; no resolution of ordinary contextual judgments; no arbitrary prompt/retrieval optimization.
acceptance_criteria:
Create Undead explicit question and Find Familiar unresolved question both surface source uncertainty and known interpretations; an approved choice creates one durable prose ruling linked to ambiguity and interpretation IDs; an existing active ruling prevents re-prompting; declined/no choice creates nothing; DM/auditor receive the same resulting prose; pack data remains unchanged.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A2 (integrated transition design section 8.3, R5;
accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282): define how an active ambiguity ruling
is made available to bounded deterministic capability preflight where execution
depends on it, not only to DM and auditor context. Today no path exists from a
campaign ruling to capability code.

The verified concrete case: magic-item:cube-of-force operation press-face-1 from
state face-1 hits transition resetsDuration { kind: 'source-ambiguity',
ambiguityId: 'ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset' }, and
state/itemState.ts matchStateTransition throws ItemStateAmbiguityError carrying
the ambiguity and interpretation IDs. A ruling selecting same-face-resets or
different-face-only-resets is exactly what would unblock it. Verified ordering
constraint: assertMagicItemOperationReady runs at itemState.ts:1888, BEFORE the
first matchStateTransition call at :1934, and every press-face-* operation clause
on that record is engine-pending, so readiness throws first and the ambiguity
error is currently unreachable through use_item. A2 must therefore be designed
WITH the eshyra-olc5 readiness owner (see eshyra-olc5.6, transition W13), not
against it: a ruling does not make an engine-pending clause ready, and a
capability may never consult a ruling that did not come through this runtime.

This may be satisfied as an acceptance criterion here or as a new child under
eshyra-jhpt; either way the ownership stays here. The discovery-side consumer
eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (transition W11) depends on this output and may not substitute
a discovery-local ruling store or resolver. Probe P7 of the transition design
expects both outcomes: with no active ruling the packet carries the ambiguity,
both interpretations, and an explicit unresolved state; with an active ruling the
packet carries the ruling beside the ambiguity and the capability preflight still
reports blocked.
notes: Delivered on branch eshyra-jhpt; PR opened https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/526 at head eeab5eb (2026-09-05). Stays in_progress until merge.

title: Add explicit campaign-rule management workflow
description:
Objective
Provide explicit player-facing management for campaign rulings and house rules: create, review, list/inspect, edit by supersession, and revoke.

Required behavior
Require player-provided or player-approved prose and an explicit kind. Show status, origin/provenance, effective position, and supersession/revocation history. Editing creates a new durable rule that supersedes the old identity rather than mutating historical semantic content. Ordinary creation applies prospectively unless invoked by the separate immediate-adjudication objection workflow.

Architecture and references
Use eshyra-jhpt.1 domain invariants and eshyra-jhpt.2 storage APIs. Preserve canonical history and ADR 0017 pack/campaign separation.

Non-goals
No arbitrary history rewrite; no direct editing of immutable rules-pack records; no automatic deterministic mechanic generation; no implicit ambiguity precedent; no DM-only unapproved rule creation; no persistence of ordinary contextual adjudications.
acceptance_criteria: Players can create ruling/house-rule prose, review and list active/history views, supersede through a new record, and revoke prospectively; confirmations expose effective timing and provenance; tests cover status transitions, deterministic ordering, invalid edits, cross-campaign isolation, and history preservation.
notes: Delivered on branch eshyra-jhpt; PR opened https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/526 at head eeab5eb (2026-09-05). Stays in_progress until merge.

title: Give the auditor exact campaign-rule context parity
description:
Objective
Supply the mechanics audit model with the exact same active campaign-rule prose set used by the primary DM for the audited turn.

Required behavior
Use one deterministic active-rule context projection for both roles. The auditor evaluates canonical pack semantics plus active rulings and house rules at the turn's effective position, including a rule established at the start of an immediately replayed disputed turn. Preserve rule IDs/kinds/provenance so audit diagnostics can identify the governing campaign rule. Add direct equivalence tests over ordering, content, status filtering, supersession, revocation, and effective position.

Architecture and references
Build on the existing mechanics-audit gate eshyra-oobh and the context/storage contracts from eshyra-jhpt.1-.3. Follow ADR 0017: models interpret approved prose; deterministic code only selects the active set and timing.

Non-goals
No independent auditor-only rule registry or retrieval policy; no auditor authority to create/modify campaign rules; no arbitrary prose compilation; no changed canonical rules-pack semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
For every tested campaign position, DM and auditor receive byte-for-byte/equivalent deterministic active rule sets; superseded/revoked/future rules are absent; disputed-turn rules are present during replay; auditor diagnostics can cite rule identity; focused tests prove parity and prevent divergent context builders.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A3 (integrated transition design section 8.3, R6;
accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282): the accepted-turn trace must retain
durable evidence of WHICH active campaign rules and rulings were supplied for the
turn and under which identities. Parity plus rule-identity citation in
diagnostics is not the same property: parity proves DM and auditor saw the same
set, while A3 proves what that set was, after the fact, from the persisted trace.

The evidence attaches to the existing accepted-turn trace authority
(memory/turnTrace.ts TurnTraceRecord). It must NOT create a second campaign-rule
store, a discovery-owned rule registry, or a parallel audit database (ADR 0017
section 8; ADR 0020 audit-architecture restraint). eshyra-jhpt.9 proves the
property end to end.

This is what lets the transition design's M5 measurement - which active rules and
rulings were requested, which matched, and which were placed beside their
governing material - be computed without a discovery-owned store. The
discovery-side consumer eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (transition W11) depends on this output
and may not substitute a discovery-local store.
notes: Delivered on branch eshyra-jhpt; PR opened https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/526 at head eeab5eb (2026-09-05). Stays in_progress until merge.

title: Supply active campaign rules and source ambiguities to DM context
description:
Objective
Make the primary DM receive the complete active campaign-rule prose set and relevant immutable rules-pack ambiguity metadata at the adjudicated campaign position.

Required behavior
At initial scale, supply all active campaign-rule prose on every applicable DM turn; correctness takes priority over selective retrieval. Include stable rule identity, kind, effective provenance, and linked ambiguity/interpretation provenance without asking the model to execute deterministic state logic. When a relevant RulesAmbiguity has no active campaign ruling, the context must preserve uncertainty and prohibit silent canonical certainty. Context assembly must use the same active-at-position query that the auditor will use.

Architecture and references
Follow ADR 0017 and docs/rules-pack-compiler.md. Consume PR #419 mechanics.ambiguities / RulesAmbiguity output from eshyra-o9bd.18.7.9. Reuse existing rules-stack lookup and campaign binding rather than copying pack data into campaign state.

Non-goals
No persistence workflow, player dialogue policy, implicit precedent creation, prompt retrieval optimization, arbitrary house-rule inference, or prose-to-mechanics compilation. Ordinary contextual DM judgments do not become campaign rules.
acceptance_criteria:
DM context contains all and only rules active at the current campaign position in deterministic order; relevant unresolved RulesAmbiguity metadata is available without a preferred/default winner; tests prove prospective/effective-turn filtering and no silent canonical certainty; no campaign prose is written to the pack.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A1 (integrated transition design section 8.3, R4;
accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282): the active-rule projection must
expose, per rule, enough association data to place an active campaign rule or
ruling beside its governing pack record or source ambiguity - the linked
ambiguity ID and, where one exists, the governing pack record key - so a
consumer can pair rule and source material without re-deriving the association.
This extends the projection only; the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model, which already
requires a ruling to record the ambiguity ID and selected interpretation ID as
provenance, is unchanged.

The discovery-side consumer is eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (transition W11), which depends
on this output and may not substitute a discovery-local campaign-rule or ruling
store, cache of record, or shadow resolver. Campaign-rule persistence, ruling
schema, active-rule resolution, supersession, revocation, and house-rule
lifecycle remain owned here. If the projection proves insufficient for the
consumer, the correct response is an amendment or a new child under eshyra-jhpt.
notes:
Supervisor review of attempt 1 (935d7d9): migration 0026, resolveCampaignPosition idempotency, and critically the position-before-SAVEPOINT placement in runTurn (which preserves a replayed turn's position for .8) are ACCEPTED, as is assembleCampaignRulesContext as the shared DM/auditor projection. Per-turn pack scan measured at ~0.13ms/1812 records - not a concern. Four findings: (1) PRIMARY - only the position idempotency test was added; assembleCampaignRulesContext and the rendered section have no tests at all, leaving prospective/effective filtering, supersession/revocation, ordering, A1 association data, all three ambiguities unresolved, ruling-beside-source, and pack immutability unproven; (2) assembleContext silently returns an empty rules context when campaignPosition is omitted, reintroducing at the context layer the trap .2 removed at the store layer - latent today since runTurn always passes it, but it makes .4 DM/auditor divergence silent; (3) localeCompare in ambiguity ordering - verified NOT currently mis-ordering the three shipped ids, but locale/ICU-dependent and the same construct removed in .1; (4) plain Error instead of CampaignRuleError. Attempt 2 dispatched as eshyra-jhpt.3.2.
Attempt 2 (c3db41c) reviewed and ACCEPTED: consolidated projection test covers all eight required cases, campaignPosition required on ContextAssemblyInput, codepoint ambiguity ordering, CampaignRuleError. One further finding: the position is still an unvalidated raw string passed to SQL, and canonical positions start with 'cp1~', so any later-sorting string satisfies effective_position <= ? for every row - reproduced with the 'test-position' sentinel attempt 2 introduced in ~10 assembleContext call sites (cp1~000000000999~s~t <= 'test-position' is true). That resurrects the .2 future-rule leak through a different door; it is inert only because those tests hold no rules. Attempt 3 dispatched as eshyra-jhpt.3.3 to parse/validate at the store boundary and replace the sentinels.
Attempt 3 (74f28bd) ACCEPTED: all position-taking store entry points parse/canonicalize and reject malformed values with CampaignRuleError. However supervisor found attempt 3 missed packages/cli/test/play.test.ts, which still holds three 'test-position' sentinels. Those did not fail because of a VERIFICATION-INTEGRITY problem, now filed as eshyra-3dmq: a linked worktree has no node_modules, so packages/cli tests resolve @eshyra/core UP to the parent checkout (main) and never saw any jhpt change. After npm ci in the worktree plus a rebuild, play.test.ts fails 2 tests with CampaignRuleError: invalid campaign position 'test-position'. Every verify:worktree run on this epic so far was green for CLI tests against main's core; core tests are unaffected because they import via relative ../src paths, and typecheck is unaffected because tsc --build compiles from source. title: Persist campaign rules in canonical campaign history
description:
Objective
Implement durable storage and query APIs for campaign-rule records defined by eshyra-jhpt.1. Rules must survive sessions, checkpoints, restores, and replay while remaining campaign-scoped and deterministically ordered.

Required behavior
Persist stable rule identity, campaign association, kind, approved prose, status, origin/provenance, optional pack ambiguity/interpretation linkage, effective campaign position, supersedes/superseded-by relation, revocation position, and deterministic ordering. Provide active-rules-at-position queries used by both model contexts. Ordinary rules apply prospectively; a rule created during an immediate adjudication objection may be effective from the start of that disputed turn. Storage mutations participate in canonical campaign history and checkpoint/replay semantics.

Architecture and references
Build on eshyra-x3w.12 campaign rules-pack binding, existing SQLite campaign persistence, and checkpoint/history foundations. Follow ADR 0017: mutable campaign rules never enter the immutable rules pack.

Non-goals
No DM/auditor prompt composition; no ambiguity dialogue; no replay orchestration; no arbitrary retroactive effective positions; no interpretation of prose into deterministic effects.
acceptance_criteria: Schema and APIs create, read, list, supersede, and revoke campaign rules; active-at-position queries are deterministic; checkpoint/restore round trips preserve identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions; tests cover prospective and disputed-turn effective positions plus invalid cross-campaign/supersession combinations.
notes:
Supervisor review of attempt 1 (87e7587): migration 0025, CHECK constraints, lossless provenance, storage-side revoked_position, and the mandatory migration-ledger test updates are ACCEPTED. Six defects found, two severe and reproduced by probe: (1) activeRulingsForAmbiguities queries with no cutoff so rulings use current-status semantics while house rules use historical semantics - at replay position 5 house rules returned h-old (correct) but rulings returned r-new instead of r-old, which breaks .4 parity and .8 replay; (2) the position-less query ignores effective_position entirely, so a rule effective at ordinal 999 is returned as active at position 1. Also: no test ever creates an ambiguity-provenance ruling, so the positive path of activeRulingsForAmbiguities is untested and its only assertion passes vacuously; checkpoint round-trip, cross-campaign isolation, disputed-turn positions and invalid-supersession tests are missing; storage throws plain Error instead of CampaignRuleError; createCampaignRuleReadSeam lacks a CampaignRuleReadSeam return annotation and casts instead; revoke/supersede do not enforce prospectivity. Attempt 2 dispatched as eshyra-jhpt.2.2.
Attempt 2 (75ef96d) reviewed: ruling/house-rule temporal divergence CONFIRMED FIXED by supervisor probe (rulings now return r-old at replay position 5). CampaignRuleError, prospectivity validation, position-aware ruling query, typed seam return all accepted. Three defects remain: (1) the position-less fallback resolves to MAX(effective_position) over the rules table, which is self-referential - the latest rule always sets the cutoff to its own position, so a rule effective at ordinal 999 still leaks at position 1, and campaignRuleStore.test.ts:121 now asserts that leak as expected behaviour; (2) discoveryBoundary.test.ts was weakened with an 'import type' exemption to accommodate campaignRuleStore importing CampaignRuleReadSeam from discovery - caused by the attempt-2 dispatch instruction, correct fix is to move the seam type into the campaign domain and revert the guard; (3) the checkpoint round-trip proof sits entirely under describe.skipIf(!doltOk) so it does not run without the dolt binary (skips rose 19 -> 20). Attempt 3 dispatched as eshyra-jhpt.2.3.
REOPENED 2026-09-02: PR #524 (head 2d6b7c7) blocking review #5097504606 under the semantic-system profile found a lifecycle-admission defect class. Supervisor independently reproduced all four sub-claims: (1) re-superseding an already-superseded rule overwrites its original supersededBy, and the historical query at position 7 then returns BOTH 'old' and its first successor 'first' as active - canonical history corrupted; (2) a revoked rule can be converted to superseded while retaining its revocation position; (3) createCampaignRule accepts a revoked rule whose revokedPosition precedes its effectivePosition, which revokeCampaignRule correctly rejects; (4) createCampaignRule accepts a superseded rule with a dangling supersededBy, because the referential check lives only in validateCampaignRules (plural) which the create path never calls. Root cause: supersedeCampaignRule lacks revokeCampaignRule's status guard AND overwrites prior.status to 'superseded' before validating, so validation structurally cannot see the real admission state. Attempt 4 dispatched as eshyra-jhpt.2.4. Reviewer classified the repair as material state-integrity work requiring a FRESH FULL REVIEW of the new head.
Fix merged into eshyra-jhpt at 0479116 and pushed; PR #524 updated and a response comment posted (issuecomment-5520070142) requesting fresh full review of the new head per the reviewer's material-state-integrity classification. Supervisor independently confirmed the negative proof: checking out campaignRuleStore.ts from 2d6b7c7 under the new tests fails exactly 4 of 11. Full verification under correct module resolution: 276 test files passed/3 skipped, 4848 tests passed/20 skipped. Bead stays in_progress until #524 merges.

title: Define campaign-rule domain model and precedence
description:
Objective
Define the closed campaign-owned contract for two distinct kinds: ruling (resolution of a source ambiguity, stable table interpretation, or recurring rules question) and house-rule (intentional override/supplement to clear canonical behavior). Rule meaning is player-provided or player-approved prose.

Required design
Deterministic fields own stable identity, campaign association, kind, status, provenance/origin, effective campaign position, deterministic ordering, and supersession/revocation. Define precedence among canonical pack semantics, unresolved RulesAmbiguity metadata from PR #419, active rulings, and active house rules. A ruling linked to a known ambiguity records the ambiguity ID and selected interpretation ID as provenance while retaining approved prose as semantic content. Specify ordinary prospective effectiveness versus effectiveness at the start of the immediately disputed turn.

Architecture and references
Follow ADR 0017 and docs/rules-pack-compiler.md. Immutable packs remain canonical semantics plus source ambiguities; campaign state/history owns prose campaign rules. Reuse campaign rules-pack binding concepts from eshyra-x3w.12 without conflating pack identity with a campaign rule.

Non-goals
No arbitrary prose-to-mechanics compiler; no campaign state in a rules pack; no arbitrary historical retroactivity; no automatic house-rule inference from canonical-rule violations; no persistence of one-off cover, visibility, terrain, or similar fictional judgments.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed types/invariants distinguish ruling from house-rule; define status, origin, effective position, ordering, supersession/revocation, and precedence; known ambiguity linkage is explicit; prospective and immediately-disputed-turn timing are the only initial temporal modes; invalid combinations fail validation; architecture/non-goals are documented and tested.
notes:
Supervisor review of attempt 1 (ce3f9a5) found 4 defects: (1) campaign position ordering is session-lexical-first, so cross-session chronological order inverts (s2/ordinal 5 sorts after s10/ordinal 6); (2) compareCampaignPositions and the orderCampaignRules tie-break use localeCompare, which is locale/ICU-dependent and diverges from codepoint order on case; (3) projectCampaignRule fabricates ambiguityId 'question:<id>' and selectedInterpretationId for recurring-question rulings, inventing source linkage and a selection that never happened; (4) tests declare sessionId once, so no ordering test crosses a session or turn. Attempt 2 dispatched as eshyra-jhpt.1.2.
Attempt 2 (88060a7) reviewed and ACCEPTED for findings 1-4: comparator now ordinal-first with codepoint tie-breaks; localeCompare removed from both ordering paths; recurring-question rulings no longer fabricate ambiguityId/selectedInterpretationId. title: Campaign rules: durable rulings, house rules, and disputed-turn replay
description:
Objective
Add a campaign-owned rule layer for durable table rulings and intentional house rules. Rulings resolve published-source ambiguity or stable recurring interpretation questions; house rules override or supplement otherwise clear canonical behavior. Semantic content remains player-provided or player-approved prose.

Architecture
Preserve ADR 0017 separation: immutable rules packs contain canonical semantics plus source ambiguity metadata; canonical campaign history contains prose rulings/house rules and effective timing; the DM model interprets pack semantics, ambiguity metadata, and active campaign prose; the audit model evaluates against the exact same active prose. Deterministic code owns identity, campaign association, kind, status, provenance, effective position, ordering, supersession/revocation, context delivery, and rollback/replay timing.

Scope
Cover domain/precedence, durable storage, shared DM/auditor context, explicit and implicit known-ambiguity resolution, management workflows, immediate disputed-turn rollback/replay, and end-to-end proof. Initial context delivery supplies all active campaign-rule prose to both models for correctness.

Non-goals
Do not compile arbitrary rule prose into deterministic mechanics. Do not store campaign choices in immutable rules packs. Do not let the DM silently select a canonical winner for source ambiguity. Do not auto-create house rules from attempts that conflict with clear canonical rules. Do not persist one-off contextual judgments such as line of sight, cover from rubble, terrain suitability, or similar fictional adjudication. Do not support arbitrary historical retroactivity.

References
ADR 0017; docs/rules-pack-compiler.md; PR #419 / eshyra-o9bd.18.7.9 RulesAmbiguity metadata, including Create Undead and Find Familiar; existing campaign binding eshyra-x3w.12; auditor eshyra-oobh; audited-turn staging eshyra-67qo; rollback/checkpoint foundations eshyra-c07.8 and eshyra-7wc.5.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are complete. Campaign rules are durable prose with deterministic identity/timing/precedence; DM and auditor receive equivalent active sets; unresolved pack ambiguities can become explicit or accepted implicit rulings; immediate objections can replay the disputed turn; canonical-rule conflicts never become inferred house rules; no ordinary contextual adjudication creates a campaign rule.

title: Character Creation Is a Program, Not a Form
description:
Tell the story of dependency-aware character creation.

Narrative hook and core question: Why not just ask the model to make a legal character?

Research initial model-generated character blobs, unsupported class or ancestry choices, impossible ability-score arrays, and the level-one HP maximum of -4. Explain why validating a complete object after generation is insufficient. Cover concept-first and ability-first creation modes, CharacterDraft, incremental dependency-aware validation, rules-pack-backed legal choice enumeration, required-choice descriptors, prerequisites, derived values, equipment and spell-choice workflows, save/resume, and how the same architecture informs level-up and progression.

Expected architectural conclusion: character creation is a stateful dependency graph disguised as a questionnaire.

Boundary: the existing rules-pack story uses character creation as evidence that prose is not enough. Cover the larger workflow and state-machine architecture without repeating the compiler story.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify claims against artifacts rather than model memory; distinguish implemented behavior from planned architecture; preserve public readability and search indexing; and follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.

title: Remembering the World Without Remembering Every Sentence
description:
Tell the story of layered campaign memory and canon.

Narrative hook and core question: How does an improvised world stay persistent without turning every adjective the model says into canonical database state?

Research the layers actually used or designed in Eshyra, including authored/module canon as an authoritative spine, campaign overlay for consequential improvised facts, scene-local facts and evidence, continuity or descriptive details that should remain stable, transient narration that should remain transient, retrieval of prior facts into future model context, and provenance or confidence where applicable. Use concrete questions: if a tavern has a blue door, should it remain blue six sessions later; if a bartender polishes a glass, should that become lore; if the bartender says the northern road washed out, is that consequential world truth?

Expected architectural conclusion: persistence requires classification of facts by meaning and lifetime, not indiscriminate transcript storage.

Boundaries: do not invent current architecture. Research repository history and clearly distinguish implemented behavior, committed design, and planned direction. Do not collapse all transcript/context work into canon.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify claims against artifacts rather than model memory. Keep the story readable without repository knowledge, static, search-indexable, and faithful to Joseph's voice: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.

title: The Turn That Did Not Happen, Except That It Did
description:
Tell the story of rejected turns, rollback, and retries.

Narrative hook and core question: What does it mean to reject an AI-generated turn after its tools have already changed the world?

Begin with the concrete failure: give_item successfully mutates state, the auditor rejects the candidate turn, repair/retry runs, and the supposedly rejected turn has already changed reality. Expand to repeated damage, resources consumed twice, duplicate combats and combatants, repeated inventory grants, exactly-once effects, speculative candidate execution versus committed turn, audit evidence, repair/retry lifecycle, rollback or transactional boundaries, and invariants showing that a rejected candidate plus repaired retry leaves one accepted world transition.

Expected architectural conclusion: an auditor cannot merely judge prose after the fact. Candidate execution, evidence, rollback, repair, and commit semantics form a transaction protocol.

Boundaries: focus on transactionality and audit lifecycle. Do not turn this into the general rules-pack story.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify claims against artifacts, not model memory; distinguish implemented architecture from planned architecture; preserve static search-indexable public readability; and follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.

title: One Goblin, Three Different Things
description:
Tell the story of actor, encounter, and combatant identity.

Narrative hook and core question: What is a goblin in a persistent AI Dungeon Master's world?

Research concrete playtest target/state thrash around goblins. Explain the difference between a source creature definition and one particular creature; persistent actor identity; encounter membership; tactical combatant projection; current HP, conditions, initiative, and other encounter-local state; recurring NPCs and creatures that survive or escape and return; and why a fresh stat-block copy is not the injured dragon or goblin already known to the campaign. Cover the lifecycle hierarchy across campaign, actor, encounter, combat, and session. Explain why a CLI session is provenance, not the lifetime of a fight, and why quitting and resuming must not implicitly end combat or create a second one.

Expected architectural conclusion: convenient technical lifetimes are not necessarily domain lifetimes. Persistent identity, episodic participation, and tactical state are separate concepts.

Boundaries: do not broaden into the full rollback and transactionality story. Include session-versus-combat lifetime only as needed to support the identity hierarchy.

title: Who Actually Rolls the Dice?
description:
Tell the story of who actually rolls the dice.

Narrative hook and core question: If the AI is the Dungeon Master, why isn't it allowed to roll the dice?

Research concrete Eshyra incidents: early combat where deterministic tools resolved attacks and damage but results were not coherently visible; the differing treatment of initiative and death saves; the distinction between a model-generated number and an actual deterministic die result; and playtest failures around Stealth and Perception secrecy. Explain why deterministic randomness alone is insufficient without meaning, ownership, visibility, and audit evidence. Cover model-declared roll intent and visibility, tool-owned randomness, a deterministic roll ledger or equivalent evidence model, auditor verification that narration agrees with mechanics, provider-neutral tool contracts, and the evolution from fenced-text pseudo-tool protocol toward native tool calls if that history materially supports the story.

Expected architectural conclusion: the model decides what is attempted and interprets what the result means; deterministic tools produce the mechanical result; the runtime preserves enough evidence to prove narration and mechanics agree.

Boundaries: do not turn this into the actor, encounter, or combatant identity story; do not make it a generic random-number article; stay anchored in actual Eshyra playtest failures.

Evidence and editorial requirements: use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify claims against artifacts, not model memory. title: Make gameplay-readiness findings actionable and fail-closable
description:
Finding sources:
- Codex readiness report still showed prose-only/mechanically shallow records across magic items, rules, equipment, features, and actions.
- ChatGPT found many deterministic mechanics gaps despite green verification.

title: Equipment-resolution audit accepts unvalidated named-item candidates
description:
Found in PR #380 review (eshyra-erf5.3.3's srdEquipmentResolutionAudit.ts).

namedItemCandidates(key) in packages/core/src/rules/srdEquipmentResolutionAudit.ts
simply returns `[key]` without checking that `key` exists in the equipment
catalog. PROFICIENCY_PHRASE_RESOLVERS uses this helper for every named
single-item weapon/tool proficiency phrase (hand crossbows, Thieves' tools,
Herbalism kit, Daggers, etc.). assertEquipmentResolution() only checks
`candidateKeys.length > 0`, so a typo in one of these hard-coded keys (e.g.
`equipment:crossbow-hnad` instead of `equipment:crossbow-hand`) would still
pass the audit because it is a non-empty one-element array.

This weakens eshyra-erf5.3.3's claim: the audit proves broad filters
(weapon category/range, armor type, equipmentGroup) resolve against actual
equipment records, but for named single-item phrases it currently proves
only that a hard-coded string is non-empty, not that it exists in the
catalog.

Acceptance criteria:
- Either make namedItemCandidates() filter against the actual equipment
  catalog (only return the key if a record with that key/kind exists), or
  add a second assertion in assertEquipmentResolution() (or a dedicated
  check) that every returned candidateKey exists in the equipment catalog.
- Add a regression test where a named proficiency resolver points at a
  missing/misspelled equipment key and assert that resolution now fails
  (currently it would silently pass).

Likely files: packages/core/src/rules/srdEquipmentResolutionAudit.ts,
packages/core/test/srdEquipmentResolutionAudit.test.ts.
close_reason: namedItemCandidates() now validates keys against the equipment catalog; regression test added for a missing/misspelled named key. PR #381.

title: findRepresentingRecord picks wrong candidate when heading-slug matches every ambiguous option
description:
Discovered while implementing eshyra-lpk9 (multi-page provenance enrichment), which surfaced this as a page-span outlier but did not fix it — it is a pre-existing source-region-ledger classification bug, unrelated to lpk9's own root cause, and out of scope to fix safely without a broader audit of its blast radius.

sourceRegionLedger.ts's findRepresentingRecord (used by classifyRegion as a document-wide text-content search fallback) prefers a candidate record whose key matches EITHER the region's section slug OR its heading slug:

  const preferred = matches.find(
    (record) =>
      (sectionSlug !== undefined && record.key.includes(`:${sectionSlug}:`)) ||
      (headingSlug !== undefined &&
        (record.key.endsWith(`:${headingSlug}`) ||
          record.key.includes(`:${headingSlug}:`))),
  );

When ALL matching candidates share the same heading-slug suffix (e.g. every class's "Ability Score Improvement" feature is named feature:<class>:ability-score-improvement and all 12 have byte-identical boilerplate text: "When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level..."), `.find()` returns the FIRST array element satisfying the OR — which is always true via the heading-slug branch for every candidate — so it never reaches a later, section-slug-correct candidate. In practice this means every class chapter's "Ability Score Improvement" region (Bard p13, Cleric p17, Druid p21, ... — verified in the committed source-region-ledger.json) resolves to `record:feature:barbarian:ability-score-improvement` regardless of which class chapter it is actually in, because feature:barbarian:... happens to sort first among the matches.

This does not corrupt the generated pack's own record content (each class's real feature text lives in its own record via the normal parser, independent of the ledger) — it only mis-attributes the LEDGER's evidence for 11 of the 12 classes to the wrong owning record. Confirmed via: grep source-region-ledger.json entries with targetKey == feature:barbarian:ability-score-improvement — 10 entries across pages 9,13,17,21,27,32,37,44,48,53, all with identical firstPhrase text, when only page 9 (Barbarian's own chapter) is genuinely that record's content.

Expected fix: when multiple matches satisfy the heading-slug branch, prefer one that ALSO satisfies the section-slug branch before falling back to the heading-slug-only choice (i.e. check section-slug across all matches first, then heading-slug only among matches lacking a section-slug hit). Likely other same-boilerplate multi-class features are affected (Ability Score Improvement is the only reviewed example so far).

Suggested tests: a source-region-ledger unit test with 3+ synthetic records sharing a heading-slug suffix, only one matching a given owner's section-slug, asserting the section match wins regardless of array order.

Likely files: packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceRegionLedger.ts (findRepresentingRecord), packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceRegionLedger.test.ts.
close_reason: findRepresentingRecord prefers section-slug matches over heading-slug; 12 ledger entries (9 ASI + 3 Extra Attack) re-attributed to the correct owning class. Unit test added. PR #381.

title: Account for Adventuring Gear / deity-table continuation pages in SRD source-region ledger
description:
Follow-up from eshyra-5c7f. After fixing the sidebar-body-prose gap (17 sidebar records + 2 incidental creature-variant sidebars now have source-region-ledger entries via the isSidebarBodyOwner fix in sourceRegionLedger.ts), three pages still have zero source-region-ledger entries and no per-caption source-coverage.json accounting:

- p69: the Adventuring Gear price/weight table's embedded sub-group captions ("Ammunition", "Arcane focus", "Druidic focus", "Holy symbol") never appear as their own source-inventory items at all (unlike the neighboring "Container Capacity" caption on the same page, which does). They are apparently being consumed by the "Adventuring Gear" table-caption's row-swallowing loop in sourceInventory.ts (buildSourceInventory's `while (isTableCell...) i += 1` after a table-caption) without being independently detected.
- p361: "Greek Deities" / "Egyptian Deities" / "Norse Deities" table captions are correctly inventoried and resolve to their table: records, but own no ledger entries because they have (almost) no non-table-cell prose before their rows start.
- p362: pure continuation of the Norse Deities table rows (Frigga through Uller); no heading at all on this page, so nothing anchors it to an owner for ledger purposes.

Verified this is an audit-evidence gap only, NOT content loss: every equipment item on p69 (abacus, hourglass, sprig-of-mistletoe, totem, wooden-staff, etc.) is present with correct cost/weight in the generated pack, and table:norse-deities already contains all 20 rows including the p362 continuation (Frigga through Uller).

Closing this requires either (a) a real extractor-level fix so embedded sub-group captions within a mega price-list table are detected as their own source-inventory items instead of being silently swallowed by the row-consuming loop, or (b) a deliberate, documented design decision that a source-region-ledger entry is not the right accounting mechanism for table-row-only pages/continuations and that source-coverage.json's table: record ownership is the intended proof instead — in which case the audit tooling should say so explicitly (e.g. a new intentionally-ignored reason or an explicit per-page allowlist) rather than silently reporting zero entries.

Likely files: packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceInventory.ts (embedded-caption detection inside the table-row-consuming loop), sourceRegionLedger.ts (continuation-page-with-no-owner accounting), and packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts if a new page-completeness proof is added.

Suggested tests: a source-inventory unit test with a synthetic multi-caption price table proving each caption becomes its own item; a source-region-ledger regression pinning p69/p361/p362 to explicit accounting once the strategy is decided.
close_reason: Option (b) implemented as a documented design decision: ledger emits explicit table-rows entries for cell runs on otherwise unaccounted pages (p69 x2, p360-361, p361 x2 incl. p362 span) and asserts summary.unaccountedPages empty at import time. table:norse-deities locator now pp. 361, 362 (source-confirmed). Thaw note 2026-07-01-erf5-remaining-followups.md. PR #381.

title: Add SRD equipment filter and proficiency resolution audit
description:
Child of the equipment grouping audit epic.

After preserving equipment grouping metadata, add an audit/resolver check that proves generated starting-equipment filters and class proficiency groups are actually satisfiable from the generated catalog.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a deterministic audit that enumerates candidates for every generated starting-equipment filter.
- The audit fails if a filter such as martial melee weapon, arcane focus, druidic focus, holy symbol, musical instrument, artisan tools, gaming set, or similar emits zero candidates.
- Add a deterministic audit or resolver check for class equipment proficiencies such as Simple weapons, martial weapons, light armor, medium armor, heavy armor, shields, and tool/instrument proficiency groups.
- The audit should report the candidate count and representative candidate keys for reviewability.
- Wire the check into the SRD audit bundle or existing playable-model gate so future regressions are visible.
close_reason: Added srdEquipmentResolutionAudit resolving every starting-equipment filter and class equipment proficiency phrase to concrete equipment candidates; wired into the audit bundle CLI and a fail-closed regression test

title: Add explicit SRD spell-list parity coverage gate
description:
ChatGPT audit finding.

The class spell-list pages are correctly represented in spell.data.classes in the current pack, but source-region accounting classifies most spell-list prose as intentionally ignored spell-list headers. That makes spell-list completeness under-proved: a future regression in class spell membership could pass the source-region ledger even if the generated records no longer match the source spell lists.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add an explicit deterministic parity check that reconstructs each class spell list from the SRD spell-list source pages and compares it to generated spell.data.classes.
- Check Bard, Cleric, Druid, Paladin, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock, and Wizard.
- The check should fail closed on missing spell names, extra spell names, wrong spell level grouping, or wrong class membership.
- The source-region ledger/report should stop describing actual spell-list content as merely ignored header prose, or should clearly point to the explicit spell-list parity check as the owning proof.
- Add regression tests or a generated audit artifact that makes spell-list coverage reviewable without relying on hotspot sampling.
close_reason: Added spellListParityAudit: re-scans the class spell-list source pages independently of applyClassLists and cross-checks against emitted spell records (missing/extra class membership + wrong level), wired as a fail-closed import-time gate. Zero findings against the committed pack.

title: Count nested creature mechanics in gameplay-readiness report
description:
`reports/gameplay-readiness.json` in the 2026-06-30 SRD audit bundle undercounts creature mechanics projections because `buildGameplayReadinessReport` only checks top-level `data.mechanics`, `data.projection`, `data.traits[].mechanics`, and `data.feature.mechanics`.

Confirmed bundle: `/home/jhbongaarts/src/dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle-0630-1.zip`, extracted to `/tmp/eshyra-audit-bundle-0630-1`.

Observed:
- `reports/gameplay-readiness.json` reports `byKind.creature.recordsWithMechanicsProjections: 100`.
- A direct scan of creature `traits`, `actions`, `reactions`, and `legendaryActions.entries` finds 314 creature records with nested `mechanics` objects.
- Existing audit docs/reporting elsewhere use the 314/317 creature mechanics count, so this report is inconsistent and understates deterministic gameplay readiness for creatures.

Relevant code: `packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts`, especially `hasMechanicsProjection` and `buildGameplayReadinessReport`.

Acceptance criteria:
- `gameplay-readiness` counts nested mechanics in creature actions, reactions, legendary actions, and traits consistently with the mechanics projection audit.
- Add a regression assertion for the creature mechanics count or for representative nested action/reaction/legendary-action mechanics.
- The report distinguishes top-level record mechanics from nested gameplay mechanics if both signals remain useful.
close_reason: hasMechanicsProjection now also checks nested actions/reactions/legendaryActions.entries; gameplay-readiness now correctly reports creature: 314/317 matching the documented mechanics-projection audit

title: Emit complete SRD provenance page ranges for multi-page records
description:
The SRD 5.1 pack often emits only the starting page in `record.provenance.locator` even when source coverage/ledger evidence shows the record spans additional pages. This weakens primary-DM discoverability and source traceability: a model following the record's locator may not find all source text.

Confirmed in the 2026-06-30 audit bundle `/home/jhbongaarts/src/dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle-0630-1.zip` by comparing `pack/records.json` locators to pages implied by `reports/source-region-ledger.json` and `reports/source-coverage.json`.

Current lower-bound result: at least 283 records have covered pages missing from their locator. This is a lower bound because the current source ledger omits some continuation pages and sidebars.

Examples:
- `action:ready` has locator `p. 93`, but coverage spans p93-p94.
- `background:acolyte` has locator `p. 60`, but coverage spans p60-p61.
- `condition:paralyzed` has locator `p. 358`, but coverage spans p358-p359.
- `creature:adult-brass-dragon` has locator `p. 291`, but coverage spans p291-p292.
- `rule:wizard-your-spellbook` has locator `p. 54`, while source text continues on p55; this continuation is also affected by the source-ledger coverage bug.

Acceptance criteria:
- Multi-page records emit complete page ranges or page lists in provenance, not only the first page.
- Add a regression check that compares provenance locators to coverage/ledger-derived pages after the source coverage evidence is fixed.
- Document the intended locator format for single-page, contiguous multi-page, and non-contiguous source-backed records.
close_reason: Added enrichProvenanceFromRegionLedger: unions source-region-ledger page evidence into single-page locators (excluding cross-document content-search matches and heading-collision outliers beyond a small continuation gap), giving 345 records complete multi-page provenance. Documented the locator format. Filed eshyra-erf5.6 for an unrelated pre-existing ledger tie-break bug discovered along the way.

title: Revisit ADR 0008 for self-contained release artifact model
description: ADR 0008 (Node runtime + native better-sqlite3 support) was written when npm install was the only distribution path, so it never distinguished dev/workspace install policy from release CI native-build policy from end-user artifact install policy. The release model has since moved to self-contained per-platform archives (ADR 0003/eshyra-upef, ADR 0011) that bundle a pinned Node runtime + ABI-matched better-sqlite3 prebuild + the app tree; end users never run npm install or compile anything. Supersede or amend ADR 0008 to encode this three-layer policy split.
acceptance_criteria: New/amended ADR documents: (1) released artifacts must never run npm install or native compilation on the end-user machine; (2) an explicit decision on whether release CI may source-compile better-sqlite3 when upstream prebuilds are unavailable or prebuild-install tooling risk becomes unacceptable; (3) a requirement for artifact smoke tests on a clean target environment lacking native build tools, with follow-up bead filed for the concrete CI implementation if not done in this bead; (4) explicit bundling requirement that the Node runtime and native addon match OS/arch/Node ABI; (5) the existing guard that moving Node majors requires an explicit dependency/runtime decision is preserved. AGENTS.md/docs/dependencies.md updated if the split changes any stated policy. eshyra-nkbo (npm deprecation warning bead) closed/annotated referencing the dev/workspace-layer decision.
close_reason: Merged as PR #378 (merge commit 4fdad8a). ADR 0016 lands the three-layer native-install model and pre-authorizes source-build-first as a future non-policy implementation choice, keeping the current prebuilt-first default. Net diff docs-only. eshyra-nkbo closed won't-fix; eshyra-w7bp (clean-env smoke) remains open as follow-up.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: PR opened: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/378

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text:
Correction applied per user feedback: the intended decision was to flip dev/workspace AND release-CI layers to source-build-first (not merely accept source-compile as a release-CI fallback). Implemented via a checked-in root .npmrc (build-from-source=true). This required real follow-up fixes beyond docs:

- ci.yml's install-smoke log-scan inverted (now requires source-build evidence, fails on unexpected downloaded prebuild). First attempt used a Windows-incompatible compiler-line pattern; fixed to rely solely on node-gyp's cross-platform "gyp info ok" line, verified via real GitHub Actions runs on Linux/macOS/Windows.
- Removed redundant per-workflow npm_config_build_from_source env vars (ci.yml, release.yml, srd-freeze-guard.yml, srd-importer-reproducibility.yml); build-release-artifact.mjs's --global --prefix install keeps an explicit override since it doesn't inherit repo .npmrc.
- Discovered and fixed a real release-build regression: compiling better-sqlite3 from source also builds its test_extension helper target + ~18MB of node-gyp intermediates, which tripped validate-release-artifact.mjs's stray-native-binary check. Added pruneNativeBuildByproducts() to build-release-artifact.mjs. Verified via a full GitHub Actions Release run: all 16 edition x platform legs + installer-smoke pass.
- Added a thaw note for srd-freeze-guard.yml (a frozen exact path) since removing its env block tripped the SRD freeze changed-path check.

All workflows (CI, Release, SRD frozen artifact guard, SRD importer reproducibility) pass on the final commit c252672. PR #378 updated.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text:
Final direction (per review): reverted the source-build-first flip; kept ADR 0016 reframed as permissive rather than mandatory.

Rationale: the flip bought resiliency (no hard dependency on prebuild-install's deprecated download path) but did NOT remove the deprecation warning (prebuild-install stays a declared dep of better-sqlite3 either way) and added per-install compile time + a mandatory toolchain everywhere. Not worth forcing now.

ADR 0016 now: (a) three-layer model (dev/workspace, release-CI, end-user artifact); (b) ADR 0008's prebuilt-first default stays in force; (c) pre-authorizes opting layers 1-2 into source-build-first later as an implementation choice with NO new policy ADR, recording the four validated conditions (mandatory toolchain; invert ci.yml compile-evidence guard keyed on `gyp info ok`; prune node-gyp byproducts incl test_extension.node from release artifacts; longer builds); (d) layer 3 = hard rule (end-user artifact never compiles). ADR 0008 gets a pointer note; AGENTS.md gets a one-line pointer.

Net PR diff vs main is docs-only. All CI green (build-test + install-smoke Linux/Win/mac, CodeQL). PR #378 updated. eshyra-nkbo stays closed won't-fix; eshyra-w7bp (clean-env smoke) stays open.

title: Promote vk23 overlay parity false mismatches into clean audit output
description:
Combined vk23 audit follow-up.

Codex GPT-5.5-max audit found and filed eshyra-jk4d for this issue. This bead exists only if the existing bead was not present in the local Beads database when this script is run; otherwise close or delete this duplicate and use eshyra-jk4d.

Finding:
The bundle's overlay parity report flags four false mismatches for prepared casters:
- cleric data.spellPreparation
- druid data.spellPreparation
- paladin data.spellPreparation
- wizard data.spellPreparation

The actual pack data is richer and source-backed because it includes preparationFormula. The parity report projection drops that field in:
- packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts

The source-backed overlay facts include it in:
- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/creationFacts.ts

This is not a gameplay data blocker, but the thaw standard requires audit output to be clean and non-misleading.

Acceptance criteria:

- Update the overlay-vs-pack parity projection to include preparationFormula or otherwise compare equivalent normalized structures.
- Regenerate the audit bundle and confirm overlay-vs-pack-parity reports no false mismatches.
- Keep prepared caster spellPreparation data richer than the overlay oracle where source-backed.

title: Add deterministic catalogs for SRD language and tool choices
description:
Combined vk23 audit follow-up.

The vk23 bundle is strong for class progression and structured choices, but some open-ended language/tool choices remain more prose-like than deterministic tooling would prefer.

Examples to inspect:
- Half-Elf / Human / High Elf language choices
- Acolyte language choices
- Bard musical instrument choices
- Monk artisan tool or musical instrument choices
- Other features/backgrounds that choose from "any language", "any tool", "musical instrument", or similar categories

This is not a source-coverage failure, but deterministic character creation needs stable choice domains and filters instead of bespoke prose interpretation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add or expose canonical SRD choice domains for languages and tool categories where the SRD provides enough structure.
- Ensure relevant ancestry, background, and class feature choices reference those domains instead of relying only on prose.
- Preserve source text and source fidelity; do not invent options outside the SRD.
- Add tests for Half-Elf languages, Acolyte languages, Bard instrument choices, and Monk tool/instrument choices.
- Update choice coverage/audit output so these choices are visible as deterministic domains.
close_reason: Wired the already-existing standard-languages table and tool-category description grouping into languages[].from and toolProficiencyChoices[].from for Half-Elf/Human/High-Elf/Acolyte/Bard/Monk. Plumbed through rulesPackResolver/requiredChoices, replacing a duplicate hardcoded list. Regression tests for all named examples against the real pack

title: Make repeated SRD feature choices advancement-level aware
description:
Combined vk23 audit follow-up.

Repeated features such as Ability Score Improvement are source-correctly represented as a feature whose source prose starts at the first level where it appears, while class advancement grants the same feature at later levels.

Example:
- Fighter has one Ability Score Improvement feature with source level metadata around level 4.
- Fighter progression grants ASI at levels 4, 6, 8, 12, 14, 16, and 19.

This is source-faithful, but deterministic level-up tooling must instantiate the choice using the class advancement row level, not only the static feature choice level. Otherwise repeated ASI choices can be mis-leveled or collapsed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Define the contract for repeated feature choice instantiation:
  - feature source level identifies where the feature prose originates
  - advancement grant level identifies the level at which a choice instance is available
- Ensure character-creation/level-up consumers can derive separate choice instances for repeated grants.
- Add regression coverage for Fighter ASI levels, including non-4 ASI grants such as levels 6 and 14.
- Audit other repeated features with choices and ensure the same contract holds.
- Document the distinction between feature source metadata and advancement instance metadata.
close_reason: Added repeatedFeatureChoices.ts: separates feature source level from advancement grant level, derives one choice instance per grant level. Mystic Arcanum's already-correct per-level entries are not duplicated. Regression coverage for Fighter ASI (incl. levels 6/14), Channel Divinity, Expertise, Metamagic against the real pack

title: Define addressable inline option IDs for SRD choices
description:
Combined vk23 audit follow-up.

The vk23 pack models several gameplay-significant options as inline structured choices rather than first-class records. This is reasonable for source fidelity, but deterministic tools and retrieval need an explicit addressing contract.

Concrete example:
- Eldritch Invocation prerequisites reference inline Pact Boon option IDs:
  - pact-boon:pact-of-the-tome
  - pact-boon:pact-of-the-chain
  - pact-boon:pact-of-the-blade
- These are not top-level records; they exist under feature:warlock:pact-boon.

Similar categories may include Fighting Styles, Metamagic options, Hunter options, Pact Boons, Eldritch Invocations, and other feature-local choices.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decide whether gameplay-significant inline options should remain nested addressable entities or be promoted to first-class records.
- If nested: define a stable address format and add resolver/index support so deterministic tools can resolve inline option IDs.
- If first-class: generate records for the selected option categories and update references accordingly.
- Add tests that Warlock invocation prerequisites resolve successfully.
- Add an audit check that reference-like fields pointing to inline option IDs are either resolvable or explicitly exempted with rationale.
close_reason: Kept inline options nested; added inlineFeatureOptions.ts resolver/index plus unresolvable-inline-option-ref audit gate. All Warlock invocation prerequisites verified resolvable against the committed pack

title: Audit bundle overlay parity flags prepared-caster formula supersets as mismatches
description: The generated D&D SRD audit bundle reports overlay-vs-pack parity mismatches for class:cleric, class:druid, class:paladin, and class:wizard data.spellPreparation. The actual pack data includes source-backed preparationFormula fields, while the parity report's expected overlay projection drops preparationFormula before comparing. This makes a successful migration to richer generated-pack facts appear as four mismatches in metadata.json and reports/overlay-vs-pack-parity.*. Update the audit-bundle parity projection or comparison so these source-backed formula supersets are treated as expected, and add/adjust coverage so future bundles report zero mismatches when generated pack facts intentionally extend the legacy overlay shape.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh npm run audit-bundle:dnd5e-srd reports overlayVsPackParity.mismatchedFacts as 0 for the current prepared-caster spellPreparation facts, without removing the preparationFormula fields from class records.
close_reason: Fixed spellPreparationFromOverlay to include preparationFormula; audit-bundle now reports 0 overlay mismatches

title: Fix the npm warning: npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: No longer maintained. Please contact the author of the relevant native addon; alternatives are available.
close_reason: wont_fix

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text:
Investigated: this warning comes from prebuild-install@7.1.3, a transitive dependency of better-sqlite3 (the only compiled dependency, pinned per ADR 0008/ADR 0016). better-sqlite3's latest published version (12.11.1, already what we're on) still requires prebuild-install@^7.1.1, and prebuild-install itself has been deprecated by its own maintainers with no maintained successor -- there is no version bump that removes the warning today. It does not fail installs or CI; it's dev-time noise, not a functional break.

ADR 0016 (docs/adr/0016-native-dependency-install-policy-by-environment.md), written while investigating this bead, formally accepts this as tracked cosmetic noise under the dev/workspace install layer, and explicitly says not to "fix" it with a risky overrides entry that could jeopardize the prebuilt-binary install path CI depends on (npm_config_build_from_source=false). Revisit only if a future better-sqlite3 release migrates off prebuild-install, or it stops producing a working binary.

Closed as won't-fix.

title: Structured Warlock invocation prerequisite modeling
description: Follow-on to eshyra-vk23.3. The invocation prerequisite STRINGS are now correct, but tools still parse prose like '12th level, Pact of the Blade feature'. Add a structured 'prerequisites' clause array on invocation options, preserving the original 'prerequisite' prose. Model: class-level (scoped to class:warlock), pact-boon option refs (pact-of-the-blade/chain/tome), and cantrip refs (eldritch blast cantrip -> spell:eldritch-blast). Tests for Book of Ancient Secrets, Chains of Carceri, Lifedrinker, Thirsting Blade, Voice of the Chain Master, and a cantrip prereq.

title: Attribute SRD invocation option source pages (48-50)
description:
Split from eshyra-vk23.3 (prerequisite parsing fix). The prerequisite-truncation bug is fixed; this bead covers the remaining source-page attribution.

Problem:
All 32 Warlock Eldritch Invocation options in feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations carry source 'SRD 5.1 p. 47' (the feature heading page). The invocation list actually spans SRD pages 48-50 (p.47 holds only the intro paragraph). Evidence from the vendored PDF text:
- p.48: Agonizing Blast, Armor of Shadows, Ascendant Step, Beast Speech, Beguiling Influence, Bewitching Whispers, Book of Ancient Secrets (start).
- p.49: Chains of Carceri, Lifedrinker, Master of Myriad Forms, Minions of Chaos, Mire the Mind, Repelling Blast, etc.
- p.50: Thirsting Blade, Visions of Distant Realms, Voice of the Chain Master, Whispers of the Grave, Witch Sight, etc.

Why deferred (per docs/importer-fix-protocol.md stop-and-report rule):
Per-option page attribution needs a NEW extractor strategy, not a localized parser fix. The options are parsed in deriveFeatureChoices.ts from the already-concatenated feature.description string, which carries no page data. The warlock pages are a TWO-COLUMN layout where invocation headings interleave with Pact Boon text; parseFeatures de-interleaves columns to build the description, so recovering a per-heading page number requires threading page-boundary data from extract.ts/parseFeatures through FeatureExtraction into the choice deriver.

Scope:
- Capture the source page for each invocation heading at parse time (column-aware).
- Thread a heading->page map on FeatureExtraction (or emit per-option source at parse time).
- Set each option's source to its true SRD page (48, 49, or 50).

title: Add ordered SRD subclass progression
description:

For example, Champion can list Additional Fighting Style before lower-level features. A deterministic resolver can sort indirectly, but simple consumers and the primary DM model benefit from direct ordered progression.

Scope:
- Inspect subclass records and feature refs.
- Either sort subclass features by level, or add an explicit progression/featuresByLevel projection.
- Ensure repeated-level subclass features remain grouped correctly.
- Preserve existing refs and source citations.
- Add tests or audit checks for deterministic ordering/projection.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each subclass exposes level-ordered feature progression directly or through an explicit projection.
- Champion progression presents level 3, 7, 10, 15, and 18 features in order.
- Consumers do not need to infer subclass progression order by joining feature refs manually unless that is explicitly documented.
- npm run typecheck passes.
- npm test passes.
- npm run check passes.

title: Replace SRD free-text choice filters

- "the wizard spell list"
- "the bard spell list"
- "your skill proficiencies"

These are discoverable by the primary DM model but weak for deterministic tools. Tools should not parse English to determine allowed choices.

Scope:

- Add guardrails so future importer changes do not reintroduce string filters for deterministic choice domains.
- Preserve source prose separately for DM context.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spell/cantrip choices use structured spell filters with class list and level constraints.
- Character-state choices use structured filters rather than prose like "your skill proficiencies".
- Any remaining string from/source values are explicitly justified as DM-only prose or unknown/unresolved.
- New tests or audit gates catch spell/cantrip choices with string filters.

title: Project creature and action attack mechanics
description:
Problem:
Creature records expose stat blocks, traits, and action arrays, but attacks and effects are mostly raw text. Deterministic combat tools cannot reliably extract attack bonus, reach/range, targets, hit damage, save DC, recharge, or condition application.

Implement:

  - one target / target count

Acceptance criteria:

- Ambiguous actions remain prose-backed with no invented fields.
- Projection diagnostics identify remaining prose-only actions.
- Tests cover common attack forms.
- Existing tests and pack verification pass.
