title: Project common spell mechanics from SRD spell records
description:
Problem:
Spell records have useful top-level metadata such as level, school, casting time, range, duration, components, classes, ritual, and material. But concentration, saving throw, spell attack, damage, condition, area, and scaling mechanics are generally still prose-only.

Implement:
- Add optional typed mechanics projection fields for spells.
- Start with high-confidence patterns:
  - concentration derived from duration text.
  - saving throw ability and DC relationship where explicit.
  - spell attack indicator.
  - damage dice/type where explicit and simple.
  - condition application where explicit.
  - higher-level scaling where regular and source-clear.
- Emit projection diagnostics for spells not projected.

Acceptance criteria:
- Representative combat spells have typed attack/save/damage projections.
- Concentration can be queried deterministically.
- Ambiguous spells remain source-prose-backed rather than guessed.
- Tests cover positive and negative examples.
- Existing tests and pack verification pass.

title: Add first-pass deterministic mechanics projections for gameplay
description:
Problem:
The pack is source-complete, but many gameplay mechanics remain prose-only after basic top-level fields. This limits deterministic tools for combat, spell use, conditions, resources, and creature actions.

Goal:
Add a first-pass projection layer for commonly needed mechanics without attempting to build a complete rules engine in one bead.

Principles:
- Projection must be derived from SRD text.
- Preserve source prose as canonical audit text.
- Prefer partial, well-tested typed projections over broad brittle parsing.
- Unknown or ambiguous effects should remain prose-backed with explicit lack of projection.

Scope candidates:
- Spell concentration flag from duration.
- Spell attack/save/damage/scaling projection where patterns are clear.
- Creature/action attack bonus, reach/range, target count, hit damage, save DC, and condition application.
- Feature resource counts and recharge/rest reset where explicit.
- Hazard detection/disable/save/damage projections where clear.

Acceptance criteria:
- A report shows which records gained mechanics projections and which remain prose-only.
- Projection fields are optional and schema-visible.
- Tests cover representative spells, creature actions, features, and hazards.
- Existing tests and pack verification pass.

title: Absorb character-creation overlays into generated pack data
description:
Deficiency #4 + thaw scope #2. Four deterministic overlays exist outside the pack only because the frozen pack lacked machine-readable facts. Move each into importer output:
  - packages/core/src/character/srdAncestryAbilityScoreIncreases.ts -> ancestry.data.abilityScoreIncreases (fixed + choice grants). ASIs are prose-only today.
  - packages/core/src/character/srdClassSpellcasting.ts -> class/feature spellcasting metadata (ability + prepared-caster formulas). Not structured today.
  - packages/core/src/character/srdClassStartingEquipment.ts -> class.data.startingEquipment with typed choice/fixed item grants. Prose-only today.
  - packages/core/src/character/srdLanguages.ts -> ancestry.data.languages and background.data.languages as structured grants. Prose/free-text today.
These become importer responsibilities during thaw. Overlay RETIREMENT is a separate downstream bead.
design:
HANDOFF PLAN (authored after .2 landed; self-contained for a clean session).

GOAL: emit the four character-creation overlays' source-backed facts INTO the generated pack so character creation needs no consumer-side overlay. DONE-MARKER: auditSrdPlayability() `overlay-dependence` count -> 0, and the .11 baseline test flips to toBe(0). Overlay RETIREMENT is .15, NOT this bead — leave src/character/srd*.ts overlays + their tests in place; this PR only ADDS pack data.

TARGET FIELDS + SHAPES (these are exactly what the .11 overlay-dependence gate checks in packages/core/src/rules/srdPlayabilityAudit.ts, function checkOverlayDependence):
- ancestry.data.abilityScoreIncreases: non-empty array. Source data: src/character/srdAncestryAbilityScoreIncreases.ts ANCESTRY_ABILITY_SCORE_INCREASES (13 ancestries, {fixed:[{ability,bonus}], choice?:{choose,bonus,from}, sourceText}).
- ancestry.data.languages + background.data.languages: non-empty arrays. Source: src/character/srdLanguages.ts (getAncestryLanguages/getBackgroundLanguages, LanguageGrant shape).
- class.data.spellcastingAbility: non-empty string on spellcasting classes only (gate detects casters via a spellcastingProgression entry in progression[].advancement[]). Source: src/character/srdClassSpellcasting.ts.
- class.data.startingEquipment.entries[]: typed objects {kind:'choice',options[],sourceText} | {kind:'fixed',text,sourceText}. Source: src/character/srdClassStartingEquipment.ts. IMPORTANT: pack already has startingEquipment.entries as PROSE STRINGS — convert them to typed objects in place (each entry's sourceText must equal the original prose string; the overlay's sourceText already mirrors the pack prose).

DATA SOURCING DECISION: copy the source-cited constant tables FROM the four overlays INTO the importer (packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/, e.g. a new creationFacts.ts) so generation owns them. Do NOT import runtime src/ overlays from scripts/. (.15 later converts the src overlays' tests into pack-vs-source oracle tests and deletes the runtime code.)

IMPORTER EMIT POINTS (all in packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/emit.ts buildPack, ~line 1240-1256, post-emit enrichment, mirroring linkAncestryOptionTables / enrichClassChapterRecords):
- ancestry records: enrich with abilityScoreIncreases + languages (new helper, or extend linkAncestryOptionTables).
- background records: enrich with languages (backgroundExtractionsToRecords ~line 1245).
- class records: add spellcastingAbility + replace startingEquipment.entries strings with typed entries — fold into enrichClassChapterRecords in classProgression.ts (it already shapes class.data).

RESOLVER: surface new fields on ResolvedAncestryData / ResolvedBackgroundData / ResolvedClassData in src/character/rulesPackResolver.ts (some types already exist for the overlays; reuse shapes). Keep parsing fail-closed.

GATE + TESTS (packages/core/test/srdPlayabilityAudit.test.ts):
- Flip the 'RED until eshyra-o9bd.5: overlay-dependence' baseline to expect 0.
- CRITICAL: once overlay-dependence hits 0, ALL implemented gate categories are 0, so srdPlayabilityHasFindings()===false. The `it.fails('re-freeze readiness...')` ratchet will then FAIL (it was expected-fail, now passes). Convert that it.fails into a normal it() asserting zero findings (green). (Later gates .8/.9 are not yet implemented in .11; .14 re-freeze adds them.)
- FIX THE STALE TOP COMMENT in srdPlayabilityAudit.ts: the 'Gate coverage status' block still says .2/.3 are RED; update to reflect .2/.3/.5/.6 all GREEN against the committed pack (reviewer-flagged on PR #353).

PROCEDURAL GOTCHAS (learned in .2):
1. WORKTREE DISCIPLINE: make ALL edits in the worktree path (.worktrees/<name>/...), NOT the parent checkout. (In .2 I accidentally edited the parent /home/jhbongaarts/src/eshyra/... because I'd opened that path pre-worktree; caught it, but verify `git -C <parent> status` stays clean.)
2. REGENERATE: npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --pdf packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/   (dry-run to a scratch --out first to inspect). Expect only records.json (+ maybe source-coverage.json/source-region-ledger.json) to change. NO record COUNT change (adding fields, not records) -> record-counts.md/evidence.json counts stay valid (unlike .2). Confirm via git status.
3. FREEZE: this is a frozen path (importer + pack + audit docs). Per docs/importer-fix-protocol.md + the umbrella thaw note convention, ADD a per-child thaw note under docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/thaw-notes/<date>-absorb-creation-overlays.md, and update freeze-manifest.json hashes for changed pinned files. Hash-sync script (run AFTER Biome format): python recompute sha256 of every freeze-manifest 'files' entry, write back changed ones. BIOME GOTCHA: `npm run format` reformats audit JSON under docs/audits (not the packages/core/data pack, which Biome ignores) — so run format FIRST, THEN re-sync hashes, else the pins break.
4. VERIFY: npm run verify:worktree (Biome+typecheck+test) AND npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-freeze -- --base origin/main (hash 13/13 + changed-path authorized by the thaw note — only passes once everything incl. thaw note is COMMITTED, since the guard diffs origin/main...HEAD).

- Leveling (XP/level/HP/features/slots) does not need currency, but treasure/quest REWARD flows do; the wallet should exist before reward flows. This epic can proceed in parallel with the progression beads.
- Coinage is rules-pack-bound (5e cp/sp/ep/gp/pp differs from other systems); it lives behind the pack like the rest of the sheet.

title: Core character registry + CLI cutover (ADR 0012 continuity/custody)
description:
Implements the cross-campaign half of the character-sheet authority model, and records the decision as ADR 0012 IN THIS PR (no separate ADR PR).

ADR 0012 (folded in): a character is a cross-campaign continuing entity; campaigns are episodes that take CUSTODY during play. The data-root character registry is the authority BETWEEN campaigns; a campaign's character_sheet row (eshyra-lupf.14.1) is the authoritative playable instance DURING play. Attach/import is copy-with-provenance, NOT a silent clone. Revisions, exit/sync-back, double-attach prevention, and the lore chronicle are deferred. Currency is a known sheet gap (eshyra-lupf.15). Cross-pack still fails closed.

Implementation:
- Add a core-owned CharacterRegistryStore backed by a data-root SQLite DB (e.g. <dataRoot>/characters.db), keyed by a stable globalCharacterId, persisting the CharacterSheet document with binding columns (schema_version/system/rules_pack_id) + created_at/updated_at. Named distinctly from the per-campaign CharacterSheetStore; may share low-level helpers.
- One-time importer: migrate legacy <dataRoot>/characters/*.json into the registry.
- Rewire the CLI: standalone create-character writes the registry; import/attach reads the registry, asserts pack match, copies the sheet into the campaign character_sheet table, projects identity/class/level/hp_max into the live character row (importFinalizedCharacter), and stamps globalCharacterId provenance on the campaign sheet.
- Remove the deprecated FinalizedCharacter alias; consumers use CharacterSheet.
- Do NOT build revisions/custody-sync/fork (eshyra-lupf.14.3) or the chronicle (eshyra-lupf.16).
acceptance_criteria:
- ADR 0012 records the continuity/custody model (registry=between-campaign authority; campaign character_sheet=during-play; attach=copy-with-provenance not clone; revisions/sync + chronicle deferred; currency a known gap; cross-pack fails closed).
- Core CharacterRegistryStore (data-root SQLite) persists sheets keyed by a stable globalCharacterId and replaces CLI JSON authority.
- Legacy <root>/characters/*.json are migrated into the registry.
- CLI create/import are wired to the registry; attach copies the sheet into the campaign character_sheet, projects the live row, and stamps globalCharacterId provenance.
- FinalizedCharacter alias removed; consumers use CharacterSheet.
- Pack mismatch fails closed on attach.
- Tests cover registry round-trip, JSON migration, attach+provenance, and pack-mismatch.
notes: PR #328 (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/328). ADR 0012 + CharacterRegistryStore + attachCharacterSheetToCampaign + CLI cutover + legacy-JSON migration; FinalizedCharacter alias removed. Open for review; close on merge.

title: Define core-owned, rules-pack-bound canonical character sheet authority
description:
TWO FIXED CONSTRAINTS (not questions to revisit):
1. CORE-OWNED: the authoritative character sheet lives behind a core-owned model and persistence/API boundary in @eshyra/core, NOT in CLI-only JSON files. CLI, future web, and future app UXes all call the same core character-sheet APIs (repo principle: UI-agnostic core, thin CLI).
2. RULES-PACK-BOUND: a character sheet is valid only for the rules system, rules pack, and schema version that produced it. It is NOT generic 'D&D-ish' data and is NOT a cross-pack universal model. The sheet stays pinned to the pack it was created under; a rules-pack upgrade must never silently rewrite a character.

This is already where FinalizedCharacter points: it carries schemaVersion, system ('dnd5e-srd'), rulesPackId (which encodes pack version, e.g. rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1), recipeId, creationMode, plus frozen class/ancestry/background refs and rules-derived fields. That type should become (or convert into) the core-owned, pack-bound canonical sheet.

Current state:
- Core live SQLite 'character' rows are sparse — fine for prompt context, not a long-term authority.
- FinalizedCharacter is a rich core TYPE but its PERSISTENCE is CLI-side (createFileFinalizedCharacterStore writes JSON).
- Leveling needs one authoritative, pack-bound record for class refs, provenance, progression events, proficiencies, equipment, languages, spells, HP, ability scores, derived values.

Non-goals:
- Do NOT design a universal character schema making 5e / Pathfinder / future systems mutually interchangeable.
- Do NOT support in-place rules-pack migration as part of leveling.
- Do NOT assume a character is playable under a different rules pack without an explicit conversion.

Open sub-decisions (the real remaining work; storage shape only):
- Versioned JSON document first, normalized tables later, or both via projection (recommended lean: core-owned versioned document + sparse live-state projection).
- Whether FinalizedCharacter evolves into the canonical pack-bound sheet type or is converted into one after creation.
- How the sparse live 'character' table relates to it (projection/cache/prompt summary — NOT an independent authority).
- Migration path from existing CLI finalized-character JSON files into core-owned storage.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical sheet records include characterId, schemaVersion, rulesSystem/system, rulesPackId (with pack version), and enough provenance to validate future reads/writes.
- Persistence and read/write APIs for the canonical sheet are owned by core; CLI calls them now, web/app later.
- Core progression APIs REFUSE to apply progression when the acting rules pack does not match the sheet's rulesPackId/rulesSystem (fail closed on mismatch).
- It is defined whether FinalizedCharacter evolves into the canonical pack-bound sheet type or is converted into one.
- The sparse live 'character' table's relationship to the canonical sheet is defined (projection/cache/prompt summary, not an independent authority).
- A migration path from CLI-side finalized-character JSON files into core-owned storage is defined.
- It is recorded that CLI-owned JSON persistence is no longer authoritative, and that cross-pack character conversion is a FUTURE explicit operation that creates a new character/sheet from old character information (new-character generation with imported source facts), NOT an in-place mutation or normal progression.
- Progression ledger (.2) and level-up engine (.8) are blocked on this boundary.
notes: PR #325 (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/325) — ADR 0011. Decision deliverable; implementation tracked as eshyra-lupf.14. Open for review; close on merge.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add rules-pack-backed character progression and leveling
description:
Eshyra can now create/finalize a level-1 D&D SRD character, but there is no durable progression model. Campaign state has a level and HP fields, but no XP/experience ledger, no milestone policy, no level-up eligibility check, and no guided level-up flow. Play can therefore run sessions without accumulating character advancement, and any level changes would be ad hoc.

This epic adds a durable, auditable, rules-pack-backed progression and leveling model so that advancement is deterministic and not LLM-improvised.
design:
This epic EXTENDS the landed guided character-creation architecture (eshyra-b69j, complete) rather than inventing a parallel model. Reuse: the pure incremental CharacterDraft engine and its 'choices keyed by generated descriptors' pattern; the FinalizedCharacter shape; RulesPackCharacterResolver; and the deterministic derived-value seams.

Grounding (verified against current tree):
- The rules pack rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1 class records carry a full per-level 'progression' table (level, proficiencyBonus, features[] with refs, spellcasting.cantripsKnown / slots by spell level) for levels 1-20 — deterministic level-up is feasible from pack data, not LLM prose.
- XP thresholds are in the frozen pack as the 'table:character-advancement' record — source thresholds from there.
- rulesPackResolver.ts parses only a level-1 slice today (ResolvedClassData.level1 via parseLevel1); .3 generalizes that seam.
- derivedValues.ts deriveLevel1Values is explicitly level-1 only; .8 generalizes it rather than adding CLI-side math.
- CHARACTER-SHEET AUTHORITY IS UNRESOLVED AND IS THE BIGGEST DESIGN QUESTION (.13): the live SQLite 'character' table is sparse (name/ancestry/class/level/hp/ability_scores_json/conditions_json), while FinalizedCharacter is a much richer artifact persisted as JSON files by the CLI-layer createFileFinalizedCharacterStore — a separate store/package/format. Leveling must pick a single authority before the ledger (.2) and engine (.8) are built.
- requiredChoices.ts is the established required-choice pattern; .9 mirrors it but must FAIL CLOSED on spell/feature choices the engine can't deterministically apply (unlike the lenient creation-time spell gate).
acceptance_criteria:
- Character progression state exists: current XP, level, advancement mode, and progression events.
- XP vs milestone policy is defined per campaign/rules binding.
- XP/milestone awards are recorded as auditable state mutations.
- Level-up eligibility is detected deterministically.
- A guided level-up flow is backed by the rules pack, not LLM prose.
- Level-up applies deterministically: HP increase, class level, new features, spell slots/spells/choices where supported.
- Unsupported choices are explicit and blocked rather than inferred.
- CLI/session commands exist for viewing progression and applying level-up.
notes:
Decompose into children for: design note, schema+ledger, resolver level-N generalization, advancement policy, award recording, eligibility detection, deterministic apply engine, required-choices+block, guided flow, CLI/session commands, and cross-class integration tests.
Authority constraint is now FIXED (eshyra-lupf.13): the canonical character sheet is core-owned (@eshyra/core), not CLI JSON. CLI/web/app all call core character-sheet APIs. Recommended work order: .1 (design note), .3 (resolver generalization), .13 (core character-sheet authority boundary), then .2 (ledger) and .8 (engine) and the rest.
All 15 children complete and landed on main: progression model/ledger, advancement policy, eligibility, deterministic level-up engine, guided flow + CLI commands, integration tests, canonical CharacterSheet authority + store/migration, structured currency wallet (.15), and portable character chronicle (.16). Closing epic.
close_reason: Closed

title: Harden tool-span diagnostics against callback failures
description:
Harden turn-loop tool span diagnostics so telemetry callback failures cannot abort gameplay/model execution.

Problem:
The turn loop documents onToolSpan as best-effort telemetry that must never throw, but the callback is invoked from the tool execution path without a local safety wrapper. A diagnostics sink failure should not fail an otherwise successful turn.

Acceptance criteria:
- Wrap onToolSpan invocation in a local try/catch.
- Preserve turn/tool success behavior if telemetry storage/reporting fails.
- Add a focused regression test where onToolSpan throws and the tool/model loop still returns the expected result.
- Optionally surface the telemetry failure through a safe debug path that cannot recursively trigger the same failure.
close_reason: Wrapped tool-span callback emission in the model loop, preserving successful tool/model execution when diagnostics callbacks throw; added regression coverage.

title: Support audit presentation-only repair without primary-DM regeneration
description: Follow-up from eshyra-d8ap.3. The engine can deterministically replace model-authored roll ledgers from structured roll metadata, but there is not yet an explicit safe patch path for auditor verdicts that say all tool calls and state mutations are valid and only presentation is wrong. Design and implement a fail-closed auditor/orchestrator path that can repair presentation-only issues without full primary-DM regeneration when structured evidence is already valid. Acceptance criteria: auditor can distinguish presentation-only from state/tool/evidence failures; code-owned ledger replacement remains deterministic; missing or incorrect model-owned visibility/category metadata still requires model repair; true state/tool errors still fail closed; retry metrics show avoided primary-DM retries for presentation-only fixes.

title: Add model-tier evaluation harness for primary DM and auditor roles
description:
Claude-vs-Codex comparison is mostly curiosity and is confounded by runtime changes like `l3b3`. The practical model question is which model tier is required for each Eshyra role. Evaluate primary DM and auditor roles independently, especially within the same provider, and measure total accepted-turn cost/usage rather than just per-call token counts.

Acceptance criteria:

- Define a short deterministic scenario that can be run under multiple primary DM / auditor model pairings on the same commit.
- Use deterministic roll fixtures for combat comparison, not live RNG.
- Scenario should include Sela / village-authority dialogue; asking what happened; asking what to expect if investigating; traveling to the watchtower; lighting a torch / entering the hollow; goblin ambush; at least one player attack; at least one enemy attack; a save/check or death save in the deterministic fixture.
- Support evaluating primary DM and auditor roles independently: fixed primary DM + varied auditor; fixed auditor + varied primary DM.
- Suggested staged matrix: Phase 1 holds primary DM constant and varies auditor with Opus + Haiku, Opus + Sonnet, Opus + Opus as a ceiling/control only if useful, GPT-5.5 + GPT-5.4-mini, and GPT-5.5 + stronger GPT auditor tier if available; Phase 2 holds best auditor constant and varies primary DM with Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku if available and GPT-5.5 vs lower GPT primary tiers if available; Phase 3 evaluates cheapest viable pairings such as Sonnet + Haiku, Sonnet + Sonnet, and lower GPT primary + mini auditor if available.
- Capture comparison metrics: first-pass audit accept rate; primary DM retry count; auditor call count; total expensive primary-DM calls per accepted player turn; auditor rejection causes; auditor false rejects; auditor false accepts; JSON/parse failures; tool correctness; player-visible roll compliance; combatant-state correctness; unsupported inference rate; qualitative prose/style notes; approximate usage by primary DM vs auditor.
- Explicitly test the hypothesis that a stronger auditor may reduce total usage by avoiding false rejects and expensive primary-DM retries.
- Document that prior Claude-vs-Codex comparisons were confounded by `l3b3` and differing session content.
- Output should make it easy to compare table feel separately from mechanical correctness.
notes: PR #309 opened for model-tier evaluation harness. Validation passed: targeted model evaluation/profile/combat fixture tests and npm run verify:worktree.
close_reason: Merged PR #309 with model-tier evaluation harness, deterministic scenario/matrix, metrics aggregation, tests, and docs.

title: Add deterministic combat regression fixture for first combat playtest
description:
Create a regression-style scripted or semi-scripted test based on the first combat playtest. Do not depend on the natural RNG stream causing Bob to drop to 0 HP. Instead, use a deterministic roll fixture / fake roll tool / roll-plan mode for exact mechanical-path tests, and keep live RNG playtest recipes branch-tolerant.

Acceptance criteria:

- Provide a deterministic combat fixture that can force Bob wins initiative; Bob's first attack misses; goblin attacks miss; Bob's second attack hits; Bob's damage kills `goblin-1`; `goblin-2` critically hits Bob; damage drops Bob to 0 HP; Bob makes a death save and succeeds.
- Assert mechanical invariants rather than exact prose: rolls are executed by tools; player-visible rolls are surfaced according to policy; HP changes are state-backed; combatant ids are stable once combatant state exists; rejected candidates do not persist state; successful retries do not duplicate state writes.
- Include a live playtest recipe using real RNG, but make it branch-tolerant: if Bob attacks, player attack roll is visible; if Bob hits, damage roll is visible; if a goblin attacks Bob, attack roll is visible; if Bob takes damage, damage and HP/state change are visible; if Bob reaches 0 HP, unconscious/dying state and death-save flow are visible; if Bob kills both goblins, combat ends cleanly and state reflects both enemies defeated.
- Mark any parts blocked on the combatant-state bead.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic first-combat regression fixture, rollback/retry invariants, and branch-tolerant live RNG playtest recipe. PR #305.

title: Expose canon-tier evidence in debug audit logs
description:
Improve debug/audit visibility for canon-tier evidence.

title: Add regression test for improvised hook continuity
description:
Add an integration/regression playtest around improvised lore becoming queryable canon.

Use a minimal module/campaign fixture or test harness. The test does not need to recreate the stale campaign from the original run.

Scenario pattern:
1. Player asks a local NPC what is wrong.
2. DM introduces a consequential local hook:
   - missing charcoal cart / missing worker
   - returned mule or equivalent evidence
   - damage at a gate or road
   - rumors about danger nearby
3. DM records those facts as campaign overlay lore with truth statuses.
4. Player later asks villagers what is known and rumored.
5. DM retrieves the overlay lore and answers without audit rejection.
6. Decorative details from the original scene are not queryable unless deliberately promoted.

Acceptance criteria:
- Test fails if the DM asserts the hook without recording it or querying existing support.
- Test fails if failed world_query calls are treated as support.
- Test passes when current-turn recorded lore supports the initial hook.
- Test passes when later world_query retrieves the overlay lore.
- Test verifies rumor truth status is respected.
close_reason: Implemented campaign overlay canon, truth-statused lore recording, world_query retrieval/search, audit/prompt guidance, docs, and regression coverage.

title: Teach the DM when to promote improvised lore
description:
Update DM runtime prompts/tool instructions to guide lore promotion.

The DM should understand when to record consequential lore and when to leave description as prose.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prompt/tool instructions define consequential lore:
  - facts that affect player choices
  - facts that create hooks
  - facts that define NPC knowledge or motives
  - facts that describe evidence/clues
  - facts that may need to be recalled later
  - consequences of player actions
- Prompt/tool instructions define decorative color:
  - sensory details
  - mood
  - incidental gestures
  - mundane props
  - non-recurring background detail
- Instructions warn against promoting every descriptive flourish.
- Instructions warn against using overlay lore to contradict module canon unless explicitly recording a consequence, reveal, or override with appropriate source/truth status.
- Examples include:
  - promote: Old Renn's mule returned alone
  - promote: axe-cuts on the north gate
  - promote: villagers may pay for investigation
  - do not promote: chipped cup
  - do not promote: damp wool smell
close_reason: Implemented campaign overlay canon, truth-statused lore recording, world_query retrieval/search, audit/prompt guidance, docs, and regression coverage.

title: Update audit rules for recorded lore and failed tool calls
description:
Update mechanics/world audit semantics for improvised lore promotion.

The auditor should accept factual assertions when supported by successful canonical evidence, including current-turn campaign-overlay recording. It must not treat failed tool calls as evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Failed tool calls with ok:false never support factual assertions.
- A successful record_world_fact/record_lore call in the same turn can support use of that newly introduced consequential fact.
- A successful world_query result can support assertions from module canon, campaign state, or campaign overlay lore.
- A recorded rumor supports "NPCs say/believe/report X" but does not support "X is true" unless truthStatus supports truth.
- The audit distinguishes:
  - established fact
  - attributed rumor/belief
  - scene-local continuity
  - unsupported invention
- Retry guidance tells the DM:
  - do not rely on failed world_query results
  - if introducing a consequential new detail, record it before treating it as established
  - if not recording it, phrase it as tentative/color or keep it non-consequential
- Regression tests cover the Hearthmere / Old Renn pattern:
  - first turn records missing-cart rumors/evidence
  - later turn can discuss them via world_query without rejection
close_reason: Implemented campaign overlay canon, truth-statused lore recording, world_query retrieval/search, audit/prompt guidance, docs, and regression coverage.

title: Make queryable world and overlay records discoverable
description:
Improve discoverability of queryable world/campaign records for the DM.

The playtest showed that asking the model to query exact records is brittle when it does not know valid IDs. Even with a fresh campaign, overlay lore will make this more important because newly introduced subjects may not have pre-authored module IDs.

This does not need to become broad semantic search in the first pass, but the DM needs a reliable way to discover relevant records.

Acceptance criteria:
- Provide a compact index/search path for world_query or a separate world_search-style operation.
- The DM can discover queryable records by natural-ish subject terms such as:
  - "north gate"
  - "Old Renn"
  - "missing cart"
  - "rumors north of Hearthmere"
- Search/discovery results include record IDs/types suitable for follow-up world_query calls.
- Results distinguish module canon from campaign overlay lore.
- Tests cover lookup/discovery for newly recorded overlay lore.

title: Return campaign overlay lore from world_query
description:
Update world_query so campaign overlay lore is returned alongside module canon.

The DM needs to be able to retrieve improvised lore after it has been promoted. Query results should make the source/tier clear so the model and auditor know whether a result came from module canon, campaign state, overlay lore, or recent scene context.

Acceptance criteria:
- world_query can return campaign overlay lore records relevant to the query.
- Query results include canon tier/source metadata.
- Module canon and overlay lore are not conflated.
- Overlay lore can be queried by:
  - location
  - NPC
  - subject
  - tags/kind
  - recent/current scene relevance where appropriate
- If module canon and overlay lore conflict, results expose that conflict rather than silently choosing one.
- Tests cover retrieving:
  - Old Renn missing-cart style hook
  - north-gate evidence style clue
  - local rumor/belief
  - decorative color not present because it was never promoted

title: Add DM tool to record consequential improvised lore
description:
Add a constrained DM tool for promoting consequential improvised lore into campaign overlay state.

The DM should not be forced to pre-author every detail in a module, but when it introduces a consequential fact that may affect future play, it must record that fact.

Possible tool names:
- record_world_fact
- record_lore
- promote_lore

The exact name is implementation-defined, but the tool must communicate intent clearly.

The tool should require constrained fields rather than accepting arbitrary unstructured memory.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a tool callable by the DM runtime to record campaign overlay lore.
- The tool validates required fields:
  - kind
  - subject or subjectId
  - fact text
  - truthStatus
  - source
  - scope
  - visibility
- The tool rejects or discourages decorative scene color unless it is promoted because the player interacted with it or it became consequential.
- The tool returns evidence that can be included in the mechanics/world audit for the same turn.
- Tests cover:
  - recording a rumor
  - recording observed evidence
  - recording an NPC detail
  - rejecting malformed records
  - preserving player-visible vs DM-only distinction

title: Add typed campaign overlay lore records
description:
Add campaign overlay lore records to campaign state/storage.

These records capture consequential improvised facts created during play. They must be queryable and auditable, but should not replace read-only module canon.

Suggested shape, adjust during implementation:

WorldFact:
- id
- kind: rumor | clue | npc_detail | location_detail | quest_hook | threat_report | scene_consequence | player_created_detail | other
- subjectId or subjectText
- locationId optional
- npcId optional
- factionId optional
- text/fact
- truthStatus
- source: dm_improvised | player_declared | module_derived | tool_result | consequence
- scope: scene | session | campaign
- visibility: player_visible | dm_only | mixed
- introducedAtTurnId/sessionId
- supersedes/invalidates optional
- tags optional

Acceptance criteria:
- Campaign overlay lore has a typed schema.
- Records can be persisted in campaign state/checkpoints.
- Records are append-friendly and auditable.
- Records can be invalidated or superseded without destructive rewriting.
- Records can distinguish player-visible knowledge from DM-only truth.
- Tests cover serialization/deserialization and checkpoint persistence.

title: Define truth status for rumors, reports, observations, and confirmed facts
description:
Define truth-status semantics for campaign overlay lore.

The system needs to record that something was said, believed, observed, reported, confirmed, disproven, or lied about without collapsing all of those into "true".

Acceptance criteria:
- Define a constrained truth-status vocabulary.
- Include at least:
  - true or confirmed
  - false or disproven
  - unknown
  - rumored
  - reported
  - observed
  - believed
  - lie
  - exaggeration
- Explain the difference between:
  - "Old Renn's mule returned alone" as reported/observed evidence
  - "Old Renn was taken by goblins" as rumor/belief unless confirmed
- Define whether truth status is player-visible, DM-only, or can have separate public/private values.
- Define how truth status changes over time when play confirms or disproves a rumor.
- Include audit rules for truth status:
  - a recorded rumor supports "NPCs say X"
  - it does not support "X is true" unless separately confirmed
close_reason: Implemented campaign overlay canon, truth-statused lore recording, world_query retrieval/search, audit/prompt guidance, docs, and regression coverage.

title: Define canon tiers for module, campaign, overlay, scene, and color
description:
Define the canon-tier model for Eshyra adventure play.

The goal is to let adventure modules remain authoritative without forcing the DM to railroad or making every useful improvisation disappear after the turn.

Document the tiers:
- Module canon: adventure-module authored content; read-only during play.
- Campaign state: deterministic state changes such as inventory, flags, clocks, quest progress, location, and relationship state.
- Campaign overlay lore: consequential improvised facts introduced during play and intentionally persisted.
- Scene facts: short-lived facts established in the current scene/session, usable for local continuity but not necessarily long-term canon.
- Decorative color: ordinary descriptive prose that should not be stored or relied on later.
- Rumor/belief: attributed information that is canonically known to have been said/believed, without asserting it is true.

Acceptance criteria:
- A design note or ADR records the canon tiers.
- The document explains what each tier is allowed to support during mechanics/world audit.
- The document gives examples from the Hearthmere playtest:
  - module canon vs improvised hook
  - Old Renn / mule / axe-cuts / drag marks as campaign overlay lore
  - chipped cup / damp wool / rough wool clothing as decorative color
- The design explicitly says not every DM sentence becomes canon.
- The design explicitly says module canon remains authoritative and campaign overlay should not silently rewrite module facts.
close_reason: Implemented campaign overlay canon, truth-statused lore recording, world_query retrieval/search, audit/prompt guidance, docs, and regression coverage.

title: Add D&D level-1 equipment and proficiency choice flow
description:

title: Decide whether character creation recipe architecture needs an ADR
description:
Decide whether the character creation architecture should be recorded as a formal ADR after the design doc lands.

Candidate durable decisions
- Eshyra uses one shared character creation CLI shell with rule-pack-specific creation recipes.
- D&D 5e SRD is the first recipe.
- Recipe implementations use generated runtime rules packs as truth.
- Legacy SRD_CATALOG is retired.
- The D&D recipe supports both Concept-first and Ability-first creation modes.

Acceptance criteria
- Either add an ADR recording these decisions, or update the design doc with a clear note explaining why an ADR is deferred.
- Do not block initial implementation work if the design doc already gives agents enough direction.

title: Invoke adventure module selector for new sessions at CLI session start
description:
Split from eshyra-w8f2 (which now implements only the replay-on-resume half).

## Context
eshyra-w8f2 asked for two session-start branches: (1) replay the DM's last output when resuming an existing campaign, and (2) invoke an adventure module selector when there is no prior DM output (a fresh campaign). Branch (1) is implemented and merged. Branch (2) was deferred because eh54 (adventure module support) landed module loading, binding (startAdventureRun), and audit, but never a *selector* — nothing lists installed adventure modules under <root>/adventure-modules/ and lets the player pick one, and nothing is wired into the CLI session-start path. The current new-campaign flow (resolveCampaign in packages/cli/src/playSession.ts) just auto-forks from deps.pack with no choice.

## What needs to be done
1. Build a module selector: enumerate installed adventure modules (adventureModulesDir(root), each holding adventure-module.json; load via loadAdventureModuleFromDir), present them, and accept a player choice through the CliIO seam.
2. Wire it into the new-session branch: in playSession.ts launch(), the 'start_new' case where state.lastDmOutput === undefined (brand-new campaign, no prior DM output) should invoke the selector and bind the chosen module to the campaign via startAdventureRun, instead of (or alongside) the current auto-fork from deps.pack.
3. Handle the empty/none case (no installed modules) gracefully — fall back to current behavior.
4. Tests for the selector and the new-session-with-selector path.

## Pointers
- Seam already in place: playSession.ts renderResumeRecap() documents this deferral; the 'start_new' + undefined lastDmOutput branch is the hook point.
- Existing infra: packages/core/src/campaign/adventureRun.ts (startAdventureRun, listAdventureRuns), packages/cli/src/adventures.ts (makeModuleResolver pattern, adventureModuleDirName, loadAdventureModuleFromDir), packages/cli/src/dataRoot.ts (adventureModulesDir).
close_reason: Implemented and merged in PR #280 (squashed to main as 59ad611): adventure-module selector at fresh-campaign session start, plus the renderResumeRecap comment fix and the '1abc' parse hardening.

title: Stop requiring memory_drilldown for inventory reads when state snapshot is sufficient
description:
Discovered during the eshyra-eh54 adventure-module/equipment playtest.

The read-only turn 'What equipment do I have?' was handled correctly by the DM — it answered from the current (empty) inventory with NO mutation — but an audit apparently required a memory_drilldown call for inventory/equipment state and produced a false-positive rejection.

When the bounded current game-state context already contains the inventory/equipment state, the auditor should NOT require memory_drilldown just because the player asked about inventory. Drilldown should only be required when the answer depends on absent / archived / older state not present in the current snapshot.
design:
Investigate where the auditor decides a turn 'missing required tool(s)' that includes memory_drilldown for inventory/equipment questions (turnAuditor.ts buildAuditSystemPrompt / required-call logic, and the bounded state context fed to the auditor). The audit should treat inventory/equipment questions as answerable from the current state snapshot when that snapshot includes the inventory state. Preserve the requirement to drill down when the question depends on data NOT in the current bounded context (archived/older/absent state). Confirm the bounded context actually carries inventory state to both the DM and the auditor; if it does not, that gap is part of this fix.

Reference tool: packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolMemoryDrilldown.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- An empty-inventory answer with no mutation is ACCEPTED when the current state snapshot says inventory is empty (no memory_drilldown required).
- The audit still REJECTS unsupported inventory claims that are not present in current state or tool evidence.
- memory_drilldown is still required when the answer depends on state absent from the current bounded context.
- Regression test covers the exact 'What equipment do I have?' turn against an empty inventory, asserting acceptance without a required drilldown.
notes:
Likely files: packages/core/src/orchestrator/turnAuditor.ts (required-tool logic, buildAuditSystemPrompt, buildAuditUserMessage), packages/core/src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts (bounded state context assembly fed to auditor), packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolMemoryDrilldown.ts. Tests: packages/core/test/turnAuditor.test.ts, packages/core/test/orchestrator.test.ts, packages/core/test/inventoryQueryGuard.test.ts (query-vs-action discrimination already exists here). Related: eshyra-hlte (same auditor evidence/decision surface). Discovered-from: eshyra-eh54 equipment playtest.
RULES-PACK RECONCILIATION (re: eshyra-t2ra / ADR 0013): This false-positive audit rejection is INDEPENDENT of the placeholder/generated SRD pack discovery. Inventory read-only questions should be answerable from the current campaign/session state when that state is bounded and present; the audit must not require memory_drilldown merely because the player asked about equipment if the current state snapshot already establishes inventory state. This bead does NOT depend on generated SRD runtime adoption (eshyra-t2ra) and remains independently workable.
close_reason: Passed the current bounded state snapshot to the turn auditor, made empty inventory explicit to the DM, and added regression coverage for accepting empty-inventory reads without memory_drilldown while preserving rejection policy for unsupported or absent-state claims.

title: Reconcile adventure rulesRef resolution against the shipped SRD rules pack
description: The adventure module rulesRef convention is <kind>:<bareKey> (e.g. creature:goblin -> looks up key 'goblin'), per references.ts examples and the loader tests. But the SHIPPED generated SRD pack (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json) uses kind-prefixed record keys (e.g. 'creature:goblin', 'magic-item:potion-of-healing'), and the in-code DND5E_SRD_RULES_PACK stub uses yet another form ('monster:goblin'). As a result, validateAdventureModuleReferences for The Hollow Beneath Emberfall (eshyra-eh54.7.2) does NOT resolve against the real SRD stack today (verified empirically). The eh54.7.3 smoke path proves content/state/runtime/persistence connect (rulesRefs are carried as strings into the bounded slice and do not require resolution), but real mechanical resolution of encounter creatures and treasure items needs the key formats reconciled. Decide the canonical rulesRef<->record-key mapping (normalize on lookup, or fix the importer/convention) and add a test resolving The Hollow Beneath Emberfall's rulesRefs against the real resolved SRD stack.
design: Canonical mapping: a module rulesRef IS the canonical rules-pack record key, both of the form <kind>:<bareKey> (e.g. creature:goblin). This already matches the generated SRD pack keys AND every other in-system cross-reference (recordsByKey, srdAudit data.tableRefs / SRD_5_1_SPELL_TABLE_OWNERS, lookup ambiguous candidateKeys all use full kind-prefixed keys). The bug was solely in adventure/references.ts assertRulesRef, which split off the <kind> prefix and looked up the BARE key (goblin) -> missed the real pack's creature:goblin. Fix: extract the kind prefix only to validate it against expectedKinds, then look up by the FULL ref (= record key). No importer change, no pack regeneration, no generated-data edit. Tests: the two fake bare-key test packs (adventureModuleLoad.test.ts, hollowBeneathEmberfall.test.ts) misrepresented the convention; fixed. Added genuine resolution of The Hollow Beneath Emberfall against the REAL bundled SRD stack (resolveRulesStack({base: getBundledDnd5eSrdPack()})).
notes: Implemented and pushed on branch eshyra-8bit; PR #275 (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/275) open for review. Fix: assertRulesRef looks up by the full kind-prefixed ref (= canonical record key) instead of the bare key. Verified the new real-SRD-stack test fails against the pre-fix lookup (regression guard). Full verify:worktree green (2278 passed). Handoff stops at open PR per AGENTS.md; close on merge.
close_reason: Merged via PR #275 (squash). assertRulesRef now resolves rulesRefs by the full kind-prefixed key against the real bundled SRD stack; regression test added.

title: Format late provider ConfigError from gameplay client construction
description:
Problem
PR #255 added provider/auth selection for claude-sub, codex-sub, anthropic-api, and openai-api. The normal provider-selection path is good, but openai-api can now resolve successfully during config loading and then throw a ConfigError later during gameplay client construction.

Current suspected issue
loadConfig can accept an environment where only OPENAI_API_KEY is present and resolve provider/auth as openai-api.

makeGameplayClient then throws a ConfigError because the OpenAI native gameplay adapter is intentionally not implemented yet, with a useful message referencing the future follow-up bead eshyra-fxxf.

However, runPlaySubcommand and runDemoSubcommand appear to format ConfigError only around config loading. Later ConfigError thrown by buildPlayDeps / makeGameplayClient may bypass the normal formatConfigError path and surface as an unhandled exception or stack trace.

Why this matters
A user with only OPENAI_API_KEY set should get a clean actionable CLI error saying openai-api is recognized but not implemented yet. They should not see an unhandled stack trace, and the message should not imply that Eshyra silently fell back to billable API behavior.

Relevant PR
- PR #255: provider/auth selection for subscription and API providers

Likely files
- packages/cli/src/play.ts
- packages/cli/src/demo.ts
- packages/cli/src/providerClients.ts
- CLI tests around play/demo config error handling

Requested fix
Ensure ConfigError thrown after loadConfig, especially from makeGameplayClient(openai-api), is caught and formatted consistently in both:
- eshyra play
- eshyra demo

Use the existing formatConfigError path if appropriate, or equivalent output with the same UX standard.

Acceptance criteria
- With only OPENAI_API_KEY set, `eshyra play` exits 1 without a stack trace.
- With only OPENAI_API_KEY set, `eshyra demo` exits 1 without a stack trace.
- The error message includes openai-api.
- The error message references that OpenAI native gameplay support is not implemented yet and points to eshyra-fxxf if that is the existing intended follow-up.
- The error message does not imply subscription/provider fallback and does not imply hidden API billing fallback.
- Existing claude-sub, codex-sub, and anthropic-api selection tests still pass.
- Add regression tests for the late ConfigError path rather than only testing loadConfig.
- Run the normal verification command before opening the PR, preferably:
    npm run verify:worktree
close_reason: Caught late ConfigError from play/demo dependency construction and added openai-api regression coverage.

title: Prevent read-only inventory questions from mutating equipment
description:
Problem
In session-mqkis411-rlsh20, the player asked "What am I equipped with?" This is naturally a read/query intent. The model responded by executing inventory mutation tools to give the character starting equipment. That is unsafe: asking what is currently recorded should not silently create or select equipment.

This is related to the broader guided session-zero work, but it is a narrower runtime safety rule:
- inventory/status queries should inspect current state
- equipment selection or item grants should require an explicit character-creation/session-zero step or explicit player confirmation

Goal
Separate read-only character/inventory inspection from inventory mutation so the DM model cannot silently populate equipment in response to a query.

Acceptance Criteria
- A player asking what they are equipped with does not cause give_item or other inventory mutation tools unless the player has explicitly entered/confirmed an equipment-selection flow.
- If no equipment is recorded, the answer should say so clearly and offer to begin/continue starting-equipment selection.
- If starting equipment is incomplete, the system should surface that as session-zero/character setup debt rather than silently patching it.
- Add tests for:
  1. "What am I equipped with?" with empty inventory does not call mutating tools
  2. explicit equipment-selection/confirmation path may call mutating tools
  3. existing inventory can be reported without mutation
- The rule should not depend only on prompt wording if a deterministic permission/tool-gating mechanism is practical.
- This bead may integrate with eshyra-4jiu, but should stay focused on preventing query-triggered mutation.

Non-goals
- Do not fully redesign character creation.
- Do not implement the complete guided session-zero flow.
- Do not require an extra model call solely to classify every ordinary inventory query unless no deterministic/gating approach is feasible.
close_reason: Already completed by eshyra-4ia4 in commit c202f55 (#246): explicit-action inventory tool gating, auditor enforcement, empty/existing inventory query behavior, valid action behavior, and regression coverage. Focused tests pass on 2026-06-21.

title: Lazy-load the Claude Agent SDK adapter so api/codex installer editions run
description: Gate for ADR 0011 api/codex editions (eshyra-7zhm). The Codex adapter (eshyra-jl8n) already imports its SDK lazily, so @eshyra/core loads without the Codex binary. The Claude adapters do NOT: agentSdkClient.ts and agentSdkMcpClient.ts statically import '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk' at module scope, and index.ts re-exports them eagerly. So the api and codex editions (which prune the ~223MB Claude binary) build at the correct small size (api=166MB vs 423MB) but CRASH at startup / fail the release validator's no-config execution smoke with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Work: (1) make agentSdkClient.ts + agentSdkMcpClient.ts dynamic-import('@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk') inside complete() (mirror codexSdkMcpClient.ts), throwing a clear edition error if absent; (2) move @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk to optionalDependencies in packages/core/package.json; (3) keep the existing vi.mock-based tests green (vi.mock intercepts dynamic import too); (4) re-enable the release validator's no-config execution smoke for ALL editions by removing the editionRunsNoConfigSmoke gate in validate-release-artifact.mjs. Verifies the editions feature end-to-end: every edition both builds lean AND runs.
close_reason: Merged in PR #254. Claude Agent SDK adapters now import the SDK lazily via agentSdkLoader.ts (types-only at module scope); claude-agent-sdk moved to optionalDependencies; validator's deferral gate removed. Proven: api (166MB) + codex (450MB) editions pass the full no-config execution smoke with the Claude SDK pruned.

title: Wire CLI/config provider selection for the Codex (openai) gameplay adapter
description: Follow-up to eshyra-jl8n. To make 'eshyra play' actually select Codex, wire: (1) provider-aware auth resolution (a Codex/OpenAI subscription path; no API-key fallback per ADR 0010), (2) drop/extend the provider==='anthropic' assertion so the openai provider instantiates CodexSdkMcpModelClient in buildPlayDeps, (3) route the auditor through the same Codex auth when the DM is Codex, (4) assertGameplayCapable on the Codex adapter at startup. title: Replay DM's last output on session resume; invoke module selector for new sessions
description:
## Why this issue exists

When a player reconnects to an existing campaign, they need immediate context — what the DM last said — before issuing their next command. Without this, the player must scroll back through history or re-read state manually, which breaks immersion and creates friction at every session boundary.

If no previous session exists (i.e. the campaign has no prior DM output), the player has nothing to replay, so the session-start flow should instead invoke the adventure module selector to begin a new adventure.

## What needs to be done

1. On CLI session start, check whether the active campaign has a recorded prior DM response (last turn's assistant message).
2. If one exists, print it to the terminal before accepting the first player input, framed clearly as a recap (e.g. a 'Resuming session…' header followed by the DM's last message).
3. If no prior DM response exists (fresh campaign, no turns yet), invoke the adventure module selector flow instead of replaying.
4. Ensure this behaviour is gated by a clean session-start signal — it should fire once per `eshyra play` invocation, not on every turn.
5. Add tests covering both branches: replay path and module-selector fallback path.
notes: Depends on eshyra-eh54 (Add first-class adventure module support) — specifically the adventure module selector UI. The module-selector fallback path at session start requires that adventure modules are a first-class concept with a working selection flow. This bead cannot be implemented until eh54 (or its selector sub-task) is complete and the module selector is callable from the CLI session-start path.
close_reason: Both session-start branches complete and merged: replay-on-resume (PR #277, commit 8c8e851) and the fresh-campaign module selector (eshyra-47ob, PR #280, commit 59ad611).

Module-selector fallback for fresh campaigns deferred to eshyra-47ob (blocks this bead). Keep w8f2 open until 47ob lands and the selector is wired into the start_new + no-prior-DM-output branch.

title: Add per-turn model/tool timing diagnostics
description:
Problem
PR #243 added aggregate model usage tracking, but the report only shows whole model-call durations by purpose/model. In session-mqkis411-rlsh20, total wall-clock time was higher than expected. The aggregate usage report showed:

- gameplay_turn: 3 calls, 132.5s, 1 failed
- turn_audit: 2 calls, 34.9s

This proves audit was not the dominant cost, but it does not explain how much gameplay_turn time was:
- model thinking
- Claude Agent SDK / harness overhead
- MCP tool execution
- retry wait time
- provider/session-limit failure delay
- orchestration overhead

Goal
Add per-turn timing diagnostics that make a slow turn explainable without exposing prompt or response content.

Scope
Instrument the model/tool execution path to produce a structural timing timeline for each player turn. The timeline should be safe to include in non-sensitive debug logs and/or usage diagnostics.

Capture at least:
- player turn id / session id / campaign id when available
- turn attempt number
- model-call purpose: gameplay_turn, turn_audit, retry, session_recap, arc_rollup, etc.
- model name and adapter capability metadata when available
- model call start/end/duration
- audit start/end/duration
- retry start/end/duration
- provider failure timing
- MCP/native tool call start/end/duration
- tool name
- tool source/transport, such as native-mcp/api-native/local
- whether each tool call was read-only, mutating, staged, committed, or rolled back when that metadata exists
- final turn outcome: accepted, rejected_then_retried, failed_before_apply, failed_after_reject, provider_limit, provider_error, audit_error, etc.

Acceptance Criteria
- A slow turn can be decomposed into model time, audit time, retry time, and tool time using debug/usage output.
- MCP tool calls executed inside the Agent SDK loop are timed individually as much as the current adapter architecture allows.
- Retry attempts are distinguishable from initial gameplay_turn attempts.
- Provider/session-limit failures record elapsed time before failure.
- The diagnostics do not write prompt text, response text, or campaign-private prose into the usage DB.
- Add tests for:
  1. successful turn with primary model + audit produces separate timing spans
  2. rejected candidate + retry produces distinct attempt spans
  3. provider-limit failure records failed attempt duration and reason category
  4. MCP tool calls are included with per-tool duration and tool name
- Existing eshyra usage output either includes a concise timing breakdown or gains a flag such as --timeline / --details for detailed per-turn timing.
- Best-effort diagnostics must not prevent gameplay startup or turn execution if timing persistence fails.

Non-goals
- Do not estimate token counts when the provider does not expose them.
- Do not record prompt/response bodies.
- Do not require an additional model call just to classify timing.
- Do not solve transactional tool rollback here, except to display staged/committed/rolled-back metadata if available from that work.

Implementation Notes
The desired output should make questions like these answerable:
- Was this slow because the primary model thought for 45 seconds?
- Was it slow because the auditor ran repeatedly?
- Was it slow because MCP tools were executed one at a time through the Agent SDK harness?
- Did a retry spend 50 seconds before returning a session-limit error?
- How much elapsed time did tool execution add compared to model/audit time?

Example conceptual timeline:
turn session-mqkis411-rlsh20 / input #2
  attempt 1 gameplay_turn claude-opus-4-8: 38.4s rejected
    tool lookup_rules: 1.2s read-only
    tool give_item: 0.8s mutating staged
    tool give_item: 0.7s mutating staged
  audit claude-haiku-4-5: 18.3s reject
  attempt 2 retry claude-opus-4-8: 52.3s failed provider_limit
  outcome failed_before_apply
notes: Implemented on branch eshyra-17ng-turn-timing-diagnostics; PR #247 (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/247) open for review. Adds tool/model/outcome timing spans + 'eshyra usage --timeline'. Awaiting review/merge.
close_reason: Merged via PR #247 (squash). Per-turn model/tool timing diagnostics + 'eshyra usage --timeline'.

- Existing eshyra usage output either includes a concise timing breakdown or gains a flag such as --timeline / --details for detailed per-turn timing.
- Best-effort diagnostics must not prevent gameplay startup or turn execution if timing persistence fails.

Non-goals
- Do not estimate token counts when the provider does not expose them.
- Do not record prompt/response bodies.
- Do not require an additional model call just to classify timing.
- Do not solve transactional tool rollback here, except to display staged/committed/rolled-back metadata if available from that work.

Implementation Notes
The desired output should make questions like these answerable:
- Was this slow because the primary model thought for 45 seconds?
- Was it slow because the auditor ran repeatedly?
- Was it slow because MCP tools were executed one at a time through the Agent SDK harness?
- Did a retry spend 50 seconds before returning a session-limit error?
- How much elapsed time did tool execution add compared to model/audit time?

Example conceptual timeline:
turn session-mqkis411-rlsh20 / input #2
  attempt 1 gameplay_turn claude-opus-4-8: 38.4s rejected
    tool lookup_rules: 1.2s read-only
    tool give_item: 0.8s mutating staged
    tool give_item: 0.7s mutating staged
  audit claude-haiku-4-5: 18.3s reject
  attempt 2 retry claude-opus-4-8: 52.3s failed provider_limit
  outcome failed_before_apply
close_reason: duplicate of 17ng

title: Prevent read-only inventory questions from mutating equipment
description:
Problem
In session-mqkis411-rlsh20, the player asked "What am I equipped with?" This is naturally a read/query intent. The model responded by executing inventory mutation tools to give the character starting equipment. That is unsafe: asking what is currently recorded should not silently create or select equipment.

This is related to the broader guided session-zero work, but it is a narrower runtime safety rule:
- inventory/status queries should inspect current state
- equipment selection or item grants should require an explicit character-creation/session-zero step or explicit player confirmation

Goal
Separate read-only character/inventory inspection from inventory mutation so the DM model cannot silently populate equipment in response to a query.

Acceptance Criteria
- A player asking what they are equipped with does not cause give_item or other inventory mutation tools unless the player has explicitly entered/confirmed an equipment-selection flow.
- If no equipment is recorded, the answer should say so clearly and offer to begin/continue starting-equipment selection.
- If starting equipment is incomplete, the system should surface that as session-zero/character setup debt rather than silently patching it.
- Add tests for:
  1. "What am I equipped with?" with empty inventory does not call mutating tools
  2. explicit equipment-selection/confirmation path may call mutating tools
  3. existing inventory can be reported without mutation
- The rule should not depend only on prompt wording if a deterministic permission/tool-gating mechanism is practical.
- This bead may integrate with eshyra-4jiu, but should stay focused on preventing query-triggered mutation.

Non-goals
- Do not fully redesign character creation.
- Do not implement the complete guided session-zero flow.
- Do not require an extra model call solely to classify every ordinary inventory query unless no deterministic/gating approach is feasible.
notes: Reviewer (PR #246) requested runtime enforcement: turn auditor must evaluate explicit-action intent for requiresExplicitAction tools and reject give_item/remove_item on read-only queries. Extending existing audit gate (no extra model call).
close_reason: Merged in PR #246: runtime auditor enforcement of requiresExplicitAction tools (give_item/remove_item rejected on read-only inventory queries).

title: Implement Codex SDK MCP subscription gameplay adapter
description:
Problem
Implement the first Codex subscription-backed gameplay adapter under the codified API-native vs agent-harness seam. This bead should wait until Codex usage is available again and the adapter seam ADR/refactor has landed.

Dependency
Depends on the model adapter seam ADR/refactor epic. Do not start until provider metadata, auth-mode selection, and tool-loop ownership are explicit enough to support a second agent-harness adapter.

Goal
Add a CodexModelClient / CodexHarnessModelClient using `@openai/codex-sdk` and Eshyra MCP tools.

Design Constraints
- This is a Codex SDK subscription adapter, not an OpenAI API adapter.
- It must use ChatGPT/Codex subscription auth for the local development/gameplay path.
- It must not use or silently fall back to OPENAI_API_KEY.
- It must not use fenced-text tool calls.
- It must expose Eshyra tools through MCP or another supported Codex-native mechanism.
- It must run in a sterile harness environment, not inside the Eshyra repo workspace.
- It should follow the seam and debug/capability conventions established by the Claude Agent SDK MCP reference adapter.
- Auditor/retry/recap calls made through this provider mode must remain subscription-backed unless the user explicitly selects API billing.

Scope
1. Build or reuse an Eshyra MCP stdio server exposing a minimal gameplay tool set, starting with `roll`.
2. Add a CodexModelClient / CodexHarnessModelClient using `@openai/codex-sdk`.
3. Launch Codex with a sterile environment:
   - temporary working directory, not the Eshyra repo
   - isolated Codex config/home if possible
   - no inherited AGENTS.md/project instructions
   - restrictive sandbox
   - no web/search/network unless explicitly needed
4. Configure only Eshyra MCP tools for gameplay.
5. Map Codex streamed MCP tool-call events into Eshyra debug/transcript records using the same provider-executed-call pattern as the Claude Agent SDK MCP adapter.
6. Delegate all gameplay tool semantics to Eshyra core.
7. Add deterministic tests for adapter configuration, capability metadata, auth isolation, event mapping, and MCP tool exposure.
8. Provide manual smoke-test commands for the user to run once Codex usage is available.

Acceptance Criteria
- Provider metadata reports subscription auth, Codex SDK transport, agent-harness turn-loop ownership, and MCP tool transport.
- Debug logs show `toolProtocolMode` or equivalent as `codex-mcp`, not fenced text.
- A manual smoke turn requiring a d20 roll causes Codex to invoke the Eshyra MCP `roll` tool.
- No Eshyra repo AGENTS.md/developer instructions are loaded into gameplay context.
- No non-Eshyra tools are available to gameplay, or unavoidable built-ins are documented and proven harmless.
- Failure to access subscription-backed Codex is reported clearly and does not fall back to API key or fenced text.

Non-goals
- Do not implement OpenAI API-native support here.
- Do not replace the Claude Agent SDK adapter.
- Do not remove fenced support repo-wide.
notes: Adapter component + in-process MCP server + offline tests + docs complete. PR #252 (feat/codex-adapter-jl8n). CLI/config provider selection split to eshyra-6ygw; lazy-Claude for editions split to eshyra-ern3. Verified: 2123 tests pass.
close_reason: Merged in PR #252. Codex SDK MCP adapter + in-process MCP server + offline tests + docs landed. Review non-blockers addressed (401/404 comment, namespace-tolerant call-id correlation). Follow-ups: eshyra-6ygw (CLI wiring), eshyra-ern3 (lazy Claude adapter).

title: Add Codex SDK MCP subscription gameplay provider
description:
Problem
Eshyra needs a second subscription-backed gameplay provider to spread development and gameplay costs. Codex SDK appears promising because it supports ChatGPT/Codex subscription auth, programmatic control, streamed events, and MCP server integration. - These are not interchangeable auth variants hidden behind one class.

- The Codex subscription adapter must not use fenced-text tool calls.

Goal
Implement a Codex subscription-backed gameplay provider using Codex SDK plus Eshyra MCP tools, after the adapter seam is codified and the Claude Agent SDK MCP adapter has established the reference agent-harness pattern.

Scope
