title: Codify API-native vs agent-harness model adapter seam
description:
Problem
Eshyra needs to support both clean API-key model adapters and subscription-backed agent-harness adapters.

The pure API approach is architecturally preferred: Eshyra owns prompt assembly, tool transport, tool execution, turn management, replay, diagnostics, and model-call lifecycle. However, API-key usage is likely too expensive for day-to-day development and may also be too expensive for normal gameplay. Subscription-backed adapters using Claude Code / Codex-style agent harnesses are therefore required for affordable development and probably affordable play.

Design Decision
Maintain separate adapters by vendor and auth/transport mode rather than pretending API-key and subscription-backed paths are equivalent.

Examples:
- Anthropic API-native adapter: API key, lower-level Anthropic Messages/tool API, Eshyra-managed tool loop.
- Anthropic Agent SDK adapter: Claude subscription/Claude Code transport, Agent SDK MCP tools, agent-harness-managed loop bridged into Eshyra.
- OpenAI API-native adapter: API key, lower-level OpenAI Responses/tool API, Eshyra-managed tool loop.
- Codex SDK adapter: ChatGPT/Codex subscription transport, Codex MCP tools, agent-harness-managed loop bridged into Eshyra.

PR #241 is the first concrete candidate implementation of the agent-harness mode, pending the turn-auditor/tool-obedience fix.

Explicit Tradeoff
We accept that tuning prompts, tool use, diagnostics, and turn management for subscription-backed agent harnesses may have unintended effects on pure API adapters that are not continuously live-tested, because API-key costs are prohibitive. Subscription-token usage is expected to be orders of magnitude cheaper in practice than equivalent API-billed usage. The codebase must reduce this risk through a clear model-call abstraction, capability declarations, deterministic tests, debug logs, and documentation, but we do not require expensive live API smoke tests for every change.

Auth Rule
Auth mode must be explicit and mutually exclusive. Subscription-backed adapters must not silently inherit or prefer API keys when a subscription/OAuth path is selected. If both ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are present, the selected provider mode must decide explicitly which one is used. Subscription mode must sanitize child SDK environments or fail fast if API-key precedence cannot be prevented.

Scope
1. Write an ADR documenting:
   - API-native adapters are the preferred clean architecture.
   - Subscription-backed agent-harness adapters are intentionally supported for affordability.
   - API-native and subscription-backed adapters are separate provider modes, not interchangeable auth variants hidden behind one class.
   - Fenced-text tool calling is not a supported gameplay protocol.
   - A provider is supported for gameplay only if its adapter can expose Eshyra tools through native API tools or harness-supported MCP/native tools.
   - Subscription gameplay calls, including primary DM calls, auditors, retries, and recaps, must stay on the subscription-backed adapter unless the user explicitly selects API billing.
   - The accepted testing/cost tradeoff: subscription paths will be exercised more often than API-key paths.
2. Update README/provider documentation with the same distinction in user-facing terms.
3. Refine the model-call abstraction so it uniformly represents both adapter families:
   - provider/vendor
   - auth mode: api-key vs subscription/harness
   - transport/client: Anthropic Messages, Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI API, Codex SDK, etc.
   - tool transport: api-native, agent-mcp, unsupported
   - turn loop owner: Eshyra-managed vs provider-harness-managed
   - capability flags for gameplay support
   - debug fields for provided tools, forwarded tools, observed/executed tool calls, auditor calls, and provider/harness errors
4. Use the finalized Claude Agent SDK MCP adapter from PR #241 as the reference agent-harness implementation once it both exposes tools and enforces required mechanical tool use.
5. Extract or document the reusable seam rather than reimplementing the Claude adapter.
6. Preserve or define the clean seam needed for future API-native adapters.
7. Create or update follow-up beads for:
   - Anthropic API-native adapter if not already present
   - OpenAI API-native adapter
   - Codex SDK MCP subscription adapter
   - removal/containment of any remaining fenced-text gameplay path

Acceptance Criteria
- ADR exists and captures the API-native vs agent-harness adapter decision and cost/testing tradeoff.
- README/provider docs describe supported provider modes and their tradeoffs.
- Model adapter interfaces or metadata make auth mode, transport, tool transport, and turn-loop ownership explicit.
- Released gameplay cannot silently proceed with tools provided but no native/MCP forwarded tools.
- Claude Agent SDK MCP path is the reference implementation for agent-harness adapters.
- Debug logs clearly distinguish API-native and agent-harness calls.
- Debug logs clearly distinguish primary model calls, auditor model calls, retries, and recap calls.
- Subscription-backed gameplay does not silently use API-billed calls for auditor/retry/recap work.
- Fenced-text tool calls are not presented as a supported gameplay fallback.
- Codex implementation is not included in this bead except as a documented follow-up.

Non-goals
- Do not implement the Codex adapter here.
- Do not implement every API-native provider here.
- Do not remove every fenced-text code path repo-wide unless trivial and in scope.
- Do not require live API-key smoke tests as a merge gate.
close_reason: Closed

title: Revisit starter adventure sourcing after module support
description:
Revisit the long-frozen starter-adventure sourcing work after Eshyra has a first-class module destination.

The old question of which starter adventure to use was premature because the project did not yet have a module schema, loader, campaign-owned binding/progress, or runtime integration. Once those exist, evaluate whether to keep using the first-party The Hollow Beneath Emberfall starter content, add a legally safe third-party sample, or convert an external adventure only as a compatibility exercise.
design:
Do not convert third-party adventure content until all of the following hold:
- the immutable adventure module source schema exists (eshyra-eh54.2),
- the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding and progress state exists (eshyra-eh54.4),
- the first-party Emberfall / The Hollow Beneath Emberfall path proves the architecture end to end (eshyra-eh54.7 and children),
- and licensing is explicitly reviewed.

This bead should be mostly decision and scoping. It may close or replace the old frozen starter-content bead if that bead's original premise is obsolete.
acceptance_criteria:
- The existing frozen starter-content bead is reviewed in light of the new adventure-module architecture.
- A recommendation is recorded: keep first-party The Hollow Beneath Emberfall only, add a legally safe third-party sample, or create a conversion/import experiment.
- Third-party adventure content stays blocked until the module source schema, the campaign-owned module binding/progress, and the first-party Emberfall path all exist, and licensing is explicitly reviewed.
- Legal/licensing constraints are explicitly considered before any third-party adventure content is added.
- The decision does not block the first-party hello-world module.
- Any follow-up beads are created with clear scope if third-party content is still desired.

title: Add adventure module progress audit output
description:
Add audit/debug output for active adventure modules and module progress.

Module support will be hard to debug if the model appears to forget the adventure, reveal secrets too early, repeat completed scenes, or ignore player-driven deviations. Add inspectable output that distinguishes the immutable source module, the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, the mutable progress/deviations, and the last bounded runtime context slice.
design:
Follow the spirit of the SRD audit/debug tooling: make invisible model/context behavior inspectable.

Output should clearly separate four things:
1. Immutable source module content (authored scenario).
2. Campaign-owned adventure run / module binding (which module is active, status, session ids).
3. Mutable progress and deviations (visited, revealed, completed, bypassed, claimed, active clocks, explicit deviations).
4. Last bounded runtime context slice supplied to the DM (eshyra-eh54.5).

Useful sections:
- Active adventure runs / module bindings
- Current module position
- Module progress
- Revealed vs unrevealed secrets
- Objectives
- Encounters
- Treasure/rewards
- Deviations from authored module
- Last runtime module context slice
acceptance_criteria:
- A debug or audit command can show active module ids and statuses for a campaign (from the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding).
- Output includes current or inferred module scene/location when available.
- Output includes visited locations, revealed secrets, completed objectives, encounter outcomes, claimed treasure, active clocks/threats, and recorded deviations.
- Output can show or capture the last bounded module context slice supplied to the DM runtime.
- Debug output clearly distinguishes immutable source module content, the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, mutable progress/deviations, and the last runtime context slice.
- Tests or snapshots cover representative debug output.
notes: Implemented; PR #266 open with green CI (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/266). Awaiting review/merge. Core adventureAudit.ts + CLI 'eshyra adventures' command. Unblocks eshyra-eh54.7.3.
close_reason: Merged via PR #266. Core adventureAudit.ts (buildCampaignAdventureAudit/formatCampaignAdventureAudit) separates source/binding/progress/runtime-slice; slice captured only for active runs. CLI 'eshyra adventures' command. Unblocks eshyra-eh54.7.3.

title: Remove fenced-text tool protocol from supported gameplay providers
description:
Problem
The released gameplay path relied on a custom fenced-text tool-call protocol even though modern model APIs provide native tool/function calling. The provider-neutral Eshyra tool abstraction was the right architecture, but allowing a custom fenced-text default made a model/provider appear supported before its adapter actually implemented native tool transport. This caused eshyra-eznk: Claude Opus could see no native tools and reported that gameplay tools were not actually present.

Decision
A model/provider is not considered supported for released gameplay unless its adapter implements native tool transport for Eshyra's provider-neutral tool definitions. Fenced-text tool calls must not be the default or fallback for any supported gameplay provider.

Scope
- Audit all model providers/adapters and identify any that still use or advertise fenced-text tool calls for gameplay.
- Remove fenced-text as the default gameplay protocol.
- Add explicit provider capability checks: gameplay startup must fail clearly if the selected model adapter cannot transport Eshyra tools natively.
- Update provider/model support docs to distinguish:
  - native-tool supported for gameplay
  - text-only/maintenance-only
  - unsupported until native tool transport is implemented
- Remove prompt instructions that teach supported native providers to emit fenced ```tool_call JSON.
- Keep any fenced parser only if it is explicitly legacy/test-only and unreachable from released gameplay; otherwise delete it.
- Ensure debug logging reports native vs unsupported accurately and never masks unsupported providers behind a fenced fallback.

Acceptance Criteria
- No released gameplay provider defaults to `toolProtocolMode: "fenced-text"`.
- Selecting a provider without native Eshyra tool transport fails before play begins with a clear actionable error.
- Tests cover provider capability enforcement.
- Tests prove supported gameplay providers must forward non-empty native tool definitions when `ModelCompleteInput.tools` is non-empty.
- Prompt snapshots or focused assertions prove native-supported gameplay prompts do not contain fenced tool-call instructions.
- Documentation explains that the core owns provider-neutral tool semantics while adapters own provider-native transport.
- Any remaining fenced-text code is either removed or explicitly marked legacy/test-only with tests proving it is not used by released gameplay.

Dependencies
- Should be started after eshyra-eznk lands, because eznk should establish the first working native AgentSDK/Anthropic gameplay path.
close_reason: Opened PR #249: buildSystemPrompt defaults to native protocol; new assertGameplayCapable startup gate (UnsupportedGameplayProviderError) wired into CLI for primary DM + auditor; fenced parser retained legacy/test-only and unreachable from released gameplay. Tests cover capability enforcement + native-default prompt. ADR 0010 updated. Full verify:worktree green (2093 pass).

title: Add explicit provider rate-limit handling for model turns
description:
Problem
Eshyra currently has generic model/provider failure handling: model turn failures roll back the turn savepoint and surface a generic "turn could not be completed" CLI message. That protects state, but rate-limit failures are not classified or explained distinctly. A rate-limited Claude/Anthropic token currently exercises only the generic failed-turn path.

Goal
Add explicit rate-limit classification and user-facing handling for model/provider calls, especially gameplay turns, without weakening rollback behavior or adding retry loops that burn quota.

Scope
- Classify provider/model rate-limit failures in the model adapter/error layer.
- Preserve the existing failed-turn rollback behavior: the player's last input must not be applied if the model call fails.
- Surface a clearer CLI message for rate limits, e.g. "Model provider rate limit reached. Try again later. Your last input was not applied."
- Keep provider details sanitized; do not print secrets or raw credential-bearing process/environment details.
- If the Claude Agent SDK exposes retry-after or structured status metadata, capture it in a safe internal diagnostic and optionally include a human-friendly wait hint.
- Do not implement automatic retries for normal gameplay turns unless bounded and explicitly justified. Avoid retry loops that consume more quota.
- Ensure the generic provider-failure path remains for non-rate-limit errors.

Implementation notes
Likely areas:
- packages/core/src/model/AgentSdkModelClient.ts or adjacent model error types
- packages/core/src/engine/turn.ts / runTurn failure handling
- packages/cli command path that prints failed-turn messages
- tests around fake model clients and CLI output

Acceptance criteria
- A fake/rate-limit-shaped model failure is classified as a rate-limit error.
- Gameplay turn failure due to rate limit rolls back the turn savepoint exactly like other model failures.
- CLI output clearly identifies rate limiting and states that the last input was not applied.
- Non-rate-limit provider failures still use the existing generic failed-turn behavior.
- Tests cover:
  - rate-limit classification from a representative Claude/Agent SDK failure shape;
  - failed-turn rollback with rate-limit error;
  - CLI user-facing message for rate limit;
  - secret sanitization / no credential leakage.
- Existing tests continue to pass.

Manual validation
With a known rate-limited Claude/OAuth/API token, run a fresh campaign and enter a simple player action. Confirm:
- Eshyra does not crash.
- The message says the provider is rate limited or equivalent.
- The failed player input is not persisted/applied.
- The user can quit cleanly.
close_reason: Rate-limit classification, CLI messaging, and session/usage exhaustion coverage all complete. PR #245 open.

title: CI-inject release version from git tag (artifact label + CORE_VERSION)
description: The release build labels artifacts and the CLI banner with version 0.0.0 because the root package.json has no version and CORE_VERSION is a hardcoded constant. Make the release build resolve the version from the pushed git tag (precedence: --version flag > ESHYRA_RELEASE_VERSION env > GITHUB_REF_NAME on tag, strip leading v > 0.0.0-dev), use it for the artifact name/README/metadata, and stamp it into the built core dist (placeholder replacement of the 0.0.0-dev sentinel, asserting exactly one occurrence) so the running CLI reports the true version. Enables tagging v0.1.0 to produce a correctly-versioned GitHub Release.

Version now resolves from git tag; verified release:build --version 0.1.0 -> eshyra-0.1.0 artifact + 'Eshyra — core v0.1.0' banner; check clean, 1850 tests pass. REMAINING: after PR merges to main, cut the release with 'git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0' on the merged commit (the injection code must be on main before the tag build runs). Keep open until v0.1.0 is tagged.

title: Add CI freeze guard for audited D&D SRD 5.1 artifact
description: The D&D SRD 5.1 rules-pack under packages/core/data/rules-packs/ is a completed, audited artifact generated by the one-time importer. It must never silently change in CI. We need a freeze guard — a CI check (checksum, snapshot, or content-hash test) that fails the build if the committed SRD artifact is modified without a deliberate, reviewed update. This prevents accidental parser or schema changes from silently corrupting the only licensed rules content we ship.
acceptance_criteria: A CI step or Vitest test computes a stable identity (file hash or structured snapshot) over the SRD rules-pack output. The check fails if the artifact diverges from the committed baseline. The baseline is updated only intentionally (e.g. a deliberate re-import with reviewer sign-off). The guard is documented so contributors know why the check exists and how to update it legitimately.

title: Build SRD source-region ledger coverage gate
description:
Implement a source-region ledger for the D&D 5e SRD importer audit artifacts. Repeated full audits keep finding new categories of missing prose after each targeted fix. The existing source-coverage artifact accounts well for headings, tables, stat blocks, and named records, but it can still hide prose-bearing regions behind broad statuses such as ignored:document-structure or ignored:record-group-heading. Recent examples included Variant rules, Equipment prose, Diseases/Poisons guidance, chapter/appendix intro prose, subclass overview prose, Magic Items A-Z, and Sample Traps.

Goal: enumerate every contiguous prose-bearing region in the vendored SRD PDF, not just table/stat-block/heading structures, and classify each region against generated records or explicit ignore reasons so missing prose is not discovered one category at a time.

The ledger should include regions such as chapter intro paragraphs; appendix intro paragraphs; prose under group headings; table prefaces and postfaces; prose between table rows and record entries; prose under subclass-family headings; prose under equipment/table group sections; prose before the first child record in a chapter/appendix; prose between adjacent generated record slices; and short one-paragraph explanations such as Magic Items A-Z and Sample Traps.

Each ledger entry should include at least: source page number or page range; heading path / source context; region type such as chapter-intro, appendix-intro, group-intro, record-body, table-preface, orphan-prose, or pure-structure; first source phrase; last source phrase; normalized body length or character count; classification such as record:<key>, child-of:<key>, intentionally-ignored:<reason>, pure-document-structure, or unrepresented; target record key when applicable; ignore reason when applicable; and confidence/guard notes when useful.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The audit bundle includes a machine-readable source-region ledger artifact, probably JSON, and optionally a readable markdown summary.
2. The ledger is generated deterministically from the vendored SRD PDF/text extraction.
3. The ledger distinguishes pure structural headings from headings that have body prose.
4. A generic ignored:document-structure or ignored:record-group-heading classification is not allowed for prose-bearing regions unless the ledger proves there is no body prose or provides a specific explicit ignore reason.
5. The audit fails if any prose-bearing region is classified as unrepresented.
6. The audit fails if any prose-bearing region is hidden behind a broad structural ignore without a specific reason.
7. Existing source-coverage artifact behavior can remain, but the new ledger must be strong enough to catch the categories missed by previous audits.
8. Tests include fixtures or SRD-slice examples for: a pure heading with no body prose; a chapter intro with prose before first child heading; a group heading with a short prose intro before records; a table heading with body prose and table rows; adjacent records with no orphan prose; and prose that should be intentionally ignored with an explicit reason.
9. Regression tests or sentinels cover previous missed classes: Variant rules; Equipment prose/item mechanics; Diseases/Poisons guidance; Feats intro; Conditions intro; Using Ability Scores intro; subclass-family overview prose; Appendix MM-A/MM-B intros; Magic Items A-Z; and Sample Traps.

Implementation guidance: prefer adding this as an audit artifact/gate rather than rewriting all parsers. The first version can be conservative and targeted if a fully generic PDF paragraph segmenter is too risky, but the model must be region-based rather than heading-only. Reuse existing page text / coordinate extraction where possible. Keep the ledger reviewable: concise first/last phrases are more useful than dumping entire prose bodies. Avoid brittle dependence on exact line wrapping when possible. Preserve deterministic behavior and source-hash/reproducibility guarantees. The ledger should help a human auditor answer: “What prose exists in the PDF, where did it go, and why is any of it ignored?”

Validation expected for implementation: focused unit tests for region extraction/classification; source-coverage/source-region artifact tests; generated audit bundle includes the new ledger; npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack; npm run audit-bundle:dnd5e-srd; npm run verify:worktree.

Out of scope: do not change record schemas unless needed and justified; do not import new SRD content as part of the ledger task unless a small sentinel fixture requires it; do not replace the existing source-coverage artifact wholesale unless that is clearly simpler and safe; do not use LLM reasoning as the source of truth because this must remain deterministic and reproducible.

title: Reconstruct apostrophes mis-mapped to space in PDF extraction
description: The SRD PDF font's ToUnicode maps certain apostrophe glyphs to a near-zero-width U+0020 space emitted as a standalone text item, so joinRowText produces 'monster s attack' instead of 'monster’s attack'. Found by PR #227 review (rule:conditions p358). Scope: exactly 7 cases across the PDF, all possessive/contraction at a word boundary — Land's Stride (p35), can't (p232), monster's (p358), Mare's/Lion's/cow's head (p361), Woman's face (p362). Distinguished from 1990 legitimate word-separator zero-width spaces (italic run boundaries like 'System Reference') by the next item beginning with an enclitic (s|t|d|m|re|ve|ll) at a word boundary. Fix in extract.ts joinRowText: when a near-zero-width ' ' item sits between a letter and an enclitic, emit U+2019. Count-neutral (text fidelity only). Add extract.test.ts coverage + rule:conditions sentinel 'a monster’s attack'.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #227 commit 6b2fd4f. extract.ts joinRowText reconstructs U+2019 between a letter and a possessive/contraction enclitic across an apostrophe-sized gap. 7 source-confirmed possessives recovered (monster's, can't, Land's Stride x2, Mare's/Lion's/cow's head, Woman's face); Ranger table cell now refs feature:ranger:lands-stride. joinRowText unit tests + rule:conditions sentinel added. verify:dnd5e-srd-pack + verify:worktree green.

Problem

Class records are structurally incomplete. The latest audit found that class records capture hit die, primary abilities, saves, armor proficiencies, and weapon proficiencies, but omit important SRD class data.

Missing or insufficiently structured areas

- class skill choices,
- tool proficiencies,
- starting equipment options,
- spellcasting progression,
- class progression tables,
- feature progression by level,
- class-specific resource columns such as Rage, Rage Damage, Sorcery Points, Pact Magic slots, and similar.

Known normalization issue

class:druid currently includes this as an armor proficiency token:

shields (druids will not wear armor or use shields made of metal)

The source parenthetical is real, but it should not be part of a normalized proficiency token. It should be represented as a note/restriction or equivalent structured field.

Task

Complete class and subclass progression/options modeling.

Implementation guidance

- Decide whether class progression tables are represented as table records, structured class progression data, or both.
- The source coverage gate must account for each class progression table either way.
- Do not duplicate feature bodies inside class/subclass descriptions when separate feature records exist.
- Normalize proficiencies while preserving source restrictions and notes.
- Preserve existing class, subclass, and feature ids where possible.

Regression cases

Add tests for:

- The Barbarian progression table.
- At least one spellcasting class progression table.
- Warlock Pact Magic progression.
- Fighter Action Surge repeated-use progression.
- Druid metal armor/shield restriction represented outside the normalized proficiency token.
- Subclass spell table or progression table such as Oath of Devotion Spells or Circle Spells.

Acceptance criteria

- Every class progression table is accounted for.
- Class records include or link to skill/tool/equipment/progression data.
- Druid proficiency normalization is fixed without losing the source restriction.
- Existing feature records remain source-backed and non-duplicated.

title: SRD: Barbarian Unarmored Defense feature swallowed — table row interleaves numeric columns into wrapped feature cell
description:
Discovered during eshyra-7tc. After eshyra-7tc recovered 13 of 14 Barbarian base-class features, the 14th — feature:barbarian:unarmored-defense (1st level) — is still missing from the generated pack. Its body heading 'Unarmored Defense' (h=13.92) is swallowed into feature:barbarian:rage's body instead of becoming its own record.

Root cause (separate from eshyra-7tc's slice-boundary fix): the SRD 5.1 Barbarian progression table's 1st-level row is extracted with the Rages/Rage Damage numeric columns interleaved BETWEEN the wrapped feature-cell words. Extracted lines:
  '1st +2 Rage, 2 +2'   (PROGRESSION_ROW; '2 +2' are the Rages=2, Rage Damage=+2 columns)
  'Unarmored'           (wrapped continuation of the Features cell)
  'Defense'
stitchProgressionRows() appends the continuation AFTER the numeric columns, yielding the row 'Rage, 2 +2 Unarmored Defense'. progressionFeaturesFromLine() strips only TRAILING numeric table cells (anchored at end), so the mid-cell '2 +2' survives and splitFeatureCell() returns ['Rage', '2 +2 Unarmored Defense']. The anchor key normalizes to '2 +2 unarmored defense', so the body 'Unarmored Defense' heading matches no anchor, has no level lead-in, and is swallowed into Rage.

This is a table-extraction/stitching root cause with broad blast radius (any class table whose feature cell wraps after interleaved numeric columns), held out of eshyra-7tc per docs/importer-fix-protocol.md hard-stop.

Expected behavior: emit feature:barbarian:unarmored-defense at level 1, and stop Rage's body at the 'Unarmored Defense' heading (Rage body should end at '...you can rage again.').

Likely files:
- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseFeatures.ts (stitchProgressionRows / progressionFeaturesFromLine / splitFeatureCell — strip interior numeric-column runs from a wrapped continuation segment without corrupting legitimate names).
- test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseFeatures.test.ts (add a fixture reproducing the interleaved-column wrap: '1st +2 Rage, 2 +2' / 'Unarmored' / 'Defense').
- test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts (bump feature 182 -> 183; add unarmored-defense to the class:barbarian projection; remove the 'Unarmored Defense intentionally absent' note).

Importer safety: follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md. Verify against SRD source; regenerate + verify:dnd5e-srd-pack.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #182: stitchProgressionRows strips the Barbarian table's trailing Rages/Rage Damage numeric columns before joining wrapped continuations, so feature:barbarian:unarmored-defense (1) emits and Rage no longer swallows it. Full 14-feature SRD Barbarian set now generated.

title: Implement native provider tool-use transport
description:
Problem
The current orchestrator executes model-requested tools only through the Eshyra fenced-text protocol parsed by protocol.ts. The ModelClient contract already has forward-looking toolCalls and stopReason fields, and PR #169 correctly guards against native tool-use responses being silently treated as final narration. That guard prevents canon corruption, but it also makes clear that native provider tool use is intentionally not wired yet.

This is acceptable as a bootstrap/runtime-neutral protocol, but it is probably not the ideal long-term path for primary frontier-model providers. Anthropic, OpenAI, and other providers increasingly tune model behavior around native tool-use channels. Staying fenced-only may leave reliability, schema conformance, and model/tool-use behavior on the table.

Goal
Implement native provider tool calls as an alternate transport into Eshyra's existing deterministic tool execution model.

Native tool calls must not replace Eshyra's canon rules. They should be normalized into the same internal tool-request path as fenced protocol calls, then validated and executed by the deterministic registry. The orchestrator should not care whether a tool request originated from a fenced block or a provider-native tool-use block once it has been normalized.

Desired architecture
Introduce or formalize an internal canonical representation for model-requested tool actions, roughly:

- source: fenced or native
- provider metadata when relevant
- provider/native tool-call id when relevant
- tool name
- raw arguments
- normalized/validated arguments
- trace/debug metadata

The orchestrator should process both fenced and native requests through the same execution path:

1. Receive model response.
2. Detect pending tool requests from native toolCalls and/or fenced text.
3. Normalize requests into the internal ToolRequest shape.
4. Validate against Eshyra's tool schemas.
5. Execute through the deterministic tool registry.
6. Persist/canonicalize state changes exactly as today.
7. Feed tool results back to the model in the provider-appropriate format.
8. Continue the loop until the model returns final narration with no pending tool calls.

Key invariant
Narration never mutates canon. Mechanical state changes only happen through validated deterministic tools, regardless of whether the tool request arrived through fenced text or native provider tool use.

Scope
- Add native tool-call ingestion to the model loop/orchestrator.
- Add provider-neutral internal normalization for native tool requests.
- Preserve the existing fenced protocol as a supported transport unless and until a separate migration decision removes it.
- Teach provider adapters to expose native tool calls only after the orchestrator can safely consume them.
- Preserve provider-specific ids and stop reasons for tracing/debugging, but do not leak provider-specific details into domain logic.
- Ensure final narration is accepted only when there are no pending native or fenced tool requests.
- Ensure native tool results are returned to the model in the correct provider-specific shape.
- Add tests using representative Anthropic-style and OpenAI-style native tool-call responses.

Out of scope
- Replacing the deterministic tool registry.
- Allowing model narration to directly change game state.
- Removing fenced protocol support.
- Changing game mechanics, rules-pack behavior, or domain schemas except where needed for tool-call normalization.
- Provider-specific behavior leaking into core domain/canon logic.
- Blindly forcing tool use for every model response; tool choice strategy should be considered carefully.

Acceptance criteria
- Native tool calls are normalized into the same internal execution path as fenced protocol calls.
- Native and fenced calls share validation, execution, persistence, replay, and error semantics.
- A response containing native tool calls is never treated as final narration.
- A response with stopReason/tool-use metadata but no consumable native calls fails loudly or is handled explicitly according to the provider contract.
- Tool-call arguments are validated against Eshyra-owned schemas before execution.
- Invalid native tool arguments produce the same class of recoverable or terminal orchestrator error as invalid fenced tool arguments.
- Provider-specific native ids are preserved where needed to send tool results back, but remain outside domain/canon state.
- Tests cover at least:
  - fenced-only tool request still works
  - native-only tool request works
  - mixed/native-plus-narration response does not skip tool execution
  - native tool-use stop reason without consumable calls fails loudly
  - malformed native arguments fail validation
  - final narration with no tool calls still works
  - representative Anthropic-style native tool response
  - representative OpenAI-style native tool response
- Replay/debug output remains understandable enough to audit what tool actions happened and why.
- Existing PR #169 guard remains valid until this epic wires native consumption; once native consumption is implemented, the guard is replaced by explicit native handling, not silent fallthrough.

Implementation notes
This should be approached as a transport-layer addition, not a change to the game-state authority model.

The preferred destination is:

provider native tool call
    -> provider adapter
    -> internal ToolRequest
    -> deterministic registry validation/execution
    -> canonical state mutation
    -> provider-appropriate tool result
    -> model loop continuation

The fenced protocol should become one supported encoding of ToolRequest, not the only mechanism by which the orchestrator understands tools.

The riskiest failure mode is accepting final narration after a native tool call was requested but not executed. Tests should make that failure mode difficult to reintroduce.
notes: Implemented native ModelClient tool-call normalization into the shared ToolRequest/ToolRegistry path; added structured native tool-result history, provider call-id and stop-reason tracing, schema validation before execution, and Anthropic/OpenAI-style orchestration coverage. Verified with npm run format, npm run check, npm run typecheck, and npm run test (1564 passed, 19 documented skips).
close_reason: Native tool calls now execute through the same validated deterministic registry path as fenced calls, with correlated provider result history and audit coverage.

title: SRD class parser: Paladin/Barbarian subclass features dropped or mis-attributed to the base class
description:
Two of the 12 SRD 5.1 subclasses emit ZERO granted feature records, while the other 10 emit theirs correctly. Distinct from loreweaver-6fw (callout-box bleed); this is a grantor-context / feature-anchor detection bug in parseFeatures (and a related subclass-description boundary issue in parseSubclasses).

Symptoms in the committed pack (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1):

1) Paladin Oath of Devotion. The Oath of Devotion subclass features are mis-attributed to the base class: feature:paladin:aura-of-devotion (L7), feature:paladin:purity-of-spirit (L15), and feature:paladin:holy-nimbus (L20) all carry data.source=class:paladin instead of subclass:oath-of-devotion. Zero features are attributed to subclass:oath-of-devotion. Separately, subclass:oath-of-devotion.description is truncated at the Oath Spells table caption (ends at the literal text Oath of Devotion Spells, ~1438 chars), so the rest of the subclass body is cut.

2) Barbarian Path of the Berserker. Its features (Frenzy L3, Mindless Rage L6, Intimidating Presence L10, Retaliation L14) are not emitted as feature records at all; the prose is folded into subclass:path-of-the-berserker.description instead.

feature-count-per-subclass audit: champion 5, circle-of-the-land 2, college-of-lore 2, draconic-bloodline 4, hunter 2, life-domain 4, oath-of-devotion 0, path-of-the-berserker 0, school-of-evocation 5, the-fiend 2, thief 3, way-of-the-open-hand 4.
design: Investigate why parseFeatures opens no subclass grantor context (or finds no feature anchors) for Oath of Devotion and Path of the Berserker specifically. Likely causes to check: (a) the subclass feature headings do not match a progression-table anchor and the leading level-clause fallback misfires for these two layouts; (b) for Paladin, the base-class progression table lists levels that capture the subclass features under the class grantor before currentSubclass is opened, or the Oath of Devotion heading is not matched exactly (whitespace/column-wrap) so currentSubclass stays null; (c) for Oath of Devotion, a repeated/near-duplicate Oath of Devotion line (e.g. the Oath Spells table caption Oath of Devotion Spells, or a running header) trips the subclass boundary so the description body ends early. Fix the detection/attribution so subclass features are keyed to their subclass with correct levels, without regressing the 10 currently-correct subclasses. Keep anchors structural (ADR 0007); do not author feature records by hand. Regenerate the canonical pack and review the diff.
acceptance_criteria: Every SRD 5.1 subclass emits its granted features as feature records keyed to subclass:<slug> with correct data.level. Oath of Devotion features (including Aura of Devotion L7, Purity of Spirit L15, Holy Nimbus L20) are attributed to subclass:oath-of-devotion, not class:paladin. Path of the Berserker features (Frenzy L3, Mindless Rage L6, Intimidating Presence L10, Retaliation L14) emit as feature records with correct levels. subclass:oath-of-devotion.description is no longer truncated at the Oath Spells table. The 10 currently-correct subclasses are unchanged. Regression assertions added; canonical pack regenerated; verify:dnd5e-srd-pack reports an exact match; full verify:worktree green.
notes:
Surfaced during loreweaver-6fw review. 6fw fixed only the trailing callout-box bleed; this attribution/boundary bug is independent and pre-existing.
Phase 1 evidence: real PDF extraction reproduces Path of the Berserker with zero feature records and Oath of Devotion truncated at 'Oath of Devotion Spells'; Aura of Devotion/Purity of Spirit/Holy Nimbus are attributed to class:Paladin. The classes slice excludes the opening Barbarian chapter line, while parseFeatures initializes currentClass=null, so all Barbarian/Berserker feature candidates are skipped. On p33 the Oath Spells table emits an exact body-font line 'Paladin' at h=8.88; both parsers treat any exact parent-class name as a chapter boundary, clearing subclass context and truncating the description. Actual class chapter headings are consistently h=25.92; subclass headings are h=13.92. Working later classes retain context because their chapter heading is present. The p8 bare 'Champion' table artifact at h=8.88 also shows parseFeatures must validate subclass parent context before defaulting the omitted first class to Barbarian.
Phase 2 comparison: parseSubclasses already defaults currentParent to Barbarian and guards subclass anchors by known parent, but parseFeatures does neither. All later real class chapter anchors are exact known names at h=25.92; the only false exact parent-name occurrence is Paladin at h=8.88 inside the oath-spells table. Hypothesis: initialize feature grantor context to Barbarian, accept subclass anchors only when their known parent equals currentClass, and on multi-tier input accept parent-class anchors only at the chapter-heading tier while retaining exact-text fallback for uniform/no-height fixtures.
Phase 3 confirmation: real-PDF-shaped RED fixtures fail exactly on the proposed context transitions. This confirms the omitted opening Barbarian anchor and body-font Paladin false boundary are the causal conditions, not downstream emit logic.

title: Class parser: Wizard 'Your Spellbook' prose bleeds into School of Evocation subclass/Overchannel feature

Overchannel is the 14th-level (last) School of Evocation feature on the Wizard page; the parser runs its body to the next heading it recognizes, which here is generic class prose rather than another feature/subclass, so the whole spellbook section bleeds in. The subclass body absorbs the same trailing prose. This is a class-parser scoping issue, distinct from the spellcasting-rules import (loreweaver-3hp). It pre-dates 3hp and was surfaced during 3hp review; 3hp only corrected the EXTRACTOR column-split that had scrambled this prose's word order (the bleed itself is unchanged and now reads in correct source order). parseFeatures/parseSubclasses (packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/) need a boundary that stops a subclass/feature body at the end of the subclass's own content (e.g. the next non-feature class section heading like 'Your Spellbook').

title: Fix SRD 5.1 magic-item column interleaving + Sword of Sharpness boundary (PR #150)
description:
PR #150 review found three contamination defects in the committed SRD 5.1 magic-item records.

Root cause 1 (extraction): SRD p217-p218 (Deck of Many Things / Defender / Demon Armor) justify the right column, pushing three line-final words (wish, spell, remove curse) flush to the page edge. That 3-item island opened a ~106pt x-gap wider than the real ~78pt gutter; the column splitter's tiny-outlier guard was capped at 2 items, so the widest-gap cut isolated the stragglers as a phantom column and collapsed both real columns into one y-interleaved flow. This spliced the embedded Avatar of Death stat block line-by-line into the Defender and Demon Armor item bodies.

Root cause 2 (parser): Sword of Sharpness wraps its category mid-rarity ('Weapon (any sword that deals slashing damage), very' / 'rare (requires attunement)'). The line ends with the bare word 'very' (no trailing punctuation, balanced parens), so categoryStartTextAt rejected it and the item heading+body were swallowed into Sword of Life Stealing. Sword of Sharpness was also missing from EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_MAGIC_ITEM_NAMES (the baseline encoded the bug).

Fix: raise TINY_OUTLIER_SIDE_MAX_ITEMS 2->3 (changes column decision on only p217/p218); accept a category-start line whose top-level comma opened the rarity field even when the rarity phrase wraps mid-word; add Sword of Sharpness to the name baseline and bump counts 237->238. title: Prevent magic item table rows from contaminating names
description: Observed during SRD 5.1 import validation: magic item records such as Armor of Vulnerability and Bead of Force were generated with preceding table rows prefixed into the name/key. Expected parser to keep embedded tables in the previous item description and use only the actual next item name.
notes:
Evidence: scratch import produced 218 magic-item records, but generated keys/names included table-row prefixes such as '1 Acid 6 Necrotic ... Armor of Vulnerability', 'Type Strength Rarity ... Berserker Axe', and '97-00 Portable Ram Rod of Absorption'. The bad values originate before emission: parseMagicItems scans backward from an item category line and treats numeric/table-header description rows as candidate name lines.
Pattern: valid wrapped item names in the focused fixtures use an actual title continuation, e.g. 'Amulet of Proof against Detection and' + 'Location'. Broken rows are body table rows immediately before a new item title; some start with digits ('1 Acid 6 Necrotic') and others are word-led table rows ('Type Strength Rarity', 'Hill giant 21 Rare'), so digit-prefix rejection alone would not address the observed artifacts.
Failing check: npx vitest run packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseMagicItems.test.ts fails before the fix. The parsed names include '1 Acid 6 Necrotic ... Armor of Vulnerability' and 'Type Strength Rarity ... Berserker Axe', and Armor of Resistance's description loses '1 Acid 6 Necrotic' because those body rows became the next entry name.
Hypothesis: body/table rows are entering names because looksLikeNameLine permits lines with ordinary numeric cells or dice/count text. Real SRD magic-item title lines that contain numbers use enhancement notation like '+1', '+2', '+3'. Rejecting title candidates with non-plus-prefixed digits should stop table-row backtracking while preserving '+N' item names and wrapped names.
Result: numeric-row filter removed the contaminated names, but the focused test still fails because 'Belt of Giant Strength' is not parsed. New evidence: category detection requires one of common/uncommon/rare/very rare/legendary/artifact and misses SRD lines that say 'rarity varies'. Additional hypothesis: include 'rarity varies'/'varies' in category detection and continuation without changing emitted rarity text.
Verified focused fix: npx vitest run packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseMagicItems.test.ts now passes, 9 tests. The regression confirms numeric and word-led table rows remain in the previous item description, following item names are clean, and 'rarity varies' category lines are recognized.
Original import verified: npm run import:dnd5e-srd now reports 222 magic items. Generated records inspection found no suspicious magic-item names matching the previous row-prefix patterns; first/last names are clean, e.g. Adamantine Armor through Wings of Flying.
close_reason: Fixed magic item name contamination by rejecting non-enhancement numeric body/table lines as title candidates and recognizing 'rarity varies' category lines; verified with focused parser regression, importer suite, and scratch SRD import/name inspection.

title: SRD 5.1 importer: Adventuring Gear, Equipment Packs, Container Capacity, and Mounts/Vehicles tables
description:
Complete the D&D SRD 5.1 equipment import by adding the equipment-chapter tables that loreweaver-3n6 intentionally left out of scope. loreweaver-3n6 reconstructed the split-column Armor (13), Weapons (37), and row-major Tools (35) tables, taking the pack from 1 to 85 equipment records, but deferred the remaining tables. These must be present in the final import — they are core player-facing equipment.

Deferred categories (currently NOT emitted):
- Adventuring Gear table (Item/Cost/Weight: backpack, rope, rations, torches, holy water, potions of healing, ammunition, spellbook, etc.) -> kind=equipment, category 'gear'.
- Tools table 'Vehicles (land or water)' row + the separate Mounts and Vehicles section (mounts, tack/harness, drawn vehicles, waterborne vehicles with speed/cost). Decide on category ('vehicle'/'mount' vs 'gear') and what structured fields, if any, to carry.
- Equipment Packs (Burglar's/Diplomat's/Dungeoneer's/etc. with bundled contents + a pack price) -- prose, not a clean table. Decide whether to model as records (e.g. category 'pack' with a contents list) or document as out of scope.
- Container Capacity table (capacity strings, no cost/weight) -- decide whether to attach capacity to the matching gear record or emit/skip.

Why this is hard (the reason 3n6 deferred it): in the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF the Adventuring Gear table extracts as TWO interleaved physical columns whose item NAMES arrive as one bare run (Abacus, Acid (vial), Ammunition, Arrows (20), ...) followed by the cost/weight cells interleaved with the adjacent column's complete rows. Several 'rows' are category headers (Ammunition, Arcane focus, Druidic focus, Holy symbol) with NO cost cell, so the name-run length != the value-run length and there is no naive positional pairing. Mounts/Vehicles is its own section after the equipment endHeading anchor. A faithful, deterministic reconstruction is required; ADR 0007 forbids guessing alignment, and 3n6 added EquipmentColumnMismatchError as the fail-closed pattern for the simple split-column tables.

Reference points in the code: parseEquipment.ts header comment documents the deferral and the gear extraction shape; sections.ts equipment anchor endHeading currently stops before 'Mounts and Vehicles' (a new anchor/region will be needed for that section); README 'Scope today' equipment row lists these as out of scope.
design: Build on the column-block reconstruction and fail-closed guard from loreweaver-3n6 (EquipmentColumnMismatchError). For Adventuring Gear, the name-run and value-run must be reconciled deterministically given the category-header rows that have no value -- likely by anchoring each value cell to its name via the (small, fixed) header structure or by a reviewed name-set baseline rather than blind zipping. Mounts and Vehicles needs a new section anchor/region. Prefer modeling decisions that keep category-specific fields optional and audit-clean (no empty strings; partial-field baseline updated like 3n6 did). If any sub-table genuinely cannot be reconstructed faithfully from the vendored PDF, that specific sub-table may stay documented out of scope with rationale -- but Adventuring Gear (the bulk of player gear) should be imported.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adventuring Gear table rows are imported as kind=equipment records (category 'gear') with verbatim cost/weight and deterministic keys + provenance, OR the specific blocking sub-table is documented out of scope with a concrete extraction rationale.
- Mounts and Vehicles entries are imported or explicitly documented out of scope (with a section anchor added if imported).
- Equipment Packs and Container Capacity are imported or explicitly documented out of scope.
- Reuse/extend the 3n6 fail-closed guard so column-block drift throws rather than emitting partial records.
- Add or extend baseline/coverage tests; update srdGeneratedPack.test.ts counts and partial-field baselines.
- Regenerate the canonical pack; npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack exits 0.
- npm run audit:rules-pack reports no new suspicious findings.
- npm run check, npm run typecheck, and npm test pass.
- Do not change source vendoring policy; do not introduce Pathfinder work.
close_reason: Imported Adventuring Gear (99), Container Capacity (attached), Equipment Packs (7), and Mounts/Vehicles (mounts 8, vehicles 6, tack/drawn gear 13). Equipment 85->218. Reused/extended the 3n6 fail-closed guard (EquipmentColumnMismatchError 'Gear' + new ContainerCapacityError). Pack regenerated; verify/audit/check/typecheck/test all green. PR pending.

title: Create D&D SRD 5.1 rules-pack audit bundle
description:
﻿Create a complete local audit bundle for external/manual review of the committed D&D SRD 5.1 rules pack.

Context:
- The committed D&D SRD 5.1 canonical generated pack is intended to be reviewed against the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF.
- A full field-by-field review is easier and cheaper if the reviewer receives a compact bundle containing the exact source artifact, generated pack, manifests, command outputs, extracted PDF text, and machine-generated audit summaries.
- The bundle must be written to D:\audit-bundle so it can be easily located and uploaded.

Output location:
D:\audit-bundle

Scope:
- Do not change parser behavior.
- Do not regenerate the canonical pack unless needed only to run an existing verification command in a temp location.
- Do not modify committed rules-pack data.
- Do not fix audit findings in this bead.
- Produce files useful for a full source-vs-pack review.

Required bundle contents:
1. Exact committed rules-pack artifacts:
   - packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json
   - packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/manifest.json

2. Exact source artifacts:
   - packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf
   - packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/manifest.json
   - packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/README.md

3. Command outputs:
   - npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack
   - npm run audit:rules-pack -- packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1
   - npm run check
   - npm run typecheck
   - npm test

4. Generated analysis files:
   - pack record counts by kind
   - list of all record keys grouped by kind
   - summary of records with partial fields / missing optional fields from auditPack
   - suspicious-record report from auditPack
   - Unicode/control-character scan of records.json
   - source manifest hash/size verification output
   - PDF text extraction by page, preferably as:
     - D:\audit-bundle\pdf-text\page-001.txt
     - D:\audit-bundle\pdf-text\page-002.txt
     - etc.
   - one combined PDF text file:
     - D:\audit-bundle\pdf-text\all-pages.txt

5. Optional but preferred:
   - extracted section spans used by the importer, if available
   - per-record source locator summary
   - generated pack diff output from verify:dnd5e-srd-pack, even when empty
   - script used to build the bundle

Implementation guidance:
- Add a script such as packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts or an equivalent repo-local tool.
- The script should create or clean D:\audit-bundle.
- The script should copy required artifacts into stable subdirectories, for example:
  - D:\audit-bundle\pack\
  - D:\audit-bundle\source\
  - D:\audit-bundle\command-output\
  - D:\audit-bundle\pdf-text\
  - D:\audit-bundle\reports\
- Prefer plain text, JSON, CSV, or Markdown outputs that are easy to upload and inspect.
- If a command fails, capture stdout/stderr and exit code in the bundle rather than discarding the output.
- Include a top-level README.md in D:\audit-bundle explaining what each file is and which repo commit produced the bundle.
- Include the git commit SHA, branch name, and timestamp in a top-level metadata JSON file.
- Avoid absolute local paths inside reports except where useful for audit traceability.
- Ensure the bundle is deterministic enough that rerunning it on the same commit produces comparable outputs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Running the new bundle command creates D:\audit-bundle.
- D:\audit-bundle contains the committed D&D SRD 5.1 pack records and manifest.
- D:\audit-bundle contains the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF and source manifest.
- D:\audit-bundle contains captured outputs for verify, audit, check, typecheck, and test commands.
- D:\audit-bundle contains extracted PDF text by page and combined PDF text.
- D:\audit-bundle contains machine-readable summaries of record keys, counts by kind, suspicious findings, partial/missing fields, and Unicode/control-character scan results.
- D:\audit-bundle contains a README.md and metadata.json identifying the repo commit and source artifact hash.
- npm run check passes after adding the bundle tool.
- The PR does not modify parser behavior or generated canonical pack data.
- Final handoff explains how to run the bundle command and where to find the output.
close_reason: Bundle script implemented and PR opened at https://github.com/jbongaarts/loreweaver/pull/142

title: Split SRD traps and hazards into structured records
description:
﻿Split D&D SRD 5.1 trap/hazard content into appropriate structured records.

Problem:
The final accuracy audit found trap content contaminating spell:zone-of-truth, and the SRD Traps section contains general trap rules, trap DC/damage tables, and sample traps such as Fire-Breathing Statue, Pits, Poison Darts, Poison Needle, Rolling Sphere, and Sphere of Annihilation. The current importer has limited hazard support and does not clearly represent this trap content as structured records.

Scope:
- First ensure trap text is not included in spell records; if not already fixed by the spell-boundary bead, depend on or coordinate with that fix.
- Parse SRD Traps section content into appropriate structured records.

title: Centralize PDF hyphen-cluster normalization in SRD extractor
description: The committed canonical SRD 5.1 pack (PR #140) contains PDF hyphen-cluster artifacts (U+00AD/U+2010/U+2011 around an ASCII hyphen) in record text from parsers lacking local normalization (e.g. parseAncestries/parseFeatures/parseRules) — examples: 'appendix PH-A', '10-year-old'. Move hyphen-cluster normalization into the extraction/text layer (extract.ts) so every parser input is normalized consistently. Collapse runs of ASCII hyphen + U+00AD + U+2010 + U+2011 to a single ASCII hyphen, using explicit \uXXXX escapes. Add a committed-pack regression test asserting the generated pack contains none of those codepoints. Regenerate the canonical pack and keep verify:dnd5e-srd-pack strict (exit 0). Out of scope: exact creature name-set validation (loreweaver-0m9.5.14).
close_reason: Centralized PDF hyphen-cluster normalization in extract.ts (normalizePdfHyphenCluster applied to every emitted line); added committed-pack regression test for U+00AD/U+2010/U+2011; regenerated canonical pack (all 403 artifacts removed, counts/dashes unchanged); verify:dnd5e-srd-pack exits 0; full suite green. Pushed to PR #140 branch (cb18008).

title: parseFeats promotes Feats-section intro prose as a feat on real SRD 5.1 PDF
description:
During the loreweaver-1pw canonical-regen review, the importer's only feat record on the real vendored SRD 5.1 PDF was 'feat:a-feat-represents-a-talent-or-an-area-of-expertise-that' — the Feats-section intro paragraph promoted as a feat, with the real Grappler feat buried inside its description.

Root cause: parseFeats detects feat-name boundaries via blank lines / section-start. The real SRD 5.1 Feats section (p75) has NO blank lines: 17 lines of intro prose flow directly into the 'Grappler' name line. So (1) the intro's first line 'A feat represents a talent or an area of expertise that' is promoted at section-start, and (2) 'Grappler' (line 17) is never promoted because no blank line precedes it. The pdfkit fixture passes because Grappler sits at the slice start with no intro.

Fix (landed under loreweaver-1pw because clean feat output is a prerequisite for committing the canonical pack): reject multi-word prose lines in isFeatName (word-count guard) and additionally promote a name line whose next non-blank line is a 'Prerequisite:' line; normalize the soft-hyphen cluster in feat bodies. Add a real-PDF regression test pinning the feat set to exactly Grappler.

Reproduce (pre-fix): npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out /tmp/x then inspect feat records.
notes: Fixed in PR #140 (with loreweaver-1pw): parseFeats word-count guard + Prerequisite-lookahead + soft-hyphen normalization; real-PDF regression test pins feat set to {Grappler}. Close on merge.
close_reason: Fixed and merged in PR #140 (merge commit 86df579, with loreweaver-1pw): parseFeats word-count guard + Prerequisite-lookahead + soft-hyphen normalization; real-PDF regression test pins the feat set to {Grappler}.

title: parseSpellClassLists: Sorcerer cantrip list truncated by column-wrap on real PDF
description:
With loreweaver-qqc landing (parseSpells body-boundary fix), Fire Bolt now extracts as its own record but data.classes is still ["Wizard"] instead of ["Sorcerer","Wizard"].

Root cause is in parseSpellClassLists, not parseSpells. On SRD 5.1 p109 the column-aware extract emits the class-lists region in column order; the right-column 'Ranger Spells' header lands in the middle of Sorcerer's cantrip list:

  9: 'Sorcerer Spells'
  12: 'Cantrips (0 Level)'
  13: 'Raise Dead'      <-- spillover from prior Druid section
  14: 'Acid Splash'     <-- valid Sorcerer cantrip
  15: 'Ranger Spells'   <-- resets currentClass to Ranger, inLevelSubsection=false
  16: 'Chill Touch'     <-- supposed to be Sorcerer cantrip; lost
  17: 'Dancing Lights'  <-- lost
  18: 'Fire Bolt'       <-- lost (this is why fire-bolt.classes drops Sorcerer)

Effect: every Sorcerer cantrip after 'Acid Splash' (alphabetically) is silently dropped from the class index. Likely affects other classes whose lists span column wraps similarly.

Investigation pointers:
- parseSpellClassLists is in packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseSpells.ts.
- The extractor's column-aware emit is in packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/extract.ts (partitionItemsByColumn / bucketItemsIntoRecords).
- One fix path: keep a per-page two-column reading order in parseSpellClassLists (skip class-header lines that appear AFTER a level subsection has already opened for the current class — i.e. don't let a header in the opposite column reset state mid-list).
- Another fix path: detect class-list pages in extract and emit them with a different (row-major) ordering than the column-aware spell-descriptions pages.

Reproduce: npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack on a tree with loreweaver-qqc merged and inspect spell:fire-bolt.data.classes (and any other Sorcerer cantrip).
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/srd-spell-class-columns-creature-subtype: extract wide-gutter hatch separates single-x spell-list columns (xbh); parseCreatures preserves parenthetical subtype (2ze). Verified against real SRD PDF; full suite green.

title: parseSpells: Fire Bolt description absorbs every subsequent F-* spell body (real SRD PDF)
description:
With loreweaver-9bu landing (parseSubclasses Champion column-wrap rejection), verify:dnd5e-srd-pack now runs end-to-end and surfaces a parseSpells body-boundary regression on the real SRD 5.1 PDF:

  spell:fire-bolt:
    data.description: <correct Fire Bolt body only> →
      "...level (4d10). Fire Shield 4th-­‐‑level evocation Casting Time: ... Fire Storm ... Flame Blade ... Flame Strike ... Flaming Sphere ... Flesh to Stone ... Floating Disk ... Fly ... Fog Cloud ... Forbiddance ... Forcecage ... Foresight ... Freedom of Movement ... Freezing Sphere ... Gaseous Form ... Gate ... Geas ... Gentle Repose ... Giant Insect ... Glibness ... Globe of Invulnerability ... Glyph of Warding ... Goodberry ... Grease ... Greater Invisibility ... Greater Restoration ... Guardian of Faith ... Guards and Wards ..."
    data.higherLevels: <missing> → <bloated with another chain of spell descriptions>
    data.classes: ["Sorcerer","Wizard"] → ["Wizard"]   (Sorcerer dropped; possibly same root cause or a parseSpellClassLists miss)

Investigation pointers:

    Fire Bolt
    Evocation cantrip
    ...
    level (4d10).
    Fire Shield                <-- new spell heading on its own line
    4th-­‐‑level evocation
- parseSpells must not be recognizing "Fire Shield" (and the subsequent F-* / G-* / ... headings) as new spell headings while scanning Fire Bolt's body. Likely a heading-detection / body-boundary mismatch against the real-PDF spell layout (h=18 spell headings?). Compare with how parseSpells works on its existing fixtures.
- See packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseSpells.ts and packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseSpells*.test.ts.
- The Sorcerer-class drop from data.classes is likely a separate parseSpellClassLists real-PDF mismatch (or could be downstream of the same heading-detection issue if the spell-list scan also keys off spell headings).

LEVELED_MARKER regex now tolerates the SRD 5.1 PDF font's four-glyph hyphen cluster (U+002D U+00AD U+2010 U+2011) via a normalize-at-flatten step. Also tolerates Contagion's 'Component:' singular typo (added KEYED_FIELD_ALIASES map). title: parseAncestries missing 5 subraces on real SRD 5.1 PDF
description:

title: parseCreatures real-PDF coverage gap (193/300+) after column-aware extraction
description:
With column-aware extraction in place (loreweaver-fct), parseCreatures advances from 0 stat blocks to 193 on the real SRD 5.1 PDF, but the MIN_EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_CREATURES floor of 300 still fails verify:dnd5e-srd-pack. The remaining gap is no longer about page-level column layout — that work landed in loreweaver-fct — it's about creature-specific stat-block structure the parser doesn't yet recognize.

Investigation needed:
- Diff the 193 parsed creature names against the SRD 5.1 monsters chapter ToC to identify which families are missing (initial scan suggests Beasts / animal stat blocks are largely absent; Bandit/Cultist/etc. are intentionally out of scope per the existing 'Nonplayer Characters' exclusion).
- Determine whether the misses are sectioning (a sub-section like 'Beasts' the slicer doesn't anchor) or parser pattern coverage (meta-line / stat-line shapes outside the current regexes).
- Confirm parseFeatures status on the real PDF (currently masked by the creature coverage check failing first).

Reproduce: npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack. See packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseCreatures.ts and sections.ts.
notes:
Root causes of the 193/300 gap, in order of impact:

1. Wrong floor — SRD 5.1 CC Monsters chapter has ~201 creatures, not 300+. The Misc Creatures appendix (MM-A) was never sliced.
2. Misc Creatures appendix (p366-394) was never sliced — adds ~95 beasts/animals/swarms.
3. Column partition picked the absolute-largest x-gap; on monster pages a far-right outlier opens a larger gap than the real gutter, so partition fell back and the page emitted y-interleaved across columns.
4. Narrow-gutter pages (49pt < 50pt threshold) were not partitioned, with the same interleaving symptom.
5. Ability-score row was found via positional adjacency to "STR DEX CON…" header; column interleaving inserts a prose line between them and the score row was missed → stat block silently dropped.
6. Compound creature names embed `-­‐` (U+002D + U+00AD soft hyphen + U+2010 Unicode hyphen) which broke the name char class; Will-o'-Wisp, Saber-Toothed Tiger, Half-Red Dragon Veteran dropped.

Fixes (PR coming on branch loreweaver-w8h):
- sections.ts: add `miscellaneousCreatures` anchor for Appendix MM-A; orchestrator concatenates with main Monsters slice.
- extract.ts: partition now picks the largest VALID gap (above threshold, passes both per-side guards), not the absolute-largest. Threshold lowered 50→45 to catch narrow-gutter pages.
- parseCreatures.ts: ability-score row detected by its own six-cell pattern (first-match-wins), not by "header line + next non-blank". Soft hyphens stripped, U+2010 folded to ASCII, runs collapsed.
- index.ts: MIN_EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_CREATURES lowered from 300 to 280. Real ceiling is 296 (201 Monsters + 95 MM-A).

Result: parseCreatures yields 296 creatures (was 193); creature coverage passes.

parseFeatures status (called out in this bead): UNVERIFIED on real PDF. verify:dnd5e-srd-pack now blocks on a downstream ancestry coverage failure (13/18 subraces missing — Mountain Dwarf, Wood Elf, Dark Elf (Drow), Stout Halfling, Forest Gnome). Filed as loreweaver-3m1; parseFeatures should be re-checked after that lands.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #132 (loreweaver-w8h branch). parseCreatures now yields 296 stat blocks vs prior 193; creature coverage gate passes. Five interacting bugs addressed: Appendix MM-A slice added, column partition picks largest valid gap (not absolute largest), COLUMN_GAP_THRESHOLD 50→45, ability-score row identified by its own pattern, soft hyphens normalized. Floor lowered 300→280 (real ceiling 296). Downstream ancestry coverage failure filed as loreweaver-3m1.

title: SRD spell parser fails on real PDF's two-column layout
description:
After loreweaver-0m9.5.20 fixed the section-anchor mismatch, npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack now fails further along the pipeline with:

  importer failed: failed to parse spell "Alter Self" at page 114: incomplete spell metadata; got fields: (none)

Cause: the SRD 5.1 spell descriptions chapter is rendered as a two-column layout. The extractor groups items by y-coordinate, so adjacent lines from the left and right columns end up interleaved in the line stream — page 114 emits "Alarm" then "Acid Arrow" immediately as adjacent lines, then their metadata interleaved row-for-row ("Casting Time:1 minute" + "Casting Time:1 action" etc.). parseSpells expects a single-column flow and treats the second name line ("Acid Arrow") as the start of the next spell, leaving "Alarm" with zero metadata fields.

Same structural issue is very likely to bite parseCreatures and parseFeatures next (Monsters chapter is also two-column, and class progression tables are tabular). Pipeline tests pass because the pdfkit fixture is single-column.

Scope:
- Make the extractor column-aware: cluster items by x position into columns, sort lines within each column by y, then emit column-by-column rather than y-interleaved across columns. PageText.lines becomes column-grouped flow.
- Verify parseSpells / parseCreatures / parseFeatures still work on both real PDF and fixture inputs.
- This may want to be split per parser; track as a child epic if scope warrants.

Reproduce: npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/jbongaarts/loreweaver/pull/131. Column-aware extraction landed (item-level x partitioning before y-bucketing) + visual-gap row join + footer filter. parseSpells now succeeds on the real SRD PDF. parseCreatures advances from 0 to 193; remaining coverage gap to 300+ tracked in loreweaver-w8h (which depends on this bead).
close_reason: PR #131 merged. Column-aware extraction landed: item-level x partitioning before y-bucketing, single-cut heuristic with item-count + distinct-x guards, visual-gap row join, and footer filter. parseSpells succeeds end-to-end on the real SRD PDF. Remaining creature coverage gap (194/300+) tracked in loreweaver-w8h.

title: Commit canonical D&D SRD 5.1 generated rules pack
description:
﻿Generate and commit the canonical D&D SRD 5.1 rules-pack output from the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF.

Context:
- The SRD 5.1 PDF is now vendored and pinned under packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/.
- loreweaver-0m9.10 added generic rules-pack audit/diff tooling.
- loreweaver-0m9.6 adds committed-pack validation and a manual/path-gated verify:dnd5e-srd-pack command.
- The committed D&D SRD pack is still a seed pack and must be replaced by the canonical generated output once the importer can parse the real vendored PDF.
- loreweaver-0m9.5.20 tracks the importer bug where the current real-PDF import fails due section-anchor / vendored-PDF parsing issues.
- This bead should run after loreweaver-0m9.5.20 is fixed and after loreweaver-0m9.6 is merged.

Goal:
Make the committed D&D SRD 5.1 rules pack the durable canonical artifact generated from the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF, then make reproducibility verification strict.

Scope:
- Run the D&D SRD 5.1 importer against the vendored SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf.
- Replace the current seed generated pack under the committed D&D SRD rules-pack output location with the full generated pack.
- Review the generated output using the audit/diff tooling from loreweaver-0m9.10.
- Update committed-pack coverage/count/audit baselines from seed-pack values to reviewed full-pack values.
- Update verify:dnd5e-srd-pack expectations/documentation so the command is expected to exit 0 after canonical regeneration.
- Flip the path-gated SRD importer reproducibility workflow from informational to strict/failing, if that workflow exists.
- Keep changes focused on committing canonical generated output and its validation baselines.

Out of scope:
- Do not implement exact creature name-set validation; that remains loreweaver-0m9.5.14.
- Do not make broad parser improvements except for tiny fixes required to complete generation and already covered by loreweaver-0m9.5.20.
- Do not change SRD source vendoring/provenance policy.
- Do not change license attribution wording except to keep generated pack metadata aligned with the pinned source manifest.
- Do not introduce Pathfinder importer or Pathfinder coverage work.
- Do not hand-curate generated records.

Implementation guidance:
1. Confirm loreweaver-0m9.5.20 is complete and the importer can parse the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF.
2. Run the importer from the vendored source artifact into a temporary directory first.
3. Run rules-pack audit tooling against the temporary output.
4. Review counts by kind, suspicious findings, missing-field summaries, and manifest metadata.
5. If output contains obvious parser failures, stop and either fix a narrow importer bug or file a child bead. Do not commit known-bad canonical output.
6. Once output is reviewed, replace the committed D&D SRD generated pack with the generated output.
7. Update tests/baselines from seed-pack values to reviewed full-pack values.

title: Harden Biome config and ignore boundaries
description:
﻿Audit and harden the repository's Biome configuration after the recent Dependabot/CI cleanup work.

Context:
- Recent dependency-update repair work touched Biome-related behavior and `.gitignore` / ignore handling.
- The intended policy is that Biome remains the canonical formatter/linter for the repo, with root scripts operating repo-wide.
- Biome should honor appropriate VCS ignore boundaries without using broad or surprising `.gitignore` changes to hide files from checks.
- Prior repair work restored repo-wide Biome scripts and enabled VCS ignore support; this bead should make sure the final configuration is intentional, minimal, and documented.

Scope:
- Review `biome.json` / Biome config.
- Review root `package.json` scripts for `format`, `format:check`, `lint`, and/or `check`.
- Review `.gitignore` only for Biome-related ignore side effects.
- Review `AGENTS.md` or equivalent contributor guidance if it documents Node/Biome/dependency workflow.
- Do not perform unrelated dependency updates.

Implementation guidance:
- Prefer repo-wide Biome commands such as checking/formatting `.` rather than narrowly targeting only package directories, unless there is a documented reason.
- Ensure Biome VCS ignore support is enabled intentionally, rather than relying on accidental command narrowing.
- Keep ignored/generated paths explicit and narrow.
- Do not add broad `.gitignore` entries just to silence Biome unless those files are genuinely generated or local-only.
- Preserve existing intended exclusions for dependency folders, build output, generated output, caches, and local runtime state.
- Add or preserve a regression check if one already exists to ensure root-level files covered by Biome remain covered.
- If adding a test/script guard, keep it small and avoid brittle assumptions about every repo file.

Acceptance criteria:
- `npm run check` passes.
- `npm run format:check` passes, if present.
- `npm run lint` passes, if present.
- Root-level repo files that should be formatted/linted are still included by Biome.
- Generated, vendored, build, cache, and local runtime files are excluded intentionally.
- `.gitignore` contains only defensible project/local/generated exclusions and is not used as a dumping ground for tool failures.
- `AGENTS.md` or contributor docs accurately describe the current Node/Biome expectations if they mention them.
- Final diff is limited to Biome config, scripts, ignore/docs, and any small regression guard needed for this policy.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #121 (branch kk7-1yj-harden-config): split Dependabot PDF tooling groups + ignore pdfjs-dist/pdfkit majors, removed unconfigured npm label, documented PR #118 as superseded; locked Biome generated-data exclusion and documented ignore-boundary policy. npm run check exit 0, full suite 958 passed/3 skipped.

title: Harden Dependabot policy for PDF tooling updates
description:
﻿Update `.github/dependabot.yml` so Dependabot no longer creates unsafe grouped PRs that combine routine PDF tooling updates with major `pdfjs-dist` migrations.

Context:
- Dependabot PR #118 attempted to update `pdfjs-dist` from 5.x to 6.x alongside `@types/pdfkit`.
- `pdfjs-dist` 6.x is a semver-major release with API removals, including lifecycle APIs relevant to the SRD importer.
- The D&D SRD importer currently depends directly on PDF.js extraction behavior, so `pdfjs-dist` major updates must be handled as intentional migration work, not as routine dependency-only PRs.
- `pdfkit` and `@types/pdfkit` are related PDF tooling dependencies, but they should not be grouped in a way that hides or blocks risky extraction-runtime updates.

Scope:
- Update Dependabot npm config only.
- Split PDF tooling groups so `pdfjs-dist` is not grouped with `pdfkit` / `@types/pdfkit`.
- Allow patch/minor updates for PDF tooling.
- Ignore semver-major updates for `pdfjs-dist`.
- Strongly consider also ignoring semver-major updates for `pdfkit`.
- Keep `@types/pdfkit` patch/minor updates allowed.
- Fix the missing configured `npm` label issue by either removing the label from Dependabot config or ensuring the repo label exists; prefer config cleanup unless there is a repo-wide reason to keep the label.

Suggested shape:
- Group `pdfjs-dist` separately as PDF extraction tooling with patch/minor only.
- Group `pdfkit` and `@types/pdfkit` separately as PDF generation tooling with patch/minor only.
- Add explicit `ignore` entries for:
  - `pdfjs-dist` semver-major
  - `pdfkit` semver-major, unless there is a clear reason not to

Acceptance criteria:
- `.github/dependabot.yml` validates according to GitHub Dependabot syntax.
- Dependabot will not open another routine PR for `pdfjs-dist` 5.x -> 6.x.
- Dependabot can still open patch/minor PRs for `pdfjs-dist`.
- Dependabot can still open patch/minor PRs for `pdfkit` and `@types/pdfkit`.
- The current risky PR #118 is either closed/ignored or documented as intentionally superseded by this policy.
- No dependency versions are changed in this bead.
- No generated files, lockfiles, Biome config, or unrelated repo config are changed.
- Final response explains the resulting Dependabot policy and why PDF.js major updates require a dedicated migration bead.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #121 (branch kk7-1yj-harden-config): split Dependabot PDF tooling groups + ignore pdfjs-dist/pdfkit majors, removed unconfigured npm label, documented PR #118 as superseded; locked Biome generated-data exclusion and documented ignore-boundary policy. npm run check exit 0, full suite 958 passed/3 skipped.
