title: SRD 5.1 class primaryAbilities from Multiclassing prerequisites
description:
The base-class parser (loreweaver-0m9.5.2) emits class records with primaryAbilities: [] because the SRD 5.1 'Class Features' block does not print a per-class primary/key ability line — per ADR 0007 the importer leaves the field empty rather than authoring it from model knowledge.

The canonical SRD source for per-class key abilities is the 'Multiclassing' section's prerequisites listing (Barbarian — Strength 13, Fighter — Strength 13 or Dexterity 13, Monk — Dexterity 13 and Wisdom 13, ...). This bead: add a deterministic slice + parser for that listing, build a class-name -> abilities map, and have the class emitter populate primaryAbilities from it. Provenance still cites the source page.

This is a normalization-mapping task (ADR 0007 says a human reviews such mappings). Verify exact section placement/format against the vendored PDF; the Multiclassing section likely falls inside the core-rules slice range (Using Ability Scores .. Spell Lists).

title: Dolt-gated checkpoint tests flake (Test timed out in 5000ms) under full-suite parallel load
description:
The Dolt-gated checkpoint tests intermittently fail with 'Test timed out in 5000ms' during the full parallel 'vitest run' on Windows when the dolt binary is present. Affected tests (varying subset, 3-5 per run observed): checkpoint.store.test.ts (checkpoints a live SQLite db and lists it), checkpoint.doltRepo.test.ts (init + applySnapshot + commit yields a listable checkpoint), checkpoint.restore.test.ts (restores a checkpoint into a new db identical to the source), packages/cli/test/checkpoints.test.ts (lists a campaign checkpoint), packages/cli/test/play.test.ts (writes a real Dolt checkpoint of the campaign on graceful exit).

Root cause: these tests spawn the slow dolt subprocess; under full-suite parallelism the per-test 5s testTimeout is exceeded nondeterministically. They pass reliably in isolation (e.g. 'npx vitest run checkpoint play' => 101/101). Not a logic regression. Documented in bd memory 'dolt-checkpoint-tests-flaky-under-parallel-load'.

Acceptance: full 'npm run test' passes deterministically with the dolt binary present (no spurious timeouts). Likely fix: bump testTimeout for the dolt-gated suites, and/or reduce their parallelism (e.g. a vitest pool/sequence constraint or per-file timeout), without slowing the rest of the suite. Confirm by running the full suite several times with dolt installed.
close_reason: Added explicit 30s Vitest timeouts to real-Dolt checkpoint/play tests so Dolt subprocess work is not aborted by the 5s default under full-suite load; verification passed: focused checkpoint/play Vitest files, npm run typecheck, npm run check, and npm run test repeated 3x.

title: Canonicalize halfling subrace records for Lightfoot and Stout lookups
description:
## Problem

The SRD source headings use bare subrace names Lightfoot and Stout, and the parser currently preserves those names directly. The emitter then derives canonical record keys and display names from ancestry.name, producing records like:

- ancestry:lightfoot
- ancestry:stout

That is source-faithful, but weak for canonical lookup. A user/player request for Lightfoot

title: SRD 5.1 importer: reference-table parser
description:
**Prerequisites (apply to all SRD 5.1 importer child issues):**
- Vendored SRD 5.1 PDF must be in place at `packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf` — see that directory's README.md.
- Reference implementation: mirror the structure of `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseSpells.ts` (parser), `emit.ts` (record builder + manifest description), `index.ts` (pipeline wiring), and the test layout under `packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/`.

---

Add a parser for freestanding reference tables in the SRD 5.1 (kind=table): exhaustion levels (if not already covered by the condition parser), encounter difficulty thresholds, treasure tables, ability-check DC tables, etc. Each table becomes a kind=table record. The `table` kindSchema requires `data.columns: string[]` and `data.rows: unknown[][]`. `key` should be `table:<slug>`.

Note: table extraction from PDFs is genuinely harder than prose extraction — pdfjs reports text items with positions but does not preserve table semantics. The parser will likely need a per-table anchor + heuristic for row reconstruction. Start with the simplest tables (encounter difficulty thresholds, ability-check DCs) and document any tables that resist clean extraction so they can be re-attempted with a smarter extractor in a follow-up.

Split from the original 0m9.5.7 to keep ticket scope shippable in one session.
acceptance_criteria:
- Parser extracts at least the simple tables (encounter difficulty, ability-check DCs).
- Records satisfy dnd5e-srd table kindSchema (data.columns string array; data.rows array of arrays).
- Manifest description includes 'table' in Included record kinds.
- Tables that resist extraction are listed in the importer README with the reason and a follow-up beads issue link.
- Unit tests cover a simple two-column table and a multi-column table.

title: SRD 5.1 importer: section detection + orchestrator
description:
Add the cross-cutting section-detection layer that finds 'Spells', 'Monsters', 'Classes', etc. section boundaries inside the SRD PDF so each kind parser receives the correct slice of PageText[]. Today the spell parser (`parseSpells.ts`) runs over the entire PDF and tolerates false negatives; once more parsers land, mis-attribution becomes possible (e.g. class-spell-list 'Magic Missile' showing up as a spell-section name line, or 'Hit Points' headers in a class entry being mis-detected by future parsers). This issue adds a section-anchor table and an orchestrator that dispatches the correct page range to each kind parser.

Reference implementation: extend `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts` and add a new `sections.ts` module under the same directory. Update `parseSpells.ts` to accept a narrowed slice (no behavior change for tests that already pass narrowed slices).

This is the architectural prerequisite for every other 0m9.5 child parser. Land first.
acceptance_criteria:
- New module `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sections.ts` defines a section-anchor table identifying each SRD top-level chapter by header line.
- Orchestrator in `index.ts` dispatches per-kind page slices to parsers; `parseSpells` is refactored to accept a narrowed slice without behavior change.
- Existing pipeline test still passes byte-stable; importer output for spells is unchanged for the same PDF.
- A regression test verifies a known false-positive shape (e.g. a class-list spell name appearing in a non-spell section) is not mis-extracted by the spell parser when run through the orchestrator.
- README updated to describe the section-anchor table and how to add a new kind to the orchestrator.

title: SRD 5.1 importer: races/ancestry parser
description:
**âš  DESIGN DECISION REQUIRED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION** â€” see HUMAN flag.

**Prerequisites (apply to all SRD 5.1 importer child issues):**
- Vendored SRD 5.1 PDF must be in place at `packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf` â€” see that directory's README.md.
- Reference implementation: mirror the structure of `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseSpells.ts` (parser), `emit.ts` (record builder + manifest description), `index.ts` (pipeline wiring), and the test layout under `packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/`.
- Depends on `loreweaver-0m9.5.9` (section detection + orchestrator).

---

Add a parser for SRD 5.1 races (kind=ancestry; SRD 5.1 uses the 'race' term, normalized to the kindSchema's 'ancestry' kind per ADR 0005). Captures ability score increases, age, alignment, size, speed, languages, racial traits, and subraces.

**Open design question (need decision before agent starts):**
- **Subraces** (Hill Dwarf and Mountain Dwarf as subraces of Dwarf; High Elf, Wood Elf, Dark Elf as subraces of Elf) â€” are these:
  (a) Separate `kind=ancestry` records, each carrying the combined parent+subrace data flattened, with `overrides: ['ancestry:<parent>']`?
  (b) Sub-records embedded in the parent ancestry record's `data.subraces[]`?
  (c) Separate records with parent reference but no override, so both are usable independently?

Until this is decided, the issue should not be claimed. Decision can be appended to this description before claim.

---

## DECISION (recorded 2026-05-28) — subrace handling RESOLVED

Chosen: **(a-variant) Separate `kind=ancestry` records, flattened.**

- Parent race and each subrace are **separate `kind=ancestry` records**.
- Each **subrace record is self-contained**: it embeds the parent's shared
  traits (size, speed, base ability score increases, racial traits) flattened
  in, merged with the subrace's own additions, so a name lookup of e.g.
  "Hill Dwarf" resolves to a fully usable record without resolving the parent.
- Subrace records carry `data.subraceOf: "ancestry:<parent-key>"`; the parent
  record lists `data.subraces: ["ancestry:<child-key>", ...]` for discoverability.
- The source term "race" is preserved in `data.source: "race"` per ADR 0005.
- **Do NOT use the `overrides` field.** Per stack.ts (namesOverride /
  overrideRefMatches), `overrides` is a cross-pack replacement mechanism keyed
  by `packId/key`; a subrace has a distinct key/name from its parent, so an
  override ref is either a dangling no-op or wrongly hides the parent. The
  bead's original option (a) wording ("overrides: ['ancestry:<parent>']") is
  therefore rejected; we keep separate-records-flattened WITHOUT overrides.

Rationale: ancestries are consumed by **name lookup**
(`lookupOfKind(stack, 'ancestry', name)`), and coverage tests count records
per kind — flat, independently-resolvable records fit both. Human gate cleared.
design: Subraces: separate kind=ancestry records, flattened/self-contained, data.subraceOf + parent data.subraces[], no overrides field. See description DECISION section.
acceptance_criteria:
- Subrace-handling decision is recorded in this issue's description before implementation starts.
- Parser extracts every SRD race (and subrace) as kind=ancestry, following the recorded decision.
- Records preserve the source 'race' term inside record data while using the canonical 'ancestry' kind per ADR 0005.
- Manifest description includes 'ancestry' in Included record kinds.
- Unit tests cover a race with no subraces, a race with subraces, and a subrace record (whichever shape was chosen).
notes: Implemented; PR #104 (work/0m9-5-6-ancestry-parser) open against main. Decision: separate flattened ancestry records, no overrides. All gates green (test/typecheck/biome). Awaiting review/merge.
close_reason: Implemented and merged via PR #104. SRD 5.1 races/ancestry parser: separate flattened ancestry records, no overrides; rebased over the equipment parser (#102) and merged.

title: SRD 5.1 importer: class parser
description:
**DESIGN DECISIONS RECORDED — see ADR 0009** (docs/adr/0009-class-subclass-feature-record-kinds.md). HUMAN flag resolved 2026-05-29.

**Scope (narrowed):** This bead now covers **base-class parsing only** — the 12 SRD 5.1 base classes as `class` records. Subclasses and features are split out (see Decisions below).

**Prerequisites (apply to all SRD 5.1 importer child issues):**
- Vendored SRD 5.1 PDF at packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf — see that directory's README.md.
- Reference implementation: mirror parseSpells.ts (parser), emit.ts (record builder + manifest description), index.ts (pipeline wiring), and the test layout under packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/.
- Depends on loreweaver-0m9.5.9 (section detection + orchestrator).

---

Add a class-section parser for SRD 5.1 base classes (kind=class). Extract each base class (hitDie, primaryAbilities, savingThrowProficiencies, armorProficiencies, weaponProficiencies) into RulesRecord shape satisfying validateDnd5eClass. The class record's `key` is the link target subclasses/features reference via data.parentClass / data.source.

**Design decisions (ADR 0009):**
1. **Subclasses** → their own new `subclass` kind (addressable by name via lookup_rules), linked to parent via data.parentClass. NOT `overrides` (that is pack-layering replacement in stack.ts). Kind infra: loreweaver-0m9.5.16; parser: loreweaver-0m9.5.17.
2. **Class features** → their own new `feature` kind (distinct from player-selected `feat`), linked to grantor via data.source + level. Kind infra: loreweaver-0m9.5.15; parser: loreweaver-0m9.5.18.
3. **Class spell lists** → already handled by parseSpells.ts parseSpellClassLists; no class-side duplication.

Rationale: the only DM query surface (lookup_rules in toolLookupRules.ts) is name+kind addressed, so subclasses/features must be top-level records to be retrievable by the names players say. Full analysis in ADR 0009.
acceptance_criteria:
- Parser extracts every SRD 5.1 BASE class (12) into kind=class records.
- Records satisfy the dnd5e-srd class kindSchema (validateDnd5eClass).
- Each class record's key is stable and usable as a parentClass/source link target for subclass + feature parsers.
- Manifest description includes 'class' in Included record kinds.
- Unit tests cover at least one class with simple progression (fighter) and one with complex features (cleric or wizard) — base-class fields only; feature/subclass extraction is out of scope here.
- Subclass and feature handling is deferred to 0m9.5.16/0m9.5.17 (subclass) and 0m9.5.15/0m9.5.18 (feature) per ADR 0009.
notes: Implemented: parseClasses.ts (Hit Dice signature detection + Armor/Weapons/Saving Throws labeled-line extraction, fail-closed on missing proficiency lines), classes section anchor, emit + index wiring, ClassExtraction type, CLI counts. 8 unit tests + pipeline integration (Fighter). primaryAbilities is best-effort [] per ADR 0007 (SRD Class Features block has no primary-ability line); Multiclassing-table cross-reference tracked in loreweaver-0m9.5.19. New kinds (subclass/feature) + ADR 0009 split to 0m9.5.15-18.

title: Refactor code organization and harden typed boundaries
description:
Address technical debt identified during code review of Loreweaver main.

The current architecture is coherent, but the code still has agent-built MVP debt:
- long compressed source files reduce reviewability
- several integration hubs own too many responsibilities
- some documented seams are symbolic rather than enforced by types
- state mutation is stringly typed and too close to persistence columns
- JSON blobs and unknown payloads need stronger schemas
- provider/tool abstractions should be prepared for multiple providers
- checkpoint/Dolt internals need separation before they grow
- the public package surface should be narrowed before first release

This epic is about making the codebase easier for future agents and humans to safely evolve.
design:
Refactor order should prioritize reviewability and safety:
1. Format the repo.
2. Split integration hubs.
3. Replace symbolic seams.
4. Harden domain schemas.
5. Introduce domain-level state tools.
6. Improve provider/tool abstractions.
7. Isolate checkpoint/Dolt internals.
8. Review public API surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repository formatting is enforced.
- Major integration hubs are split along responsibility lines.
- Architectural seams are either real contracts or removed.
- Model-facing state mutation moves toward domain-level operations.
- Important live-state and rules data gain stronger schemas.
- Provider/tool interfaces are prepared for native tool schemas.
- Persistence/checkpoint internals are better isolated.
- Public export surface is reviewed before first package release.
- Existing tests pass after refactors.
close_reason: Completed: all stated refactor and typed-boundary acceptance criteria are satisfied. The sole open child, eshyra-7kn, is an explicitly gated optional follow-up requiring a future history-UX consumer.

title: Add D&D SRD coverage and audit tests
description: Add tests and audit reports that verify D&D SRD generated-pack completeness, expected categories, stable keys, schema validity, and suspicious/missing fields.
design:
Default Vitest tests operate on the COMMITTED pack at packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/, not on live importer output. Importer is treated as a one-shot construction tool, not a per-PR generator.

DEFAULT TESTS (packages/core/test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts):
- loadRulesPackFromDirectory + validateRulesPack succeed for the committed pack.
- auditPack(pack).countsByKind exactly matches a small baseline object literal (today {spell:1, creature:1}; updated by the canonical-regen PR when the pack grows). Acts as a regression guard against accidental pack drift.
- Every record.key matches /^[a-z]+:[a-z0-9-]+$/ and uses the correct kind prefix; no duplicate keys.
- Selected stable keys present (today spell:fire-bolt, creature:goblin; list grows alongside baseline).
- auditPack(pack).suspiciousRecords === [] AND missingFieldSummary === [] strict (clean today; regen PR fixes any new findings or documents a baseline before merging).
- Pack manifest license/source fields cross-check against packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/manifest.json (licenseName, attributionText, sourceTitle, sourceVersion, sourceUrl). Bridges the source-pin test (srdSourceArtifact) and pack content.

MANUAL VERIFICATION COMMAND (NOT in default test suite):
- New script packages/core/scripts/verify-dnd5e-srd-pack/cli.ts + npm script verify:dnd5e-srd-pack.
- runImporter against the vendored PDF into a temp dir, diffPacks(committed, regenerated), formatDiffReport printed, exit non-zero on any change. Prints source SHA-256 + per-kind counts so PR notes capture them.
- Today exits 1 (committed pack is seed); after the canonical-regen PR, exits 0 unless importer/parser/source/schema/lockfile changes.

PATH-GATED CI JOB:
- New workflow .github/workflows/srd-importer-reproducibility.yml triggered on push/pull_request only when these paths change: packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/**, packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/**, packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/**, packages/core/src/rules/**, package-lock.json, package.json, and the workflow file itself.
- Single job: install deps, run npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack.
- continue-on-error: true initially (committed pack is still the seed; diff is expected). The canonical-regen PR flips it to strict. Comment in the workflow points at the regen bead.

REGEN-PR PROCESS NOTE:
- Documented in packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/README.md (or that file is created): the regen PR must paste verify:dnd5e-srd-pack output (no-changes + per-kind counts + source SHA-256) into the PR description and flip the gated CI job to strict.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE:
- Exact creature name-set validation: stays in loreweaver-0m9.5.14.
- Regenerating the canonical pack from the importer: future bead/PR.
- Pathfinder coverage tests: loreweaver-0m9.9.
acceptance_criteria:
- Coverage tests assert expected category counts or reviewed coverage baselines.
- Schema validation covers all generated records.
- Audit report identifies missing optional/required fields.
- Tests fail on nondeterministic output or malformed records.

title: Fix 5 CodeQL alerts: ReDoS + workflow permissions
description:
GitHub code scanning reports 5 open alerts (all 'warning'; ReDoS ones are security-severity high):

1. packages/core/src/orchestrator/dice.ts:30 — DICE_RE has adjacent \s* groups + trailing \s*$, classic polynomial ReDoS on model-supplied dice notation.
2. packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts:13 — TOOL_CALL_FENCE has \s*\n where \s matches \n, then lazy [\s\S]*?\n?, polynomial on model output.
3. packages/cli/src/registry.ts:131 — slugify uses /^-+|-+$/g, the canonical CodeQL BAD example. Input is trusted CLI name; trivial harden.
4. packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/separation.ts:30 — normalizeRemoteUrl uses /\/+$/. Trusted local config input; trivial harden.
5. .github/workflows/ci.yml:49 — workflow has no permissions block; add top-level contents: read.

Fix all on one feature branch + PR. No behavior change expected; existing tests must keep passing.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 CodeQL alerts close after merge; npm run typecheck and npm run test pass; PR open against main.
notes: PR open: https://github.com/jbongaarts/loreweaver/pull/62 — close after merge + CodeQL re-scan confirms alerts #1–#5 resolved.
close_reason: Merged via PR #62; all 5 CodeQL alerts addressed.

title: Brainstorm: Multi-session arc boundaries (x63)
description: Explore the design space for multi-arc support in a campaign: arc data model, arc boundaries (declared vs inferred), how the active arc is surfaced to orchestrator/contextAssembler, and CLI plumbing for arc transitions. Produces an approved feature epic by updating loreweaver-x63 in place.
notes:
User clarified purpose (2026-05-24): arc tier exists for DM-agent memory management, not narrative bookkeeping. Goal is to reliably surface relevant info inside a bounded context window. Module/quest framing is intuitive but not load-bearing — what matters is when prior session history is safe to compress into a single arc summary so the DM can drop detailed recaps. Reframe arc-boundary question around the compression trigger.
Bible faithfulness audit (2026-05-24): (1) extractCampaignBible rebuilds bible from scratch each close; prior bible isn't shown to the model, no append-and-dedupe contract. (2) Prompt has no completeness/no-omit instruction. (3) No thread-resolution state machine; threads are 'open' or 'missing'. (4) Existing tests cover parsing only; no faithfulness golden test as recap volume grows. (5) Multi-arc would strictly reduce input signal (arc summaries are lossy summaries-of-summaries). Conclusion: bible is not engineered to be the active-narrative safety net today. Either strengthen it before relying on it, or pick a multi-arc design that doesn't depend on it solely.
Decomposition decided (2026-05-24): two sibling epics, no dep. New epic for bible strengthening; x63 stays scoped to arc machinery + K-recap overlap window as the independent no-forget guarantee. Player not involved in arc decisions (user constraint).
Brainstorm complete (2026-05-24). Produced: loreweaver-x63 (multi-arc lifecycle, populated with description/design/acceptance) and loreweaver-06b.1 (sibling 'Strengthen campaign bible faithfulness' epic). Both pass bd lint. Two epics are independent (no bd dep).
close_reason: Brainstorm complete. Produced loreweaver-x63 (populated with description/design/acceptance) and sibling loreweaver-06b.1 (Strengthen campaign bible faithfulness). User approved x63 design and elected to proceed directly to writing-plans for x63.

title: Brainstorm: model-extracted campaign bible (06b-B)
description: Explore design for loreweaver-5ze. Decide: combine bible extraction with the arc-summary model call or run as two separate calls; JSON parsing/validation strategy; error-handling interaction with the arc rollup. Reuses 4ua plumbing pattern.
notes:
Decision (Q1): Pipeline — extract bible first, then pass bible into the arc-summary prompt so the summary can reference named NPCs/factions canonically. Implication: composeArcSummary signature grows to accept a CampaignBible input; CLI rollupCampaignArc orchestrates two sequential model calls.
Decision (Q2): Bible failure path = retry once, then atomic-skip (skip both bible and arc summary; prior arc_summary stays). Arc-summary call retains 4ua's single-attempt contract. Combined contract: bible-extract call -> on error, retry once -> on second error, log warning + return early. If bible succeeds and arc-summary subsequently fails, atomic-skip (log warning + return early before rollupArcSummary write).

Decision (Q3 — JSON parsing): follow orchestrator's fenced-block pattern. Dedicated fence tag (e.g. 'bible_json'); parse with a small regex + JSON.parse + shape check (object with worldFacts/majorNpcs/factions/openThreads each string[]); throw typed MemorySummaryError on parse/shape failure.
close_reason: Design approved; epic populated on loreweaver-5ze; 5 child tasks filed under loreweaver-5ze.1-5.

title: Brainstorm x3w: Ask clarifying questions
description: Ask focused questions one at a time to clarify scope, constraints, and success criteria for multiple rules-pack support.
notes:
Clarification: support both concepts: (1) mutually distinct base RPG systems such as D&D vs Pathfinder, and (2) additive/expansion rules packs that layer onto a compatible base system. Campaign binding should distinguish base system identity from ordered compatible add-ons rather than treating all active packs as equivalent.
Clarification: additive rules packs must have explicit load order/precedence. The campaign binding should persist an ordered add-on list, not an unordered set, so lookup and validation can make deterministic conflict decisions.
Clarification: same-key conflicts across ordered rules packs must be explicit. A later add-on may override a base/add-on record only when the record or pack declares an explicit override relationship; accidental duplicate keys fail validation.
Clarification: module/adventure packs must declare rules requirements: required base rules system plus any required/compatible add-on packs. Campaign creation should reject a module paired with an incompatible rules binding before forking campaign content.
Clarification: the first non-D&D sample/fixture should be based on a real open-licensed RPG system, not an invented toy-only rules model. Candidate selection must be verified against primary license/source materials before bundling or test fixture inclusion.
Clarification: the first real non-D&D fixture should be Pathfinder, preferably Pathfinder 2e Remaster/ORC-licensed material unless later requirements select a different Pathfinder edition/source.
Clarification: include rules-system-aware character generation in the first implementation plan. Pathfinder coverage should extend beyond pack loading/lookup into character creation validation, while preserving existing D&D SRD character creation behavior.
Clarification: Pathfinder character generation should be broad/playable rather than a narrow level-1 test-only subset. The implementation plan should still stage this carefully because Pathfinder character creation spans ancestry, background, class, ability boosts, proficiencies, feats, equipment, spells, and validation interactions.
Clarification: favor level-1 Pathfinder character generation for the first deliverable, but design data structures and validation seams to allow future level advancement without replacing the rules-pack model.

title: Fix POSIX installed CLI symlink entrypoint
description: PR 30 CI shows npm global install smoke invokes prefix/bin/loreweaver on Linux and exits 0 with no output. Root cause: npm creates a POSIX bin symlink, but the CLI entrypoint guard compares import.meta.url to process.argv[1] without resolving symlinks, so main() is skipped. Expected: installed loreweaver command runs main() and reports first-run config guidance when config env is missing.
notes:
Evidence: gh run view 26265719687 --log-failed showed npm run smoke:cli-install failing in CI at scripts/smoke-cli-install.mjs:43: expected installed loreweaver without config to exit 1, got 0, with no stdout/stderr. CI is Ubuntu Node 22, while local Windows smoke passed.
Root cause: POSIX npm global install exposes bin as prefix/bin/loreweaver symlink to @loreweaver/cli/dist/index.js. index.ts guarded main() with import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href, so symlink invocation uses argv[1]=prefix/bin/loreweaver and fails to match the real module URL. main() is skipped and Node exits 0.
Verification: npm run typecheck -> exit 0; npm run test -> exit 0 with 36 files passed / 1 skipped and 229 tests passed / 2 skipped on Windows (new POSIX symlink regression skipped locally); npm run smoke:cli-install -> exit 0. CI will verify the POSIX symlink path.
close_reason: Resolved POSIX npm-bin symlink entrypoint by realpath-resolving process.argv[1] before the import.meta.url guard; added POSIX symlink regression test. Verification: npm run typecheck, npm run test, and npm run smoke:cli-install passed locally; PR CI will verify Linux path.

title: Support multiple RPG rules packs
description: Design and implement rules-pack support for multiple tabletop RPG systems while preserving licensing boundaries, campaign compatibility, deterministic tool behavior, and system-specific terminology. A campaign binds to one base RPG rules system, such as D&D 5e SRD or Pathfinder 2e Remaster, plus an explicitly ordered stack of compatible additive packs such as expansions, bestiaries, or optional subsystems. The initial implementation must preserve existing SRD-backed behavior and add a real Pathfinder/ORC-backed fixture and broad level-1 Pathfinder character generation support.
design:
Goal: Support both distinct base RPG systems and additive expansion packs through a rules System Stack. Campaigns bind to exactly one base rules system plus an ordered list of compatible add-on packs. The binding distinguishes RPG type from expansion content, persists in the campaign SQLite database, and is used by lookup, module compatibility, tools, context assembly, and character creation.

Architecture: Add a `rules` subsystem beside the existing `srd` and `world` subsystems. Rules packs carry metadata for `systemId`, `packId`, `version`, role (`base` or `addon`), compatibility, dependencies, source, license/allowed-use policy, and explicit override declarations. The resolver validates the selected stack, sorts add-ons by explicit order, rejects incompatible systems or missing dependencies, and rejects duplicate record keys unless the later pack explicitly declares an override. Rules records expose provider-neutral fields: `systemId`, `kind`, `key`, `name`, structured `data`, `source`, `license`, and optional override metadata.

Campaign and module binding: Persist the resolved campaign rules binding in the campaign DB as authoritative campaign state using a singleton `campaign_rules_binding` table with base system/pack/version, ordered add-ons JSON, and resolution timestamp. The CLI registry may record pointer metadata, but play, checkpoint, restore, and unmanaged `LOREWEAVER_DB_PATH` campaigns read the DB binding. Module packs gain `rulesRequirements` declaring required base system/version and required/optional add-on packs. `createCampaign` validates the selected rules binding against module requirements before forking module content. Existing SRD-only campaign DBs without an explicit binding default/migrate to the current D&D SRD base binding.

Lookup and tools: Replace the model-facing `lookup_srd` seam with provider-neutral `lookup_rules`. The tool accepts `kind`, `name` or `ref`, and optional `systemId`; by default it resolves through the campaign binding. Tool results include the resolved record, source pack, license metadata, and override chain. `lookup_srd` may remain temporarily as a compatibility wrapper, but the default tool registry and system prompt should move to `lookup_rules` and avoid D&D-only language. Module encounter references move from `srdRef` to provider-neutral rules refs.

Character creation: Make character creation rules-system-aware. Existing D&D SRD character creation keeps current behavior through a D&D validator. Pathfinder gets a separate validator backed by Pathfinder rules records. The first deliverable favors broad, playable level-1 Pathfinder generation rather than a tiny fixture: ancestry, background, class, ability boosts, proficiencies, feats, equipment, spells where applicable, HP, and derived values. Data structures and validation seams should remain open to future advancement beyond level 1. The canonical `character` singleton remains the shared live-state projection for now, with system-specific sheet detail carried in JSON fields and the same `mutate_state` write path.

Licensing and storage: Rules-pack license metadata should reuse or generalize the existing `PackLicense` policy shape. Bundled/public rules packs must pass a shippable policy check; user-private packs can install under `<root>/rules-packs/` but are not bundled, published, or used for hosted/public demos without a later policy. Pathfinder material should use ORC-licensed rules content only and avoid Paizo reserved material/trademarks beyond permitted references; no Paizo compatibility logo/branding is needed for core fixtures. Bundled rules packs ship with core, non-bundled packs live under `<root>/rules-packs/`, and campaign DBs persist the binding rather than copying all rules data.

File map: Add `packages/core/src/rules/*` for pack types, validation, stack resolution, lookup, bundled D&D SRD adapter, Pathfinder fixture, and licensing policy. Update `packages/core/src/campaign.ts`, `packages/core/src/persistence/schema.ts`, `packages/core/src/world/types.ts`, `packages/core/src/world/validate.ts`, and `packages/core/src/world/forkCampaign.ts` for binding and module requirements. Update `packages/core/src/orchestrator/tools.ts` and `packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts` for `lookup_rules`. Update `packages/core/src/characterCreation.ts` or split into `packages/core/src/character/*` to dispatch by rules system. Update CLI campaign creation/play paths only where they need to select or pass the rules binding. Update docs in `docs/storage.md`, `docs/world.md`, and `docs/character-creation.md`.

Tradeoffs: The System Stack is more structured than a flat list but reflects the product model: one RPG type plus deterministic expansion order. It avoids full multi-engine duplication while allowing system-specific character validators where a single generic sheet would be premature. Explicit override declarations add authoring burden but prevent accidental shadowing and make lookup results auditable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rules-pack metadata validation covers system identity, pack identity, version, role, compatibility, dependencies, license policy, allowed use, and explicit overrides.
- At least two distinct base rules systems load in tests: existing D&D SRD behavior and a real Pathfinder 2e Remaster/ORC-backed fixture.
- Campaign DBs persist an authoritative rules binding with one base pack and ordered add-ons; existing SRD-only DBs without a binding continue as D&D SRD campaigns.
- Add-on ordering is deterministic; incompatible add-ons, missing dependencies, and duplicate record keys without explicit override declarations fail validation.
- Module packs declare rules requirements, and campaign creation rejects incompatible module/rules pairings before forking module content.
- Public/model-facing lookup uses `lookup_rules` and provider-neutral rule refs/results; default prompt/tool registry no longer assume only D&D SRD naming. Existing SRD lookup compatibility remains where needed during migration.
- Licensing/allowed-use metadata is enforced for bundled/public rules packs, including rejection of user-private or unshippable material at bundle/public boundaries.
- D&D SRD character creation behavior remains covered and passing.
- Pathfinder character creation validates a broad playable level-1 character draft, including ancestry, background, class, ability boosts, feats/proficiencies/equipment/spells as applicable, HP, and derived values, with structures open to later advancement.
- Tests cover pack validation, campaign binding persistence/defaulting, lookup routing, module compatibility, explicit override behavior, licensing rejection, D&D compatibility, and Pathfinder character validation.
- Final verification commands: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` pass.

title: loreweaver play: EOF/Ctrl-D on stdin skips graceful close (session left open)
description: Found during ve6 MVP acceptance verification. In packages/cli/src/play.ts, nodeIO().prompt assumes rl.question() throws on a closed/EOF stdin and catches it to return undefined (which turnLoop treats as a graceful quit). On Node 24, rl.question() on an EOF'd stdin neither resolves nor rejects -- it hangs. The turn loop never breaks, gracefulClose never runs, and the process drains its event loop and exits 0 with the session still status=open, no session_recap, and no Dolt checkpoint. Verified: a real 'loreweaver play' run with stdin redirected from /dev/null creates the campaign and session but leaves the session open; the documented '/quit' path works correctly. The code comments in play.ts (nodeIO.prompt, turnLoop, and the CliIO.prompt contract) all explicitly promise EOF/Ctrl-D triggers a graceful quit, so this is a contract violation. Impact: Ctrl-D degrades to the crash path (session stays open, relaunch offers Resume/Close-and-recap), so there is no canon loss, but graceful close + recap + checkpoint are silently skipped.
design: Fix is localized to nodeIO() in packages/cli/src/play.ts: make prompt() resolve undefined when the readline interface emits 'close'. E.g. race rl.question() against a promise that resolves on the rl 'close' event, or set a closed flag in an rl.on('close') handler and short-circuit prompt(). Add a play.test.ts case feeding an exhausted/EOF io that asserts the close pipeline runs.
acceptance_criteria: A 'loreweaver play' turn loop that hits EOF on stdin runs the full graceful close pipeline (session marked closed, recap written, checkpoint attempted) just like the /quit path. Covered by an automated test.
notes: TDD: RED — added subprocess test 'play graceful close on stdin EOF' in packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts (spawns built CLI with empty/EOF stdin); failed against buggy dist (no 'closed and recapped', session left open). GREEN — fixed nodeIO() in packages/cli/src/play.ts to race rl.question() against the readline 'close' event so EOF resolves as undefined. REFACTOR — npm run typecheck + npm run test all green (195 pass/1 skipped). Verified with the real binary: 'loreweaver play < /dev/null' now prints 'closed and recapped (checkpoint ...)' and the session ends status=closed.

title: E8: dolt CLI is an unsatisfied external runtime dependency — embed or minimize deployment cost
description: E8 DoltRepo drives checkpoint/history/branching by shelling to a standalone 'dolt' CLI (execFileSync). That binary is NOT present on dev/CI hosts and is NOT provided by the fact that bd/beads uses Dolt internally (beads is Go and statically links the Dolt engine as a library; Loreweaver core is Node/TS and cannot consume a Go library in-process). So campaign checkpointing currently cannot run anywhere without a manual, undocumented 'install dolt' step — a real deployment-ease regression for a text-first product whose differentiator is checkpoint/restore/fork. GOAL: (1) determine whether Dolt can be embedded for a Node/TS consumer; (2) if not, deliver a design that minimizes the deployment cost of the dolt dependency (resolver + lazy/managed provisioning) so end users get zero-touch checkpointing. Relates to epic loreweaver-7wc, gates with loreweaver-d7y, and the deployment-ease principle in ADR-0001.
design:
FINDING: Dolt cannot be embedded in-process from Node/TS. Dolt's 'embedded' mode = embeddable into a Go process (beads' path) or run as a MySQL server; no official npm pkg, no WASM, no N-API binding. Beads' static-link trick is unavailable to a Node consumer.

PROPOSAL — minimize the dependency cost via a resolver + lazy managed provisioning, never a hard npm dep:

1. Resolver seam (THIS issue, implemented now, pure/offline): resolveDoltBinary() precedence = (a) explicit override env LOREWEAVER_DOLT_BIN / opt; (b) Loreweaver-managed cache dir (LOREWEAVER_DOLT_HOME or OS default); (c) PATH (dolt/dolt.exe); (d) else throw DoltUnavailableError with an actionable message (set LOREWEAVER_DOLT_BIN, brew install dolt, install.sh URL, Windows .msi, future 'loreweaver dolt install'). DoltRepo uses the resolved path instead of literal 'dolt'. Net: operators/CI can point at ANY dolt with one env var; missing-dolt still degrades to skip, never a hard failure.

2. Managed provisioner (SEPARATE approval-gated sub-issue, NOT auto-built here): opt-in 'loreweaver dolt install' that downloads the pinned dolt release for the current platform/arch from github.com/dolthub/dolt/releases, verifies checksum (and signature if available), unpacks into the managed cache. Security-sensitive (fetch+exec third-party binary) => explicit user action, pinned+verified, NOT an npm postinstall, offline/air-gap fallback via LOREWEAVER_DOLT_BIN. Hosted web/PWA future is unaffected (server image bakes dolt in).

3. CI: keep dolt-gated tests skipIf; add one dolt-equipped job (ties to loreweaver-d7y) so acceptance #1-#4 are actually exercised.

Rationale vs ADR-0001: MVP is CLI/local for dev/power users + BYOK; hosted later. This keeps zero-touch local UX, no compiled/native hard dep, dolt cost paid only by users who actually checkpoint.
close_reason: Embedding infeasible from Node (Dolt = Go-embeddable/MySQL-server only; no npm/WASM/N-API). Delivered the dependency-minimizing design: resolveDoltBinary() seam (explicit-override > managed-cache > PATH > actionable DoltUnavailableError), DoltRepo refactored off the hardcoded 'dolt', 6 offline tests, full suite 36 passed/5 skipped, typecheck 0. Operators/CI can now point at any dolt via LOREWEAVER_DOLT_BIN; missing dolt still degrades to skip. Auto-provisioner deliberately NOT built here (security-sensitive) — spun out as loreweaver-8kt (approval-gated). Proposal recorded in this issue's design field.

description: Surfaced during cck.6 review. The epic acceptance #1 boundary proof (clear dist, build core alone, assert packages/core/dist/index.js exists) is fragile: 'tsc --build' is incremental and keys off packages/core/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo. If only dist is cleared but tsbuildinfo is left, tsc reports up-to-date, emits nothing, exits 0 — making the core-alone build appear to produce no dist and the full build fail with TS2307 (a false negative observed by a reviewer). From a fully clean state (dist AND tsbuildinfo cleared) the full and core-only builds both exit 0 and emit dist/index.js (verified). Fix: make the boundary-proof procedure (and any CI step) clear tsbuildinfo too, or use 'tsc --build --force' / add a 'clean' script, so the proof is deterministic. Pure infra/hygiene — no product code change.

title: Task 6: fork campaign from checkpoint into new branch
design:
Fork = `dolt branch <name> <checkpointId>` (a new named line rooted at the chosen
commit) + materialize a fresh SQLite working copy from that checkpoint via the
existing restore path. Isolation is structural: `readSnapshotAt` time-travels with
`AS OF '<commit-hash>'`, so the fork's working copy is bound to the exact commit,
not to any branch tip — later main-line checkpoints (cp2) cannot retroactively
change what the fork materializes. The test proves this by checkpointing a mutated
mainline AFTER forking and showing a re-materialized fork is byte-identical to the
original fork and free of the mainline change. `forkFromCheckpoint` reuses
`restoreToNewWorkingCopy` (DRY) so fork and restore share one materialize path.
acceptance_criteria: npx vitest run packages/core/test/checkpoint.fork.test.ts shows 1 passed with dolt or 1 skipped without; full checkpoint suite green/skip; npm run build exits 0.

title: Task 5: restore checkpoint into new SQLite working copy
design:
Restore reads the snapshot at a commit via Dolt `AS OF '<id>'` (time-travel),
parses the generic `campaign_snapshot` rows, and rebuilds a BRAND-NEW SQLite file
at `destDbPath` — the live campaign db is never touched (single live truth
preserved). Schema records are replayed first (original SQLite `CREATE` text, so
no MySQL/SQLite DDL mismatch), then rows are inserted from canonical JSON, with
`__blob` markers decoded back to Buffers. Round-trip fidelity is asserted by
comparing `canonicalize(serializeCampaign(...))` of source vs. restored — the same
deterministic function used for the history, so equality is exact. `id` is
single-quote-escaped into the `AS OF` literal (ids are dolt hashes/refs, but the
escape keeps it injection-safe by construction).
acceptance_criteria: npx vitest run packages/core/test/checkpoint.restore.test.ts shows 1 passed with dolt or 1 skipped without; prior checkpoint suites unchanged; npm run build exits 0.

title: Task 4: CheckpointStore checkpoint + list
design:
`CheckpointStore` is the public seam for E6/E4 call sites (session-close, arc
roll-up). Constructor enforces the beads separation guard up front so an
misconfigured campaign fails fast, before any Dolt repo is created. `checkpoint`
opens the live SQLite read-only-in-effect (only SELECTs via serialize), closes it
in `finally`, and never mutates it — SQLite stays the single live truth. It is a
plain synchronous call invoked OUTSIDE the turn loop. `list` is a thin pass-through
to `DoltRepo.log`. Restore/fork are added in E8.T5/T6 to keep each task one
coherent area.
acceptance_criteria: npx vitest run packages/core/test/checkpoint.store.test.ts shows 2 passed with dolt or 1 passed (separation) + 1 skipped without; npm run build exits 0.

title: Task 3: DoltRepo CLI wrapper
design:
Dolt is driven via `execFileSync('dolt', ...)` (argv form, no shell — injection-safe
for args; SQL values are single-quote-escaped via `sq`). No long-running
sql-server: every call is a short CLI invocation, so nothing here can sit in a
per-turn path. The generic `campaign_snapshot(tbl,kind,ordinal,payload)` table
sidesteps SQLite->MySQL DDL translation entirely while still giving Dolt real
table-level versioning (so `dolt_diff`/`AS OF` work in E8.T5). `--allow-empty`
keeps checkpointing idempotent when nothing changed. `available()` probes the
binary so suites can `skipIf` on machines/CI without dolt. `log --oneline` parse is
intentionally minimal (`<id> <message>`); if a future dolt changes oneline format,
only this method needs adjusting — the `Checkpoint` shape stays stable.

title: Task 2: deterministic SQLite snapshot serializer
design:
Determinism strategy avoids SQLite->MySQL DDL translation: rows are stored as
canonical JSON keyed by sorted column names; schema is captured verbatim as the
SQLite `CREATE` text (used on restore to rebuild the SQLite working copy, not fed
to Dolt). Row order is made physical-insert-independent by sorting the encoded JSON
strings; table order is `ORDER BY name`. Blobs are base64-wrapped so JSON is total.
`canonicalize` is a fixed field-order renderer so the determinism tests assert on
exact bytes. `SnapshotRecord[]` is the interchange type consumed by E8.T3
(`DoltRepo.applySnapshot`) and E8.T5 (restore). Pure + offline: runs in CI with no
dolt binary.

title: Task 1: beads-Dolt separation guard
design:
Pure path logic, zero Dolt/IO, so it runs in CI without the dolt binary. `isInside`
uses `path.relative`: empty (equal) or a non-`..`, non-absolute relative path means
containment. Checked both directions (dolt inside beads AND beads inside dolt) plus
equality. `BEADS_RESERVED_REF` is exported as the single source of the forbidden ref
namespace so DoltRepo (E8.T3) and any sync code refuse to reuse `refs/dolt/data`.
Remote-URL collision is enforced later in `DoltRepo` (it owns remote config); this
unit covers the filesystem and ref-namespace halves of the parent-epic separation
constraint.

title: Task 3: SQLite persistence with atomic withTransaction
design:
`better-sqlite3` is synchronous, so the unit-of-work is a plain function — no
async/Promise. `db.transaction(fn)` returns a wrapped function that runs fn inside
`BEGIN`/`COMMIT` and automatically issues `ROLLBACK` if fn throws, then re-throws.
`withTransaction` simply invokes it, giving E3 (`mutate_state`) an atomic-per-turn
primitive. `:memory:` databases are used in tests (fast, isolated, supports
transactions). `Db` is re-exported as the canonical handle type so later epics
depend on this module, not on better-sqlite3 directly. `initSchema` is idempotent
(`IF NOT EXISTS` + `INSERT OR REPLACE`); E3/E4 will extend it with real tables.
WAL + foreign_keys pragmas set at open time for crash-safety/integrity per the
parent-epic design.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text:
Code review summary for `6f2f3ff..66362c4`:

Assessment: Ready to merge

Critical:
- none

Important:
- none

Minor:
- `packages/core/src/persistence/schema.ts` — `initSchema` runs two separate implicit transactions (`db.exec(...)` then `db.prepare().run(...)`). If the process crashes between them the meta table exists but has no `schema_version` row. Because `initSchema` is idempotent the next call will repair it, so this is safe in practice; but wrapping both statements in a single `db.transaction(...)` call would make the intent explicit and guard against hypothetical future statements being inserted between them.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/db.ts:7` — WAL pragma silently degrades to `memory` journal mode on `:memory:` databases (confirmed: `pragma('journal_mode = WAL')` returns `[{journal_mode:'memory'}]`). The production code path (file DBs) is correct. The tests still validate all three real behaviors (commit, rollback, schema version). No test incorrectly asserts WAL mode is active, so this is a documentation/comment gap only, not a test accuracy issue.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/db.ts` — `openDatabase` lets `new Database(path)` throw natively on bad path (e.g., `TypeError: Cannot open database because the directory does not exist`). This is fine for a foundational primitive; just note that callers will need to handle or wrap this if user-facing error messages are required in E3/E8.
- `package-lock.json` — `prebuild-install` is marked deprecated in the lock file (`"deprecated": "No longer maintained…"`). `better-sqlite3` v11 still uses it as the prebuild download mechanism, falling back to `node-gyp rebuild` when no prebuilt matches. On this machine it compiled via node-gyp (no `prebuilds/` dir present). CI environments without C++ build tools will need either a `.npmrc` with `msvs_version` / a build container, or a later `better-sqlite3` version that ships napi prebuilds for Node 24. Not a blocker for merging (works locally, tests pass), but worth a follow-up chore before adding a CI pipeline.

title: Task 1: Monorepo scaffold + vitest smoke test
description:
Objective:
Stand up the npm-workspaces monorepo (core + cli), TypeScript strict ESM build,
and vitest, proving the toolchain with one smoke test.

Files:
- Create: `package.json` (root)
- Create: `tsconfig.base.json`
- Create: `tsconfig.json` (root solution)
- Create: `vitest.config.ts`
- Create: `.env.example`
- Create: `packages/core/package.json`
- Create: `packages/core/tsconfig.json`
- Create: `packages/core/src/index.ts`
- Create: `packages/cli/package.json`
- Create: `packages/cli/tsconfig.json`
- Create: `packages/cli/src/index.ts`
- Test:   `packages/core/test/smoke.test.ts`

Steps:

1. Create `package.json` (root):
```json
{
  "name": "loreweaver",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "workspaces": ["packages/core", "packages/cli"],
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc --build",
    "typecheck": "tsc --build --force",
    "test": "vitest run"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/node": "^24.0.0",
    "typescript": "^5.6.0",
    "vitest": "^2.1.0"
  }
}
```

2. Create `tsconfig.base.json`:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "strict": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "composite": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true
  }
}
```

3. Create `tsconfig.json` (root solution):
```json
{
  "files": [],
  "references": [
    { "path": "packages/core" },
    { "path": "packages/cli" }
  ]
}
```

4. Create `vitest.config.ts`:
```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: { include: ['packages/**/test/**/*.test.ts'] },
});
```

5. Create `.env.example`:
```
# Path to the SQLite database file for the active campaign
LOREWEAVER_DB_PATH=./campaigns/dev.db
# Claude model id used by the DM agent
LOREWEAVER_MODEL=claude-opus-4-7
# Anthropic API key for the Claude Agent SDK
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
```

6. Create `packages/core/package.json`:
```json
{
  "name": "@loreweaver/core",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "./dist/index.js",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": { ".": "./dist/index.js" },
  "scripts": { "build": "tsc --build" }
}
```

7. Create `packages/core/tsconfig.json`:
```json
{
  "extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "rootDir": "src", "outDir": "dist" },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

8. Create `packages/core/src/index.ts`:
```ts
export const CORE_VERSION = '0.0.0';
```

9. Create `packages/cli/package.json`:
```json
{
  "name": "@loreweaver/cli",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "bin": { "loreweaver": "./dist/index.js" },
  "scripts": { "build": "tsc --build" },
  "dependencies": { "@loreweaver/core": "0.0.0" }
}
```

10. Create `packages/cli/tsconfig.json`:
```json
{
  "extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "rootDir": "src", "outDir": "dist" },
  "references": [{ "path": "../core" }],
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

11. Create `packages/cli/src/index.ts`:
```ts
import { CORE_VERSION } from '@loreweaver/core';

export function placeholder(): string {
  return `cli wired to core ${CORE_VERSION}`;
}
```

12. Write the failing smoke test `packages/core/test/smoke.test.ts`:
```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { CORE_VERSION } from '../src/index.js';

describe('toolchain smoke', () => {
  it('exposes a core version string', () => {
    expect(typeof CORE_VERSION).toBe('string');
    expect(CORE_VERSION.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

13. Install dependencies.
   Command: `npm install`
   Expected: installs root devDeps and links workspaces, exit 0.

14. Run the smoke test (should now PASS — pure scaffold, no RED phase for pure config).
   Command: `npx vitest run packages/core/test/smoke.test.ts`
   Expected: 1 passed.

15. Verify the build (proves project refs + core/cli wire up).
   Command: `npm run build`
   Expected: exit 0, `packages/core/dist/index.js` and `packages/cli/dist/index.js` exist.

16. Commit.
   Command: `git add -A && git commit -m "feat(e0): npm-workspaces TS scaffold + vitest smoke test"`
design:
Scaffold-only task: no RED phase because there is no behavior yet — the "test"
is that the toolchain (install, vitest, tsc project-reference build) works end to end.

Key constraints:
- ESM everywhere: `"type": "module"`, `module`/`moduleResolution` = NodeNext.
  Relative imports in source/tests MUST use the `.js` extension (e.g.
  `../src/index.js`) even though the file is `.ts` — required by NodeNext.
- `composite: true` is mandatory for `tsc --build` project references.
- `@loreweaver/cli` depends on `@loreweaver/core` and never the reverse; npm
  workspaces symlink resolves the dependency.
- `.db` is already gitignored (campaign DBs are not committed).

This task only establishes structure; config/persistence/model/seam modules are
added by Tasks 2–6 which import from `packages/core/src`.
acceptance_criteria: npm install exits 0; npx vitest run packages/core/test/smoke.test.ts shows 1 passed; npm run build exits 0 with packages/core/dist/index.js and packages/cli/dist/index.js present.
close_reason: Scaffold complete; spec-compliant and code-quality approved. Commits caa915b, 2c3ba58, a997ea0.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text:
Code review summary for `1423dbe..2c3ba58`:
Assessment: Ready to merge

Critical:
- none

Important:
- `packages/core/package.json` exports map uses only the bare string `"./dist/index.js"` with no condition keys (`import`/`default`). NodeNext consumers can resolve this, but when later tasks add CJS interop or type-only re-exports the lack of a `types` condition in the exports map will require a breaking change. Recommendation: expand now to `{ ".": { "import": "./dist/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } }` so the `types` field inside `exports` is authoritative for TypeScript ≥5.0 `bundler`/NodeNext resolution (the top-level `"types"` key is a fallback).
- `.env` is not gitignored. `.env.example` is committed (correct), but if a developer creates `.env` from it the actual secrets file will be untracked but not ignored — no protection against accidental `git add`. Add `.env` to `.gitignore` in the same chore commit or a follow-up.

Minor:
- `package.json` has no `engines` field. The repo is running Node 24; later tasks will use Node-24-only APIs (e.g. the Anthropic Agent SDK). Adding `"engines": { "node": ">=22" }` now documents the minimum and npm will warn on mismatched installs.
- `package.json` has no `packageManager` field. Adding `"packageManager": "npm@11.12.1"` (current version) enables corepack enforcement and signals intent to future contributors.
- `vitest.config.ts` glob `packages/**/test/**/*.test.ts` will silently skip a test file placed in e.g. `packages/core/src/__tests__/foo.test.ts`. The pattern is fine for the current layout; just document the convention (tests go in `test/`) somewhere visible (CLAUDE.md architecture section) before task 2 adds more tests.
- `typecheck` script uses `tsc --build --force` which re-compiles all packages regardless of cache, making it slow at scale. It is a reasonable escape hatch but the name `typecheck` implies type-checking-only (no emit), whereas `--force` still emits. Consider `tsc --build --noEmit` or renaming to `rebuild`.

Follow-up:
- loreweaver-cck.2+ authors should be aware: adding new source files to `packages/core/src` requires no tsconfig change (glob via `include: ["src"]`), but test files outside `packages/*/test/` will not be picked up by vitest — document in CLAUDE.md.
- Expand `exports` map in core before first public-facing release (task 6 or sooner).
- Add `.env` to `.gitignore` (can be done in task 2 chore).

title: E6 Session lifecycle + thin CLI front-end
description: Player-facing wrapper: campaign create/fork, Campaign/Session/Scene lifecycle with explicit start and AUTO-CLOSE on graceful exit, idempotent close pipeline, crash-safe resume, thin CLI over the core.
design: Session states open/closed; at most one open session per campaign. Launch: if open session exists offer Resume (reattach, reload scene tail) or Close-and-recap; else Start new. Graceful exit runs close pipeline: final scene_summary, session_recap, state reconciliation, arc roll-up if milestone, mark closed. Crash: session stays open, only current unsummarized scene tail volatile (survives in scene_log), no canon loss. Close pipeline idempotent. CLI is a thin presentation layer (campaign select/create, prompt I/O, streaming, resume prompt) with no game logic.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Create/fork a campaign from a module template via CLI. 2. Start, play, graceful-exit auto-runs full close pipeline. 3. Simulated crash leaves session open; relaunch offers Resume and Close-and-recap; Resume reloads scene tail with zero canon loss. 4. Re-running close pipeline after partial failure produces no duplication/corruption. 5. CLI contains no game-rule logic.
notes: SYNTHESIS UPDATE 2026-05-17: E6 remains CLI/local-first. CLI is the near-term power-user/dev surface and should keep game logic in core. Medium-term public UX is a hosted mobile-friendly web/PWA over the same core; native mobile is deferred. BYOK is the default early billing shape. Hosted BYOK requires separate secret-handling design; hosted credits are future optional and not an MVP blocker.
close_reason: All 12 children complete; thin CLI front-end (ua0.12) merged in PR #12, exit-time Dolt checkpoint in PR #13. Epic acceptance #1-#5 met.

title: E5 Orchestrator + turn loop + Context Assembler + tools
description: The integrating loop: per-turn cycle via Agent SDK, bounded-context assembly, deterministic tools (roll, mark_scene), and the DM system prompt encoding the refined-Hybrid rules contract.
design: Orchestrator: player text to Context Assembler builds bounded prompt (campaign_bible + current arc_summary + last session_recap + full structured-state snapshot + current scene live transcript) to Agent SDK call to execute tool calls deterministically to stream narration to append scene_log to (if scene boundary) write scene_summary. Tools: roll(dice,reason) code-owned RNG, mark_scene(boundary,title). Integrates lookup_srd (E1), mutate_state/overlay (E3/E2), memory_drilldown (E4). System prompt: DM persona + Hybrid contract (narrate freely; all math/dice/state via tools; lookup_srd before running any creature). Turn atomic; tool error returns structured error to model; model/SDK failure leaves pre-turn state intact.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A full player turn runs end to end: prompt assembled, model called, tools executed, narration streamed, scene_log appended. 2. Assembled prompt contains only the bounded set, excluding older history unless drilled down. 3. roll RNG is code-owned and reproducible under seed in test. 4. Model attempting to change state via prose (not tool) does not mutate canon. 5. lookup_srd invoked before a creature is run in a combat scenario test.
notes: SYNTHESIS UPDATE 2026-05-17: E5 owns bounded context and model quality discipline. The Context Assembler must avoid whole-history prompts, use compact active-scene/state/memory slices, and leave room for provider prompt caching where available. Turn orchestration should emit cost/latency/quality instrumentation by model profile and support an evaluation harness for premium_dm continuity, canon, NPC consistency, structured output, rules, tool use, and memory-update quality.

title: E4 Memory pyramid + roll-up + structural drill-down
description: Hierarchical memory as the CORE continuity mechanism: scene to session to arc to campaign_bible, bounded always-on context independent of campaign length, anchored by E3 structured state. Raw scene_log persisted for future RAG (deferred).
design: Tables: scene_log (append-only raw), scene_summary (incremental, salient_refs linking to state/overlay rows), session_recap, arc_summary, campaign_bible (standing world_facts, major_npcs, factions, open_threads). Roll-up steps are separate focused agent invocations writing strictly upward, each citing source ids (re-runnable, idempotent). memory_drilldown(selector) pulls a specific older summary/log slice into context on demand only. Semantic/RAG retrieval DEFERRED - structural drill-down only for MVP.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Scene summaries written incrementally during play. 2. Session close produces a recap from scene summaries plus state delta. 3. Arc milestone folds recaps into arc_summary and reconciles campaign_bible. 4. Roll-up idempotent (re-run yields no corruption). 5. memory_drilldown returns a specific past scene/session without it being permanently in context. 6. Always-on memory footprint stays bounded as session count grows.
notes: SYNTHESIS UPDATE 2026-05-17: Memory rollups should also preserve structured turn traces useful for future eval/helper-model training: retrieved context, prompt profile, model output, tool calls, accepted/rejected state deltas, memory updates, corrections, and quality flags. Raw transcripts alone are not the valuable future dataset.

title: Brainstorm: Loreweaver agentic Dungeon Master
description: Explore requirements and produce an approved feature epic for an agentic DM: reusable rules KB, campaign KB (template + instances), cross-session memory, DM agent on Claude Agent SDK, deterministic tools.
notes:
MVP target: Solo persistent campaign - single player, small campaign across many sessions, persistent memory, world mutates over time. Exercises memory + campaign-state subsystems from day one.
Rules approach DECIDED: refined Hybrid. (1) Model-trusted for narrative rule adjudication. (2) All math/dice/state changes via deterministic tools. (3) Structured SRD monster/spell stat-block lookup tool (queryable data store, NOT fuzzy RAG). (4) Prose-rules RAG DEFERRED until proven necessary in real play (YAGNI for MVP). Reframes 'reusable rules KB' as lightweight structured stat-block store + lookup tool.
Memory model DECIDED: Hierarchical memory as CORE architecture. Pyramid: scene->session->arc->campaign-bible summaries, rolled up by reasoning steps. DM always holds bounded top-of-pyramid in context; drill-down on demand via tool. Anchored by EXACT annotated/provenance-bearing structured state (re-asserted every turn, anti-drift). Raw scene log persisted from day one. Semantic retrieval (RAG) DEFERRED - added later only as drill-down accelerator if real play shows pinpoint-recall gaps. Never RAG-only. Context budget bounded regardless of campaign length - key requirement (user: continuity over long campaigns is top priority).
Campaign content DECIDED: Real deliverable = structured module SCHEMA (locations[], keyed encounters[], npcs[], triggers/plot_flags[], lore[]). MVP seeds it via ONE-TIME model-assisted conversion of ONE openly-licensed adventure - content task, NOT a reusable parser. General importer DEFERRED. World mutation = immutable authored module (template) + per-campaign diff/overlay = current world (git-like, parallel to structured-state design). OPEN QUESTION/RISK: must identify a specific confirmed openly-licensed (CC-BY/ORC/OGL) adventure - SRD itself has NO adventures. Lost Mine of Phandelver etc. are NOT open-licensed.
Interface DECIDED: Local CLI as THIN presentation layer over a UI-agnostic CORE library (game loop, agent orchestration, memory, storage, tools). Future web/multiplayer = new front-end on same core (DEFERRED but unblocked by this boundary). Model: Campaign (long-lived) > Session (explicit open; AUTO-CLOSE on graceful exit runs recap+scene->session roll-up+state reconciliation) > Scene (roll-up granularity, summaries written incrementally during play). Crash/non-graceful exit leaves session OPEN; relaunch offers Resume vs Close&recap. Canon crash-safe via live tool state writes + incremental scene summaries; only current scene transcript tail volatile.
Language DECIDED: TypeScript with official Claude Agent SDK. Rationale: Agent SDK is Python/TS-only (no official C#/Kotlin); user dislikes Python, native C#/Kotlin, reviews-not-writes code; TS static typing strong for schema-heavy core (module schema, annotated structured state, pyramid nodes, overlay diff); reads close to C#/Kotlin for review; shares types with future web front-end. Polyglot/raw-API-in-native REJECTED as premature/off-norm.
DESIGN APPROVED by user (with tweaks incorporated). Tweak: added E7 Character creation & import; broadened E1 to SRD reference store (creatures+spells+character-build options). Creation = agent-guided conversational + deterministic validation tools, MVP. Import (D&D Beyond, OCR paper, VTT) DEFERRED, all map onto one canonical character schema (E3-owned). Proceeding to create overarching epic + E0-E7 sub-epics.
Epics created: parent loreweaver-ve6; sub-epics E0=cck E1=zzy E3=c07 E7=ay3 E4=wsv E2=hlu E5=ws9 E6=ua0; legal-source risk task loreweaver-40w. Dependencies wired for build order E0 -> (E1||E3) -> E7 -> E4 -> E2 -> E5 -> E6; parent depends on all sub-epics.
close_reason: Brainstorm complete; design approved; overarching epic loreweaver-ve6 + sub-epics E0-E7 + risk task created and approved by user. Transitioning to implementation planning for E0 (loreweaver-cck), the only unblocked epic.

title: Polish rules-pack story with final author edit
description:
Follow-up editorial refinement for the existing /rules-pack/ article originally implemented under eshyra-5f2w. The article is already good enough to ship and remain public long-term. This is optional P3 refinement, not a correctness blocker.

This task is deliberately split between agent work and human authorship. The agent may make only the narrow factual and wording corrections below, then must pause before creating a PR and explicitly ask Joseph to perform his own hand-edit pass on the article. The PR must not be created until Joseph confirms that his edits are complete. The intent is not to have an agent simulate Joseph's voice. The article has already had substantial model-assisted drafting and editing, and Joseph must perform the final personalization pass himself.

Required agent edits:
1. Replace the overstatement approximately phrased as "The pack never needed more data." Preserve the distinction that adding unstructured content was insufficient, richer semantic representation was necessary, and the deeper issue was semantic structure and execution ownership. Use wording such as "The problem was not simply that the pack needed more data." or "More data was not the answer by itself." Choose what fits the surrounding prose.
2. Replace the imprecise statement approximately phrased as "None of that survives as English." The source information does exist in prose and can be understood by a person or model. Clarify that the semantics are not deterministically enforceable while represented only as prose, using wording such as "None of that is machine-enforceable while it exists only as English prose."
3. Restore personal ownership of the importance judgment, preferring "The second example is subtler, and I think more important."
4. Rewrite the line that reads like an editing instruction, approximately "One distinction here is easy to misread, so state it flatly." Use natural prose such as "One distinction here is easy to misread, so it is worth stating flatly."
5. Rewrite the awkward "guessed at into" construction while preserving fail-closed semantics. A suitable shape is: "Prose that falls outside the reviewed shape contributes no semantics at all. The grammar fails closed rather than inventing something plausible."
6. Remove the minimizing "only" from the playtest conclusion. Preserve the boundary that the compiler owns immutable pack semantics, live state remains separate, engine execution remains separate, and playtesting changed the project's understanding of how much semantic information the pack needed to provide. Prefer wording such as: "What playtesting changed was our understanding of how much the pack itself had to say for those other layers to function."

Required human hand-edit checkpoint:
1. The implementation agent creates a branch or worktree for the task and applies only the six narrow corrections.
2. Run enough local verification to ensure the article still builds.
3. Commit the agent-authored mechanical/editorial corrections if that makes the handoff cleaner.
4. Stop before creating a PR.
5. Tell Joseph the exact worktree path, the file to edit (site/src/rules-pack.html.tmpl), and a useful local preview or build command.
6. Explicitly ask Joseph to edit the article directly and tell the agent when his personal prose pass is complete.
7. Wait for Joseph's confirmation.
8. After confirmation, inspect the diff, preserve Joseph's prose choices, and do not normalize his voice toward generic model prose. Make only obvious typo, HTML, or factual corrections if needed, preferably flagging substantive concerns instead of silently rewriting them.
9. Commit Joseph's hand-edit changes separately from the agent edits where practical. Do not add an AI co-author trailer to a commit whose substantive prose changes were written by Joseph.
10. Run full required verification, then create the PR only after the human checkpoint is complete.

Voice guidance:
Preserve Joseph's established authorial traits: analytical and curious; concrete examples before abstraction where useful; audience-calibrated jargon; dry humor that arises naturally; visible uncertainty where real; willingness to show how the conclusion was reached; and parenthetical precision where useful.
Use we for shared work, discovery, accomplishment, and credit. Use I for personal judgment, doubt, criticism, uncertainty, mistakes, and negative responsibility. Reflect praise and absorb blame.
No em dashes and no literal em dash characters or —. Do not introduce repetitive "not X, but Y" constructions, artificial three-part cadence, excessive rhetorical questions, slogan-like conclusions, generic polished transitions, or paragraphs that over-explain examples. The goal is genuine authorship, not model imitation.

Tooltip verification:
The article contains a tooltip-style author aside that previously had clipping problems. During final verification check normal desktop width and narrow/mobile width. Confirm the entire tooltip remains readable, clips on neither side, creates no horizontal scrolling, reveals on keyboard focus, and retains accessible wiring. Make a CSS change only if a real presentation problem remains.

Acceptance criteria:
- All six identified wording issues are corrected.
- No substantive architecture claim is changed.
- Joseph is explicitly invited to perform the final hand-edit pass before PR creation.
- No PR is created until Joseph confirms his hand edits are complete.
- Joseph's resulting prose edits are preserved rather than rewritten by the agent.
- The final article contains no em dashes.
- Tooltip behavior is verified at desktop and narrow widths.
- The site builds successfully.
- No unsubstituted placeholders remain.
- Homepage, article, and download links still work.
- ZIP and checksum generation still work.
- Repository-required checks pass.
- No generated rules-pack records change.
- No freeze manifests or audit artifacts change.
- The final PR description distinguishes the narrow agent corrections from Joseph's hand-edit pass.

title: What Actually Transfers?
description:
Tell the deferred story of adding a second game system.

Narrative hook and core question: After building a deeply D&D-specific compiler, what parts of the architecture were actually reusable?

Do not draft or publish until Pathfinder implementation has materially tested the abstractions. Research source and license authority, source inventory, format-appropriate extraction boundaries, structural parsing versus semantic projection, shared semantic grammars, source-grounded executable curation, pack semantics versus engine services, system-specific versus shared engine behavior, tool integration, character-creation recipes, quality bars, freeze policy, and the lesson that reuse contracts, not document heuristics. The second system is the first honest test of abstraction.

Expected architectural conclusion: only Pathfinder evidence can show which contracts transfer and which apparent abstractions were D&D-shaped assumptions.

Boundary: do not write speculative architecture storytelling based only on D&D. Do not draft or publish before meaningful Pathfinder implementation and campaign-facing evidence exists.

This bead is intentionally deferred. Treat repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence once Pathfinder work exists. Verify claims against artifacts rather than model memory; distinguish implemented architecture from planned architecture; preserve public readability and search indexing; and follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.

title: The Adventure Is Not the World
description:
Tell the story of first-class adventure modules.

Narrative hook and core question: What is an adventure module in a system that can improvise indefinitely?

Write only after module architecture is implemented and exercised enough to tell the history honestly. Research why prompt injection of adventure text is insufficient; module as authored canonical spine; module schema and typed records; campaign binding; module progress state; DM runtime context; progress audit; module truth versus player-discovered knowledge; authored content versus campaign divergence; and how improvised consequences overlay authored content without rewriting the source module. Cover Ember Hollow only when the evidence and naming in the repository support it.

Expected architectural conclusion: an adventure module is authored scenario truth with campaign-owned progress and divergence, not the whole world and not a prompt pasted into context.

Boundaries: do not treat the current module epic as complete if it is not. Do not claim module UX or playtest maturity that artifacts do not support. Do not absorb the campaign-memory or rules-pack compiler story.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify claims against artifacts rather than model memory; distinguish implemented from planned architecture; preserve public readability and search indexing; and follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.

title: A Save Game Is Not a History
description:
Tell the story of campaign checkpoints and history.

Narrative hook and core question: What changes when a campaign must answer not only “can I restore?” but also “what changed, when, and why?”

Research local SQLite campaign/session state, checkpoint snapshots, restore authority, Dolt's role in canonical history, semantic projections or useful diffs, rewind, timeline branching and forking, zero-ops CLI constraints, why a database in the hot gameplay path and a history system are different concerns, and how checkpointing interacts with long campaigns and auditability.

Expected architectural conclusion: a save file restores state. Campaign history also needs explainable change, chronology, and eventually branching.

Boundaries: do not claim unimplemented history UX is shipped. Distinguish current behavior, committed architecture, and future direction. Do not turn this into a generic database article.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify factual claims against artifacts rather than model memory. Keep the story static, search-indexable, and readable without prior repository knowledge. Follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.
